109-1-LB100_IntroLB100_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentThe bill requires the Director of Economic Development to electronically file an annual report (first due July 1, 2026) to the Legislature documenting: (a) the percentage of economic development funds awarded to (i) individuals starting new businesses or (ii) individuals/entities that provide services to businesses established within the previous five years and based in Nebraska; and (b) the total dollar amount of such awards. Beginning July 1, 2026, the Department of Economic Development is encouraged (not required) to allocate five percent of its economic development funds to those recipients. "Economic development funds" is defined as amounts budgeted for programs administered by the Department, including community development block grants. No specific appropriations or mandatory budget transfers are imposed.Key additions affecting the Department of Economic Development (effective July 1, 2026): - The Director must annually file a report with the Legislature (by July 1 each year) showing (a) the percentage and (b) the total dollar amount of economic development funds awarded to (i) individuals starting new businesses and (ii) individuals/entities that provide services to businesses established within the previous five years and based in Nebraska. - The Department is encouraged (not required) to award 5% of its economic development funds to those same startups/service providers. - "Economic development funds" are defined as amounts budgeted for programs the Department administers, including Community Development Block Grants. - No mandatory appropriation changes to the Department’s budget are prescribed.
109-1-LB101_IntroLB101_Intro_Copy.docxLB101 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to (1) bar rental‑agreement waivers of state and federal rights and certain indemnifications, and (2) create/clarify a right to jury trial in eviction (restitution) actions. Procedural changes assign duties to courts and court staff: complaints for possession are filed with the clerk of the district or county court and may demand a jury; summonses must notify defendants of the right to a jury trial; courts must inform/confirm a defendant’s jury demand if not timely made; nonjury trials are set 10–14 days after summons and jury trials are scheduled as practicable (courts may require tenants to deposit rent if a jury trial is continued). If judgment issues, constables or sheriffs execute writs of restitution within ten days. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Original sections amended are repealed.Adds procedural protections in possession actions requiring the complaint to notify defendants of the right to a jury trial. If no jury demand is made by first appearance, the court must inform the defendant and, in county court, ask whether they demand a jury or waive it. Timelines: bench trials must occur 10–14 days after summons; jury trials scheduled as practicable. If a tenant requests a continuance of a jury trial beyond the initial date, the court may require the tenant to deposit accrued rent with the clerk of the court. Agencies mentioned: courts (county court) and the clerk of the court. No funding or appropriation changes.
109-1-LB102_IntroLB102_Intro_Copy.docxLB102 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-513 to set the aid-to-dependent-children (ADC) "standard of need" at $1,132.50 for a single individual plus $393.00 for each additional ADC unit member, effective July 1, 2026. It requires annual adjustments each July 1 beginning July 1, 2026, based on the prior calendar year's Consumer Price Index as determined by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics. The standard of need continues to be used to calculate ADC benefit amounts (capped by §43-512). The bill repeals the original §43-513. No specific government agency or department is named, nor does the text create an explicit appropriation or new funding line—it sets benefit-calculation parameters.
109-1-LB103_IntroLB103_Intro_Copy.docxLB103 amends Nebraska Evidence Rule §27-412. It clarifies that evidence that a victim engaged in other sexual behavior, was the victim of another sexual assault, or that shows sexual predisposition is generally inadmissible in civil or criminal sexual-misconduct cases, with limited exceptions: (1) evidence to show another person was the source of physical evidence; (2) evidence of specific prior sexual behavior with the accused, if similar and probative of a pattern bearing on consent; and (3) evidence required by the accused’s constitutional rights. In civil cases, such evidence is admissible only if probative value substantially outweighs harm. The bill requires a written pretrial motion (generally 15 days before trial), service on parties and the victim, an in camera hearing, and prohibits questioning victims in pretrial proceedings about matters inadmissible under the section. No state agencies or departments are named and no funding or appropriations are affected.Adds a provision that a victim may not be questioned during any pretrial hearing or proceeding — including depositions — about matters that are inadmissible under this section. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.

109-1-LB111_IntroLB111_Intro_Copy.docxLB111 regulates insurer practices for motor vehicle repairs involving nonoriginal equipment manufacturer (non‑OEM/aftermarket) parts. It (1) defines terms (referencing consumer definitions in sections 60‑2701 and 60‑1401.10); (2) bars insurers from requiring non‑OEM parts that lack permanent manufacturer identification or that are not equal in fit and performance to OEM parts (including consideration of modification costs); (3) requires written consumer consent before using non‑OEM parts, clear identification of such parts on estimates, and a prescribed ten‑point notice to consumers; (4) prohibits insurers from charging consumers the price difference if the consumer elects OEM parts; (5) forbids requiring aftermarket parts for vehicles manufactured within 36 months of damage; and (6) permits a specific policy notice for older vehicles. Violations are Class I misdemeanors. No state agencies are named and there are no funding or appropriation changes.Adds definitions (consumer; consumer care; insurer; nonoriginal equipment manufacturer; part) and prohibits insurers from requiring non‑OEM parts that lack permanent manufacturer ID or that are inferior in fit/performance. Insurers must notify consumers in writing (≥10‑point type) and obtain written consent before using non‑OEM parts; identify any such parts in the repair estimate; and may not require aftermarket parts for vehicles <36 months old. Policies for vehicles >36 months may include a capitalized 10‑point notice allowing aftermarket parts. Violations are a Class I misdemeanor. No government agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations are mentioned.
109-1-LB112_IntroLB112_Intro_Copy.docxLB112 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§60-171 and 60-173 concerning salvage-branded certificates of title. Key agency references and changes: - Department (and its director): required to receive insurer notifications when owners retain salvage vehicles, immediately enter a salvage brand on the department’s computerized record, and accept insurer electronic reporting via the department’s electronic reporting system once the director sets an implementation date under §60-1508. - County treasurer: must receive properly endorsed certificates and issue salvage or previously salvaged branded certificates (previously salvaged if repaired and inspected under §60-146). - Insurers: must obtain and surrender titles or notify the department if owners retain vehicles, report electronically when required, and may apply to the department for a salvage brand without an endorsed title after 30 days if they submit a prescribed affidavit documenting attempts to obtain the title. No appropriations, funding, or budgetary changes are included.Adds definitions and deeming rules: "consumer care" is defined by reference to section 60-1401.10. A vehicle may be deemed "structurally totaled" by a facility performing consumer care or by the insurer that covered the vehicle when damaged. "Structurally totaled" is specified to mean totaled because of a kink/crease in a frame rail, unibody, or structural component (including engine cradle or rear differential). Exclusions: total loss due solely to hail/cosmetic damage, or where repair cost does not exceed 75% of the vehicle's actual cash value. 109-1-LB123_FinalLB123_Final_Copy.docxLB123 amends procedures enforced by the Auditor of Public Accounts and the State Treasurer. Governmental units must submit calculated restricted funds authority with budget filings; the Auditor notifies the governing body and the State Treasurer of budget-limit noncompliance. The State Treasurer must suspend state aid to noncompliant units, hold funds for six months (returned if compliance occurs), and after six months forfeit and redistribute funds to other county recipients or to the Highway Allocation Fund (homestead exemption reimbursements to the General Fund). Forfeiture continues until Auditor confirms compliance; failure to comply for 12 months renders the subdivision ineligible for future state aid until compliance. For municipalities that fail to file required annual audits, the Auditor notifies the State Treasurer, who withholds distributions under sections 39-2511–39-2520 and redistributes withheld funds after six months; 12‑month noncompliance bars future distributions until remedied. Original sections are repealed.Agencies mentioned: the Auditor of Public Accounts and the State Treasurer. 109-1-LB127_IntroLB127_Intro_Copy.docxLB127 expands remedies for persons against whom criminal charges are dismissed, result in acquittal, or whose convictions are overturned by adding statutory damages and procedural rules. 109-1-LB130_IntroLB130_Intro_Copy.docxLB130 amends §77-4602 to revise reporting and automatic transfer rules tied to General Fund net receipts. It directs the Tax Commissioner (within 15 days after each month and fiscal year) to publish comparisons using forecasts from the Nebraska Economic Forecasting Advisory Board and, after each fiscal year, to calculate: (i) actual minus estimated General Fund net receipts and (ii) fifty percent of a growth-based formula. If (i) is positive, the Tax Commissioner must certify the larger amount to the Director of Administrative Services. Upon that certification, the State Treasurer transfers the certified sum from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund—an amount equal to (i) immediately and any remainder by the end of the next fiscal year. Transfers are reduced if they would push the Cash Reserve Fund above 16% of budgeted General Fund expenditures; the Legislature may authorize exceeding 16%. The Director of Administrative Services, Tax Commissioner, State Treasurer, and the Forecasting Advisory Board are implicated. The bill takes effect immediately.The added text assigns the Tax Commissioner responsibility to calculate, within 15 days after each fiscal year, two measures of excess General Fund net receipts: (i) actual minus certified estimated receipts (per §§77-4601, 77-4603) and (ii) 50% of a growth-based formula comparing the most recent annual receipt increase to the 20-year average (excluding the lowest year). If (i) is positive, the Tax Commissioner must certify the larger amount to the Director of Administrative Services, who triggers the State Treasurer to transfer that certified sum from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund. Transfers are split: an amount equal to (i) immediately and any remainder by the end of the following fiscal year, but reduced if the transfer would push the Cash Reserve Fund above 16% of budgeted General Fund expenditures (unless the Legislature authorizes exceeding 16% for specific needs).
