For FY2026-27 it provides $30,921 from the General Fund and $28,236 from the Nebraska State Patrol Cash Fund. Expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from these appropriations are capped at $33,856 for FY2025-26 and $34,872 for FY2026-27.Appropriates to the Nebraska State Patrol (Program 100) funds to implement Legislative Bill 148 (109th Legislature, 1st Sess., 2025): FY2025‑26 — $29,629 General Fund and $28,236 from the Nebraska State Patrol Cash Fund; FY2026‑27 — $30,921 General Fund and $28,236 Cash Fund. Limits permanent/temporary salary and per diem expenditures from these appropriations to $33,856 for FY2025‑26 and $34,872 for FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB148_FinalLB148_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB148 amends section 38-131 to add subsection (6) specifying that, for purposes of interpretation by the FBI, the term "department" in that section means the Division of Public Health of the Department of Health and Human Services. No provisions in the bill explicitly allocate funds, appropriate monies, or change budgetary amounts for the Department of Health and Human Services.For the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): - DHHS would serve as (or work with) the State Licensing Authority to implement the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact: enforce state licensure rules, investigate and report adverse actions, monitor the Compact Data System, and issue or revoke compact privileges under state law. - The Compact requires DHHS to share licensure, disciplinary, and investigative information and to comply with Commission rules and reporting duties. - Fiscal provisions create a multistate Commission that can set a budget, charge licensees fees, accept grants/donations, and levy annual assessments on Participating States — meaning DHHS/the state could face assessments or administrative costs, and remain liable for obligations if the state joins. - No specific appropriation, state funding increase, or earmarked budget allocation to DHHS is included in the added text.
109-1-LB149_IntroLB149_Intro_Copy.docxLB149 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§79-263, 79-265, and 79-267, repeals the originals, and outright repeals §79-265.01. It removes the statutory prohibition on suspending students in pre-K through grade two (harmonizing student-discipline provisions), clarifies that principals may impose short-term suspensions (up to five school days) and restates grounds for long-term suspension, expulsion, or reassignment. School districts must continue annually to report to the State Department of Education an assurance that the district has the required one-year firearm-expulsion policy and provide details of any expulsions under that policy. Superintendents and local school boards retain authority to modify expulsions on an individual basis. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The added text consists only of the words "Each The The." It does not reference any government agency or department, nor does it include any funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB14_IntroLB14_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureThe bill repeatedly references the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA): “eligible breakfast” and “eligible lunch” are defined as meals reimbursable under USDA regulations implementing the Child Nutrition Act and the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act; the “federal reimbursement rate” is defined as the payment levels published by the USDA (as of Jan 1, 2023); and the “identified student percentage” is determined under USDA regulations for high‑poverty schools. State reimbursements to schools are calculated using those USDA federal reimbursement rates (e.g., the state pays the difference between USDA free and fully paid rates for fully paid meals). The Legislature also states its intent to appropriate General Fund money to implement the Hunger‑Free Schools Act.No direct changes to the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) or its funding are made. The bill repeatedly adopts USDA definitions, regulations, and the federally published "federal reimbursement rate" (per the Child Nutrition Act and National School Lunch Act) as the basis for state calculations. The new Hunger‑Free Schools Program is administered by the State Department of Education, which will reimburse qualified schools (per formulas tied to USDA reimbursement rates and fixed per‑meal supplements) to allow universal no‑cost school breakfasts and lunches. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate General Fund dollars to carry out the act. In short: USDA roles remain definitional and regulatory only; no USDA appropriation or program changes are created.
109-1-LB150A_FinalLB150A_Final_Copy.docxLB150A appropriates federal funds to the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice (Program 155) to implement Legislative Bill 150. It provides $146,056 in FY2025‑26 and $147,609 in FY2026‑27. Of those amounts, total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $97,078 for FY2025‑26 and $101,932 for FY2026‑27.Appropriates federal funds to the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice (Program 155) to implement Legislative Bill 150: $146,056 for FY2025-26 and $147,609 for FY2026-27. Specifies that total expenditures from these funds for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems shall not exceed $97,078 (FY2025-26) and $101,932 (FY2026-27).
109-1-LB150_FinalLB150_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and Finance, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue, Department of TransportationThe bill centralizes parole and reentry authority in the Department of Correctional Services (DOC), abolishing the Division of Parole Supervision and its director and reallocating duties to the DOC and Director of Correctional Services. DOC must administer parole services, supervise parole officers, develop risk/needs assessments and training, operate a pilot residential program for technical violations, expand reentry planning and lifetime community‑supervision procedures, and partner with probation on statewide community correctional/reentry facilities. By July 1, 2026 DOC must adopt a private‑provider procurement plan; the Reentry Continuity Advisory Board reports annually (first due Oct. 1, 2025). Key fiscal changes: intent to appropriate $1,000,000 GF for Community Work Release and Reentry Centers and a $25/month parole programming fee credited to a Parole Program Cash Fund that DOC may use and invest. Department of Banking and Finance must maintain/process service‑of‑process filings and is granted immunity. DHHS gains data access, licensing/EMPC certificate authority, maintenance of firearm‑disability/NICS data, and limits on overdose‑review disclosures; labs must forward paternity testing audits to DHHS. Department of Transportation must verify tourist‑oriented sign applicants’ anti‑discrimination compliance. Department of Revenue employees are excluded from the law‑enforcement definition under §77‑366.- Department of Banking and Finance: Adds definitions and service rules for garnishment on corporate entities—defines "corporate entity," permits service under section 25-509.01 or by mutual agreement, requires sending a copy to the registered agent's location if not served there, and states proof of that mailing is not required to continue a garnishment. - Department of Correctional Services: Authorizes temporary placement of certain individuals (non‑convicted sex offenders excluded) in jails or DCS facilities under the new Regional Mental Health Expansion Pilot Program until appropriate medical facilities are available; explicitly permits videoconferenced mental‑health board hearings; references DCS custody/record obligations related to parole and community supervision. - Department of Health and Human Services: Adds/clarifies the use and definition of videoconferencing for hearings and references medical facility placement interplay with jails/DCS under the pilot. - Department of Revenue and Department of Transportation: No substantive additions affecting these agencies identified. - Funding: Commission must identify grant/federal funding for the Regional Mental Health Expansion Pilot Program; no specific appropriations or budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB151_IntroLB151_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB151 assigns the Department of Revenue (department) administrative duties for the new First‑Time Homebuyers Savings Account Act. The department must provide forms for account designation and beneficiary designation, annual reports, and transaction reports; adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the Act; and receive annual reports, IRS Form 1099s, and transaction reports from account holders. The department is directed to collect statutory penalties (10% on certain withdrawals) and remit them to the State Treasurer for constitutionally prescribed distribution. The bill expressly relieves financial institutions of duties to report or verify account use. No appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included in the bill.Department of Revenue responsibilities: adopt rules and create forms to implement the First‑Time Homebuyer Savings Account program (account designation, beneficiary designation, annual report, transaction report). Account designations and beneficiary designations must be submitted on department forms by the individual income tax filing deadline; annual reports and any IRS Form 1099 must be included with the Nebraska income tax return; transaction reports are required on withdrawals. The Department will collect 10% penalties on nonqualified withdrawals and remit those penalties to the State Treasurer for constitutional distribution. Financial institutions are explicitly not required to verify, label, report, or administer accounts for the Department. No explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included.
109-1-LB152_IntroLB152_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB152 amends the Property Tax Credit Act (77-4212) to tie future minimum relief amounts to changes in statewide assessed value as determined by the Department of Revenue. For tax year 2029 the minimum relief equals the prior year minimum plus the percentage increase in total assessed value of all real property (as determined by the Department of Revenue) plus an additional $75 million. For tax year 2030 and thereafter the minimum equals the prior year minimum plus the percentage increase in total assessed value as determined by the Department of Revenue.Summary (Department of Revenue focus): The added language declares legislative intent to expand the homestead exemption and, effective January 1, 2026, exempts the first $100,000 of actual value of every homestead from property taxation. Existing exemptions in sections 77‑3506, 77‑3507, and 77‑3508 remain available in addition to this new exemption. For the Department of Revenue, this requires implementing the new $100,000 exemption in assessment and exemption processes, issuing guidance, and adjusting administration and revenue forecasting. No explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included in the added text.
109-1-LB153_IntroLB153_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB153 requires the Department of Health and Human Services to take multiple federal actions and implement coverage changes under the Medical Assistance Act. Key department obligations: - Submit a state plan amendment (SPA) to CMS to extend postpartum Medicaid coverage from 60 days to at least six months (may seek 12 months) (by Oct 1, 2023). - Submit an SPA to CMS to provide at least six months postpartum coverage under the Children's Health Insurance Program for mothers of unborn-child-option children (by Oct 1, 2025); funding is intended from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund. - Submit a Medicaid waiver or SPA to designate two medical-respite facilities for homeless adults in the expansion population (by Oct 1, 2025); services funded by the same fund. - Implement coverage deadlines for continuous glucose monitors, electric personal-use breast pumps, lactation visits, and translation/interpretation services; several of these are to be funded from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund. The bill amends the fund statute to explicitly permit use for CHIP postpartum coverage and lists fund mechanics (source, first use to offset losses, and investment earning treatment).Department of Health and Human Services must, by October 1, 2025, seek CMS approval via a CHIP state plan amendment to obtain federal matching funds to provide at least six months of postpartum coverage for mothers whose child is enrolled under the unborn child option. Covered services must match the comprehensive postpartum services provided under Medicaid; the department may pursue a 12‑month option. The Legislature intends to fund these services from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (section 68‑996). No specific appropriation amounts are specified.
109-1-LB154_IntroLB154_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill revises the Hearing Instrument Specialists Practice Act and related Audiology and Speech‑Language Pathology provisions. It makes the Department (the state licensing department) the agency that issues and renews hearing‑instrument specialist and temporary training licenses, receives annual filings from organizations that employ licensed specialists, and retains practitioner records for seven years. It clarifies that audiologists credentialed by the State Department of Education and licensed audiologists are exempt from separate hearing‑instrument licensure in certain circumstances. The Hearing Instrument Specialists Board (five professionals, one public member) is adjusted in composition and makes licensure recommendations to the Department, including examination and training standards. The Board must consult the Board of Medicine and Surgery when adopting cerumen‑removal course requirements. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Added provisions give the state "department" (the licensing/health department) and the relevant licensing "board" expanded administrative roles: organizations employing licensed hearing instrument specialists must annually file lists and compliance statements on department forms; the department, with the board's recommendation, will determine eligibility for examinations, may waive exam components, approve/accept foreign training, prescribe forms (including receipts) and require seven-year record retention. The board must consult the Board of Medicine and Surgery before adopting rules for initial cerumen‑removal courses. Private certifying bodies (International Hearing Society, National Board for Certification in Hearing Instrument Sciences) are referenced for credentialing. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB155_IntroLB155_Intro_Copy.docxLB155 amends Neb. Rev. Statutes §§28‑1406, 28‑1409, and 28‑1410 (use of force/justification). It clarifies definitions and the scope of who is an "actor" (excluding duly authorized law enforcement officers) and defines "public officer" as any elected or appointed officer or employee of the State of Nebraska or its political subdivisions (excluding law enforcement). The bill explicitly states there is no duty to retreat before using deadly force when lawfully present in a motor vehicle and harmonizes related retreat provisions for dwellings, workplaces, and motor vehicles. It also references peace officers and persons assisting public officers in enforcement contexts. Original sections are repealed. No funding, appropriations, or budgetary changes are included.Added language clarifies that "actor" does not include any duly authorized law enforcement officer of the State of Nebraska or its political subdivisions. It also references "motor vehicle" as defined in section 28-109 and adds definitions and no‑retreat rules concerning unlawful force and presence in motor vehicles. No state agencies, departments beyond Nebraska law enforcement or political subdivisions are newly created or altered, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocations in the added text.
109-1-LB156_IntroLB156_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB156 amends the State Tort Claims Act (section 81-8,219) to create a specific exception concerning the Department of Health and Human Services. While misrepresentation or deceit claims generally remain excluded, the bill provides that, in adoption or placement cases, the State Tort Claims Act does apply to claims against DHHS for misrepresentation or deceit in failing to warn, notify, or inform about a ward’s mental and behavioral health history, educational history, and medical history, including any history as a victim or perpetrator of sexual abuse. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DHHS are included.Added language defines covered offenses as those arising from a sexual assault of a child that occurred: (i) on school grounds; (ii) in a vehicle owned, leased, or contracted by a school and used for a school purpose; (iii) in a vehicle being driven for a school purpose by a school employee or designee; or (iv) at a school‑sponsored activity or athletic event. There is no mention of the Department of Health and Human Services, nor are there any funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes affecting DHHS.
109-1-LB157_IntroLB157_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Revenue- Sec. 2 defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue. - Sec. 3(3): Beginning for taxable years on/after Jan. 1, 2027, the Department must adjust the Child Tax Credit amounts, phase‑out thresholds, and reduction increments for inflation using the same percentage used to adjust individual income tax brackets under section 77‑2715.03. - Sec. 4: Beginning in 2027, the Department must submit an annual report to the Legislature on Child Tax Credit usage by July 15 each year. - Sec. 5 grants the Department rulemaking authority to implement the Act. - Sec. 7(7)(d) authorizes the Department of Revenue to recapture a $5,000 home‑purchase tax credit if the residence is sold or ceases to be the claimant's primary residence within five years. - No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns it administration duties: beginning tax year 2027 the Department must inflation‑adjust the child tax credit amount, the income thresholds where the credit phases down, and the phase‑down increments using the same percentage applied to individual income tax brackets (section 77‑2715.03). The Department must submit an annual report on credit usage to the Legislature by July 15 each year and may adopt rules and regulations to implement the Act. No explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department are included.
109-1-LB158_IntroLB158_Intro_Copy.docxLB158 requires health carriers and pharmacy benefit managers (as defined in Neb. Rev. Stat. §44-1303 and §44-4603) to count amounts paid by a plan enrollee or paid on the enrollee’s behalf toward the enrollee’s overall contribution to any out-of-pocket maximum or other cost‑sharing requirement for health benefit plans issued, amended, extended, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026. An exception preserves health savings account (HSA) eligibility under federal tax law: the rule applies only after the enrollee meets the IRC §223 minimum deductible, except that preventive care per IRC §223(c)(2)(C) counts immediately. No appropriation, funding change, or budget allocation is included.Adds definitions and requires that for health plans entered, amended, extended, or renewed on/after Jan. 1, 2026, health carriers and pharmacy benefit managers must count any amount an enrollee (or someone paying on their behalf) pays toward the enrollee’s out‑of‑pocket maximums and other cost‑sharing. It preserves HSA/HDHP rules: this counting won’t apply if it would make an HSA ineligible under IRC §223 until the plan deductible minimum is met, except preventive services under IRC §223(c)(2)(C) are counted regardless. References state code definitions (§44‑1303, §44‑4603) and the Internal Revenue Code; no agencies are newly created and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB159_IntroLB159_Intro_Copy.docxLB159 (Introduced by Guereca; Judiciary Committee) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29-2260 to require sentencing courts, when deciding whether to withhold imprisonment for non‑mandatory misdemeanor or felony convictions, to consider an offender’s status as a victim of abuse or human trafficking as a mitigating factor to be accorded weight in favor of withholding sentence. The bill retains existing statutory guidance on juvenile adjudications under section 43-247 and application of the Nebraska Juvenile Code. No state agencies or departments beyond the courts and juvenile system are newly directed to act, and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB15_IntroLB15_Intro_Copy.docxLB15 states the Legislature's intent to provide additional General Fund appropriations to the Nebraska Supreme Court. Specifically, it calls for an extra $600,000 in FY2025‑26 and an extra $600,000 in FY2026‑27 to the Supreme Court (Agency 5), Court Administration, Program No. 34. These funds are restricted for increased payments for interpreter services for deaf and hard of hearing persons and for persons unable to communicate in English. The bill includes an emergency clause making it effective upon enactment.Legislature intends to appropriate an additional $600,000 General Fund for FY2025‑26 and an additional $600,000 General Fund for FY2026‑27 to the Supreme Court (Agency 5), Court Administration (Program No. 34). The funds are designated to increase payments for interpreter services for deaf and hard of hearing persons and for individuals unable to communicate in English, and must be used solely for that purpose.
109-1-LB160_FinalLB160_Final_Copy.docxLB160 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §71-216.01 governing barber licensure examination procedures administered by the state licensing board (the "board"). Under the bill, an applicant who fails the barber exam may retake it up to two additional times without further schooling; a third failure triggers a required additional 500‑hour course of study in a barbering school (maximum ten hours per working day). After completing 250 hours, an applicant may seek board approval to demonstrate proficiency and waive the remaining hours; if the applicant then fails, they must finish the remaining 250 hours before a fifth exam attempt. The bill was handled by the Legislature’s Health and Human Services Committee. No funding, appropriation, or other budget changes are included.Adds procedures for applicants to the barbering licensing board: applicants may retake the board exam two additional times without further coursework; after a third failure they must complete 500 additional barbering school hours (maximum 10 hours per day) before reexam. After 250 hours, the applicant may request board-approved proficiency testing to waive the remaining 250 hours; if they fail the exam after that waiver opportunity, they must finish the remaining 250 hours before a fifth exam attempt. No agencies beyond "the board" are referenced and no funding or appropriations are changed.
109-1-LB161_IntroLB161_Intro_Copy.docxLB161 amends section 79-1003 of the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act, updating statutory definitions used to calculate state aid. Key agencies/departments referenced: the State Department of Education (defined as "Department"), the State Board of Education, the School Employees Retirement System of the State of Nebraska, the Class V School Employees Retirement Act retirement system, and the Clerk of the Legislature (for lobbyist reporting). The substantive change revises the "formula students" computation to explicitly include one hundred percent of qualified early childhood education fall membership and average daily membership in aid calculations. No direct appropriations or dollar funding changes are contained; the amendment affects aid and budget allocation mechanics by altering the student-count basis used in state aid and general fund operating expenditure calculations. The bill repeals the original section.The added text consists only of the repeated words "one hundred one hundred." It does not reference any government agencies, departments, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations, and therefore makes no substantive changes to agency responsibilities or fiscal provisions.
109-1-LB162_IntroLB162_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the Child Care Safety and Security Act and the Child Care Safety and Security Fund, administered by the State Department of Education (SDE). The fund consists of money transferred by the Legislature and is invested by the state investment officer under existing state investment law. Subject to available appropriations, SDE competitively awards grants to educational service units to fund designated public entities (designees—e.g., school districts, cities/villages, local public health, law enforcement, early childhood support agencies, local emergency management) for emergency response notification systems, training, and safety/reunification materials. Grant limits: funding for each designee activity (notification system, distribution of materials, training) shall not exceed $1,000 per year. Educational service units must use memoranda of understanding with designees. SDE must submit an annual electronic report to the Clerk of the Legislature. The State Board of Education may adopt rules to implement the Act.Creates the Child Care Safety and Security Fund, administered by the State Department of Education (SDE) and funded by money transferred by the Legislature; the state investment officer will invest fund balances under existing state investment law. Subject to appropriations, SDE competitively awards grants to educational service units on behalf of "designees" (public school districts, cities/villages, local public health, law enforcement, early childhood support agencies, or local emergency management agencies) for emergency notification systems, training, and reunification/safety materials. Educational service units must enter MOUs with designees to qualify. Grant limits: up to $1,000 per designee per listed activity (notification administration, materials distribution, and training). SDE must file an annual December 1 electronic report to the Clerk of the Legislature (aggregate grant usage and denials); the State Board of Education may adopt rules to implement the Act.
109-1-LB163_IntroLB163_Intro_Copy.docxLB163 creates a new state Office of Climate Action and directs it to carry out specified duties and meet statutory deadlines; the bill also includes a defined term (not shown in the excerpt). No other state agencies or departments are named in the provided text. The excerpt contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB164_IntroLB164_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Economic Development and makes the department the administering agency for the Urban Development Incentive Act. The department must review applications in receipt order, award grants for affordable commercial-space projects (with a per-project maximum of $3.5 million) and administer annual category caps: up to $20M (20% of project costs), $10M (10%), $5M (down payment), $2.5M (job training), $2M (public engagement), $4M (sustainability), and $3M (technical assistance). The department must electronically report annually to the Governor and Legislature (grant totals, project types, jobs created) and may adopt rules and regulations. The Legislature intends to appropriate $46.5 million annually from the General Fund to the department.Defines "Department" as the Department of Economic Development and tasks it with administering the Urban Development Incentive Act: accepting applications on department forms, reviewing them in receipt order, awarding grants (with a $3.5 million per-project cap) across specified categories (up to 20% of project costs; financing assistance up to 10%; down‑payment aid; job training; community engagement; sustainability; technical assistance) and annual category caps: $20M, $10M, $5M, $2.5M, $2M, $4M, and $3M respectively. The department must electronically report annually to the Governor and Legislature (grant totals, project types, jobs created) and may adopt rules to implement the Act. The Legislature intends to appropriate $46,500,000 annually from the General Fund to the department to carry out the program.
109-1-LB165_IntroLB165_Intro_Copy.docxLB165 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§28-441 and 28-442 to authorize syringe services programs and to create narrow exceptions to drug‑paraphernalia penalties under the Uniform Controlled Substances Act. The exceptions cover program operators, staff, volunteers, and participants engaged in retrieval or disposal of syringes, needles, or related equipment at or immediately adjacent to program sites. The bill retains a Class II misdemeanor penalty for violations of the amended section. No state agency or department is named in the provided text, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation provisions. The bill also repeals the original versions of the amended sections.Adds that a program participant is covered (i.e., treated as part of the program) when the participant is retrieving or disposing of syringes, needles, or related equipment at or immediately around the program site. No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes in this text.
109-1-LB166_FinalLB166_Final_Copy.docxBill LB166 amends public‑records and candidate‑filing statutes. It requires the county treasurer (in addition to county assessors and registers of deeds) to withhold residential addresses of judges, law‑enforcement officers, and certain Nebraska National Guard members who apply, with five‑year renewals. It makes written retention requests by judicial officeholders filed with the Secretary of State nonpublic under section 84‑712.01 and otherwise exempt from disclosure, while requiring the Secretary of State to electronically publish a list of names and respective districts/areas seeking retention. It clarifies candidate filing form contents and confirms filing officers: Secretary of State for multi‑county/state offices and election commissioners or county clerks for county, city, and most school‑district filings. No funding or appropriation changes.Requires the Secretary of State to treat any written request filed with the office as non‑public under Neb. Rev. Stat. §84‑712.01 and exempt from disclosure under §§84‑712 to 84‑712.09 and other law. The sole exception is that the Secretary of State must electronically publish an annual list of judicial officeholders who filed for retention that calendar year, showing each name and the district or area served. No agencies beyond the Secretary of State (and the referenced judicial officeholders) are tasked with duties, and no funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB167_FinalLB167_Final_Copy.docxLB167 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-1566 to extend the termination date of the Nebraska Litter Reduction and Recycling Act from September 30, 2025, to September 30, 2030. It directs "the department" named in the statute to review and evaluate achievement of the act’s purposes and the need for continuation, with that review completed at least six months before the termination date. The bill repeals the original section and contains an emergency clause, making it effective on passage. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The underlined addition is simply the numeral "2030." It does not name or alter any government agency or department, nor does it include any funding, appropriation, or budget allocation language. No fiscal impact or agency responsibilities are specified.
109-1-LB168_FinalLB168_Final_Copy.docxLB168 enacts the "340B Contract Pharmacy Protection Act," prohibiting manufacturers, their agents/affiliates, and third‑party logistics providers from denying, restricting, or conditioning delivery/acquisition of 340B drugs to locations authorized by 340B entities, or from requiring data beyond what federal law mandates. Enforcement: the Nebraska Attorney General or any county attorney may sue in the name of the State of Nebraska for injunctions or other relief to prevent violations. The bill includes severability and an emergency clause making it effective on enactment. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Creates the "340B Contract Pharmacy Protection Act," defining "340B drug," "340B entity," and "Manufacturer." It bars manufacturers, their agents/affiliates, and third‑party logistics providers from denying, restricting, or conditioning supply or delivery of 340B drugs to locations authorized by 340B entities, and from requiring submission of claims, utilization, purchasing, or other data as a condition for access unless federal law requires it. Enforcement authority is vested in the Nebraska Attorney General and county attorneys, who may sue in the name of the State for injunctions or other relief. The provision defers to federal law where applicable. No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB169A_IntroLB169A_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill appropriates General Fund amounts to the Department of Revenue, Program 102: $278,900 for FY2025-26 and $262,100 for FY2026-27 to assist with implementation of Legislative Bill 169. Expenditures from these appropriated funds for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are limited to no more than $190,900 in FY2025-26 and $197,000 in FY2026-27. The act takes effect immediately upon enactment.Appropriates General Fund: $278,900 for FY2025-26 and $262,100 for FY2026-27 to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to implement Legislative Bill 169 (109th Legislature, 2025). Caps permanent and temporary salaries and per diems at $190,900 for FY2025-26 and $197,000 for FY2026-27.
109-1-LB169_IntroLB169_Intro_Copy.docxLB169 amends Nebraska tax law and reporting requirements. Key agency provisions: - Department of Revenue: expands the Tax Expenditure Reporting Act to require reporting of revenue loss from failing to tax services purchased for nonbusiness use and to list specified sales-and-use tax expenditures by category. - Nebraska Investment Finance Authority, State Racing and Gaming Commission, and Nebraska State Fair Board are explicitly listed among entities referenced in the sales-and-use tax expenditure categories. - Political subdivisions and electric cooperatives are addressed regarding exclusions for certain utility-related services. - Mechanical Amusement Device Tax Act: clarifies the state occupation tax is in addition to state sales and use taxes on mechanical amusement device gross receipts and prohibits political subdivisions from imposing additional mechanical-device taxes other than local option sales and use taxes. Operative date: October 1, 2025. No direct appropriations or new funding allocations are specified.Added text enumerates a broad set of service receipts (chartered flights; clothing cleaning except amounts exempt under §77‑2704.14; dating; hair care except cutting; interior design; lobbying; chartered local passenger transportation; marketing/telemarketing; massage; nail care; dance/golf/tennis instruction; ground sightseeing; skin care; pool cleaning/maintenance; tattoo/body modification; telefloral delivery; travel agency; weight‑loss services) and expressly includes state sales and use tax on gross receipts from operation of mechanical amusement devices (excluding local option sales/use taxes). No government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB16_IntroLB16_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Military DepartmentLB16 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81‑1021 to clarify exceptions to the State motor‑vehicle lettering requirement. It exempts vehicles of the Department of Correctional Services and the Department of Health and Human Services when used to apprehend or return escaped offenders or parole violators, and when transporting DOC offenders and personnel or DHHS patients and personnel engaged in off‑campus program activities. The bill also exempts vehicles of the Military Department. No funding, appropriations, or budgetary changes for these agencies are included.No added provisions directly reference the Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, or the Military Department, nor do they appropriate funds to those agencies. The amendments create the Nebraska Consumable Hemp Control Commission, establish license/fee structures, an excise tax remitted to the General Fund, and a Nebraska Consumable Hemp Control Commission Cash Fund (funds may be used for commission administration and may be transferred to the General Fund). No specific budget allocations or appropriations to DOC, DHHS, or the Military Department are included.
109-1-LB170A_IntroLB170A_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of RevenueThe bill directs the State Treasurer to transfer $100,000,000 from the General Fund to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund in FY2025‑26 and another $100,000,000 in FY2026‑27, with transfer dates and amounts to be set by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services. It appropriates $100,000,000 (FY2025‑26) and $100,000,000 (FY2026‑27) from that Fund to the Department of Revenue, Program 121, for implementation of LB170. Each year’s appropriation is Cash Funds designated solely for state aid and may not be used for permanent/temporary employee salaries or per diems.- Department of Administrative Services (DAS): The budget administrator in DAS’s budget division is authorized to direct the timing and amounts of two transfers from the General Fund to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund — $100,000,000 to be transferred during FY2025-26 and $100,000,000 during FY2026-27. - Department of Revenue: The bill appropriates $100,000,000 from the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund to the Department of Revenue (Program 121) for each of FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 to implement Legislative Bill 170 (2025). Each appropriation is designated as $100,000,000 Cash Funds for state aid only. These funds may not be used for permanent/temporary salaries or per diems of state employees.
109-1-LB170_IntroLB170_Intro_Copy.docxLB170 (Revenue Committee) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-2704.24 to eliminate the sales and use tax exemptions for candy and soft drinks. The bill redefines key terms (including candy, soft drinks, food and food ingredients, prepared food, dietary supplement, and food sold through vending machines) and harmonizes related provisions. Prepared-food exceptions (e.g., bakery items, certain raw animal foods, manufacturing classifications) remain specified. The bill becomes operative October 1, 2025, and repeals the original section. No state agencies or departments are expressly named in the text, and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds definitional language for "candy" and "soft drinks." - Candy: preparations of sugar, honey, or other natural/artificial sweeteners combined with chocolate, fruits, nuts, or flavorings in bars, drops, or pieces; excludes products that contain flour or require refrigeration. - Soft drinks: nonalcoholic beverages containing natural or artificial sweeteners; excludes beverages with milk/milk substitutes (soy, rice) or those that are more than 50% vegetable/fruit juice. No government agencies, departments, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned or changed.
109-1-LB171_IntroLB171_Intro_Copy.docxLB171 amends Nebraska individual and corporate income tax statutes and assigns administrative duties to the Tax Commissioner. Key agency references: - Nebraska Tax Commissioner: directed to update and publish tax rate schedules and tables, adjust individual tax brackets for inflation using specified methods, and prescribe new schedules when brackets or rates change. - U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics: CPI data specified for inflation adjustments. - Internal Revenue Code (section 1(f)) referenced for historical adjustment methodology. Substantive changes: phased reductions in higher individual income tax rates, culminating in a 4.99% top individual rate for taxable years beginning on or after Jan. 1, 2026; corporate income tax set at 4.99% on all taxable income effective Jan. 1, 2026. Original sections are repealed. No direct funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds repeated text strings reading "and 4.99%" (one instance rendered as "and 4.99"). No government agencies or departments are referenced and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are affected or specified.
109-1-LB172_IntroLB172_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill directs the Department of Correctional Services (DCS) to order mental‑health evaluations to determine "dangerous sex‑offender" status for specified sexual‑offense convictions, with evaluations ordered at least 180 days before scheduled release and written findings provided by 150 days before release. Failure or refusal to participate in or complete sex‑offender treatment offered by DCS or the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) while incarcerated may trigger such evaluation; inability to complete treatment due to time constraints or unavailable programming is explicitly not treated as refusal. Victims under 18 must report sexual assault to DHHS, and confidentiality exceptions allow sharing victim identity/information with DHHS for child abuse/neglect investigations. The Attorney General’s Child Protection Division may investigate or prosecute upon written DHHS request if a county attorney declines. No appropriations or budget allocations for DCS or DHHS are included.Added provisions expand and clarify child‑pornography offenses and definitions: they list covered statutes, define terms (electronic communication device, sexually explicit conduct, visual depiction, and “indistinguishable”), set affirmative defenses, and create age‑based and repeat‑offender sentencing tiers (under 19 = Class III felony; 19+ = Class ID; prior covered‑offense conviction = Class IC). The text also cross‑references the Child Pornography Prevention Act and related sections. There are no funding, appropriation, or explicit administrative changes naming the Department of Correctional Services or the Department of Health and Human Services; DOC would implement any new sentences under existing authority, and DHHS is not assigned duties or budget changes.
109-1-LB173_IntroLB173_Intro_Copy.docxLB173 (109th Legislature, 1st Session, 2025), introduced by Senators Prokop (27), Dover (19), and Quick (35) and referred to the Appropriations Committee, is an appropriations bill expressing state intent regarding aid to community colleges and includes an emergency clause to take effect immediately. The provided text contains no specific funding amounts, appropriations, budget allocations, or named state agencies or departments charged with administering the aid.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB174_IntroLB174_Intro_Copy.docxLB174 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25‑1558 (wage garnishment). It preserves existing garnishment limits for most creditors (generally the lesser of 25% of disposable earnings, the amount exceeding 30× the federal minimum hourly wage, or 15% for a head of family) and court exceptions for support orders, Chapter 13 bankruptcy, and tax debts. It creates a separate garnishment framework for medical debt sought by “medical debt buyers” or “medical creditors,” setting the maximum garnishable portion at the lesser of: 10% of disposable earnings, the 30× federal‑wage threshold, or 20% where the debtor is shown not to be a head of family by sworn affidavit. The bill adds statutory definitions (including medical debt, medical debt buyer/creditor, and health care services), directs the Commissioner of Labor to set equivalent rules for nonweekly pay periods, and repeals the original section. No state funding or appropriations are included.Adds caps and definitions for garnishment of wages for medical debt. Garnishment may not exceed the lesser of: (a) 10% of disposable weekly earnings; (b) the amount by which weekly disposable earnings exceed 30 times the federal minimum hourly wage (citing 29 U.S.C. 206(a)(1)); or (c) 20% of disposable earnings if the debtor is not head of household, as alleged by the creditor in a sworn affidavit. New definitions: “health care services,” “medical debt,” “medical debt buyer,” and “medical creditor.” The provision cites the federal minimum-wage statute (29 U.S.C. 206(a)(1), administered by the U.S. Department of Labor). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budgets are included.
109-1-LB175_IntroLB175_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB175 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §74-1335 to expressly include a railroad’s "successor in interest" and directs that any landowner with property on both sides of a railroad right-of-way may file a written complaint with the Department of Transportation if a crossing is inadequate or unsafe. The Department of Transportation must investigate, hold hearings, and issue necessary orders. The department may require overhead, underground, or grade crossings, wing fences, or relocation of existing crossings. For special crossings costing more than $1,500, the landowner must pay one-half of the expense amount exceeding $1,500. The bill contains no changes to DOT appropriations or budget allocations.Adds/clarifies a definition of “successor in interest” to include any agent, successor, assignee, trustee, receiver, or other person acquiring interests or rights in railroad land — explicitly including owners/holders of servient estates or rights of reversion. Also inserts repeated language to cover references to “its successor in interest.” No Department of Transportation programs, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned or changed.
109-1-LB176_IntroLB176_Intro_Copy.docxLB176 amends §86‑1304 of the Nebraska Broadband Bridge Act, updating application and project requirements overseen by the commission. Key agency-related provisions: - Applicants (providers, cooperatives, political subdivisions, Indian tribes) apply to the commission; political subdivision or tribal applicants must participate via a public‑private partnership with a provider. - Matching funds: 50% of development costs outside high‑cost areas, 25% inside; federal funds are exempt from matching. - Each county, city, and village in the project area must adopt a resolution of project support (must include project map, acknowledgment of permit applications, and proposed timeline). - The commission sets application deadlines and enforces an 18‑month completion target (with extension rules), repayment schedules for missed deadlines, and required one‑week speed tests; failure after remediation triggers grant repayment. - Grants are barred for projects using equipment on the FCC’s Covered List (Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau). No specific appropriations or new funding allocations are included.Adds an application requirement that the applicant submit a resolution of project support adopted by each county, city, and village where the project will be located. Each resolution must, at minimum, include: (a) a map of the proposed project area; (b) an acknowledgement that the applicant will apply for appropriate permits; and (c) a proposed project timeline. No state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are specified.
109-1-LB177A_FinalLB177A_Final_Copy.docxLB177A appropriates funds to the Nebraska State Patrol (Program 100) to implement Legislative Bill 177. For FY2025‑26 it provides $233,030 from the General Fund and $135,750 from the Nebraska State Patrol Cash Fund. No funds are appropriated for FY2026‑27. Expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from the appropriated funds are capped at $179,591 for FY2025‑26 and $0 for FY2026‑27.Appropriates funds to the Nebraska State Patrol (Program 100) to implement LB 177 for FY2025-26: $233,030 from the General Fund and $135,750 from the Nebraska State Patrol Cash Fund. No funds are appropriated for FY2026-27. Caps total expenditures from these appropriations for permanent/temporary salaries and per diems at $179,591 for FY2025-26 and $0 for FY2026-27.
109-1-LB177_FinalLB177_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB177 designates "Department" as the Department of Revenue and repeatedly authorizes the department to: conduct background checks (including fingerprinting and FBI criminal-history checks) of applicants and licensees for operator, distributor, and manufacturer cash-device licenses; require submission of a department personal history report; conduct investigations and facility inspections; and determine whether there is cause to deny, suspend, revoke, or terminate licenses. Applicants and licensees must pay background-check costs and any required fees as determined by the department. Operators and distributors must remit amounts withheld from winnings to the Department of Revenue to be credited against outstanding state tax liabilities. No appropriations, budget allocations, or other funding changes to the Department of Revenue are included.The added language authorizes the Department of Revenue to require fingerprinting and an FBI criminal history check (via the Nebraska State Patrol) of applicants and licensees for the covered license, both at application and on a biennial basis or "at any time." Applicants/licensees must submit a department personal history report and may be subject to background investigations and inspections of their facilities. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are stated.
109-1-LB178_IntroLB178_Intro_Copy.docxLB178 directs the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission to establish and approve mandatory server alcohol-training programs, issue certificates of completion, and maintain a list of certified persons. Beginning January 1, 2026, retail liquor licensees may employ staff who sell, serve, mix alcohol, provide security, or verify age only if certified (or become certified within 90 days); licensees must keep employee certificates on premises. The commission may charge enrollment fees (up to $30) and certification fees (up to $20); all fees are collected by the commission and remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission Rule and Regulation Cash Fund. The fund’s purposes are expanded to include administering these training provisions, and to cover administrative costs (including salary/benefits), electronic regulatory transactions, education, enforcement training, and equipment. The Legislature may direct transfers from the fund to the General Fund; investments handled by the state investment officer.Requires the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission to create and administer a mandatory server alcohol training and certification program (per section 6 and 53-117.03). The commission may charge an enrollment fee up to $30; fees are collected by the commission and remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission Rule and Regulation Cash Fund. Effective January 1, 2026, retail licensees may only employ persons who have completed (or obtain within 90 days of hire) the commission‑approved training and certification for roles involving sale/service/mixing of alcohol, security, or age verification. Licensees must keep employee certificates or proof of recent hire; violations can lead to suspension, cancellation, or revocation of the license by the commission.
109-1-LB179_FinalLB179_Final_Copy.docxLB179 amends two retirement statutes affecting cities of the first class. - Dept./agencies referenced: Police Officers Retirement System (employee accounts and Police Officers Retirement System Fund), retirement committee, city council, cities of the first class, Internal Revenue Service, and the retirement system’s unallocated employer account. - Police officers (sec. 16-1005): employee contribution rate increases from 7% to 9% of salary effective October 1, 2025. Cities of the first class “pick up” these contributions and treat them as employer contributions for federal tax purposes; withholding continues until IRS/federal rulings. Voluntary additional contributions remain allowed. - Firefighters (sec. 16-1027): optional benefit forms must include single lump-sum or one-or-more partial lump-sum distributions for retirees with retirement dates on or after Jan 1, 1997; retirement committee and city council retain roles in funding/annuity choices. If a firefighter’s retirement value cannot provide a required minimum pension, the city must use funds from the retirement system’s unallocated employer account. - Operative dates: firefighter changes and repeal of original 16-1027 effective Oct 1, 2025; other sections effective on their statutory effective dates.Adds that beginning October 1, 2025 police officers must contribute 9% of salary to the (public) retirement system. Also authorizes firefighters, upon retirement, to elect to receive their retirement value as a single lump sum or as one or more partial payments at chosen amounts/frequencies. No specific state agencies or budget appropriations are named and no direct funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB17_IntroLB17_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to restrict landlord fees and require disclosures related to tenant screening. Government entities and authorities referenced: - Consumer reporting agencies: landlords must provide copies of any consumer/tenant screening reports obtained, plus the name, address, and phone number of each consumer reporting agency that furnished a report, and notify tenants of their right to access and dispute information held by those agencies. - Attorney General: enforcement authority alongside private civil actions; violations are treated as violations of section 59-1602 (Consumer Protection Act). - State and federal credit reporting law references: the Credit Report Protection Act and federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (including cited FCRA provisions) are preserved for limiting rights/duties and liability. Civil penalties: landlords who knowingly violate the section may incur up to $300 per violation, plus court costs and reasonable attorney fees. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds comprehensive limits on landlord fees and new disclosure and enforcement rules. Key government-related items: - Requires landlords to provide prospective tenants any consumer or tenant background reports obtained and to identify the consumer reporting agency (name, address, phone). - Advises tenants of rights to access and dispute information with the consumer reporting/credit reporting agency and references the state Credit Report Protection Act and the federal Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. provisions cited). - Permits enforcement under the Consumer Protection Act by an aggrieved person or the Attorney General; knowing violations may incur civil penalties up to $300 per violation plus costs and attorney fees. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB180_FinalLB180_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Insurance, Department of TransportationLB180 amends section 73-813 to add explicit procurement exceptions. It exempts Department of Insurance contracts for financial or actuarial examinations; for rehabilitation, conservation, reorganization, or liquidation of licensees; and for professional services related to residual pools or excess funds under the agency's control from the requirements of sections 73-807, 73-815, 73-816, and 73-817. It also exempts Department of Transportation contracts for all road and bridge projects from those same procurement provisions. The bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.The added language references the Public Water and Natural Resources Project Contracting Act and explicitly covers Department of Natural Resources contracts for all water infrastructure projects. There is no mention of the Department of Insurance or the Department of Transportation, and the snippet contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for any agency.
109-1-LB181_IntroLB181_Intro_Copy.docxLB181 amends the Young Adult Bridge to Independence Act to (1) exempt program participation from lawful‑presence verification and (2) extend program eligibility to young adults not lawfully present in the United States. It directs the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to: submit a state plan amendment to seek federal Title IV‑E funding (deadline listed Oct. 1, 2023); submit a Medicaid state plan amendment to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) by Oct. 1, 2025 to provide Title XIX/XX (Medicaid/CHIP) coverage to program participants (including under‑21, not lawfully present); and adopt implementing rules by Oct. 1, 2025. DHHS must pursue other coverage options for uninsured participants, “including, but not limited to, payment from the General Fund.” The bill also repeals the original cited statutory sections. No specific appropriation amounts are included.Adds that young adults in the "bridge to independence" program (per the Young Adult Bridge to Independence Act) are eligible for medical care under federal Title XIX (Medicaid) or Title XXI (CHIP), regardless of lawful presence. If they are not eligible under those programs, "the department" must seek other coverage options, including payment from the state's General Fund. The department is required to submit a Medicaid state plan amendment to the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) by October 1, 2025 to provide medical assistance to participating young adults — including those under 21 who are not lawfully present.
109-1-LB182_FinalLB182_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThis bill designates the Department of Revenue as the administering agency for the Child Care Tax Credit Act and assigns several specific duties to the Department. It requires pass-through entities and taxpayers to notify the Department of Revenue at least 30 days before claiming allocated, transferred, sold, or assigned Nebraska affordable housing tax credits, providing the transferee’s tax identification number in the manner prescribed by the Department. The Department is authorized to declare Nebraska affordable housing tax credits disallowed or recaptured, which increases the claimant’s tax liability in the year of declaration. For the Child Care Tax Credit, the Department receives applications, approves and certifies credit amounts in receipt order (subject to a $2.5 million annual approval cap), and must limit use of DHHS verification data to administration of the Act.Summary (Department of Revenue focus): - Expands pass‑through rules for the Nebraska affordable housing tax credit, allowing allocation among partners/members/shareholders and permitting transfer, sale, or assignment of credits between taxpayers. - Requires any pass‑through entity or taxpayer that allocates, transfers, sells, or assigns a credit to notify the Department of Revenue at least 30 days before a return claiming the credit is filed, and to provide the transferee’s tax identification number in the manner prescribed by the Department. - Clarifies credits may offset income tax, certain insurance premium/retaliatory taxes, and franchise taxes; claiming such credits won’t trigger additional retaliatory tax and is treated as a tax payment for section 77‑2734.03(1). - Effective for taxable years beginning (or deemed to begin) on or after January 1, 2024. - No direct changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included.
109-1-LB183_FinalLB183_Final_Copy.docxLB183 amends the Uniform Disposition of Unclaimed Property Act. Key agency actions and fiscal provisions: - State Treasurer: continues publishing and mailing owner notices; must record holder reports and deposit unclaimed property receipts (including from §69‑1307.05) into the Unclaimed Property Trust Fund, pay claims and related expenses, and may deduct costs into a newly created Unclaimed Property Cash Fund. Both funds may be transferred to the General Fund at the Legislature’s direction. - Fiscal flows: on or before Nov. 1 annually, any Trust Fund balance over $1,000,000 is distributed to the permanent school fund. Money in the Cash Fund may be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. - Records/confidentiality: social security numbers, DOBs, and last-known addresses receive Department of Revenue–level confidentiality; Auditor of Public Accounts retains unrestricted access. Unclaimed property records may be withheld from public or shared with other states only on a reciprocal basis. - Finder rules: commercial/professional locators cannot charge fees until 24 months after publication/disclosure; professional finder fees capped at 10% with disclosure requirements to owners.The added language bars commercial or professional locators from charging fees in connection with property presumed abandoned. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes included.
109-1-LB184_IntroLB184_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill adds prohibitions and penalties related to nitrous oxide and assigns enforcement roles to existing agencies. It bars tobacco specialty stores and licensed tobacco retailers from selling or distributing nitrous oxide and prohibits sale of devices specifically designed for recreational inhalation. Violations carry misdemeanor penalties, license revocation/forfeiture by the courts, and seizure and destruction of contraband at the violator’s expense. Agencies mentioned/affected: - Cigarette Tax Division of the Nebraska Tax Commissioner: may revoke or suspend licenses for related violations and treat contraband cigarettes as subject to seizure and destruction. - Courts: authorized to order revocation/forfeiture of tobacco-related licenses. - U.S. Food and Drug Administration and federal foreign-trade-zone provisions are referenced for exclusions. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds prohibitions and penalties on sale, distribution, and transport of objects containing nitrous oxide: - Applies to holders of licenses under sections 28‑1420 to 28‑1429 (tobacco specialty stores): selling or allowing removal of nitrous oxide items is a Class II misdemeanor for a first offense, Class I for subsequent offenses, and courts may revoke and forfeit the license per section 28‑1429. - Delivery sales by licensed sellers are a Class I misdemeanor; common carriers who knowingly transport such items for violators are also guilty of a Class I misdemeanor. - Selling devices designed for recreational inhalation: Class III misdemeanor first offense, Class II thereafter. - Violations are deemed deceptive trade practices under the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act. All offending items are subject to seizure, forfeiture, destruction, with costs borne by the person from whom seized. - Exemptions: shipments to foreign trade zones per 19 U.S.C. §81a et seq., and government employees acting in official duties. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB185_FinalLB185_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB185 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (section 76-1410) to define "qualified third party" as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or a federally recognized Indian tribe that has an affiliation agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services to provide services to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault under the Protection from Domestic Abuse Act. No provisions in the bill change funding, appropriations, or budget allocations involving the Department of Health and Human Services.The underlined additions expand the definition of “writing/written” to expressly allow electronic delivery, storage, and presentation of landlord-tenant notices (including email and posted notices) if they meet Uniform Electronic Transactions Act standards; set detailed consent, hardware/software notice, verification/acknowledgment, withdrawal, and fallback-to-mail rules; and preserve federal E‑SIGN protections. There are no provisions in the added text that reference the Department of Health and Human Services, nor do they create or modify any DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB186_IntroLB186_Intro_Copy.docxLB186 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §53-123.17 (Nebraska Liquor Control Act) governing entertainment districts. Local governing bodies may designate or revoke districts and must file actions with the commission. The Nebraska Liquor Control Commission processes entertainment-district license applications, notifies the local clerk and provides an application copy. Eligible holders (retail, craft brewery, microdistillery, or manufacturer's licenses) may obtain annual entertainment-district licenses issued/renewed on the same schedule as underlying licenses. The bill imposes a $300 additional annual entertainment-district license fee payable to the local governing body’s clerk and explicitly authorizes local governing bodies to impose an occupation tax on entertainment-district businesses under section 53-132. Local governing bodies may cancel licenses for cause; canceled licensees may appeal to the commission under section 53-134. An emergency clause is included.Adds definitions of where holders of an "entertainment district" license may sell: it distinguishes cities by class. For primary or metropolitan-class cities, five specified area criteria apply (items I–V). For first- and second-class cities, villages, or unincorporated county areas, permitted sale areas are (i) within an entertainment district designated by the local governing body and (ii) areas shared by authorized licensees holding entertainment district licenses. No state agencies or departments besides local governing bodies are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB187_FinalLB187_Final_Copy.docxLB187 amends Nebraska real estate statutes and affects actions by the Nebraska Real Estate Commission, Nebraska State Patrol, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with a reference to the State Department of Education for school-exemption status. Key agency provisions: the Commission retains rulemaking, course approval and monitoring authority, may suspend/withdraw course or instructor approvals, and may investigate, discipline, fine, suspend/revoke licenses, and set licensing requirements. Fingerprinting and national criminal-history checks are required for original license applicants; fingerprints are submitted by the Nebraska State Patrol to the FBI and applicants pay actual fingerprinting costs. Operative dates: most changes effective July 1, 2025 (some provisions effective Jan 1, 2026); an emergency clause makes the act take effect immediately. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Adds requirements around real estate agency and licensing: buyers of residential property (1–4 units) must enter a written agency agreement; designated brokers acting as single agents for other property types are constrained when performing acts under section 81-885.01. The bill authorizes "the commission" to adopt and promulgate rules specifying mandatory course subject matter and sets that satisfactory evidence of course completion is valid for four years for license applications. It also inserts language about referral-fee compensation and references nonresident/citizen status. No specific state agencies beyond "the commission" are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB188_IntroLB188_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesBill LB188 states legislative intent regarding appropriations to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) for Medicaid nursing facility rates (Program No. 348). It specifies total amounts: $462,480,546 for FY2025‑26 and $476,717,026 for FY2026‑27 (General/Federal splits not specified). Those amounts are to be used in the Medicaid nursing facility rate calculation, including the annual inflation factor, and include rate enhancements and other Medicaid nursing facility purposes. DHHS must electronically report to the Legislative Fiscal Analyst and Clerk by August 1, 2025 on how the FY2025‑26 inflation factor was calculated, and between December 15–31, 2025 on any remaining unobligated prior appropriations (including encumbrances and retroactive payments). The act takes effect immediately upon passage.Department of Health and Human Services — Program No. 348 (Medicaid nursing facility rates) - Legislature specifies total appropriations for Medicaid nursing facility rates as $462,480,546 for FY2025‑26 and $476,717,026 for FY2026‑27 (General/Federal splits not specified). - These amounts must be included in the Program 348 rate calculation, including the annual inflation factor, and cover rate enhancements and other Medicaid nursing facility purposes. - Reporting requirements: DHHS must electronically report to the Legislative Fiscal Analyst and Clerk of the Legislature by Aug 1, 2025, on how the FY2025‑26 inflation factor was calculated; and again between Dec 15–31, 2025, identifying any remaining unobligated prior appropriations for Medicaid nursing facility payments, including encumbrances and retroactive payments.
109-1-LB189_IntroLB189_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB189 amends the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund statute (71-7611) to retain a provision authorizing a transfer of $15 million from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to the University of Nebraska Medical Center for pancreatic cancer research (to occur on or after July 1, 2022, but before June 30, 2023). That transfer is expressly made contingent upon receipt of matching private or other funds "certified by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services." Upon such certification, the State Treasurer is directed to transfer an equal amount from the Health Care Cash Fund to the Board of Regents.No provisions specifically assign duties to the Department of Administrative Services. Key fiscal changes affecting state finance and operations: - Creates the Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance Fund, administered by the Commissioner of Labor, to be financed by covered‑individual contributions, private donations, legislative transfers, and employer donations. - On Oct. 1, 2026, $5,558,000 is transferred from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to the new fund to cover upfront administrative costs; the amount must be repaid from the new fund no later than Oct. 1, 2030 when the commissioner determines funds are sufficient. - Contributions begin on an implementation date on or before Jan. 1, 2027; the commissioner will set and annually adjust contribution levels. - Fund investments to be handled by the state investment officer under existing state investment law. - Bill expresses intent to reuse existing state data/technology (e.g., unemployment insurance systems).
109-1-LB18_IntroLB18_Intro_Copy.docxLB18 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §86-1236 (Small Wireless Facilities Deployment Act) to specify duties for a right-of-way authority and requirements for wireless providers. Key agency-related provisions: - Authority: prohibited from granting exclusive right-of-way arrangements; may charge nondiscriminatory fees (or charge nothing) consistent with §86-1239; may impose objective, nondiscriminatory design/concealment measures in pre‑2019 historic districts; may require repair of right-of-way damage and recover reasonable costs; may approve height exceptions subject to nondiscriminatory rules; must determine compliance with the federal Americans with Disabilities Act and that installations do not obstruct travel, public safety, or utility operations before permitting new/modified poles. - Wireless providers: granted permitted-use rights for collocation and pole work subject to height limits and authority conditions. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Requires any permitting authority to, before installing or modifying a utility pole in a right‑of‑way, verify the installation: (1) complies with the federal Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and its federal implementing regulations as they existed on Jan 1, 2025; (2) does not obstruct or hinder usual travel or public safety in the right‑of‑way; and (3) does not obstruct another utility’s legal use of the right‑of‑way or impede safe operation or service. If the authority finds noncompliance with these criteria, it must deny the installation. No state or agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB190_IntroLB190_Intro_Copy.docxLB190 amends §50‑1208 of the Legislative Performance Audit Act, revising duties of the Legislative Performance Audit Committee and procedures for the Legislative Auditor’s office. Key agency-related changes: requires a five‑year rotating audit schedule for all state agencies; permits the committee (majority vote) to adopt additional performance‑audit requests; mandates written pre‑audit notice to the agency director, program director (when relevant), and the Governor; requires an entrance conference and written agency instruction to cooperate; directs the office to draft a scope statement and audit plan (including methodologies and projected completion date) subject to committee majority approval; obligates political subdivisions to provide requested information; and requires committee approval for scope/plan revisions with written notice to the agency. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a requirement that "the committee" must review and approve a rotating audit schedule covering all state agencies (or portions thereof), ensuring each is audited at least once every five years. No specific agencies or departments are named beyond "state agencies," and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB191_IntroLB191_Intro_Copy.docxLB191 (Introduced by Bosn, Jan 13, 2025; referred to Transportation and Telecommunications) proposes an amendment to section 76-2325.01 of the One-Call Notification System Act to alter the statutory provisions addressing unlawful interference with telecommunications. The bill repeals the original section and replaces it with revised language. The provided excerpt does not identify any specific state agencies or departments, nor does it include any funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB192_FinalLB192_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends section 68-1017.02 to direct the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to maximize Nebraska participation in the federal Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), seek federal funding, minimize use of state General Funds, and employ staff to evaluate available options and produce an annual report to the Legislature. DHHS may apply for and accept gifts, grants, and donations and must submit a state outreach plan to the Food and Nutrition Service of the United States Department of Agriculture for approval and federal matching funds. DHHS may partner with counties or nonprofits, be exempt from implementing outreach if insufficient private/federal funds exist, create a TANF-funded categorical eligibility policy, limit seeking SNAP work‑requirement waivers, and may require participation in employment and training per federal law.Requires the state agency that administers SNAP (typically the Department of Agriculture or the Department of Health and Human Services) not to seek, apply for, accept, or renew federal waivers of SNAP work requirements, except that the agency may use the federal statutory option to exempt individuals under 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(6). It also authorizes the department to require non‑exempt recipients to participate in SNAP employment and training programs under 7 U.S.C. 2015(d). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB193_IntroLB193_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the Committee on Pacific Conflict and specifies membership: the Director of State Homeland Security (chair), the Director of Administrative Services, the state investment officer, the Adjutant General, and three Governor‑appointed subject‑matter experts (including at least one representative of critical‑infrastructure operators). It also provides for legislative members appointed by the Executive Board of the Legislative Council as nonvoting participants. The committee may meet at least quarterly, is exempted from the Open Meetings Act, and its records are not public. Powers include convening secure briefings with critical‑infrastructure providers, establishing advisory boards, liaising with federal and other state authorities and research institutions, producing policy recommendations, issuing a public annual state threat assessment (to accompany the Governor’s annual address), and preparing a confidential report accessible only with gubernatorial approval. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The provided underlined text is only a sequence of numbers ("five (4) (5) (6) (7) (8) (9) (10) (11) (12)"). It does not mention any government agencies, departments, or programs, nor does it include any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
