109-1-LB194_FinalLB194_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB194 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-902 (documentary stamp tax exemptions). It retains the requirement (subdivision (19)) that, for deeds transferring property into a trust qualifying for an exemption, the register of deeds must be presented a signed statement certifying the exemption and that supporting evidence is maintained and available for inspection by the Department of Revenue. No provisions in the bill alter funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue.Requires the Department of Revenue to treat step-relationships as equivalent to blood relatives for the family transfer exemption and to apply that exemption to deeds conveying property to a corporation or LLC that is wholly owned by a single shareholder/member in three situations: (1) grantor is the same person as the entity’s sole owner; (2) spouses transfer property to an entity wholly owned by one spouse; (3) family members (including step-relations) transfer property to an entity wholly owned by one family member. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB195_FinalLB195_Final_Copy.docxLB195 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-470 to grant immunity to emergency responders and to peace officers or law enforcement employees who, in good faith, obtain from their agency and administer FDA‑approved opioid overdose reversal medications (e.g., naloxone, nalmefene). Such individuals are protected from administrative action, criminal prosecution, and personal civil liability for acts or omissions in providing overdose reversal care, except for willful, wanton, or grossly negligent conduct; agency or organizational liability is not affected. Definitions reference state agencies/authorities: emergency responders licensed under the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act or the EMS Personnel Licensure Interstate Compact; health professionals licensed under the Uniform Credentialing Act; law enforcement agencies (police departments, town marshals, offices of sheriff, Nebraska State Patrol); and statutory cross‑references to sections 38‑2806, 38‑2817, and 49‑801. No funding or appropriation provisions are included. The original section is repealed.Defines "opioid overdose reversal medication" as any lifesaving drug FDA-approved to reverse opioid overdose (prescription, provided by a health professional, or over-the-counter), explicitly including naloxone and nalmefene. Agency mentioned: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB196_FinalLB196_Final_Copy.docxLB196 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-6,356 to permit operation of all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) and utility-type vehicles (UTVs) between sunset and sunrise when used for snow removal within corporate limits of a city or village or within an unincorporated village. Operators must hold a valid Class O license or farm permit (per §60-4,126), carry liability insurance and produce proof within five days to a peace officer, limit speed to 30 mph, use headlights/taillights, and display a required safety flag. Electric utility personnel are exempt from the daytime-only rule when working outside municipal limits. The bill preserves rules for crossings of controlled-access highways, allows UTV crossings at signalized or stop-sign intersections when authorized by local ordinance or county resolution, and allows agricultural crossings. Cities, villages, county boards, the State of Nebraska, and its departments/boards/commissions/political subdivisions retain authorization and regulatory roles. Original section repealed. No funding or appropriation changes.Added language permits operation between sunset and sunrise for snow removal within corporate limits of a city, village, or unincorporated village. Other added subsections appear to impose equipment/vehicle-related criteria (phrases beginning “have” and excluding “all‑terrain or utility‑type” vehicles), but text is fragmentary. No state agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the provided additions.
109-1-LB197_FinalLB197_Final_Copy.docxLB197 amends Nebraska's Employment Security Law, affecting the Nebraska Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor's adjudicative processes. Key changes: determinations must state reasons and parties be promptly notified; benefits found payable continue during appeal; erroneous benefit overpayments are handled under section 48-665. Redeterminations may be issued by an adjudicator designated by the commissioner for errors in computation/identity, newly discovered wages, misrepresentations of fact, or errors identified by the federal benefit accuracy measurement program (20 C.F.R. part 602). Redeterminations are barred after two years, notice must follow section 48-630, appeals are limited to the issues changed, and the Commissioner may seek revised decisions even after a final hearing officer or court decision. Original sections 48-628.09, 48-630, and 48-631 are repealed. No funding or appropriation changes.Adds that a representative designated by the commissioner (an "adjudicator") may make a redetermination on claims under §48‑629, and explicitly allows a redetermination when a review under the federal Benefit Accuracy Measurement (BAM) program finds an error. It defines the BAM program as the quality‑control program required by 20 C.F.R. part 602. No specific state agency beyond the commissioner is newly created or named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB198_FinalLB198_Final_Copy.docxLB198 amends the Pharmacy Benefit Manager Licensure and Regulation Act to (1) define terms including clinician‑administered drug, specialty pharmacy, and spread pricing; (2) restrict pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) and health carriers/health benefit plans from excluding accredited Nebraska specialty pharmacies, imposing stricter terms on unaffiliated specialty pharmacies, demanding excessive reporting, or compelling clinician‑administered drug handling that undermines provider administration or timely delivery; (3) bar health plans/carriers/PBMs from forcing exclusive mail‑order use, transferring prescriptions without member consent, or auto‑enrolling members in mail order except limited maintenance‑medication exceptions; (4) permit network pharmacies to decline to fill if paid below acquisition cost without retaliation; (5) protect retail pharmacies offering ancillary delivery services; and (6) prohibit spread pricing in new PBM‑plan contracts after Jan. 1, 2026, with a full ban by Jan. 1, 2029. Operative date: Jan. 1, 2026. No appropriations or funding changes are included.No state agencies or departments are newly created or referenced; the only government law cited is the federal Drug Supply Chain Security Act (21 U.S.C. 360eee et seq.) for track-and-trace compliance. The additions define "clinician‑administered drug" and set numerous limits and obligations on pharmacy benefit managers, health carriers, specialty and retail pharmacies (reporting frequency, nondiscrimination, delivery timing, appeal processes, prohibitions on forcing use of certain pharmacies, protections for providers who decline under‑reimbursed drugs, and rules on mail‑order auto‑enrollment). Contracts with PBMs may not start new spread‑pricing after Jan 1, 2026, with a complete ban by Jan 1, 2029. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB199_IntroLB199_Intro_Copy.docxLB199 makes several administrative changes affecting state actors: - Secretary of State: retains authority to issue, renew, deny, suspend, or revoke certificates of registration for civil litigation funding companies; may discipline registrants for specified violations including knowing failure to disclose funding contracts. Registrants must annually submit prescribed data (number/amount of fundings, repayment metrics, fees charged, shortfalls). Secretary must prepare and electronically submit an aggregate annual report to the Clerk of the Legislature and the Legislature’s Judiciary Committee. Administrative Procedure Act procedures apply to enforcement actions; temporary certificates may be issued while applications are pending. - Courts, agencies, and tribunals: recipients of mandatory disclosure of nonrecourse civil litigation funding contracts. - Revisor of Statutes: to assign the new statute of limitations section to Chapter 25, article 2. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are addressed.Adds a disclosure duty for nonrecourse civil litigation funding: consumers or their attorneys must promptly provide copies of such contracts to each opposing party or their attorney, "any court, agency, or tribunal" where the claim is pending, and any known indemnitor/insurer. The duty applies even before a lawsuit or administrative proceeding is filed, is ongoing, and requires disclosure of new or amended contracts within 30 days. The existence of the contract and all participants are discoverable. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB19_IntroLB19_Intro_Copy.docxLB19 amends multiple statutes governing cities of the metropolitan class to shift candidate nomination to the statewide primary and election of the mayor and seven city council members to the statewide general election beginning with the 2028 statewide primary/general cycle. Terms continue to commence the fourth Monday after election; incumbents whose terms began after the May 2025 general election serve until the fourth Monday after the 2028 statewide general and may run in 2028. The bill harmonizes references throughout law to the statewide primary/general election (Election Act) and updates procedural roles for municipal entities: city councils, mayors, city clerks, county clerks or election commissioners, and canvassing authorities for special, franchise, ordinance, bond, and condemnation questions. It retains existing local bond provisions (annual $100,000 park bonds without voter approval; bridge acquisition/revenue bond limits including a $2 million threshold and up to 15% for repairs). No state appropriations are made.Adds that, beginning with the 2028 statewide primary and every four years thereafter, candidates for elective office in "cities of the metropolitan class" will be nominated and elected at the statewide primary and general elections, with terms commencing the fourth Monday after the general election. A transitional clause extends terms that began the fourth Monday after the May 2025 general election until the fourth Monday after the 2028 statewide general, and allows those officers to seek reelection in 2028. It also specifies each metropolitan class city shall elect seven council members per section 32-536. Affected entities: city governments and statewide election authorities. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB1_FinalLB1_Final_Copy.docxLB1 amends definitional provisions in Initiative Law 2024, No. 437 (Nebraska Medical Cannabis Patient Protection Act) and Initiative Law 2024, No. 438 (Nebraska Medical Cannabis Regulation Act) to correct an incorrect subdivision reference adopted by voters. Changes clarify definitions (e.g., “cannabis,” “allowable amount,” “caregiver,” “health care practitioner,” “registered cannabis establishment,” and “registration”) and retain cross‑references to licensing under the Uniform Credentialing Act and to health care facility and home health agency definitions (sections 71‑413 and 71‑417). The bill identifies the Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission in the regulatory act. It repeals the original sections and includes an emergency clause making the act effective on passage. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.I don't have the underlined text — only the section label. 109-1-LB200_IntroLB200_Intro_Copy.docxLB200 reinstates the Personal Property Tax Relief Act exemptions effective for tax years after 2024 and updates administration and reporting. The Property Tax Administrator and Tax Commissioner implement the exemption and a compensating exemption factor affecting railroads, car lines, public service entities, and air carriers. County assessors and treasurers must certify lost tax revenue to the Tax Commissioner (by Nov. 30); the Tax Commissioner notifies the Director of Administrative Services, who draws warrants against General Fund appropriations for reimbursement in two roughly equal installments after the State Treasurer verifies available funds. Reimbursement distribution formulas to taxing subdivisions are specified (including a 1% county general fund deposit and prescribed allocation methods for public service entities, railroads, car lines, and air carriers). The bill also updates filing deadlines (county assessors to electronically file personal property abstracts with the Property Tax Administrator by July 20) and repeals the original sections amended.The added text consists of ten repeated insertions of the phrase “after 2024.” It names no government agencies or departments and contains no language changing funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The effect or placement of these insertions is unclear from the provided excerpt.
109-1-LB201_IntroLB201_Intro_Copy.docxLB201 amends the Nebraska Money Transmitters Act (section 8-2701) to require licensees or authorized delegates to collect a fee for each money transmission sent outside the United States equal to 10% of the transaction value, capped at $10,000. Fees are remitted quarterly to "the department" on forms prescribed by the department with the assistance of the Nebraska State Patrol, due by the 15th day following each calendar quarter. The act becomes operative January 1, 2026, and repeals the original section. No specific appropriations or budget allocations are included.Adds a requirement that licensees or authorized delegates collect a fee on each money transmission to persons outside the U.S.: 10% of the transaction value or $10,000, whichever is less. Fees must be remitted quarterly to "the department" using a form prescribed by that department, prepared with assistance from the Nebraska State Patrol. All fees and forms are due by the 15th day of the month following each calendar quarter. No explicit appropriations or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB202_IntroLB202_Intro_Copy.docxLB202 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §38-2037 (Medicine and Surgery Practice Act). It preserves disciplinary authority (per §§38-178, 38-179 and procedures in §38-196) for physicians, osteopathic physicians, and physician assistants who fail to comply with statutes on signing birth and death certificates (§§71-603.01, 71-604, 71-605, 71-606). It also adds an explicit protections clause: a license to practice medicine and surgery (MD/DO) shall not be subject to disciplinary measures for an applicant’s or licensee’s expression of an opinion in public or professional forums (First Amendment intent). The bill repeals the original §38-2037. No agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary provisions.Adds a legislative intent protecting First Amendment rights of physicians and osteopathic physicians to express differing medical opinions in public or professional forums. It bars disciplinary action against an applicant or licensee solely for expressing such opinions. No specific government agencies or departments are named and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed.
109-1-LB203_IntroLB203_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services- The bill requires county, district, or city-county health departments to be approved by the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to qualify as local full‑time public health services and to be operated in conformity with DHHS rules, regulations, and policies. - Agreements creating city‑county health departments must be approved by DHHS. - Health directors are directed to distribute free vaccines, drugs, serums, and other public‑health preparations obtained from DHHS. - The bill allows local departments to utilize local, state, federal, and other funds but contains no explicit changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or state budget allocations.Adds a definition of "community-wide directed health measure" as a public‑health action by a local health department covering the entire jurisdiction when there are no known epidemiological links. Requires a local health director to obtain written approval from a majority of the publicly elected county board members (or, for city–county health departments, a majority of the publicly elected city council members) before issuing such measures, and to submit the measures to the city‑county board of health for ratification at its next regular meeting. No references to the Department of Health and Human Services or to any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations; no fiscal changes included.
109-1-LB204_IntroLB204_Intro_Copy.docxLB204 (2025) enacts the "Biometric Autonomy Liberty Law" regulating biometric data. It defines "public entity" to include the State of Nebraska, state and local agencies, political subdivisions, courts, and the Legislative Council. The Attorney General is empowered to issue subpoenas, pursue civil damages and injunctive relief, and enforce violations under the Consumer Protection Act (with a 60‑day cure notice). The bill references the State Department of Education for consent‑language lexile standards. Exemptions include law enforcement uses, security purposes, HIPAA‑covered health information, emergency medical services, DMV facial recognition for fraud detection, FERPA‑protected education records, and GLBA‑covered financial data. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. The act is operative January 1, 2026.Adds a Biometric Autonomy Liberty Law defining public entities to include the State of Nebraska (and its agents), state/local agencies, political subdivisions, Nebraska courts, and the Legislative Council. The State Department of Education sets the seventh‑grade lexile standard for consent language. The Attorney General is given enforcement authority — subpoena power, civil actions for damages, and injunctive relief — with a 60‑day cure notice requirement before suit. Law enforcement agencies (and cooperating processors) have specified disclosure/use exceptions; the Department of Motor Vehicles is explicitly exempted for facial‑recognition fraud detection. Other statutory exceptions reference HIPAA, FERPA, the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act, the Data Privacy and Genetic Information Privacy Acts, and Gramm‑Leach‑Bliley. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB205_IntroLB205_Intro_Copy.docxLB205 revises evidentiary rules and damage limits in Nebraska personal injury and wrongful death cases. Agencies/departments referenced: - Medicare and Medicaid: Recoverable medical damages are tied to Medicare reimbursement rates (generally 120% for past/future calculations) or, where no Medicare rate exists, 170% of the applicable state Medicaid rate. If private coverage exists, amounts are limited to what the coverage would pay plus the claimant’s share. - State courts (Judiciary): Courts/juries must first find noneconomic damages without regard to limits, then reduce awards to statutory caps; courts must apply the statute’s disclosure and admissibility rules. - Statutory reference to section 60-316 (commercial driver licensing) ties the commercial motor vehicle definition to motor-vehicle licensing law. Financial impact: No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are included.Added provisions reference Medicare and Medicaid rates for calculating admissible medical damages: unpaid past or future medical charges are limited to amounts actually paid, insurer-allowed amounts, or—when uninsured or covered by Medicare/Medicaid—100%–120% of applicable Medicare reimbursement rates (and 170% of applicable state Medicaid rates when no Medicare rate applies). The text also invokes 42 U.S.C. section 1396d(l)(2)(B) (as of Jan 1, 2025) and requires disclosure of factoring-company purchases of medical receivables, the claimant's health coverage, and letters of protection (including attorney referrals). A $1,000,000 cap on noneconomic damages is added for claims involving commercial motor vehicles. No changes to agency budgets, appropriations, or funding allocations are made.
109-1-LB206_IntroLB206_Intro_Copy.docxLB206 amends the Nebraska Criminal Code to create enhanced penalties for specified "covered offenses" (assaults, robbery, arson, burglary, theft, criminal mischief/trespass, and related inchoate and accessory conduct) when committed in a "disaster area" during an "emergency period." Disaster area is tied to: a gubernatorial emergency proclamation (section 81-829.40), a local emergency declaration (section 81-829.50), a Presidential major disaster/emergency declaration under 42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq. (Stafford Act), or a mandatory evacuation order by the appropriate local, state, or federal official. Penalties increase one classification (Class I misdemeanor elevated to Class IV felony). Prosecutors must allege enhancements in charging documents and prove them beyond a reasonable doubt to judge or jury. No funding or appropriation changes.Adds a new crime-enhancement provision. Key points: - Defines covered offenses (various assaults, robbery, arson, burglary, theft, criminal mischief/trespass, and related inchoate or accessory conduct). - Defines "disaster area" to include: emergency proclamations by the Governor (sec. 81-829.40), local emergency declarations (sec. 81-829.50), Presidential major disaster/emergency declarations under the Stafford Act (42 U.S.C. 5121 et seq.), or mandatory evacuation orders by the appropriate local, state, or federal official. - Defines "emergency period" as the duration of the proclamation/declaration/order (or 30 days after issuance if no end date). - Penalty enhancement: offenses committed in a disaster area during the emergency period are punished at the next higher classification (Class I misdemeanor enhanced to Class IV felony). - Enhancement allegations must appear in the charging document and be proved beyond a reasonable doubt by the prosecuting attorney. No agencies are granted funding or appropriations; no budgetary changes are included.
109-1-LB207_IntroLB207_Intro_Copy.docxLB207 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-3,191 to set specific registration fees for alternative-fuel motor vehicles. It establishes a $75 fee for motorcycles and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, a $150 fee for other alternative-fuel vehicles, and a commercial-vehicle provision making registration for alternative-fuel vehicles over 7,500 pounds three times the applicable fee. County treasurers collect the fees and remit them to the State Treasurer for credit to the Highway Trust Fund. The bill repeals the original section. Agencies explicitly affected: county treasurers and the Office of the State Treasurer (Highway Trust Fund receipt).Adds an alternative-fuel vehicle registration fee schedule: commercially registered alternative-fuel vehicles over 7,500 lbs pay three times the applicable alternative-fuel vehicle fee (as referenced in subdivision (1)(c)), and all other alternative-fuel motor vehicles pay $150. No government agency or department is named, and there are no explicit funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the added text.
109-1-LB208_FinalLB208_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Agriculture, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of RevenueLB208 affects the Department of Revenue (DOR), Department of Administrative Services (DAS), and Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV); the Department of Agriculture is named but no specific duties are detailed in the summaries provided. DOR: ratifies Streamlined Sales & Use Tax Agreement amendments through Dec. 31, 2024; may act jointly with other states, adopt rules, procure services, maintain sales-tax rate/ZIP-code databases, notify retailers via its website, and share confidential returns with auditors under specified confidentiality and data‑retention/model‑1 seller privacy rules. DOR will administer tax-credit programs, including a new nonrefundable food‑donation credit (50% of value, up to $2,500) for grocery stores, restaurants, and agricultural producers (tax years beginning Jan. 1, 2025) with a $500,000 annual approval cap (prorated if exceeded). Under section 77‑7012 DOR may approve $1,000,000 in credits in FY2024‑25 and $1,500,000 annually thereafter; refundable child‑care credits will be approved until $15 million total approvals. DAS personnel are explicitly prohibited from disclosing confidential tax information (Class I misdemeanor). DMV: certain collection penalties are set at $5.Department of Administrative Services: no changes indicated. Department of Agriculture: no changes indicated. Department of Motor Vehicles: no changes indicated. Department of Revenue: multiple tax law adjustments. Model 1 sellers whose sales/use tax functions are performed by a certified service provider (and the provider is compensated under the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement) will not receive collection fees. Establishes a refundable Child Care Tax Credit per section 77-7203 for taxpayers for taxable years beginning or deemed to begin on/after Jan 1, 2024. Clarifies rate sourcing: use nine‑digit ZIPs and, if a five‑digit area contains multiple tax rates, apply the highest combined tax rate. Annual credit caps are enforced with proration among requests received on the day the limit is exceeded. Adds a residency specification (Nebraska resident). No explicit appropriations, funding or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB209_FinalLB209_Final_Copy.docxLB209 amends Nebraska property tax law (sections 77-202 and 77-3506). Key agencies mentioned: United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), county assessors, and the Nebraska Tax Commissioner; federal programs referenced include the BEAD (Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment) program under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. Major changes: - For-profit skilled nursing, nursing, and assisted‑living facilities that house Medicaid beneficiaries receive a property tax exemption equal to the facility’s average Medicaid‑occupied bed percentage over the most recent three years (does not affect nonprofit exemptions). - Homestead exemptions clarified to cover veterans with 100% service‑connected permanent disability or total disability per 38 C.F.R. 4.16, and veterans with 100% temporary service‑connected disability; surviving spouses remain eligible. VA certification required; application timing adjusted (subdivision (2)(a) application every year evenly divisible by five; others annually with certification required only in years evenly divisible by five). - Broadband equipment exemption procedures: owner applies to county assessor by Dec. 31; assessor must approve within 30 days; forms prescribed by the Tax Commissioner. No direct appropriations or budget reallocations are specified. The bill takes effect immediately due to an emergency clause.Adds language clarifying that the subdivision does not change or reduce: (1) any property tax exemption for nonprofit skilled nursing facilities (administered by state/local taxing authorities), and (2) the assignment of a total disability rating for compensation under 38 C.F.R. §4.16 (a Department of Veterans Affairs regulation). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB20_FinalLB20_Final_Copy.docxLB20 defines "agricultural self-generation facility" (≤100 kW, on same premises as the owner's electric account, using methane, wind, solar, biomass, hydropower, or geothermal, no backfeed device, not net‑metered, used for agricultural/horticultural purposes) and "local distribution utility" (owner/operator of distribution equipment, including public power districts, public power and irrigation districts, electric cooperatives, and municipal electric systems). The bill prohibits a local distribution utility from denying electric service to a customer with such a facility; requires the owner‑generator to notify the utility before installation; and subjects owner‑generators to the utility’s interconnection requirements, safety standards, rates, charges, and service agreement terms. Utilities may set rates/fees to fully recover costs. No changes to state agency budgets, appropriations, or funding are included.Adds definitions for "agricultural self-generation facility" (≤100 kW, on-site, owner-controlled, uses methane/wind/solar/biomass/hydro/geothermal, prevents backfeed, not for net metering) and clarifies "local distribution utility" to include public power districts, public power and irrigation districts, electric cooperatives, and municipal electric systems. Prohibits those utilities from denying service to customers with such facilities. Owner-generators must notify the local distribution utility and comply with the utility's interconnection, safety, rate/charge, and service-agreement requirements; utilities may set rates/fees to fully recover their costs. References statutes 77-1359 and 70-2002. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB210_IntroLB210_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Insurance, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB210 designates the Department of Health and Human Services (department) as the lead agency under the Population Health Information Act. Key department actions: impose fees on every pharmacy benefit manager for operational, non‑treatment use of the prescription drug monitoring program and remit those fees to a newly created Population Health Information Assessment Fund (fee amount left unspecified). The Fund is established to cover nonfederal costs and to reimburse the department for assessment collection costs (up to $250,000 annually); transfers to the General Fund are prohibited and investment earnings accrue to the Fund. The department must share vital‑statistics data quarterly with the designated health information exchange and report managed‑care organization compliance to the Health Information Technology Board by June 30 each fiscal year (beginning 2025‑26); the Board must notify the Department of Insurance of MCO noncompliance within 60 days.- Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): New authority to impose and remit fees from pharmacy benefit managers to the State Treasurer for credit to a newly created Population Health Information Assessment Fund (fee amount shown as "XXX"). The Fund is dedicated to nonfederal costs of the designated health information exchange and prescription drug monitoring program and may reimburse the department up to $250,000 annually for assessment collection costs; transfers to the General Fund are prohibited and investment earnings are credited to the Fund. DHHS must annually report (by June 30, beginning FY2025‑26) each managed care organization's compliance with claims‑sharing to the Health Information Technology Board and must share vital‑statistics data files quarterly with the designated HIE/operator. - Department of Insurance (DOI): The Health Information Technology Board must report MCO noncompliance in the medical assistance program to DOI within 60 days after receiving DHHS’s status report. Insurers/health plans may also be subject to charges by the operator as a condition of doing business in Nebraska.
109-1-LB211_IntroLB211_Intro_Copy.docxLB211 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §13-3403 (Property Tax Growth Limitation Act). It specifies that a political subdivision’s preliminary property tax request authority equals the amount of property taxes levied by the county board of equalization in the prior year, less exceptions used under §13-3404. It permits additional increases based on (a) the subdivision’s growth percentage and (b) an inflation component that varies by public-safety intensity: if public safety services (per §13-320) comprise ≥20% of the subdivision’s property-tax-funded budget, the inflation adjustment is the greater of zero or the inflation percentage; if <20%, the inflation adjustment is the greater of 2% or the inflation percentage. The bill repeals the original §13-3403 and takes effect immediately due to an emergency clause. No appropriations or agency funding changes are included.Adds a formula allowing a political subdivision to increase its property tax request authority in two components, both applied to prior-year property taxes net of exceptions (per §13-3404(1)–(2)): (1) a growth-percentage increase; and (2) an inflation-based increase. If public safety services (per §13-320) are ≥20% of the property-tax–funded budget, the inflation component is the greater of zero or the inflation percentage. If public safety is <20%, the inflation component is the greater of 2% or the inflation percentage. No specific agencies receive direct appropriations; this changes allowable tax request authority.
109-1-LB212_IntroLB212_Intro_Copy.docxLB212 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-4008 (Tobacco Products Tax Act). Key changes: sets the tax on cigars, cheroots, and stogies at 20% of the first‑owner purchase or sale price with a $0.50 maximum per cigar; retains snuff at $0.44 per ounce; taxes electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) ≤3 mL at $0.05 per mL and ENDS >3 mL at 10% of the first‑owner purchase or sale price; taxes other tobacco products at 20% of purchase or sale price. For retail dealers, tax timing for untaxed ENDS is clarified. When a licensed purchaser buys from another licensed seller (per §77‑4009), the seller is liable for the tax. Revenues continue to be distributed pursuant to §77‑4025. Act operative October 1, 2025; original section repealed. No direct appropriations or agency budget changes are included.Adds a 20% excise tax on cigars, cheroots, and stogies, calculated on either (i) the purchase price paid by the first owner or (ii) the price at which a first owner who made/manufactured/fabricated them sells them, with a per-item cap of $0.50. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no appropriations, funding, or budget allocation changes in the added text.
109-1-LB213_IntroLB213_Intro_Copy.docxLB213 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-760.01, directing the State Board of Education to adopt measurable academic content standards (already required for reading, writing, mathematics, science, and social studies) and to: 1) adopt human embryology science standards by March 1, 2026, to be implemented by the 2026-27 school year—including instruction on human development (explicitly citing the Carnegie Stages) and provision of high‑definition 4D visual recordings showing brain, heart, sex organs, and other vital organs; and 2) continue requirements for social studies to include financial literacy and Holocaust/recognized genocide education and for prior computer science standards (due March 1, 2024). The board must review/update standards every seven years, including commonly accepted district standards. Parents/guardians/educational decisionmakers may opt students out of the embryology instruction. The bill takes effect on passage; no funding or appropriation changes are included.Requires the board (presumably the state education board) to adopt measurable human embryology academic standards under science standards by March 1, 2026, and integrate them into every school's curriculum by the 2026–27 school year. Required content: accurate biological instruction including the Carnegie Stages of human embryonic development and high‑definition “4D” visual recordings showing development of brain, heart, sex organs and other vital organs. Parents, guardians, or “educational decisionmakers” (per §79‑530) may opt their student out. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB214_IntroLB214_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services- Defines "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services. - Requires the Department to develop and publish procedures (on its website) to allow anonymous submission of medical history, reconsideration of surrender, and paternity testing for surrendered newborns. - Requires staff at device sites to notify the Department of any device failure and mandates Department approval of signage. - Legislative intent to appropriate $15,000 to the Department for FY2025-26 to award grants for installation (not purchase or ongoing operation, unless lack of funding jeopardizes use) of newborn safety devices. - Amends intent language to appropriate $65,000 to the Department for FY2024-25 and $10,000 annually thereafter, subject to available funding, to develop/maintain a public information program (including a permanent interactive website, statewide literature distribution, educational materials, training, and public awareness of newborn safety devices).Summary (Dept. of Health and Human Services focus): - Defines "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and requires DHHS oversight of newborn safety device program. - DHHS must approve signage (English, Spanish, other local languages) and receive notifications of device failures; staff at sites must document inspections/repairs. - DHHS must develop and publish on its website procedures allowing anonymous submission of a surrendered newborn's medical history, reconsideration of surrender, and paternity testing. - The Legislature intends to appropriate $15,000 to DHHS for FY 2025–26 to award grants for installation (not purchase or ongoing operation) of newborn safety devices, unless funding shortfalls would jeopardize continued use.
109-1-LB215A_IntroLB215A_Intro_Copy.docxLB215A appropriates General Fund dollars to the Nebraska Board of Parole (Program 358) to implement Legislative Bill 215 (2025). It provides $122,000 for FY2025‑26 and $125,966 for FY2026‑27. Of those amounts, total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $85,400 for FY2025‑26 and $88,015 for FY2026‑27.Appropriates General Fund money to the Board of Parole, Program 358, to implement Legislative Bill 215: $122,000 for FY2025‑26 and $125,966 for FY2026‑27. Specifies that of those appropriated amounts, expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems may not exceed $85,400 in FY2025‑26 and $88,015 in FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB215_IntroLB215_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles- Department of Correctional Services: Section 11 directs the department (with the Division of Parole Supervision and the Board of Parole) to establish a "second chance relief" program to identify eligible committed offenders, regularly provide lists of eligible or soon-to-be-eligible offenders to the Board of Parole, and assist offenders in applying for commutations. The department's role is incorporated into the Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act by amending section 83-1,135 to include section 11. - Department of Health and Human Services: The Clean Slate provisions exclude offenses involving assault on a Department of Health and Human Services employee and require that, when an order to seal an adjudication is entered, notice be sent to DHHS if the person was a ward of the state at the time or if DHHS was a party. - Department of Motor Vehicles: Courts must notify the DMV when a sealed adjudication included impoundment or prohibition to obtain a license or permit under section 43-287. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are included.Department of Correctional Services: Establishes a "second chance relief" program with the Division of Parole Supervision and Board of Parole. The department must regularly identify committed offenders who are or will be eligible (within five years) and provide lists to the Board of Parole. The Board of Parole conducts risk assessments, involves community stakeholders, recommends commutations to the Board of Pardons, and, if parole is granted, develops reentry plans, mentorship, restorative-justice options, and monitoring. Department of Health and Human Services: Will receive notice to seal records when an adjudication involved a ward of the state or when DHHS was a party. Assaults on DHHS employees are excluded from clean-slate eligibility. Department of Motor Vehicles: Will receive notice to seal records when an adjudication included impoundment or prohibitions on licensing under section 43-287. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are added.
109-1-LB216_IntroLB216_Intro_Copy.docxLB216 centralizes court administrative functions under the Nebraska Supreme Court. Key agency effects and fiscal changes: - Transfers all elected clerks of the district court and their employees to state employment under the Supreme Court effective January 7, 2027; salaries, benefits, and expenses to be paid by the State (funds appropriated to the Supreme Court). - State Court Administrator receives court records and will negotiate agreements with the Department of Health and Human Services for child-support reporting; federal reimbursements for direct costs will be credited to Agency 5 – Supreme Court. - Computer hardware/software and related communications for district and separate juvenile courts become state-paid (Supreme Court appropriation) beginning January 7, 2027; county-purchased property remains county-owned. - Retirement/benefit transfers addressed: county retirement members transition with protections; counties and State share any additional retirement costs proportionately; transferred employees gain State Employees Retirement System eligibility where applicable. - Counties must reimburse the State or employees for portions of accrued sick/vacation leave when transferred (specified percentages). - Clerks are prohibited from serving on mental health boards; oaths filed with Secretary of State; various county bond and salary provisions adjusted.Adds that beginning January 7, 2027, elected clerks of the district courts and their employees become state employees under the Nebraska Supreme Court. Counties must provide leave accrual data; the State of Nebraska — using funds appropriated to the Supreme Court — will directly pay all salaries, benefits, and expenses of transferred clerks/employees. County-owned furniture/equipment remains with counties; books/files transfer to the State Court Administrator. Retirement rules reference the Retirement System for Nebraska Counties and the State Employees Retirement System, with intent that accrued benefits not be lost and additional retirement costs shared pro rata between county and state. Leave-transfer rules set limits (sick up to 1,440 hrs, vacation up to 280 hrs) and require county reimbursement to the state or employees at specified percentages. Transferred staff may join the Nebraska State Insurance Program immediately. State will also pay certain district court IT and communication costs from Supreme Court appropriations. Federal reimbursements for child-support-related costs credit Agency 5 – Supreme Court via the State Treasurer.
109-1-LB217_FinalLB217_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB217 assigns the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) specific duties regarding suicide awareness and prevention training for the child welfare system. DHHS must develop a baseline curriculum and training materials in consultation with statewide and national experts (including the Nebraska State Suicide Prevention Coalition and the Behavioral Health Education Center of Nebraska), incorporating evidence‑based and trauma‑informed practices. DHHS must provide annual suicide awareness/prevention training for staff who provide direct services or interact with children/families, delivered within existing departmental training programs and completed prior to independent contact. The department must incorporate such training into foster‑home licensure initial and renewal requirements and adopt related rules and regulations; it may issue waivers for non‑safety licensing standards for relative homes. DHHS will also establish standardized training requirements for child‑placing agency employees and may approve agency curricula that meet the baseline. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. The act becomes operative October 1, 2025.DHHS must develop a baseline suicide-awareness-and-prevention curriculum for child welfare training, in consultation with statewide and national behavioral-health and suicide-prevention experts (e.g., Nebraska State Suicide Prevention Coalition, Behavioral Health Education Center of Nebraska). Training must use evidence-based practices and cover early warning signs, appropriate responses, and trauma-informed care. All DHHS child‑welfare staff who provide direct services or otherwise interact with children/families (and others as the Division of Children and Family Services designates) must receive annual training and complete required training before any independent contact with youth/families; the training is to be delivered within existing DHHS training programs. DHHS must include this training for initial licensure and renewal and establish standardized training requirements for employees of child‑placing agencies, allowing agency curricula if they meet the baseline. No funding or appropriation changes are specified.
109-1-LB218_IntroLB218_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Veterans' Affairs- Secretary of State shall contract with the Department of Administrative Services for storage and distribution of election forms. - The Department of Motor Vehicles must: enter into an agreement with the Secretary of State to match DMV records with the statewide voter registration list (including citizenship verification); incorporate a voter‑registration portion into operator's‑license, state‑ID, employment driving permit, medical hardship permit, and commercial license/CLP application forms; transmit applicant data (including digital image/signature) electronically to county election officials; and may still issue licenses/IDs if the voter‑registration portion is incomplete or declined. - Social Security number use is authorized to furnish information to the Department of Revenue under section 77‑362.02. - Veteran designation on licenses requires registration with the Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs registry. - No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.Summary (underlined additions): - Department of Motor Vehicles / Department of Administrative Services: Applicants for operator's licenses or state ID must be given a voter-registration portion that is transmitted to the county election official unless the applicant expressly opts out. Applicants must be advised: "We will use your information to update your voter registration record or register you to vote," and given an opportunity to decline. If the voter portion is partially completed or refused, the department may still issue the license/ID but must transmit whatever voter information was provided. Commercial learner's permit/commercial driver's license applicants are required to answer the voter-registration question. - Department of Revenue / Department of Veterans' Affairs: No changes or responsibilities in the added text. - Funding/appropriations: None specified.
109-1-LB219_IntroLB219_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB219 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-105. The provision specifying that "all sentences for maximum terms of imprisonment for one year or more for felonies shall be served in institutions under the jurisdiction of the Department of Correctional Services" remains in the statute. The bill contains no language changing funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services.Adds language specifying that the statute’s minimum penalties are “none for imprisonment and none for post‑release supervision.” There are no provisions affecting the Department of Correctional Services’ funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB21_FinalLB21_Final_Copy.docxLB21 adopts the Uniform Unlawful Restrictions in Land Records Act. It authorizes property owners to record an amendment removing an unlawful restriction; the amendment must identify the owner, the affected real property, and the original document and include a mandated conspicuous statement. Amendments must be executed and acknowledged according to the requirements for recordation and recorded in the land records of each county where the original document is recorded (i.e., county land records/registries). The amendment does not affect restrictions that are lawful, nor does it constitute republication that would extend a restriction’s statutory expiration. No state agencies, departments, appropriations, or budget changes are specified.The added text prescribes the form and recording procedure for an owner's amendment under the Uniform Unlawful Restrictions in Land Records Act. It must identify the owner, affected property and original document, include a required conspicuous statement, be executed and acknowledged as required for recordation, and be recorded in the land records of each county where the original document appears. It clarifies the amendment does not revive or impair lawful restrictions and includes a sample form with fields for owner, property, and amended document. No state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are mentioned.
109-1-LB220_IntroLB220_Intro_Copy.docxLB220 directs the Legislature to require developmental and intellectual disability (DID) impact notes for proposed legislation and assigns related powers and duties to the Nebraska Legislative Research Office. The bill states legislative findings and authorizes the Office of Legislative Research to prepare and manage these impact assessments. No other state agencies are named in the provided excerpt, and the text does not include any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB221_IntroLB221_Intro_Copy.docxLB221 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §50-1301 to add legislative findings about growth of boards and commissions and to establish procedures for filling extended vacancies in gubernatorial appointments. If a gubernatorial-appointed seat is vacant six months or more, the legislative committee of jurisdiction may accept applications and forward recommendations to the Governor. If the seat remains vacant three months after recommendations are forwarded, the Executive Board of the Legislative Council may make the appointment. The bill references the Legislature, the Governor, legislative committees of jurisdiction, and the Executive Board of the Legislative Council. The original section is repealed. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a procedure for filling gubernatorial vacancies on statutory boards, commissions, and similar entities: if a gubernatorial-appointed seat is vacant six months, the legislative committee of jurisdiction may accept applications and forward recommendations to the Governor; if the seat remains vacant three months after those recommendations are sent, the Executive Board of the Legislative Council may make the appointment. Mentions the Governor, the Legislature, legislative committees of jurisdiction, and the Executive Board of the Legislative Council. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB222_IntroLB222_Intro_Copy.docxLB222 amends duties and limits on law-enforcement authority under the Nebraska Rules of the Road. It explicitly involves the Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety and officers of the Nebraska State Patrol (with carrier enforcement officers excepted) and other peace officers. Key changes: peace officers generally may not stop or detain vehicle operators for nonmoving violations, for driving with a suspended/revoked license under specified statutes, or on most misdemeanor warrants (with narrow enumerated exceptions). Stops for equipment violations are limited to defects that relate to the vehicle and pose an objectively reasonable immediate, serious safety threat; officers must log or notify dispatch of the primary reason before stopping and inform the operator on contact. Vehicle searches require a warrant or written, bilingual consent form (explained orally, revocable, right to counsel/interpreter); evidence seized in violation is inadmissible. The act takes effect immediately (emergency clause). No appropriations or funding changes.Adds limits on vehicle stops, detentions, and searches by peace officers. Key agency references: peace officers and dispatch; interpreter services are required where needed. Major provisions: - Defines “immediate, serious threat” for equipment-failure stops. - Prohibits stops/detentions for nonmoving violations, certain license suspensions, and many misdemeanor warrants (with listed exceptions), and bars stops where equipment violations do not pose an immediate serious threat to safety. - Requires officers to log digitally or notify dispatch the primary reason for an equipment-related stop before initiating it, inform the operator on first contact, and restrict questioning to the equipment issue unless plain-view evidence creates separate reasonable suspicion. - Establishes that an “authorized person” is the vehicle operator and requires a warrant or written consent before vehicle searches. Consent must be preceded by oral explanation, given on a written form (English and Spanish), state voluntariness and right to counsel, allow revocation, and note no punishment for refusal. Evidence obtained in violation is inadmissible. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB223_IntroLB223_Intro_Copy.docxLB223 amends the Nebraska Fair Housing Act to add “lawful source of income” and protection for persons subject to public-assistance requirements. It defines lawful source of income (e.g., social security, child support, veterans benefits, federal/state/local housing assistance and vouchers). Agency impacts and duties: - Equal Opportunity Commission: expanded enforcement, investigation, conciliation, data collection (including protected characteristics and lawful source of income), and required electronic annual reporting to the Legislature; authority to adopt rules and enter cooperative agreements with HUD and with testing organizations (prohibits pay-for-performance compensation to testers). - State Fire Marshal: retains administration of accessibility standards. - County attorneys: explicitly authorized to enforce the Act and must notify the commission of complaints. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a definition of “lawful source of income” to include social security, child support, foster care subsidies, alimony, veterans benefits, any federal/state/local public general or housing assistance (including vouchers under 42 U.S.C. 1437f), housing-assistance payments/credits, and other lawful income. It clarifies such assistance may be paid directly, indirectly, or on behalf of a renter or attributed to a landlord. It also states the Nebraska Fair Housing Act does not bar otherwise nondiscriminatory measures that benefit public-assistance recipients (e.g., housing limited to such recipients or favorable loan/lease/mortgage terms). Government references are to federal, state, and local assistance programs and the federal voucher authority (42 U.S.C. 1437f, i.e., HUD Section 8); no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed.
109-1-LB224_IntroLB224_Intro_Copy.docxLB224 establishes a paid maternity‑leave benefit for Nebraska state employees. Key provisions: - Defines terms (maternity leave, maternity‑leave eligible employee, retaliatory action, state employee). - Entitles eligible state employees who give birth and assume a parental role to 12 weeks paid maternity leave (prorated for part‑time employees); maximum 12 weeks in any 12‑month period. - Leave may not begin before birth, must be used within six months, and is non‑intermittent except by mutual written agreement or medical necessity for the child; runs concurrently with the federal Family and Medical Leave Act. - Requires ~30 days’ notice when practicable; the state may not charge other accrued leave for this maternity leave. - No cash‑out on termination; employees must be reinstated to the same or equivalent position after leave. No specific agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a state-level paid maternity leave entitlement: full‑time state employees receive 12 weeks (part‑time prorated) to bond with a newborn. The bill defines "state employee," "maternity leave," and "retaliatory action"; requires leave to begin no earlier than birth and be used within six months; bars intermittent use except by mutual written agreement or medical certification for the child; and makes state maternity leave run concurrently with the federal Family and Medical Leave Act. It requires ~30 days' notice (or as soon as practicable if unforeseen), prohibits charging other leave banks (except as FMLA allows), provides job restoration to the same or equivalent position, and disallows pay for unused maternity leave at termination. No specific state agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to appropriations or budget allocations in the added text.
109-1-LB225_IntroLB225_Intro_Copy.docxLB225 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-168 governing duplicate vehicle certificates of title. It continues to authorize the Department (state motor vehicle department) or any county treasurer to issue duplicates on a department-prescribed form upon payment of the fee set in §60-156, and requires the application to be signed by the applicant or an authorized signer under §60-151. County treasurers may issue duplicates with department approval or when title records have been destroyed under §60-152 upon sufficient proof; applicants lacking proof may apply directly to the Department, which may authorize a county treasurer to issue a duplicate. Duplicates will show only unreleased liens; procedures for new purchasers and indemnity/cancellation remain. The bill repeals the original section. No changes to appropriations or funding are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB226_IntroLB226_Intro_Copy.docxLB226 permits courts to set aside convictions or juvenile adjudications for certain "concealed weapon" offenses and requires courts, upon granting relief, to notify and order sealing by relevant agencies. Agencies named: county, district, and separate juvenile courts (venue for motions); Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice; Nebraska State Patrol; local law enforcement agencies; county and city attorneys. The bill expands sealing procedures (including for victims of sex trafficking and pardoned persons) and authorizes motions to seal once convictions are set aside. It creates a private cause of action under the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act, (1) waives sovereign immunity for the state, its agencies, political subdivisions, officers, and employees, (2) excludes such claims from the State and Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Acts, and (3) sets a four‑year statute of limitations (with a January 1, 2029 backstop for certain governmental-capacity claims). No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds procedures allowing courts to set aside and then order sealing of convictions or juvenile adjudications for certain "concealed weapon" offenses, with filings made in the county, district, or separate juvenile court where convicted. Cites and conditions application of the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act and creates private liability where a state agency, political subdivision, or their officers/employees fail to follow those rules. Consent is given to join the state, any state agency or political subdivision, and their officers/employees as defendants; sovereign immunity is waived for such actions. Claims under this provision are excluded from the State Tort Claims Act and Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act and are subject to a limitations deadline (generally four years, or by Jan 1, 2029 for certain older accruals). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB227_IntroLB227_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB227 amends carrier statutes to address Medicaid-related transportation contracts with the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). Key provisions: - Regulated motor carriers may receive a designation of authority to provide Medicaid nonemergency medical transportation (NEMT) only for contracts with (i) DHHS, (ii) DHHS-contracted Medicaid managed-care organizations, or (iii) DHHS agents per section 75-303.01. - In evaluating such designations, the Public Service Commission must consult with the Director of Medicaid and Long-Term Care (or designee) of DHHS’s Division of Medicaid and Long-Term Care. - Applicants seeking NEMT authority bear the burden to show the service meets public demand; protestants must show existing carriers meet the need or that the applicant would impair existing operations. - Transportation network companies or participating drivers must obtain specific commission authorization before transporting persons under contract with DHHS or its contractors; the commission must grant authorization unless protestants demonstrate harms as specified. - No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds a requirement that when the commission considers authorization for providers of Medicaid nonemergency medical transportation (NEMT) under a contract with the Department of Health and Human Services, a Medicaid managed‑care organization contracting with the department, or another agent acting for the department per §75‑303.01, the commission must consult with the Director of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care (or designee) of the Division of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB228_IntroLB228_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB228 amends tax-incentive audit definitions to reference the Department of Labor as the official source for several data points: (1) "Distressed area" is determined by the Department of Labor under the Nebraska Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act; (2) "Full‑time worker" and "high‑quality job" require employment to be reported to the Department of Labor on two consecutive quarterly wage reports; (3) "Nebraska average weekly wage" is the Department of Labor's annual report (by Oct. 1); and (4) NAICS code designations for "high‑tech firm" and "renewable energy firm" are those assigned by the Department of Labor. No changes to Department of Labor funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a requirement to include planning documents and, if applicable, any correspondence between the office and an audited agency (e.g., Department of Labor) as part of the referenced records/submissions. No language in the added text changes funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor.
109-1-LB229_FinalLB229_Final_Copy.docxLB229 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-604 (Employment Security Law) to exclude "service by a marketplace network contractor for a marketplace network platform" from the definition of employment, provided four conditions and definitions for "marketplace network contractor" and "marketplace network platform" are met. Agencies or officials referenced: the commissioner (who may approve employer elections under §48-604(3)(a)), the Secretary of Labor (federal certification under section 3304), the Public Service Commission and its Division of Motor Carrier Services (referenced in §48-604(6)(q) regarding motor carrier rules), and federal agencies/Congress (in various federal-law cross-references). The bill contains no provisions changing funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a new carve‑out defining and treating "marketplace network contractors" as independent contractors when (1) there is a written independent‑contractor agreement with the marketplace network platform, and the platform does not set mandatory hours, bar outside work, or terminate for refusing a specific request; (2) defines "marketplace network contractor" and "marketplace network platform" by written agreement, digital‑only request intake, and absence of a physical platform business location; and (3) excludes services for employers listed elsewhere in the statute (subdivisions (4)(a), (4)(b), or §48‑603.01) and services for which federal taxes must be paid that are creditable against the Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) or required for full FUTA credit under the state Employment Security Law. Mentions FUTA and the state unemployment compensation fund/Employment Security Law; no new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB22A_FinalLB22A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill appropriates funds to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program 348, to implement Legislative Bill 22. For FY2025‑26 it provides $380,628 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (cash) and $694,972 federal funds. For FY2026‑27 it provides $774,002 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (cash) and $1,377,198 federal funds. Each year's amounts are designated as state aid and may be used only for that purpose. The appropriated funds may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates to the Department of Health and Human Services (Program 348) funds to implement Legislative Bill 22: FY2025-26 — $380,628 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (cash) and $694,972 federal; FY2026-27 — $774,002 cash and $1,377,198 federal. Each year’s amounts are earmarked for state aid only. Funds may not be used for permanent/temporary salaries or employee per diems. (Biennial totals: $1,154,630 cash and $2,072,170 federal; $3,226,800 combined.)
109-1-LB22_FinalLB22_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill designates the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) as the implementing agency for the Family Home Visitation Act and requires DHHS to: fund only evidence-based home visitation programs (including workforce and certification support); adopt rules; and submit electronic reports (due Feb. 15, 2026–2028) with program, outcome, demographic, and expenditure data. DHHS must file federal state-plan/waiver amendments: to implement targeted case management for evidence-based nurse home visiting services by Oct. 1, 2025 (for Medicaid postpartum mothers and infants ≤6 months) and for medical respite facility designation; DHHS is directed to expand Medicaid coverage (breast pumps, lactation consultations, continuous glucose monitors) with specified funding intents. Funding: the Legislature intends these services to be financed from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (MMCEPF), not the General Fund; MMCEPF’s uses are expanded to include evidence-based nurse home visiting and related services, and investment earnings are credited to the General Fund beginning Oct. 1, 2024.The additions establish the Family Home Visitation Act under the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). DHHS may fund only periodic, evidence‑based home visitation programs (defined by model fidelity, workforce training, certification, community links, standards, etc.) serving families with children ≤5 or pregnant persons; funds may be used for workforce development and provider certification. DHHS may adopt rules and must submit electronic reports to the Legislature (due by Feb 15, 2026, and through Feb 15, 2028) detailing program types, outcomes, populations served, expenditures, and related data. By Oct 1, 2025 DHHS must seek CMS approval for a Medicaid state plan amendment to secure federal matching funds for targeted case management providing nurse home visits to Medicaid postpartum mothers and infants ≤6 months, with legislative intent to fund these services from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (not the General Fund).
109-1-LB230A_FinalLB230A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill appropriates funds from the Department of Revenue Enforcement Fund to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to implement Legislative Bill 230. It provides $251,010 for FY2025-26 and $121,600 for FY2026-27. Of those appropriated funds, total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $88,600 for FY2025-26 and $91,400 for FY2026-27.Appropriates Department of Revenue Enforcement Fund money to the Department of Revenue (Program 102) to implement LB 230: $251,010 for FY2025-26 and $121,600 for FY2026-27. Limits salary and per diem spending from these appropriations to no more than $88,600 in FY2025-26 and $91,400 in FY2026-27.
109-1-LB230_FinalLB230_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns it primary administration and enforcement of the Kratom Consumer Protection Act, including rulemaking, requiring independent third‑party lab testing of suspected adulterated kratom products, and imposing civil penalties (up to $1,000 first, up to $5,000 second, $5,000–$20,000 for third and subsequent violations plus a three‑year processor sales prohibition). Violations require notice and, if requested, a hearing before the Tax Commissioner. The measure creates a Department of Revenue Enforcement Fund: tax‑amnesty receipts split (≥80% General Fund; 10% to the Enforcement Fund, capped $500,000; excess to General Fund); FY2005‑06 proceeds are appropriated to the Department to hire investigators/agents/auditors. Thereafter, 20% of new revenue attributable to those hires (cap $750,000) and 10% of specified contract proceeds are deposited to the Fund. The Fund may receive transfers/credits; investment earnings (beginning Oct 1, 2024) flow to the General Fund. The Department must issue annual program reports.Summary (Department of Revenue focus): - "Department" is defined as the Department of Revenue. - The Department may require an independent third‑party test of a suspected adulterated kratom product by a laboratory of the Department’s choosing. - The Department may adopt and promulgate rules to implement the Kratom Consumer Protection Act. - The Department is authorized to impose civil penalties on processors/retailers (up to $1,000 first, up to $5,000 second, $5,000–$20,000 for third/subsequent violations) and, for processors on a third violation, ban sales in-state for three years. Determinations require notice and a Tax Commissioner hearing if requested. - Money paid for kratom registration certificates (including forfeited fees) shall be used by the Department of Revenue to defray administrative costs of the Act.
109-1-LB231_FinalLB231_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and FinanceLB231 adopts the Uniform Special Deposits Act. The bill’s only explicit reference to the Department of Banking and Finance appears in the definition of “financial institution,” which includes banks, savings banks, building and loan associations, savings and loan associations, credit unions, trust companies, and digital asset depositories “chartered by the United States, the Department of Banking and Finance, or a foreign state agency.” No sections of the bill propose changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Banking and Finance.The bill enacts the Uniform Special Deposits Act and explicitly defines "financial institution" to include entities chartered by the Department of Banking and Finance (alongside U.S. and foreign chartering authorities). That means state‑chartered banks, savings associations, trust companies, credit unions, and certain digital asset depositories under the Department's charter are covered by the Act's rules on special deposits, beneficiary rights, obligations, limitations on liability, termination, and related procedures. No provisions in the added text create new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Banking and Finance.
109-1-LB232_IntroLB232_Intro_Copy.docxLB232 amends Nebraska insurance law to require insurers issuing life policies subject to assignment as security for indebtedness to provide known assignees at least 30 days’ advance notice of pending lapse/termination. Insurers may send electronic notice (assignee must request it in writing before default; request becomes effective within 10 business days) and may charge the owner up to $2.50 per notice. Assignees must promptly send a release upon termination of assignment. The bill also allows Nebraska residents age 65+ with individual premium-paying life policies to designate one third-party to receive notices of cancellation, nonrenewal, and conditional renewal (written designation and acceptance required; termination procedures specified). No state agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.Adds consumer protections for life insurance in two areas; no government agencies or departments are mentioned and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. Key additions: - Defines "life insurance policy" to include individual and group policies. Requires insurers to give any known assignee (for policies assigned as security) at least 30 days' notice of pending lapse/termination. Insurers must electronically notify assignees who request notice; insurers may charge the policy owner up to $2.50 per notice. Specifies written/electronic request procedures, effective timing, required info, and that assignees must mail a release upon termination of rights. - Defines "senior-citizen insured" (Nebraska resident age 65+) and permits such insureds to designate one third-party to receive notices of cancellation, nonrenewal, and conditional renewal. Specifies designation, acceptance, termination, dual transmission to insured and designee, and annual insurer notice of the option.
109-1-LB233_IntroLB233_Intro_Copy.docxLB233 amends statutes governing the Nebraska State Insurance Program (sections 84-1607, 84-1608, 84-1609). It transfers and consolidates provisions allowing optional, employee-paid special coverages into the group life (84-1607) and group health (84-1608) insurance provisions—examples include accidental death and dismemberment, additional life amounts, dental, disability, disability income replacement, and dependent coverage—with uniform availability and employee choice to elect or decline. Section 84-1609 is amended to require the Nebraska State Insurance Program to include coverage for in vitro fertilization beginning July 1, 2025. The bill repeals the original sections and declares an emergency. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.Requires the Nebraska State Insurance Program to include coverage for in vitro fertilization beginning July 1, 2025. The program is granted discretion in how it provides that coverage. No agencies beyond the Nebraska State Insurance Program are named and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes specified.
109-1-LB234_IntroLB234_Intro_Copy.docxLB234 (consolidated with Sec. 77-6906, R.R.S.) amends the Urban Redevelopment Act’s definition of “economic redevelopment area.” It directs use of data from the United States Bureau of the Census (most recent federal decennial census or American Community Survey 5‑Year Estimate) to identify qualifying areas where (1) the area’s unemployment rate is at least 150% of the Nebraska statewide rate and (2) the federal census tract’s poverty rate is 20% or higher. The bill also includes any federal census tract directly adjacent to such an area. It repeals the original section. No state agency funding changes, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a provision expanding the covered area to include any federal census tract directly adjacent to the area described in subdivision (1) (which itself is subdivided into (a) and (b)). No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text.
109-1-LB235_IntroLB235_Intro_Copy.docxLB235 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1446 (Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act). It permits the court to grant additional time for a trial on actions for possession beyond the prior 10–14 day window and retains bench trials (no jury). It narrows early execution of writs of restitution by allowing a writ to be executed fewer than ten days after issuance only if the court finds the defendant poses a true and imminent threat to the safety of other tenants, the landlord, or the landlord’s employees/agents, or if the parties give informed, express agreement. The writ continues to direct the constable or sheriff to restore possession. The plaintiff must follow the Disposition of Personal Property Landlord and Tenant Act and subsection (5) of §76-1414 when removing remaining personal property. No state agency funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. The original section is repealed.Adds an exception allowing a court to order a writ of restitution to be executed fewer than ten days after issuance only if: (a) the defendant poses a true and imminent threat to the safety of other tenants, the landlord, or the landlord’s employees/agents; or (b) the parties give informed, express agreement. No government agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations are mentioned or changed.
109-1-LB236_IntroLB236_Intro_Copy.docxLB236 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §13-910 (Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act) to permit tort claims previously barred by immunity when the harm from child abuse or sexual assault of a child is a proximate result of a political subdivision or its employee failing to exercise reasonable care to (a) control a person in its charge or (b) protect a person in its care, custody, or control. The bill preserves existing enumerated immunity exceptions (e.g., discretionary acts, inspections, recreational-activity claims) and retains prior Motor Vehicle Certificate of Title Act and State Boat Act references (including electronic dealer services under section 60-1507). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds civil liability where child abuse or sexual assault results proximately from a political subdivision—or its employee—failing to exercise reasonable care to (i) control a person it has taken charge of, or (ii) protect someone in its care, custody, or control from harm by a non‑employee actor. The provision targets political subdivisions (e.g., counties, municipalities) and their employees. No specific state agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes included.
109-1-LB237_IntroLB237_Intro_Copy.docxLB237 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §32-960 to permit counties to conduct elections by mail after the county election commissioner or county clerk applies to and receives approval from the Secretary of State. Applications must include a written plan and timetable and provisions for election notices and early-voting ballot applications.
