Approved counties must follow §§32-953 to 32-959 procedures, with the ballot receipt deadline set by §32-908(2). The election commissioner or county clerk must allow hand-delivery of ballots to their office; provide at least one secure 24-hour ballot drop-box beginning at least ten days before the election through the receipt deadline; maintain at least one in-person voting site at the commissioner’s or clerk’s office open on election day through the receipt deadline; and offer in-person early voting per §32-942. Additional drop-boxes or sites may be provided. The bill repeals the original §32-960. No funding or appropriation changes are included.The underlined addition repeatedly inserts the term “election commissioner” (multiple consecutive instances). No other government agency or department is referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations included.
109-1-LB238_IntroLB238_Intro_Copy.docxLB238 amends the Foster Care Review Act. It clarifies that the executive director of the office (responsible for foster care review) selects local foster care review board members (boards of 4–10) and must send member lists to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) and the Office of Probation Administration. It bars employees of the office, DHHS, residential child‑caring or child‑placing agencies, and courts from board appointment. Local foster care review boards are expressly exempted from the Nebraska Open Meetings Act. The bill preserves board duties to conduct foster care file audit reviews at least every six months, submit findings and recommendations to the court within 30 days, and request court review hearings when appropriate. It repeals original sections 43‑1304 and 43‑1308 and outright repeals section 43‑1306. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a provision stating that "local boards" are not considered public bodies for purposes of the Open Meetings Act. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB239_IntroLB239_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB239 revises DHHS duties for developmental disabilities services. DHHS must administer Medicaid HCBS waivers and set funding amounts using an objective assessment published on the department website and approved by the Governor's developmental disability advisory board or stakeholder group. The assessment may not reduce an individual's budget to the point of removal from a setting, must be person‑centered, include an independent mediated review administered outside the department, and require redeterminations within 30 days. DHHS must provide or contract service coordination (individuals choose the provider) and create an expedited form/process for funding‑priority one requests with a five‑calendar‑day response. The department must maximize federal funding and require eligible residents to apply for Medicaid and other benefits. If funds are insufficient for subsection (4)(d), DHHS must provide comparable day services and annually report by Sept. 15 to legislative committees the estimated need and net additional resources required.For the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): - Must publish the objective assessment formula on its website and obtain approval from the Governor’s developmental disability advisory board or the required stakeholder group. - Must ensure the assessment tool cannot reduce an individual’s budget so as to remove them from a setting. - Must offer residential settings as options for individuals in funding priorities 1, 2, 3, and 5, and make them available for priorities 4 and 6 through the assessment process. - Must complete redeterminations within 30 days and design the assessment to be person‑centered and consistent with the individual support plan. - Must create an expedited form/process for requesting funding‑priority‑one consideration and respond within five calendar days. - The assessment must include an independent mediated review administered outside DHHS; the individual/legal representative selects the review entity. No explicit changes to appropriations, funding levels, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB23_IntroLB23_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentThe bill directs the Department of Economic Development to establish a program to award grants to nonprofit organizations to operate bike‑sharing programs. The department must determine eligibility, require reporting to verify grant funds were used for their intended purpose, and provide a process for return of funds not used as authorized. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate $250,000 from the General Fund to the Department of Economic Development to establish this program.Requires the Department of Economic Development to create a grant program funding nonprofit-run bike‑sharing operations. The department will determine eligible nonprofit recipients, issue grants, require recipient reporting to verify proper use, and set a process for returning unspent or misused funds. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate $250,000 from the General Fund to the department to establish the program.
109-1-LB240_FinalLB240_Final_Copy.docxLB240 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §18-2147 (Community Development Law). Key agencies/entities: redevelopment authority (per §18-2103), county assessor, county board of equalization, county clerk, county treasurer, Property Tax Administrator, Tax Equalization and Review Commission, and cities (including metropolitan class). The bill prescribes that the authority must send notice of any provision dividing ad valorem taxes to the county assessor on Property Tax Administrator forms on or before July 1 of the year the provision takes effect. Failure to provide timely notice causes taxes for affected years to remain undivided and be paid to the public bodies; remaining tax-increment valuations use the last certified pre‑effective-year valuation. The bill reiterates allocation rules: base levy to public bodies, tax increment to an authority special fund to repay bonds/loans, interest/penalties to public bodies; division terms: up to 20 years for extremely blighted areas, otherwise up to 15 years. Act takes effect immediately.The added text consists solely of the phrase "All July." It does not mention any government agency or department, nor does it create or change any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB241_FinalLB241_Final_Copy.docxLB241 (2025) creates a data-privacy statutory framework that defines terms and grants certain private entities an exemption from liability for data-related claims, except when harm results from the private entity’s willful, wanton, or gross negligence. The bill was introduced in the One Hundred Ninth Nebraska Legislature and referred to the Banking, Commerce and Insurance Committee. No state agencies or executive departments are named in the provided text, and the bill contains no provisions establishing new appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations.Adds the phrase “willful, wanton, or gross negligence on the part of the private entity.” No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The insertion clarifies liability standard for private entities by requiring willful, wanton, or gross negligence.
109-1-LB242_IntroLB242_Intro_Copy.docxLB242 amends Nebraska tax law and reporting requirements, affecting county and municipal officials, the Property Tax Administrator, State Treasurer, Tax Commissioner, county treasurers, county boards of equalization, and county clerks/election commissioners. Key fiscal changes: a multi‑year School District Property Tax Relief schedule ($750M in 2024 up to $902M in 2029, then +3% annually), with counties retaining 1% of each county allocation for costs; the Property Tax Administrator certifies county disbursements to the State Treasurer by Sept. 15, paid in two equal installments (by Jan. 31 and Apr. 1). The bill revises property tax request authority calculations to add growth‑ and inflation‑based increases, expands allowable exceptions (including county attorneys/public defenders, behavioral‑health/substance‑abuse programs, matching grants, revenue replacement), caps unused carryforward at 5%, and allows limited conversion of prior restricted‑fund authority. Municipalities imposing or raising occupation taxes must post annual collection/use reports.Adds rules affecting political subdivisions' property-tax calculations and uses. Key changes: - Includes accumulated "excess valuation" existing July 1, 2025, in the increase-in-excess-valuation calculation for the governmental unit's first fiscal year on/after July 1, 2025 (see §18-2147). - Explicitly allows property-tax budgeting for substance-abuse prevention, behavioral health, opioid-use prevention, matching state and federal grants, and to replace prior-year revenue streams eliminated or reduced by legislation. - Permits political subdivisions to convert unused restricted funds authority (as of June 30, 2025, per §13-521) into unused property-tax request authority for fiscal years beginning on/after July 1, 2025, capped at 5% of the subdivision's total 2024 property tax levy. - Directs the county treasurer to retain 1% for costs and disburse remaining collected funds.
109-1-LB243_IntroLB243_Intro_Copy.docxLB243 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §23-367 to specify that special sidewalk assessments levied by county government may be collected in the same manner as the collection or foreclosure of county taxes against real estate. The bill repeals the original version of §23-367. No state agencies or departments beyond county governments are referenced, and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB244_IntroLB244_Intro_Copy.docxLB244 (Sanders) amends section 49-1402 of the Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act (Reissue Revised Statutes) to revise the Legislature’s findings regarding the need for increased accountability, disclosure, and prevention of conflicts of interest in state and local elections and governmental service. The bill repeals the original section and replaces the findings language to emphasize disclosure of campaign funding, prevention of corruption and appearance of corruption, and guidance for public officials and employees. No state agencies or departments are newly created or altered, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.The added text contains no references to any government agencies or departments and makes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The language appears incomplete or nonsensical and does not convey substantive policy or budgetary content.
109-1-LB245_FinalLB245_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureLB245 adopts by reference several National Institute of Standards and Technology handbooks (Handbook 44, Handbook 130, and Handbook 133, as of Jan. 1, 2025) for weights and measures. It requires that copies of the adopted handbooks be filed with the Secretary of State, the Clerk of the Legislature (filed electronically), and the Department of Agriculture. The bill contains no explicit appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations directed to the Department of Agriculture.For the Department of Agriculture: the bill adds higher inspection/permit fees and procedural rules for food-related and weighing/measuring permits. Annual permit fees for Salvage Operation, Commissary, and Establishment are raised to $171. Effective 2025, scale inspection fees are updated (new rates): up to 35 lb $20; multiunit scales $114; >35–1,000 lb $36; >1,000–4,000 lb $72; >4,000–50,000 lb $83; >50,000–150,000 lb $88; over 150,000 lb $192. Rounding rules (nearest dollar or one‑half dollar) and a provision voiding a weighing/measuring permit if fees remain unpaid 90 days after due date are added. Educational institutions, health care facilities, nursing homes, and governmental organizations are exempt from owner fees, but outside food service providers used by those entities must pay applicable fees. No direct appropriations or new budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB246_FinalLB246_Final_Copy.docxLB246 amends the Nebraska Pure Food Act (sections 81‑2,239, 81‑2,240, 81‑2,282) and the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act (section 87‑302) to add a statutory definition of "cultivated‑protein food product" and to classify such products as adulterated. The bill prohibits manufacturing, producing, importing, distributing, promoting, offering, or selling adulterated food—including cultivated‑protein food products—and makes violations a deceptive trade practice under state law. It retains references to the Food Code and Current Good Manufacturing Practice standards adopted by reference, harmonizes related provisions, and repeals the prior sections. No state agencies or departments are explicitly named in the bill, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a definition of "cultivated-protein food product" as a food resembling animal tissue but produced from manufacturing cells grown in vitro (including stem-cell–derived processes). Prohibits producing, importing, promoting, displaying for sale, or attempting to sell such products. Creates an additional civil consequence: violations committed in the course of business are also treated as deceptive trade practices, without altering liability under the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act. References enforcement/penalty via section 81-2,282. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes in the added text.
109-1-LB247_FinalLB247_Final_Copy.docxLB247 amends statutes administered by the Department of Environment and Energy governing solid-waste disposal fees and the Petroleum Release Remedial Action Cash Fund. Key agency actions and fiscal changes: - Imposes a disposal fee of $2.34 per specified unit of solid waste. Fee receipts: 65% to the Integrated Solid Waste Management Cash Fund (administered by the department) to cover department direct/indirect costs including spill response, CERCLA nonfederal cost‑share/operation & maintenance for Superfund sites, regulation, investigation, remediation and monitoring; department may seek cost recovery. - 35% to the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund for grants and reimbursements to political subdivisions (reimbursement disbursements capped at 5% of prior fiscal year disposal‑fee revenue; director to seek geographic distribution). - Petroleum Release Remedial Action Cash Fund (administered by the department): continues funding sources and allowable uses, and limits department CERCLA cost‑share/O&M payments to up to $1.5 million per fiscal year through June 30, 2025. Investment earnings credited to the fund; State Treasurer, State Fire Marshal, State Claims Board and state investment officer referenced for administration. The bill repeals the original sections, declares an emergency, and states an operative date of July 1, 2025, while taking effect upon passage and approval.Adds authority to provide cost‑share, operation, and maintenance funding for remediation of Superfund sites to cover nonfederal costs (including in‑kind services) under the federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (42 U.S.C. 9601 et seq.). The provision runs through June 30, 2025. No specific dollar appropriation is stated in the underlined text.
109-1-LB248_FinalLB248_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB248 amends section 71-1910 of the Child Care Licensing Act to explicitly define "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services. The bill repeals the original section and contains no provisions affecting funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department.Adds to the bill’s covered settings: programs located on military bases or other federal property, and facilities licensed as family child care providers by a branch of the U.S. Department of Defense or the U.S. Coast Guard. For the Department of Health and Human Services, this expands the scope of locations to which the bill’s requirements or benefits apply. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included in the added text.
109-1-LB249_IntroLB249_Intro_Copy.docxLB249 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act to require the Department (responsible for K‑12 state aid determinations) to establish and certify a new military impact funding stream beginning FY2025‑26 for districts receiving Section 7003 federal impact aid for federally connected active‑duty students. The Department must calculate, certify budget authority, and set applicable allowable reserve percentages on or before June 15, 2025, and March 1 annually thereafter; any prior certifications for FY2025‑26 are void. The bill also alters local system formula resource treatment for FY2023‑24 and FY2024‑25 and mandates the Appropriations Committee include the amounts necessary to fund the newly certified state aid in its budget recommendations. The act takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.Creates a military impact aid program, effective school fiscal year 2025-26 and thereafter, administered by "the department" (state education agency) to determine payments to school districts. Eligibility: district must have received a federal impact aid basic support payment under section 7003 of the federal Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA) in the prior year and educate federally connected children with parents on active duty. The payment formula: department computes a per‑pupil federal impact aid (prior year §7003 payment ÷ enrolled federally connected active‑duty pupils) and a per‑pupil general fund tax levy (prior year local property tax receipts ÷ fall membership excluding those federally connected pupils). Military impact funding = (per‑pupil tax levy − per‑pupil federal aid) × number of federally connected active‑duty pupils, floored at zero. No separate appropriation or new budget allocation language is specified.
109-1-LB24_IntroLB24_Intro_Copy.docxLB24 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§29-2262.06 and 29-2267 to (1) require courts to assess a $30 one-time administrative enrollment fee and monthly probation programming fees ($25 for standard probation; $35 for intensive supervision and for participants in non‑probation programs that use probation personnel under interlocal agreements funded per §29-2262.07); (2) direct clerks of court to remit collected fees to the State Treasurer for credit to the Probation Program Cash Fund; (3) preserve waiver authority where indigence or undue hardship (including limited income, work/school status, or physical/mental disability) is shown and bar revocation for nonpayment if the probationer is financially unable and so states under oath with a court finding; and (4) revise revocation procedure: revocation requires a hearing with clear-and-convincing proof, felony revocations for substance-abuse or noncriminal violations require the probationer to have served 90 cumulative days of custodial sanctions in the current term, and courts may extend probation at joint request until resolution if counsel or a valid waiver is present.Adds two court-administered protections: (1) Courts must waive fees referenced in subdivisions (2)(m) and (o) of §29-2262, in whole or part, for offenders previously found indigent in that case or when payment would be an undue hardship (limited income, work/school status, or disability). The waiver applies only while the probationer/participant cannot pay the monthly probation programming fee. (2) When a motion or information to revoke probation is filed, the probation term may be extended at the joint request of the probationer and the prosecutor until final resolution or the statutory maximum. The court must accept such extensions if the probationer has counsel or affirmatively makes the request freely, knowingly, and intelligently in open court. No state agencies beyond courts/prosecutors are newly created or any funding/appropriations changed.
109-1-LB250_FinalLB250_Final_Copy.docxLB250 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §8-126 to revise qualifications and oversight for bank directors. It requires reasonable efforts that a majority of a bank’s board have primary residences: in Nebraska, within 25 miles of the bank’s main office, in the main-office county, or in counties where branches are located. Directors must be of good moral character, with integrity and business experience. No person may serve as a director until the bank obtains approval from the Department of Banking and Finance. The Director of Banking and Finance may revoke approval after notice and hearing if a director acts unsafely or unauthorizedly, and may adopt rules and forms to implement the section. The bill repeals the original section. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The added text requires that "reasonable efforts shall be made" to accomplish a primary action across four listed options ((a), (b), (c), (d)). The fragment does not identify any specific government agency or department, nor does it include any funding, appropriation, or budget allocation language. No fiscal or administrative agencies are referenced and no changes to appropriations are indicated.
109-1-LB251_FinalLB251_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and Finance, Department of InsuranceLB251 centralizes and clarifies regulatory authority for the Department of Banking and Finance (DBF) and confirms limited Department of Insurance roles. The bill: defines "Department" and "Director" as DBF for multiple statutes; empowers the Director to adopt rules (including definitions and alignment with 12 U.S.C. §84/Regulation O as of Jan. 1, 2025); grants DBF emergency powers to act against failing or endangered Nebraska‑chartered institutions (conversion/merger, asset/liability transfers, possession) and, on notice from a primary regulator, against federal or out‑of‑state institutions, while preserving hearing and appeal rights. It requires franchise sellers to file a notice with DBF and pay a $100 filing fee (credited to the Securities Act Cash Fund), allows DBF to demand disclosure documents within 10 business days, and to deny/revoke/suspend exemptions with notice/hearing. Section 45‑101.04 exempts certain loan‑rate limits for DBF‑licensed entities and insurers; Section 44‑708 gives the Director of Insurance rulemaking authority over funding agreements by admitted life insurers. No appropriations or budget changes are included.Department of Banking and Finance - Adds procedural requirements: applicant banks and credit unions must submit an affidavit of publication and proof of payment (in a director‑prescribed form) for required notices. - Tightens collateral rules for the additional 10% lending limit: livestock (and receipts securing obligations) must maintain a current market value of at least 115% of the secured amount that exceeds specified concentration thresholds (25% of capital/surplus and capital notes/debentures or 15% of unimpaired capital and unimpaired surplus and capital notes/debentures). - Grants the director immediate (no‑hearing) authority to convert/merge charters, assets, branches, or ownership to facilitate acquisition where a primary regulator deems the out‑of‑state or federally chartered institution impaired or unsafe. - Clarifies naming use for applicants and fixes certain federal securities definitions to their Jan. 1, 2025 versions. Department of Insurance - No added text affects the Department of Insurance; no funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB252_IntroLB252_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB252 directs the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), when establishing and maintaining the Medicaid formulary and preferred drug list, to ensure FDA‑approved non‑opioid pain drugs are not disadvantaged or discouraged relative to opioids. Prohibited actions include designating a non‑opioid as nonpreferred if an opioid is preferred and imposing more restrictive utilization controls (e.g., prior authorization or step therapy) on non‑opioids than on opioids. The requirement applies immediately upon FDA approval and covers drugs provided under DHHS contracts with managed care organizations. No changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are contained in the bill.Requires the Department of Health and Human Services, when setting and maintaining the Medicaid formulary and preferred drug list, to ensure FDA‑approved non‑opioid pain treatments are not disadvantaged or discouraged compared with opioids. Prohibited actions include labeling a non‑opioid as nonpreferred when an opioid is preferred and imposing more restrictive utilization controls (e.g., prior authorization, step therapy) on non‑opioids than the least restrictive controls applied to opioids. The rule allows intra‑class preferences (opioid vs opioid, non‑opioid vs non‑opioid). It takes effect for a non‑opioid immediately upon FDA approval and applies to drugs provided under DHHS contracts with managed care organizations. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB253_IntroLB253_Intro_Copy.docxLB253 requires coverage of biomarker testing for diagnosis, treatment, management, or monitoring when supported by medical/scientific evidence, including FDA-labeled indications, FDA drug test indications/warnings, CMS national or Medicare administrative contractor local coverage determinations, and nationally recognized clinical guidelines. It directs Nebraska health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs to provide such coverage in ways that limit care disruptions and to post an exception process on their websites. Prior‑authorization decisions must be issued within 72 hours for nonurgent and 24 hours for urgent requests. The state medical assistance program must implement equivalent biomarker coverage by January 1, 2026; contractors must provide testing at the same scope/frequency, follow the same prior‑auth timeframes, and post the exception process on the Department of Health and Human Services website. No funding or appropriation changes are specified.Adds requirements that biomarker testing be covered when supported by medical/scientific evidence, including FDA-approved/cleared test indications and drug labels, CMS national coverage determinations or local Medicare administrative contractor decisions, and nationally recognized clinical guidelines. Requires the state medical assistance program (Medicaid) to cover biomarker testing by Jan 1, 2026, and obligates entities contracting with the program to provide equivalent scope, duration, and frequency. Sets prior‑authorization decision timelines (72 hours nonurgent, 24 hours urgent) and requires an exceptions/appeals process be posted on the Department of Health and Human Services website. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB254_IntroLB254_Intro_Copy.docxLB254 directs the Legislature’s intent to transfer state General Fund appropriations into the Rural Workforce Housing Investment Fund: $25 million for fiscal year 2025‑26 and $25 million for fiscal year 2026‑27. Funds are designated to provide workforce housing grants under the Rural Workforce Housing Investment Act. The bill includes an emergency clause making the act effective upon enactment. No specific executive agencies or departments are named.Legislature states its intent to transfer $25 million from the General Fund in FY 2025–26 and $25 million from the General Fund in FY 2026–27 into the Rural Workforce Housing Investment Fund. The funds are to be used for workforce housing grants under the Rural Workforce Housing Investment Act.
109-1-LB255_IntroLB255_Intro_Copy.docxLB255 expands uses of the Opioid Treatment Infrastructure Cash Fund and directs related state entities. Key provisions: - Creates/affirms the Opioid Treatment Infrastructure Cash Fund (funded by transfers from the Nebraska Opioid Recovery Trust Fund). - Authorizes appropriations from that fund to the Nebraska Supreme Court for problem‑solving courts to order medication‑assisted treatment (FDA‑approved medications plus counseling/behavioral therapies). - States legislative intent to appropriate $1,000,000 in FY2025‑26 and $1,000,000 in FY2026‑27 from the fund to the Supreme Court for that purpose. - Requires the State Court Administrator to ensure each judicial district has at least one problem‑solving court and to submit annual outcome reports to the Legislature. - Permits “the division” to fund public‑private opioid prevention/treatment infrastructure projects (including capital/renovation); limits administrative distribution costs to 5%. - Authorizes investment of fund balances by the State Investment Officer. Act takes effect immediately (emergency).Adds legislative intent and appropriation authority directing money from the Opioid Treatment Infrastructure Cash Fund to the Colorado Supreme Court to support problem-solving courts in ordering medication‑assisted treatment (FDA‑approved medication plus counseling and behavioral therapies) under section 24-1302. Specifically, it states the Legislature intends to appropriate $1,000,000 for FY 2025‑26 and $1,000,000 for FY 2026‑27 to the Supreme Court for this purpose.
109-1-LB256_IntroLB256_Intro_Copy.docxLB256 adopts the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact and creates a multistate commission to coordinate and advocate for Midwestern intercity and high‑speed passenger rail. Membership includes each state’s Governor (or designee), a gubernatorial private‑sector appointee, and two legislators. The commission will work with federal agencies, members of Congress, local elected officials, economic development organizations, and state departments/municipalities; may establish an office, hire staff, contract services, assess dues, accept federal/state/local grants and gifts, and must report annually to member Governors and legislatures. Finance: general operations are to be funded by appropriations from compacting states (equal apportionment) when authorized by each legislature; the commission must submit budgets to the officer designated by each party state’s law. Nebraska restrictions: the state may not participate in or appropriate funds for any compact rail project (including planning) unless a legislative bill specifically authorizes it. The bill creates the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact Cash Fund; the Nebraska State Investment Officer will invest fund balances per state investment law.Creates a Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact commission funded by equal appropriations from compacting states (when authorized by each legislature). The commission may accept donations, grants, gifts or appropriations from the federal government, any party state, or any department, agency, or municipality, but may not issue debt. It must submit budgets to the officer designated by each member state’s law. Nebraska-specific provisions bar the State of Nebraska from participating in or appropriating funds for any rail project (including planning) unless a legislative bill authorizes it. Establishes the Midwest Interstate Passenger Rail Compact Cash Fund (gifts, grants, bequests, or legislative transfers) to support compact initiatives; funds are investable by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act.
109-1-LB257_FinalLB257_Final_Copy.docxThis bill directs state licensing and enforcement actions across multiple agencies: - Department (credentialing): with board recommendations, may issue licenses/certificates based on out-of-state licensure for marriage and family therapists and other mental-health credentials, and implements interstate compact privileges for counselors and occupational therapists. The board gains rulemaking authority over training/certification for occupational therapy modalities (including dry needling) and supervision/delegation limits. - Department (child care licensing): requires written proof of liability insurance ($100,000 per occurrence) before licensing and continuous coverage thereafter; allows State/political subdivisions to use risk pools or self-insure; inspectors must verify coverage at unannounced inspections and may suspend licenses if coverage is not restored within three business days. - Nebraska State Patrol/FBI: fingerprinting for national criminal history checks for child care staff, with checks every five years; checks are portable. Department may seek federal funds to offset fingerprinting costs. - State Fire Marshal and local environmental health personnel: may perform delegated fire and sanitation inspections.Added provisions assign duties to "the department" (acting with the recommendation of "the board") to issue licenses or certificates by endorsement to marriage and family therapists and to certify occupational therapists for specific modalities (including dry needling) when board-approved training/exams are met. Inspectors acting for the department must verify required liability insurance at unannounced inspections and investigations; the department will notify licensees and suspend licenses if proof is not provided within three business days, restoring licensure upon verification. The bill repeatedly references the board, the department, and inspectors; no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB258_FinalLB258_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborThe bill directs the Nebraska Department of Labor to calculate and publish, no later than October 15 of each year beginning October 15, 2026, the minimum wage rate that will take effect the following January 1. No provisions in the bill explicitly change funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor.Creates two new wage schedules the Department of Labor would implement and enforce: - Youth minimum wage: employers may pay 14–15‑year‑olds $13.50/hour; beginning Jan 1, 2030 and every fifth year thereafter the youth rate rises by 1.5% (rounded to the nearest cent). - Training wage: set at $13.50/hour through Dec 31, 2026; beginning Jan 1, 2027 and annually thereafter it increases by 1.5% (rounded to the nearest cent). No appropriation, funding, or budget allocation language is included in the added text.
109-1-LB259_IntroLB259_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the "Faithful Delegate to Federal Article V Convention Act," establishing how Nebraska's legislative delegates and alternates to a U.S. Article V convention are chosen, instructed, and removed. Key state bodies and roles: - Legislature: adopts delegate instructions, elects delegates/alternates (based on Committee on Committees' nominations), determines unauthorized votes, fills vacancies. - Committee on Committees: nominates one delegate and one alternate per legislative caucus. - Article V Convention Committee: composed of elected delegates/alternates; elects chair and vice-chair. - Executive Board of the Legislative Council + Lieutenant Governor: serve as the advisory committee when the Legislature is not in session (chair is executive board chair; Lt. Gov. breaks ties). - Secretary of State: receives delegates' signed oaths; Speaker must notify the committee chair and convention presiding officer of disqualifications. References existing expense reimbursement statutes (secs. 81-1174 to 81-1177). Delegates receive no compensation; no appropriations or new funding are included. Prohibits accepting gifts from registered lobbyists.Creates the "Faithful Delegate to Federal Article V Convention Act" and delegates responsibility to state legislative bodies and officers. Key agencies/departments and roles: - Legislature: adopts instructions, elects delegates/alternates, determines unauthorized votes, fills vacancies. - Committee on Committees (Legislature): nominates one delegate and one alternate per legislative caucus. - Executive Board of the Legislative Council + Lieutenant Governor: serve as the advisory committee (chair = executive board chair); Lieutenant Governor breaks ties; advisory committee acts only when Legislature is not in session and requires six votes to find an unauthorized vote. - Secretary of State: receives executed oaths. - Speaker of the Legislature: must notify Article V Convention Committee chair and the convention presiding officer of disqualifications. Also references lobbyist registration (Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act) and federal offices (Secretary of the U.S. Senate, Clerk of the U.S. House). No new appropriations or funding increases; delegates are unpaid but may be reimbursed under existing statutes (secs. 81-1174 to 81-1177).
109-1-LB25_IntroLB25_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB25 appropriates $5,000,000 from the General Fund for FY2025-26 to the Department of Administrative Services, Program 245, exclusively for state aid to support interoperable communications for volunteer departments (per section 35-901) via a grant program. Grants may fund mobile radios, programming, installation and related equipment, require a one-to-one local match, and are capped at $3,500,000 per applicant. The appropriation is restricted to the stated purpose. The act contains an emergency clause making it effective upon enactment.Appropriates $5,000,000 General Fund for FY2025‑26 to the Department of Administrative Services (Program 245) for a state aid grant program to fund interoperable communications for volunteer departments (per §35‑901). Funds may only be used to provide mobile radios, programming, and installation. Grants require a 1:1 local match and are limited to a maximum award of $3,500,000 per applicant.
109-1-LB260_FinalLB260_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of RevenueDepartment of Health and Human Services (DHHS): Multiple appropriations and authorizations for FY2023-24 and FY2024-25, including Medical Assistance (Program 348) totals of $3,564,427,540 (FY23-24: GF $1,000,583,595; CF $133,894,141; FF $2,429,949,804) and $3,170,728,603 (FY24-25: GF $1,059,760,230; CF $72,117,244; FF $2,038,851,129). FY24-25 state aid earmarks include Children's Health Insurance ($6,000,000 GF, $3,000,000 CF, $14,300,000 FF), Child Welfare Aid ($15,000,000 GF), Mental Health Operations ($4,500,000 GF), juvenile services salary limit ($500,000), pharmacy dispensing fee increases ($2,510,597 GF; $4,466,385 FF), and dental reimbursement increases ($3,054,187 GF; $5,611,661 FF). LB1087A funds for Program 348 and authority to certify/unexpended-balance transfers to Developmental Disability Aid are retained; DHHS must provide specified reports. Department of Revenue: Homestead Exemption (Program 108) appropriation of $2,000,000 General Fund for FY2024-25 (state aid). Department of Administrative Services (DAS): $100,000 Cash Fund for State Insurance (FY24-25); DAS must draw warrants and monitor Program 348, the budget administrator may administratively increase salary/per diem limits and execute transfers between DHHS programs as certified.Department of Administrative Services (DAS) - Adds a FY2024-25 $100,000 Cash Fund appropriation for Program 594 (State Insurance). - Grants the DAS budget administrator authority to administratively increase salary/per diem spending limits to cover certified payouts (e.g., accumulated vacation/sick leave) to former employees. Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) - FY2024-25 appropriations: Program 344 (Children’s Health Insurance) — $6,000,000 General Fund, $3,000,000 Cash Fund, $14,300,000 Federal funds (total $23.3M), designated as state aid. Program 354 (Child Welfare Aid) — $15,000,000 General Fund for state aid. Program 365 (Mental Health Operations) — $4,500,000 General Fund and a salary-limit of $6,300,000. Program 250 (Juvenile Services Operations) — salary-limit increase to $500,000. Department of Revenue - Program 108 (Homestead Exemption) — FY2024-25 $2,000,000 General Fund appropriation, designated as state aid.
109-1-LB261_FinalLB261_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Agriculture, Department of Banking and Finance, Department of Economic Development, Department of Insurance, Department of Labor, Information Management Services, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Department of Veterans' Affairs, Military DepartmentThe bill centralizes extensive budget and administrative authority in the Department of Administrative Services (DAS): drawing warrants, timing and directing major transfers and reappropriations, monitoring allotments and agency appropriations, administratively transferring certified unexpended balances and salary‑limit exceptions, accepting gifts and creating cash/revolving/trust funds, and overseeing OCIO/Information Management Services and state building/capital programs. Major appropriations include DHHS (biennial Medical Assistance ~$5.71B/$5.657B with GF ~$1.083B/$1.078B; Behavioral Health ~$104.6M/$104.1M; Developmental Disability Aid ~$535.5M/$544.2M; Public Health, $15M/year biomedical research; capital/transfer authorizations), DOT (salary caps ~$155.4M/$161.3M; Highway→Roads transfers $543.9M/$550.7M; construction ~$1.038B/$1.044B; carrier enforcement transfers), Department of Correctional Services (Operations GF ~$363M/$375M; NCCF capital $135M FY25‑26/$10M FY26‑27), Economic Development, Veterans’ Affairs (~$100M/$102.2M), Military Department emergency/match funds, DMV, Revenue, Labor, Banking & Finance, and Insurance with specified program and cash fund allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB262_FinalLB262_Final_Copy.docxLB262 appropriates funds to the Legislative Council (Program 1) for payment of Nebraska Legislature members' salaries and other payments under Chapter 68, article 6. It provides $632,982 from the General Fund for FY2025‑26 and $632,982 for FY2026‑27 to the Legislative Council. Expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from these appropriations are capped at $588,000 in each fiscal year. The act becomes operative July 1, 2025, and—due to an emergency clause—takes effect upon passage and approval.Appropriates $632,982 from the General Fund to the Legislative Council (Program 1) for each of FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 to cover legislative member salaries and related payments under Chapter 68, article 6. Although $632,982 is allocated each year, total expenditures from these funds for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $588,000 for FY2025-26 and $588,000 for FY2026-27. No other agencies are affected.
109-1-LB263_FinalLB263_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Revenue- Department of Administrative Services (DAS): The Director of Administrative Services is authorized to draw warrants against appropriate state treasury funds up to the act's appropriations; the State Treasurer shall pay such warrants. Workers' compensation premium assessments are prohibited from being paid from the listed programs. The budget division of DAS may administratively transfer General Fund appropriations and/or salary limits among Supreme Court Programs 3–7 (Programs for judges) upon written certification by the State Court Administrator that such transfers are necessary. - Department of Revenue: Program No. 13 (Tax Commissioner) appropriations and salary limits—FY2025‑26: General Fund $211,572; Cash Fund $64,212; Program Total $275,784; Salary Limit $212,972. FY2026‑27: General Fund $219,088; Cash Fund $66,436; Program Total $285,524; Salary Limit $219,613. The Tax Commissioner must seek additional legislative appropriation or higher salary limit via the deficit process if amounts are insufficient; DAS may not administratively increase the appropriation or salary limit without legislative authorization.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB264_FinalLB264_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Banking and Finance, Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Department of Veterans' Affairs, Military DepartmentLB264 centralizes fiscal authority in the Department of Administrative Services (DAS) budget administrator, authorizing timing, certification, administrative transfers, warrant draws, and crediting certain investment earnings to the General Fund. DAS is assigned numerous directed transfers (notably $147M to the General Fund in FY2026‑27, $10M to School Safety, $25M and $10M to the Governor’s Emergency Cash Fund, capital construction transfers, and intent to begin $200M Cash Reserve transfers to a Transformational Project Fund in FY2027‑28). Agency-specific provisions/funding: - DMV: new motor carrier system; multiple interfund transfers including $500K (FY25‑26)/$250K (FY26‑27) to GF, $3M transfers to DMV Cash Fund, $7.5M/$6M to operator license replacement fund, and $12.5M (FY26‑27) to GF. - Revenue: $2M/year (FY25‑26, FY26‑27) from Enforcement Fund to GF; creates Tobacco Products Admin Cash Fund with mandated transfers ($9.5M FY25‑26 & FY26‑27; $9M later) and an Unclaimed Property Cash Fund. - Banking & Finance: creates Settlement Cash Fund; transfers of $1M (FY25‑26) and $750K (FY26‑27) to GF. - Economic Development: administers ImagiNE Revolving Loan Fund, advises Economic Opportunity Program and Transformational Project reviews. - Transportation: administers Economic Opportunity Program with DED (up to $20M, ends 6/30/25). - Labor: administers Sector Partnership and Workforce Development cash funds; may transfer to GF or Opportunity Grant Fund. - Health & Human Services: receives directed transfers ($3.224M FY25‑26; $1.47M FY26‑27; additional $3.5M) and will administer a post‑acute care transition pilot (legislative intent $1M). - Veterans’ Affairs & Military Department: Veterans’ Affairs administers Military Installation Development & Support Fund requiring ≥50% public/private match; references Nebraska Military Department. - Correctional Services: may use Prison Overcrowding Contingency Fund for an inmate‑classification study.Summary of additions (by agency): - Department of Administrative Services (DAS): Budget division directs timing of numerous statutory transfers; DAS must create a subaccount in the Nebraska Soil and Water Conservation Fund for Environmental Trust transfers. - Department of Banking and Finance: $1,000,000 (FY25‑26) and $750,000 (FY26‑27) transferred from the Settlement Cash Fund to the General Fund; fund may be redirected (Legislature). - Department of Economic Development: Remaining Economic Development Cash Fund balance to General Fund (FY25‑26); JEDI $4.4M to General Fund; Customized Job Training and Intern Nebraska balances to General Fund; $25.5M from Military Installation Development & Support Fund moved to Site & Building Development Fund; ImagiNE loan fund $3M (FY26‑27) to General Fund. - Department of Labor: Transfers include $1.5M (Employment Security Special Contingent), $2.25M (Nebraska Training & Support FY25‑26; $500k FY26‑27), $1M Workforce Dev, $2M Workforce Dev → Nebraska Opportunity Grant, $200k Sector Partnership to General Fund. - Dept. of Correctional Services: $500,000 from Prison Overcrowding Contingency to General Fund. - Health & Human Services: $3.224M (FY25‑26) and $1.47M (FY26‑27) from HHS Cash Fund to General Fund; $4.0M Lead Service Line Cash Fund → General Fund. - Department of Motor Vehicles: Multiple transfers — Vehicle title/registration/system funds and Motor Carrier funds move millions to/from DMV Cash Fund and General Fund (notably $5.5M and $1.5M, $3M transfers to DMV, $12.5M DMV Cash Fund → General Fund FY26‑27; Operator's License Services fund receipt of $7.5M FY25‑26 and $6.0M FY26‑27); Ignition Interlock fund transfers ($500k; $250k). - Department of Revenue: $2.0M transfers from Enforcement Fund in each of FY25‑26 and FY26‑27 to General Fund; remaining Miscellaneous Receipts to General Fund; $250k Marijuana Admin → Property Assessment Division Cash Fund. - Department of Transportation: Transportation Infrastructure Bank and Surface Water Irrigation funds shifted to General Fund ($2M FY25‑26, $4.5M FY26‑27; $2.5M each year); Motor Carrier/vehicle system transfers noted; Economic Opportunity Program terminates June 30, 2025; Trail Development $3.35M to General Fund. - Department of Veterans' Affairs: No explicit transfers or appropriations added. - Military Department: $25.5M moved from Military Installation Development & Support Fund to the Site and Building Development Fund (FY25‑26).
109-1-LB265_FinalLB265_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill centralizes fiscal direction with the Department of Administrative Services (DAS): the budget administrator of DAS instructs the State Treasurer to execute multiple timed interfund transfers (notably $440,000,000 from the General Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund; $29,458,800 to the Nebraska Capital Construction Fund; $10,000,000 to the Critical Infrastructure Facilities Cash Fund; transfers into the Governor’s Emergency Cash Fund of $25,000,000 and $10,000,000; $28,000,000 from the JEDI Fund to the Cash Reserve Fund; and smaller transfers including $3,500,000 to the Health & Human Services Cash Fund and $11,320,000 from the Cash Reserve Fund to HHS). The Department of Labor (DOL) will administer a new Manufacturing Modernization and Workforce Development Pilot (grants up to $250,000) and consolidates several workforce-related accounts into a Workforce Development Program Cash Fund (effective July 1, 2025); unemployment tax receipts will flow there, uses are expanded, and the final average combined tax rate is reduced 5% for 2025–2029. The Department of Economic Development retains oversight of the Job Training Cash Fund and authorized transfers.- Department of Economic Development: establishes a Manufacturing Modernization and Workforce Development Pilot Investment Act grant program (applications 10/1/2025–11/1/2026). Grants match private financial support (up to $50,000 per award); projects begun before application are ineligible; grantees who cease to qualify must repay. The administering department may award up to $250,000 for the pilot from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund and adopt rules to implement the program. - Department of Labor: expands authorized uses of the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund (including the manufacturing pilot, unemployment benefits, studies, admin costs). It codifies the Nebraska Workforce Development Board’s annual grant proposal process (up to 18 proposals; commissioner discretion to approve/modify/reject; up to 3 approvals annually without board sign‑off, with reporting if they exceed 25% of unobligated balance). - Department of Administrative Services: the budget administrator may direct the State Treasurer to transfer $2,950,000 from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund to the General Fund on or after 7/1/2025 but before 6/30/2026, and $5,000,000 from the Cash Reserve Fund to the General Fund on or after 7/1/2026 but before 6/30/2027. - Department of Health and Human Services: no substantive changes or funding actions referenced.
109-1-LB266_FinalLB266_Final_Copy.docxLB266 prohibits local governments — defined as cities, villages, counties and any agency or subdivision thereof — from enacting or enforcing any ordinance (including resolutions, rules or regulations) that would have the effect of imposing rent controls on private property. Exceptions allow ordinances that (1) increase affordable housing supply via land‑use or inclusionary housing requirements, or (2) create voluntary, contractual programs in which private property owners agree to limit rents. The prohibition applies notwithstanding home‑rule charters, and any ordinance violating the bill is declared null and void. No state agencies are assigned new duties and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a statewide ban on local rent-control ordinances. Defines "local government" to include cities, villages, counties and their agencies/subdivisions, and bars them from enacting or enforcing ordinances that impose rent controls on private property, except where state law otherwise permits or under two exceptions: (1) ordinances adopted to increase affordable housing via land‑use or inclusionary housing requirements; and (2) voluntary, contract‑based programs landlord(s) opt into that limit rent increases. The provision overrides home‑rule charters and declares any violating ordinance null and void. No state agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations changes are specified.
109-1-LB267_IntroLB267_Intro_Copy.docxLB267 amends the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to allow tenants who are victims of domestic violence to remove a cotenant/occupant perpetrator from a rental agreement (upon providing a protective/ restraining order or certified documentation) and to require landlords to pursue possession against that perpetrator in court. Courts may award landlord court costs and reasonable attorney fees if judgment is entered. For non‑cotenant perpetrators, landlords must change unit locks within 24 hours upon tenant request and documentation; landlords may charge actual reasonable costs and may retain a key/code. Law enforcement may be required to escort a perpetrator reclaiming property. No state agency appropriations or other funding changes are included.No state agencies or departments are newly created or directed; the only government actor mentioned is a "law enforcement officer" (to escort a perpetrator reclaiming property). The additions let tenants with a protective order or certified domestic-violence documentation: (1) remove a cotenant perpetrator from the rental agreement (tenant provides documentation and written notice; landlord pursues eviction/possession actions only against the perpetrator; landlord must re-key and notify the tenant; landlord may recover court costs and attorney fees from the perpetrator; landlord not liable for good-faith actions); and (2) require immediate lock changes when the perpetrator is not a cotenant (landlord must change locks within 24 hours or tenant may do so and must provide the landlord a key/code). No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB268_IntroLB268_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB268 directs the Department of Health and Human Services to implement, beginning FY2025-26, an increase to Medicaid reimbursement rates for providers of developmental disability services equal to 150% of the state minimum wage. The bill states the Legislature's intent to appropriate an unspecified amount ("$XXX") of federal funds beginning in FY2025-26 to the department to fund those increased reimbursement rates; those appropriations are to be adjusted annually by the change in the core Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers and may be used only for this purpose. The act takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.For the Department of Health and Human Services: beginning in FY 2025–26 DHHS must raise reimbursement rates for developmental disability service providers to an amount equal to 150% of the state minimum wage. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate $XXX in federal funds starting FY 2025–26 to DHHS to cover these reimbursement increases. That appropriation is to be adjusted annually by the change in the core Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI‑W), and the funds are restricted for use solely to pay these provider reimbursement increases.
109-1-LB269_IntroLB269_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB269 directs that retailer notices of local sales/use tax changes or terminations may be provided via the Department of Revenue’s website (or other electronic means). It further requires the Tax Commissioner to adopt rules obligating the Department of Revenue to verify: (1) addresses contained in the State’s address‑based boundary database used to assign taxing jurisdictions; and (2) appropriate sales and use tax rates reported on returns when online or remote transactions are included. No appropriations or funding changes are specified.Requires the Tax Commissioner to adopt rules obligating the Department of Revenue to verify addresses in the state's address-based boundary database and to verify that appropriate sales and use tax rates are used on returns that include online or remote transactions. Adds a state-maintained zip code boundary database assigning each 5- and 9-digit ZIP to the correct tax rates/jurisdictions (to be used only as allowed above). For the streamlined sales/use tax agreement, the ZIP database must apply the lowest combined tax rate when multiple rates exist in an area. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are included.
109-1-LB26_IntroLB26_Intro_Copy.docxLB26 (Ballard) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-929.01 to broaden the term "health care professional" for purposes of criminal statutes (§§28-929, 28-929.02, 28-930, 28-931, 28-931.01). The bill (1) retains "emergency care provider" as persons licensed/classified under the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act, (2) explicitly includes physicians and other licensed/certified/registered practitioners who practice at a hospital or health clinic, and (3) adds any other employee of a hospital or health clinic to that definition. It references statutory definitions for health clinic (§71-416) and hospital (§71-419) and repeals the original section. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a new clause making “any other employee of a hospital or health clinic” explicitly covered/covered by the provision. No federal, state, or local agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in this addition.
109-1-LB270_IntroLB270_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Labor, Department of RevenueLB270 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-2711 with provisions affecting the Department of Revenue, Department of Labor, and Department of Administrative Services: - Department of Revenue: Expands audit access by requiring the Tax Commissioner to make tax returns/return information available to the Auditor of Public Accounts/Legislative Audit for audits of the Department of Revenue under specified statutes (including new references). Confidential returns must be audited on Department premises; audit work papers are to be stored securely in the Department of Revenue. The Department must also provide municipalities (via a certified municipal designee) sales/use tax permit and remittance information and is protected from liability for municipal disclosures. - Department of Labor: Permits disclosure of tax information to the Department of Labor as necessary to administer the Employment Security Law, Contractor Registration Act, or Employee Classification Act. - Department of Administrative Services: Employees are included among officers prohibited (Class I misdemeanor) from impermissible disclosure of tax return information. No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.Added language lets a municipality‑certified reviewer notify the Auditor of Public Accounts of any suspected irregularity or discrepancy found in the documents described earlier; the Auditor may then conduct an audit under the authority of subsection (11). There is no mention of the Department of Administrative Services, Department of Labor, or Department of Revenue in the added text, and no new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are authorized or referenced. No direct fiscal impact on those agencies is indicated.
109-1-LB271_IntroLB271_Intro_Copy.docxLB271 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-101 to add a prohibition on interference with railroad infrastructure, equipment, and personnel, establishes definitions, harmonizes related statutory language, and repeals the prior version of the section. The bill text as presented does not reference any specific state agencies or departments, nor does it include changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB272_IntroLB272_Intro_Copy.docxLB272 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77‑3506 to expand homestead tax exemptions tied to United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) disability ratings. Effective January 1, 2026, veterans rated at least 10% but less than 100% service‑connected disabled (and qualifying surviving spouses) are eligible for a partial exemption equal to the VA disability percentage. The bill requires VA certification of eligibility; applicants under subsection (2)(a) must reapply and recertify in years evenly divisible by five, while applicants under (2)(b)–(f) and the new (g) must apply annually but need VA recertification only in years evenly divisible by five. The original section is repealed. No changes to state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a tax exemption tied to VA disability and expands eligible veterans/surviving spouses. Specifically: - Exempts from taxation on qualifying homesteads a percentage of the exempt amount equal to the veteran’s disability rating as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs. - Effective January 1, 2026, expands eligibility to veterans discharged honorable/general who receive VA compensation for a service‑connected disability of at least 10% but under 100%, and to their unremarried surviving spouses or spouses who remarry after age 57. No agencies beyond the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs are referenced, and no funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB273_IntroLB273_Intro_Copy.docxLB273 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §30-3417 governing powers of attorneys‑in‑fact under powers of attorney for health care. Key government-related provisions: county courts retain final authority to adjudicate incapacity — a principal’s objection prevails over an attorney‑in‑fact’s decision unless the county court determines the principal is incapable (cross‑references §30‑3412). Health care providers are not required to accept an attorney‑in‑fact’s decisions until presented with a signed original or copy of the power of attorney. The bill also defers to a treating physician’s determination when life‑risk to a pregnant principal is asserted (limits decisions affecting an unborn child) and references §30‑3418 for end‑of‑life decision exceptions. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.Adds a medical-exception clause tying authorization to the principal’s treating physician: if an act would result in the death of the principal’s unborn child (and the unborn child is likely to die), it applies only when the principal’s treating physician determines the principal’s life is at risk. No government agencies or departments are referenced and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed.
109-1-LB274_IntroLB274_Intro_Copy.docxLB274 amends the Child Care Licensing Act's licensing, inspection, and background-check processes. Key agency actions and changes: - Department (state licensing agency) must require applicants to show liability insurance of at least $200,000 per occurrence before issuing a license and verify ongoing coverage at each unannounced inspection. If proof is not provided within three business days after notice, the department will suspend the license until verification. - Department may investigate licensees/applicants, delegate sanitation inspections to local environmental health personnel, and request fire-safety inspections from the State Fire Marshal. - Nebraska State Patrol will handle fingerprint transmission to the FBI for national criminal history checks; the department may seek federal funds to help cover fingerprinting costs and may adopt implementing rules with the State Patrol. - Background checks remain portable; no direct appropriations or new budget allocations are specified.Adds requirements that licensees must maintain required liability insurance while children are in their care. Department inspectors must request and verify current proof of insurance at every unannounced inspection and investigation. If a licensee cannot produce proof or coverage has lapsed, the department will notify the licensee and require proof within three business days; failure to do so results in license suspension. Licenses are reinstated when the department receives and verifies required proof per section 71-1911.03. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB275A_FinalLB275A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill appropriates General Fund amounts to the Department of Health and Human Services to implement LB275. For Program 33: $0 for FY2025‑26 and $329,347 for FY2026‑27, with a cap on permanent/temporary salaries and per diems of $0 in FY2025‑26 and $95,442 in FY2026‑27. For Program 354: $0 for FY2025‑26 and $629,165 for FY2026‑27, with the FY2026‑27 amount designated solely as state aid; no FY2025‑26 state aid is provided. Funds in Program 354 may not be used for state employee salaries or per diems.DHHS appropriations added to implement Legislative Bill 275 (109th Leg., 2025): - Program 33: $0 GF for FY2025‑26; $329,347 GF for FY2026‑27. Of the FY2026‑27 funds, up to $95,442 may be used for permanent/temporary salaries and per diems (no salary spending authorized in FY2025‑26). - Program 354: $0 GF for FY2025‑26; $629,165 GF for FY2026‑27, all designated as state aid and restricted to that purpose. No portion of the Program 354 appropriation may be used for permanent or temporary state employee salaries or per diems. All funding is General Fund and applies only in FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB275_FinalLB275_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB275 amends §43-907 to impose specific duties on the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) for children under its charge. DHHS must screen each child for Social Security benefit eligibility within 60 days, submit applications and appeals as needed, and serve as representative payee when appropriate. As payee, DHHS must manage, use, conserve, and hold benefit payments separately (including trust accounts), avoid exceeding federal asset/resource limits, conserve specified minimum percentages by age (20% at 14+, 30% at 16+, 40% at 17+, 50% at 18+), and maintain/produce accounting and notices to the juvenile court at each review. DHHS must publish a beneficiary request form and adopt rules by October 1, 2026, and must maximize federal Title IV‑E funding before using General Funds for implementation costs.Adds duties for the Department of Health and Human Services concerning children in its charge who receive Social Security benefits: screen each child within 60 days and apply/appeal for benefits as needed; provide age‑appropriate written notices and accounting (including total spent and itemized expenditures) and permit requests for access to funds. When DHHS is representative payee it must hold benefits separately (trust account), conserve specified minimum percentages by age (14+: 20%; 16+: 30%; 17+: 40%; 18+: 50%), avoid exceeding federal asset/resource limits using vehicles like PASS, ABLE, IDAs, special‑needs trusts, and dedicated back‑payment accounts, and consult beneficiaries at least every six months. Youth 14+ may petition juvenile court to direct use of funds. DHHS must provide exit notices and create a public request form by Oct 1, 2026. Funding: DHHS must seek federal Title IV‑E funds before using General Funds; no new appropriation is specified.
109-1-LB276_IntroLB276_Intro_Copy.docxLB276 creates the Municipal Police Oversight Act and amends law enforcement reporting and public-disclosure duties. Key agencies/departments and requirements: - Cities (metropolitan and primary class): must establish seven-member citizen police oversight boards by Jan 1, 2028 (appointment by city council). Boards may subpoena, inspect police records (including personnel), investigate complaints/shootings/misconduct, consult Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice and Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council, and report findings to police departments, mayors, city councils and county attorneys for criminal referral. Reports and agency responses are public; meetings subject to the Open Meetings Act. - City attorneys, county attorneys, and the Attorney General: must maintain and publicly post Brady/Giglio lists (updated at least monthly). Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice to adopt rules by Sept 1, 2025. - Chiefs, sheriffs, Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety, and agency heads: must file personnel changes with the training-center director within seven days; retain separation records five years; permanently retain records relevant to certification revocation and report terminations/resignations for serious conduct to the commission within 30 days. - Nebraska Commission: must post a public registry of officers with surrendered/revoked certifications, convictions, or adjudicated serious misconduct (with agency affirmation and status); council to allow challenge procedure and notify commission within 30 days of actions. - Revisor of Statutes: assigned to place the new act in chapter 18. Also prohibits issuance of no‑knock warrants by judges or magistrates. No funding or appropriation changes included. The act takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.Creates a Municipal Police Oversight Act requiring each metropolitan/primary class city to establish a seven-member citizen oversight board by Jan 1, 2028, appointed by the city council. Boards may subpoena, inspect police records (including personnel files), investigate misconduct/shootings, publish reports, submit evidence to county attorneys, and consult standards from the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice and the Nebraska Police Standards Advisory Council. City police departments must respond to board recommendations. City, county attorneys, and the Attorney General must each maintain and publicly post monthly-updated Brady/Giglio lists on their websites beginning Sept 1, 2025; the Nebraska Commission must adopt rules by that date. Oversight boards are immune from good-faith liability; conflicting employment or bargaining provisions are void. No appropriations or funding changes are included.
109-1-LB277_IntroLB277_Intro_Copy.docxLB277 amends procedures for grand juries when a death occurs during apprehension or while in custody. It requires district courts to call a grand jury upon certification by the county coroner/coroner’s physician. The court must appoint a special prosecutor (minimum five years’ criminal/felony litigation experience) who will select a team of three peace officers trained in homicide investigation from outside the jurisdiction. Local law enforcement must secure the scene, preserve evidence, investigate, and transfer assembled materials to the special prosecutor. A grand jury must be impaneled within 30 days unless extended. Any involved officer or detention personnel may not return to duty until grand jury proceedings conclude. If a licensed physician certifies a natural death and the county attorney (or staff) presents that finding, a special prosecutor need not be appointed. No funding or appropriation changes are specified.Adds requirement that the court appoint a special prosecutor with at least five years’ experience in criminal litigation, including felony cases (the text contemplates use of prosecutors from outside the local jurisdiction). It requires that any law enforcement officer or detention personnel involved in a death not return to duty until the grand jury finishes its investigation. Agencies implicated: the courts (appointing authority), prosecutor’s offices, law enforcement agencies, and detention/corrections authorities. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB278_IntroLB278_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB278 amends section 44-4109.01 (insurance provider participation rules) to preserve a pre-termination opportunity for a provider to enter and complete a corrective action plan, except in cases of fraud, imminent harm, or when the provider’s ability to provide services has been restricted by action (including probation or compliance agreements) by the Department of Health and Human Services or another governmental agency. No provisions in the bill reference funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds/clarifies that “provider” includes (a) a practice and (b) an individual holding a visiting faculty permit under §38‑2045, and includes a provision beginning “An insurance arrangement shall not be prohibited…” (text fragmentary). No language in the provided addition addresses the Department of Health and Human Services, nor does it include any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB279_IntroLB279_Intro_Copy.docxLB279 amends the Motor Vehicle Registration Act to require only one license plate to be displayed on registered motor vehicles and trailers (generally on the rear), clarifies that when two plates are issued only one must be prominently displayed, and retains front-placement for certain apportionable vehicles and truck‑tractors. The bill references the department (responsible for issuing plates and designing/procuring decals), the director (to secure competitive bids under the State Procurement Act when plates change), county treasurers (to furnish decals), the State Treasurer, and the Highway Trust Fund. Existing law’s optional single‑plate authorization for certain passenger cars — including the $50 annual nonrefundable fee plus decal cost remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Highway Trust Fund — is preserved. No new appropriations or other budget reallocations are created.Change clarifies that only one license plate is required (replacing language requiring "at least one"). No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes in the added text.
109-1-LB27_IntroLB27_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill amends the Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act and related statutes. It creates the Nebraska Rural Health Advisory Commission and expands the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund’s permissible uses to include loan repayments under the Act. The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) will execute and pay loan-repayment agreements (exempt from the State Procurement Act) and must use only specifically appropriated monies for dentist-specific agreements. General loan-repayment agreements require equal state and local funding and DHHS makes payments directly to recipients. New dentist-specific agreements (for dentists with <5 years’ practice and no prior program assistance) require five years’ practice in Nebraska, specified Medicaid patient thresholds, payments up to $60,000/year for up to five years, and full repayment with 8% simple interest on breach. The Legislature intends a $1.5 million appropriation from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund to DHHS for FY2025‑26. The state treasurer and state investment officer administer the fund.Creates a DHHS-administered loan repayment program for dentists who treat Medicaid patients. Eligible dentists must have practiced <5 years and not previously received Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act aid. Agreements (exempt from the State Procurement Act) require five years of in-state practice and a commission‑specified minimum share/number of Medicaid patients. DHHS pays recipients directly for qualified educational debt—up to $60,000 per year for up to five years (maximum $300,000). Recipients must document use of funds. Breach requires repayment to the state of 100% of funds plus 8% simple annual interest; obligations cancel on death or total permanent disability. DHHS may only use specifically appropriated funds; Legislature intends to appropriate $1,500,000 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for FY2025‑26 for this purpose.
109-1-LB280_IntroLB280_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill amends Neb. racetrack gaming law to (1) require each authorized gaming operator to obtain and pay for an annual independent CPA audit of its Nebraska operations, including internal control reports, and to submit the audit electronically to the State Auditor (Auditor of Public Accounts) and the State Racing and Gaming Commission within six months (unless extended); (2) direct the Auditor to review audits for calculation errors or deficiencies—particularly those affecting gross gaming revenue or tax—and to report findings to the Governor, Legislature, and the Commission, and to exercise prescribed examination powers over operator books, records, funds, and accounts; and (3) explicitly permit the Racing and Gaming Commission to use the Racing and Gaming Commission's Racetrack Gaming Fund for administration and for any audit, examination, or review authorized under the new audit section. Investment earnings of the fund are credited to the General Fund beginning Oct. 1, 2024.Requires each authorized gaming operator to obtain, at its own expense, an annual independent CPA audit (including internal control report) of all Nebraska financial transactions. The audit must be submitted electronically within six months after fiscal year-end to the Auditor of Public Accounts and the gaming commission (with possible written extension from the Auditor). The Auditor of Public Accounts must review the audit for calculation, accounting, or other deficiencies—particularly those affecting gross gaming revenue or the gaming tax—and report results electronically to the Governor, the Legislature, and the gaming commission. No new appropriations or government funding changes are specified; operators bear audit costs.
109-1-LB281_IntroLB281_Intro_Copy.docxLB281 revises Nebraska nursing governance. It consolidates and clarifies statutory references to the Board of Nursing (amending sections 38-204, 38-605, 38-703, 38-904) and removes separate qualifications and duties for a Board of Advanced Practice Registered Nurses. The State Board of Health remains responsible for appointments and must attempt representative membership. The Board of Nursing composition is specified: eight registered nurses, two licensed practical nurses, and three public members, with registered-nurse seats delineated (including four advanced practice registered nurses). It updates qualifications and staggered terms for APRN members (effective Jan 1, 2026) and sets preferred APRN representation (CRNA, nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist, certified nurse midwife). The board’s duties are harmonized, including administering the Nurse Licensure Compact and reporting to the coordinated licensure information system; the statutory allowance for disclosure of personal identifying information to that system is included. Sections 38-205, 38-206, and 38-2307 are repealed.
