No funding or appropriation changes are made.Starts Jan. 1, 2026, terms for advanced practice registered nurses on the board are staggered: initial appointments of one 3‑year, one 4‑year, and one 5‑year term; all subsequent appointments are five years. The board’s preferred APRN composition is one certified registered nurse anesthetist, one nurse practitioner, one clinical nurse specialist, and one certified nurse midwife; if that mix isn’t possible, vacancies may be filled from the applicant pool. No state agencies beyond the board are newly created or referenced, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB282_IntroLB282_Intro_Copy.docxLB282 (2025) authorizes the State Department of Education to accept applications, on department-prescribed forms, from K–12 teachers employed at approved or accredited public, private, denominational, or parochial Nebraska schools for reimbursement of up to $300 for teacher‑purchased school supplies (receipts required), effective for the 2025–26 school year. The State Board of Education must develop and post a policy on qualifying supplies and may adopt rules and regulations to implement the program. The bill contains an emergency clause to take effect upon passage. No specific appropriation or funding source is stated.Beginning with the 2025–26 school year, teachers in approved or accredited K–12 public, private, denominational, or parochial schools may apply to the State Department of Education (on department-prescribed forms) for reimbursement up to $300 for school supplies, with receipts required. The State Board of Education must create a policy (to be posted on the State Department of Education website) defining qualifying supplies and may adopt rules and regulations to implement the program. The provision specifies the reimbursement amount but does not identify funding sources or appropriate additional appropriations.
109-1-LB283_IntroLB283_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB283 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §68-901 (Medical Assistance Act) to require the Department of Health and Human Services to file specified state plan amendments. The bill directs DHHS to take those filing actions as prescribed and repeals the original section. No provisions in the bill reference changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB284_IntroLB284_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB284 appropriates funds to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), Program 514: $500,000 from the Health and Human Services Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 and $500,000 from the same fund for FY2026‑27 (total $1,000,000) as Cash Funds designated as state aid. The aid is limited to a single nonprofit (501(c)(3)) providing health screenings, sports competitions, educational opportunities, and leadership training for persons with developmental or intellectual disabilities. The appropriation specifically prohibits using these funds for state employee permanent/temporary salaries or per diems. The act takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.Appropriates $500,000 in FY2025-26 and $500,000 in FY2026-27 from the Health and Human Services Cash Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program 514. Funds are state aid to a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that provides health screenings, sports competitions, educational programs, and leadership training for persons with developmental or intellectual disabilities. Each $500,000 is cash-designated solely for state aid. The appropriation prohibits using these funds for state employee permanent/temporary salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB285_IntroLB285_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill bans marketing, sale, and Tobacco Products Tax Act certification of "flavored vapor products" (defined) that are electronic nicotine delivery systems. It directs the Tax Commissioner (and the cigarette tax division within the Tax Commissioner’s office) to refuse certification under section 77-4011.01 for such products and authorizes the cigarette tax division to revoke or suspend licenses for violations (including seizure and destruction of contraband cigarettes). Licensing penalties and revocation timelines are retained/clarified (e.g., specified multi‑year license‑bar periods for certain violations). Enforcement actions may include court‑ordered license revocation. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are provided.Adds a definition of "flavored vapor product" (ENDS with a taste/smell other than tobacco/menthol, marketed as such, or claimed by a manufacturer/seller). New prohibitions: holders of licenses under sections 28-1420 to 28-1429 are barred from marketing, advertising, or selling flavored vapor products; the Tax Commissioner is prohibited from issuing certifications under section 77-4011.01 for any ENDS that is a flavored vapor product; and manufacturers may not cause flavored ENDS to be sold at retail in the state. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB286_FinalLB286_Final_Copy.docxLB286 amends two statutes to impose application deadlines and clarifies reporting/fee handling. It directs the department (and its director) to accept Nebraska Innovation Hub (iHub) applications only through December 31, 2025, and requires the director to determine iHub designations and enter MOUs with approved applicants. It also bars new applications under the Nebraska Rural Projects Act after December 31, 2025, while allowing consideration and execution of any complete applications filed on or before that date. Application fees ($1,000 each) are collected by the director and remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Innovation Hub Cash Fund and the Nebraska Rural Projects Fund. Annual iHub reports are filed with the director, the chairperson of the Urban Affairs Committee, and posted with notice to the Governor and Legislature. Original sections are repealed.Adds a deadline extension: the director will accept applications under this section through December 31, 2025. No specific government agency or department is named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB287_IntroLB287_Intro_Copy.docxLB287 amends the Nebraska Housing Agency Act (section 71-1572) to assign specific bed‑bug responsibilities to the housing agency for a city of the metropolitan class. It defines "bed bug" and "pest control professional" (a commercial applicator licensed under the Pesticide Act). Requirements include pre‑rental visual inspections and disclosure of adjacent-unit infestations; prohibition on showing or renting units known or reasonably suspected to be infested; complaint response timelines (acknowledge and inspect within five days; remediate within 14 days if infestation is confirmed); inspection of adjacent units; advance notice to tenants for entry; five‑day tenant notification of pest‑professional determinations; and two‑year retention of complaint and treatment records. The bill makes the housing agency financially responsible for investigation and remediation costs. The original section is repealed.Adds duties for the housing agency of a city of the metropolitan class regarding bed bugs. Defines "bed bug" and "pest control professional" (must be a commercial applicator licensed under the Pesticide Act). Requires pre‑rental visual inspections, prohibits showing/renting units known or reasonably suspected to be infested, and mandates disclosure to prospective tenants if adjacent units are infested or being treated. On notification of suspected infestation the agency must: acknowledge the complaint within 5 days; inspect or retain a licensed pest control professional within 5 days; inspect adjacent units within 5 days; provide remediation within 14 days of confirmed infestation; give tenants advance notice of entry; notify affected tenants of the professional's determination within 5 days; and keep written records (including chemicals used) for two years. The housing agency is financially responsible for investigation and remediation costs.
109-1-LB288A_FinalLB288A_Final_Copy.docxAppropriates funds to the Nebraska Department of Economic Development, Program 601, to implement Legislative Bill 288. For FY2025-26: $97,030 from the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund and $103,200 from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. For FY2026-27: $118,110 from the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund and $126,410 from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. Limits total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from these appropriated funds to $103,520 in FY2025-26 and $138,030 in FY2026-27.Appropriates funds to the Department of Economic Development (Program 601) to implement Legislative Bill 288. FY2025‑26: $97,030 from the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund and $103,200 from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (total $200,230). FY2026‑27: $118,110 from the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund and $126,410 from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (total $244,520). Caps permanent/temporary salaries and per diems charged to these appropriations at $103,520 for FY2025‑26 and $138,030 for FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB288_FinalLB288_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of Labor- Department of Economic Development (DED) responsibilities: - Administer the Nebraska Affordable Housing Act and Affordable Housing Trust Fund: fund applications in priority order, contract for services or provide funds to other governmental entities, recapture misused or unexpended funds (crediting recaptures to the Trust Fund), and proportionally recapture funds for incomplete projects. - Annual reporting requirements: include funded applications, recipients, locations, amounts, leveraged funds, units/occupancy, expected rents/payments, projected employment/community investment, revenue into the Trust Fund, total applications, year-end balance, appropriated funds actually expended, DED’s current administration budget and planned use/distribution of funds, plus project summaries. - Establish and award workforce housing investment grants (director authority); grant caps ($10M per grantee over two years), changed matching requirements (50% pre‑7/19/24; ≥25% on/after 7/19/24), and unallocated funds roll forward. - Create/administer the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund, including a subaccount for Economic Recovery Act land-prep, apply interest earnings to grants, require return of grants to General Fund if inactive 24 months, and transfer remaining fund balance to the General Fund on July 1, 2029. - Require annual certification and reporting from nonprofit grantees to be included in DED’s status report. - Department of Labor (U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics): - DED shall annually update specified housing cost thresholds using the Producer Price Index for all commodities published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.Department of Economic Development - Prohibits DED from imposing other department program application/requirement conditions on new construction or rental-conversion projects receiving Affordable Housing Trust Fund (AHTF) funds. - Grants DED enforcement options for misuse of AHTF funds, including recapture, up to 24-month disqualification from AHTF applications, and other measures that avoid undue reputational harm; illegal acts (e.g., fraud, theft) remain separately actionable. - Requires DED to recapture a pro rata share of awarded AHTF funds when a recipient fails to complete agreed housing and to credit recaptured dollars back to the AHTF. - Requires recipients to recapture and return AHTF-provided homebuyer assistance from net sale proceeds when the assisted home is sold. Department of Labor - No changes or funding actions for the Department of Labor appear in the provided text.
109-1-LB289_FinalLB289_Final_Copy.docxLB289 amends village governance, zoning, and municipal economic development statutes. Key agency/deparment actions: - County board: may incorporate villages that specify whether the initial village board will have three or five trustees; appoints initial trustees accordingly. - Election commissioner or county clerk and county canvassing board: handle petitions or board resolutions to change trustee number (petitions require signatures from at least 5% of registered village electors, procured via the village clerk with election commissioner/county clerk assistance, filed ≥70 days before the general election, and canvassed post‑election). - Village clerk: provides petition forms. - City councils (first/second class) and village boards of trustees: may, by ordinance, serve as a board of adjustment; decisions require a two‑thirds concurring vote. The bill expands “qualifying business” under the Local Option Municipal Economic Development Act (adds advanced telecommunications, tourism, film production, housing construction/rehab, early childhood care/education, retail trade, and a relaxed standard for cities ≤5,000). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds procedures allowing village electors to choose at a statewide general election whether their village board of trustees has three or five members. Agencies/departments referenced and responsibilities: - Village board of trustees: may adopt resolution to submit the question (majority vote) and will follow statutory procedures if size changes. - Registered voters: may file petitions (>=5% of prior statewide-election registrants) to trigger the question. - Village clerk: must provide petition forms. - Election commissioner or county clerk: assists with petitions, receives petitions/resolutions (filed >=70 days before the general election), places the question on the ballot, and conducts/counts the vote. - County canvassing board: completes the canvass and decides the proposition. Statutory follow-up: if increased to five, vacancies handled per sections 32-568/32-569; if decreased to three, follow section 17-202. Initial term lengths for trustees after incorporation or change are specified. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB28_IntroLB28_Intro_Copy.docxLB28 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-2716 to add a new adjustment permitting individuals to subtract tip income (to the extent included in federal adjusted gross income) for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025. The section continues to reference the Tax Commissioner for rulemaking related to net operating loss and other income modifications. The statute also addresses income rules affecting Nebraska National Guard members and cites federal agencies (U.S. Department of Defense and U.S. Office of Personnel Management) in the context of military retirement reporting. The bill repeals the original section. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are included.Adds a provision (effective for taxable years beginning or deemed to begin on or after Jan. 1, 2025) allowing individuals to subtract from their federal adjusted gross income any tip income that was included in federal AGI. The text cites the Internal Revenue Code of 1986; no specific government agencies, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB290_FinalLB290_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentLB290 amends §81‑12,241 to direct the Economic Recovery and Incentives Division of the Department of Economic Development to administer federal and state grant programs, providing a 50% advance with remaining funds paid monthly until paid in full or by December 31, 2026, and authorizing recoupment or reduction for unused funds. It creates a Qualified Census Tract Recovery Grant Program (caps: up to $10M for tracts in primary‑class cities; up to $10M for tracts outside metro/primary cities; remaining funds prioritized to metro‑class city tracts). It also authorizes the Division to award additional grants, including up to $90M to a nonprofit for a business park (with pre‑release conditions: advisory‑committee participation, separate bank account, 15‑year use restriction, 10‑year pro forma/due diligence, two public input meetings, and inland port support), and specified caps of $6M, $5M, $20M, $20M, $5M, and $1M for other listed purposes. Federal grants must comply with ARPA/Treasury guidance; state grants must align with ARPA intent.For the Department of Economic Development: the bill adds that an inland port district may be located within a metropolitan-class city, but expressly bars use of grant funds in that city’s downtown and northern downtown areas. This imposes a geographic restriction on DED-administered grants/eligible expenditures; no new appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB291_IntroLB291_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentThe bill designates "Department" to mean the Department of Economic Development and places administration of the new Aid to Municipalities Act with that Department. Municipalities apply to the Department on a prescribed form; the Department reviews applications in receipt order and may approve grants within available appropriations (individual grants capped at $5 million). The Act makes state aid to municipalities part of the defined "state aid." Under amended section 13-522, if a city or village is found noncompliant with budget limits, the Auditor must notify the Department (and State Treasurer), and the Department, with the Treasurer, shall suspend distribution of state aid to the unit until compliance; suspended funds are held six months then forfeited and redistributed if noncompliance persists.The addition establishes the "Aid to Municipalities Act" and designates the Department of Economic Development as the administering "Department." The Department will prescribe application forms, accept municipal grant applications, review them in the order received, and may approve grants up to $5 million each, subject to available appropriations. It also will receive notifications of governmental-unit noncompliance (alongside the State Treasurer). No specific new appropriation amounts or budget line-item allocations are provided—approval authority is limited only by available appropriations and the $5 million per-grant cap.
109-1-LB292A_IntroLB292A_Intro_Copy.docxLB292A is an appropriations bill introduced by Senator McKinney (read Feb 28, 2025) that would appropriate funds to implement Legislative Bill 292 (109th Legislature, 2025). The excerpt contains no specific state agencies, departments, funding amounts, or line-item allocations. Thus, based on the provided text, the bill's effect is to authorize appropriation for LB292 without identifying which state entity receives funds or any budgetary figures.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB292_IntroLB292_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development- The Department of Economic Development (DED) will administer the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund, establish a subaccount to fund affordable housing and land-parcel preparation under the Economic Recovery Act, and may solicit additional private/nonstate contributions (including from the Nebraska Investment Finance Authority). Interest earned on grant funds is to be applied to the grant program. - DED shall award a grant to a qualified applicant to conduct a study of prefabricated housing in Nebraska; the grantee must deliver a comprehensive presentation and an electronic report to DED by April 1, 2026. - The Legislature intends to appropriate $500,000 from the Fund to DED for the Sec. 2 grant. - If grant recipients fail to engage in qualified activity within 24 months, proceeds must be returned to DED for credit to the General Fund. Any Fund balances held by DED transfer to the General Fund beginning July 1, 2029.The added text directs the Department of Economic Development to administer a grant-funded study on prefabricated housing in Nebraska. The Legislature intends to appropriate $500,000 from the Middle Income Workforce Housing Investment Fund to DED for the grant (section 2). Prefabricated housing is defined to include manufactured homes and other factory-built components. DED must award the grant to a qualified applicant who demonstrates capacity (personnel and technology), a commitment to deliverables, relevant expertise/track record, and ability to engage stakeholders (municipalities, counties, manufacturers, utilities). Deliverables include a comprehensive presentation and an electronic report due April 1, 2026. The study must examine zoning regulations affecting siting of prefabricated housing across municipalities and counties.
109-1-LB293A_FinalLB293A_Final_Copy.docxLB293A is an appropriation bill that provides funds to implement Legislative Bill 293 (One Hundred Ninth Legislature, First Session, 2025). The provided text does not identify any specific state agencies or departments to receive funding, nor does it specify appropriation amounts, allocations, or budget line-item changes. Introduced by Senator Ballard and read the first time March 6, 2025.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB293_FinalLB293_Final_Copy.docxLB293 amends the Professional Employer Organization Registration Act to (1) impose regulatory duties on the department (with oversight tied to the Commissioner of Labor) for PEO-sponsored health plans: self-funded plans must file quarterly and annual reports with the department, maintain ERISA-style trust accounts, demonstrate actuarially sound reserves, hold stop‑loss coverage naming the PEO and providing 30 days' notice to the PEO and the Commissioner of Labor before termination, and provide participant notice that plans are self-funded; the department may hold compliance hearings, issue 30‑day corrective orders, and revoke a PEO's registration for noncompliance. (2) Clarify that an employee welfare benefit plan (including health benefits) offered by a single PEO is a single employer plan exempt from MEWA registration and that, under the Small Employer Health Insurance Availability Act, the PEO is treated as the employer for insurance acceptance. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Added provisions require professional employer organizations (PEOs) offering self‑funded health plans to use a licensed third‑party administrator, hold plan assets in an ERISA §403 trust, meet actuarial reserve standards, notify employees the plan is self‑funded, and file quarterly and annual reports with "the department." Reports must include financial statements, an actuary's rate/reserve certification, confirmation of stop‑loss insurance from an insurer licensed in this state (naming the PEO and requiring 30‑day advance notice to the PEO and the Commissioner of Labor before termination), and a state law compliance certificate. The department may hold compliance hearings, issue corrective orders (to be complied with in 30 days), and revoke PEO registration under the Professional Employer Organization Registration Act for failure to comply. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB294_FinalLB294_Final_Copy.docxLB294 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-3720 governing the County Visitors Improvement Fund. The fund remains administered by the county governing body with advice from the county visitors committee (per §81-3717). Grants may be awarded to public or nonprofit-owned visitor attractions for facility expansion, exhibits, construction, planning, or development. Annual grant payments are capped at the greater of proceeds from a county 1% sales tax dedicated to the Fund or $5,000 and may be made for terms up to 20 years; recipients may pledge grant payments to secure bonds, which are payable solely from those grant funds and are not county obligations. The bill repeals the original section and takes effect immediately due to an emergency clause.The added language authorizes grants and sets a minimum award equal to the greater of an unspecified comparator or $5,000. The fragment names no government agency or department and contains no explicit appropriations, funding sources, or budget allocations. The text is incomplete and does not identify who may make or receive the grants.
109-1-LB295_FinalLB295_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB295 references the Department of Labor in two ways. First, it uses U.S. Department of Labor/Bureau of Labor Statistics indices — the CPI‑U for annual cost‑of‑living adjustments and the Medical Price Index for supplemental medical COLAs — and directs selection of a substitute U.S. Department of Labor index if the CPI‑U is discontinued (selection by the board before Sept. 1, 2024, or by the retirement board on/after that date). Second, it modifies State Employees Retirement Act treatment of Department of Labor employees: those employed before July 1, 1984 and paid from Title III or other federal sources remain excluded from “employee” status unless a pre‑Jan. 1, 2018 contributory plan/contract is terminated; upon termination they become members of the State system effective the first pay period and receive vesting credit for prior participation. No Department of Labor funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed.No provisions in the added text affect the Department of Labor, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes for that agency. Substantive additions address public retirement administration: accept DHS/USCIS‑extended identity documents (and state learner’s permits) as valid; authorize the Public Employees Retirement Board to waive repayment of inadvertent benefit overpayments when repayment would cause significant hardship; allow independent lump‑sum payments; revise how the 20‑hours/week threshold is calculated; clarify meeting/travel reimbursement and electronic access rules for retirement‑planning materials (time limits and access window); and restrict use of retirement system names/logos in financial solicitations, requiring prominent disclaimers to avoid misleading affiliation or endorsement.
109-1-LB296A_FinalLB296A_Final_Copy.docxLB296A affects the State Department of Education. It specifies an appropriation of $0 from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund for both FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27 to the State Department of Education (Program 161) to aid in carrying out Legislative Bill 296. The bill establishes limits on expenditures from the funds appropriated in this section for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems: not to exceed $160,197 for FY2025‑26 and $165,403 for FY2026‑27. No other agencies or budget changes are referenced.Adds an appropriation clause directing funds from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund to the State Department of Education (Program 161) to support implementation of Legislative Bill 296 (109th Legislature, 2025). However, the appropriation amounts are $0 for both FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27. The provision caps total expenditures from the appropriated funds for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems at $160,197 for FY2025‑26 and $165,403 for FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB296_FinalLB296_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB296 requires the State Department of Education, the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), the Office of Probation Administration, and the State Court Administrator to enter a memorandum of understanding to share data on students under juvenile‑court jurisdiction. The MOU contemplates SDE contracting a consultant; DHHS is included in the collaborative development of policies and will receive the consultant’s draft report. SDE must create and maintain a centralized education records system and employ registrars; the cost of that system and the registrars is to be paid from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund. That fund is comprised of lottery transfers, grant repayments, and interest, may be transferred to the Education Future Fund, and is administered by SDE. No direct appropriations to DHHS are specified.No changes affect the Department of Health and Human Services. The added provisions require the State Department of Education to create and maintain (beginning July 1, 2026) a centralized education records system for students under juvenile court jurisdiction, employ registrars to ensure uninterrupted services, timely record transfer, and award credit for completed academic work. Schools must immediately share records on request. Registrars will analyze high school records and the Commissioner may award credit and, in some cases, a state diploma (beginning 2026-27). Costs for the system and registrars are to be paid from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund; no DHHS appropriations or budget allocations are changed.
109-1-LB297_FinalLB297_Final_Copy.docxLB297 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-649.03 (Employment Security Law) governing calculation of employers' combined tax rates. It specifies the state's reserve ratio uses amounts available to pay benefits in the Unemployment Trust Fund and the State Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund and uses "total wages for contributory employers" as the denominator. The commissioner retains authority to lower the scheduled yield factor when the reserve ratio is 0.70% or greater. The bill sets the average combined tax rate normally assigned to category 12, but fixes category 12's rate at 0.48 for tax year 2025. Filing-delinquent employers remain assignable to category 20 unless corrected. No new appropriations or budget allocations are created. An emergency clause makes the act effective on passage.Adds a temporary rate change for contributory employers: for tax year 2025 only, the "category twelve" rate is set at 0.48. No state agencies or departments are mentioned and there are no explicit funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the added text.
109-1-LB298A_FinalLB298A_Final_Copy.docxLB298A (Arch) amends section 21 of Legislative Bill 261 (2025), makes an appropriation to implement Legislative Bill 298 (2025), modifies an existing appropriation, repeals the original section, and declares an emergency. The bill’s text provided does not specify agencies, departments, or dollar amounts; its primary fiscal effect is to authorize funding changes and allocations necessary to carry out LB298 and to alter the prior appropriation set in section 21 of LB261.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB298_FinalLB298_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Insurance, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Veterans' AffairsThe bill creates an Office of Public Counsel with deputies, including a deputy for corrections (oversight of the Department of Correctional Services and county/municipal jails) and a deputy for institutions (oversight of Department of Health and Human Services mental‑health institutions and veterans institutions operated by the Department of Veterans' Affairs). It establishes an Office of Inspector General for the Nebraska Correctional System within Legislative Oversight; DOCS must notify the IG of inmate deaths, serious injuries, hospitalizations and provide personnel/record access (medical/mental‑health records require individual consent except in death investigations). DHHS, juvenile services and youth rehabilitation centers must report child‑welfare incidents to the Inspector General. The Department of Administrative Services Accounting Administrator must furnish data to the Legislative Fiscal Analyst; DAS (with the Tax Commissioner and State Treasurer) is barred from unauthorized taxpayer disclosure. The Department of Revenue retains tax administration and must permit sampled, on‑premises auditor access to returns under strict safeguards. Department of Labor, DMV, DHHS and Department of Insurance may receive limited tax information to administer specified programs. Staffing for the Public Counsel and Inspector General is limited to amounts available by appropriation, and agencies must report to Legislative Oversight when implementation used additional appropriated funds.Creates expanded Legislative oversight: establishes Office of Public Counsel, Inspector General offices for Nebraska Child Welfare and for the Nebraska Correctional System, and a Legislative Audit Office within the Division of Legislative Oversight with subpoena and audit powers. For the Department of Health and Human Services: gives the child‑welfare IG broad access to records/personnel, requires the department to notify the IG when criminal investigations involving death/serious injury begin/conclude, allows negotiated disclosure or subpoena if needed, and protects employee interview rights. For the Department of Correctional Services: parallel IG authority, notification, secure electronic information‑sharing, audits/inspections, negotiation or subpoena authority, and expedited court review (Lancaster County; court decision within 20 days; 10‑day appeals). For Departments of Administrative Services, Insurance, Labor, Motor Vehicles, Revenue, Veterans' Affairs (and other agencies): subject to performance audits and committee‑authorized subpoenas to produce records/testimony within 30 days; counsel/witness protections apply. No changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB299_IntroLB299_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of LaborLB299: Department-specific items only - Department of Administrative Services: Section 4-111 requires applicants attesting lawful presence or eligible-alien status for certain public benefits (including professional/commercial license applicants) to use an attestation format prescribed by the Department of Administrative Services; agencies may permit electronic attestations substantially similar to that format. - Department of Labor: Section 84-1307(5)(b) provides that if a specified contributory retirement plan or contract is terminated, Department of Labor employees who were active participants on the termination date shall be granted vesting credit for years of participation. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.- Department of Administrative Services: The bill requires applicants for the enumerated public benefits to "attest in a format prescribed by the Department of Administrative Services" that they are an "eligible alien" (defined by 8 C.F.R. 274a.12 as of Jan 1, 2025). DAS must therefore create and prescribe the attestation format/procedure. - Department of Labor: The bill explicitly includes "benefits under the Employment Security Law" among benefits to which eligible aliens authorized for employment are entitled, meaning unemployment/employment security programs administered by the Department of Labor must be made available to such eligible aliens (and related family/dependent benefits when tied to employment). - Funding/appropriations: No specific appropriations, budget allocations, or funding changes are included in the added text.
109-1-LB29_IntroLB29_Intro_Copy.docxLB29 amends the Administrative Procedure Act to require state agencies to review all existing and pending rules beginning January 1, 2026 and every three years thereafter. Each agency head must designate an oversight individual. Agencies must submit an electronic report to the Clerk of the Legislature by June 30 in review years addressing: public health/safety/welfare necessity; cost–benefit; effectiveness measurement; consideration of less restrictive alternatives; and whether the rule stems from state statute, federal mandate, or court order. The Reference Committee will refer reports to appropriate legislative standing committees, which must report to the Clerk by December 15 with recommended legislative or clarifying actions. Agency rulemaking is suspended during the review except for rules affecting health/safety/welfare, time-sensitive rules, or those subject to statutory deadlines. Section 84-920 is amended to incorporate this new requirement. No funding or appropriations are specified.Beginning Jan 1, 2026, and every three years thereafter, each state agency must: conduct a review of all existing and pending rules; have the agency head designate an individual to oversee the review; and file an electronic detailed report and supporting documentation with the Clerk of the Legislature by June 30 of the review year. Reports must address whether rules are essential to public health/safety/welfare, cost‑benefit, measures of effectiveness, consideration of less‑restrictive alternatives, and whether rules stem from state statute, a federal mandate, or a court decision. The Legislature’s Reference Committee will route reports to appropriate standing committees, which must return committee reports with any legislative recommendations to the Clerk by Dec 15. Rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act is suspended during the review, except for rules affecting health/safety, time‑sensitive rules, or those subject to statutory deadlines. No funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB2_FinalLB2_Final_Copy.docxLB2 outright repeals terminated statutory provisions establishing and governing: the Children and Juveniles Data Feasibility Study Advisory Group; the Crimes Against Children Fund; the Industrial Recovery Fund; the Medical Cannabidiol Pilot Study; the Municipal Natural Gas System Emergency Assistance Act; and the Nebraska Economic Development Task Force. It specifically repeals sections 19-5601 through 19-5608, 28-463 through 28-469, 50-435, 81-1213, 81-1429.01 (Reissue Revised Statutes of Nebraska), and section 43-1306 (R.R.S. Cumulative Supp., 2024). The bill does not name state departments or agencies for reassignment nor include any new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB300_IntroLB300_Intro_Copy.docxLB300 amends statutes to extend the Superintendent Pay Transparency Act to require superintendent and educational service unit (ESU) administrator compensation to comply with that Act. It (1) defines benefit, compensation (including employer retirement and insurance contributions), beginning-teacher compensation, and salary; (2) caps total compensation paid by a school district or ESU to a superintendent or ESU administrator at five times the district’s/ESU’s beginning-teacher compensation for the same contract year; (3) makes contracts violating the cap invalid, prohibits expenditure of district/ESU funds on such contracts, requires forfeiture and return of excess payments, and mandates filing notice with the Commissioner of Education within 30 days; and (4) requires pre-approval and post-approval public publication of proposed/approved contracts and reasonable estimates of current and future costs. The bill references school boards, school districts, ESUs, the Commissioner of Education, and the School Employees Retirement Acts.Adds definitions for "benefit," "compensation," "compensation for a beginning teacher," and "salary," specifying that benefits include employer retirement contributions (School Employees Retirement Act and Class V), annuities, insurance premiums, severance, and other employer-paid amounts. Requires school districts and educational service units (and their boards) to cap superintendent/administrator total compensation at no more than five times the beginning teacher compensation in the same district/ESU. Contracts exceeding the cap are invalid, such payments may not be expended, and excess compensation must be forfeited and returned; a notice (including the maximum allowed compensation) must be filed with the Commissioner of Education within 30 days. No new appropriations or budget allocations are created.
109-1-LB301_IntroLB301_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Revenue- Department of Administrative Services: The bill requires applicants for certain public benefits to attest in a format prescribed by the Department of Administrative Services that they are U.S. citizens or lawfully present; applicants who are eligible aliens and employed as or training to be law enforcement officers must likewise attest in a DAS-prescribed format. State agencies may offer electronic filing substantially similar to the DAS format. - Department of Labor: If a contributory retirement plan or contract described in prior law (section 48-609 as it existed before 2018) is terminated, Department of Labor employees who were active participants at termination shall receive vesting credit for years of participation. - Department of Correctional Services and Department of Revenue: Employees of the Department of Correctional Services and employees of the Department of Revenue (under section 77-366) are explicitly excluded from the statutory definition of "law enforcement officer." No direct appropriations or other funding changes to these agencies are specified.Summary of added provisions (impact by agency): - Department of Administrative Services (DAS): must prescribe the attestation format for applicants to confirm they are an "eligible alien" employed as or training to become a law enforcement officer. - Department of Labor: Employment Security Law benefits are explicitly included among public benefits that eligible aliens in law‑enforcement employment/training must be allowed to receive. - Department of Correctional Services: no explicit programmatic or funding changes; however, employees classified as law‑enforcement officers (per section 81‑1401) who are eligible aliens would be entitled to the same employment‑related benefits (retirement, unemployment, deferred compensation, scholarships, etc.). - Department of Revenue: not mentioned; no changes. Funding/appropriations: the added text contains no appropriations, budget allocations, or funding changes.
109-1-LB302_FinalLB302_Final_Copy.docxLB302 eliminates observation of daylight saving time in Nebraska (exempting the state from 15 U.S.C. 260a(a)) contingent on Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, and Wyoming adopting similar laws; section making DST effective becomes null when that contingency is met. Agency-specific provisions and impacts: - Director of Personnel: authorized to adopt rules to administer vacation/sick leave provisions. - Employing agencies: must provide opportunity to use accrued vacation; if a reasonable written request is denied and leave is forfeited, the agency must pay the employee the cash equivalent within 30 days. - Public Employees Retirement Board: cash payments for forfeited vacation count as compensation for defined contribution or cash balance plans only. - Governor (or Executive Board of the Legislative Council for legislative employees): may extend annual leave in special cases. - Beneficiaries: paid unused vacation upon an employee’s death. No appropriations or budget allocations are included.Added provisions set Nebraska’s standard time under the Uniform Time Act of 1966 but exempt the state from observing daylight saving time and from 15 U.S.C. 260a(a) (the federal provision authorizing advancing clocks). The exemption becomes effective January 1 following the date when Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, and Wyoming each enact similar laws. The provision also states it becomes null and void if subsection (2) of §49-1301 becomes operative. No executive agencies or departments are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB303_FinalLB303_Final_Copy.docxLB303 amends §79-1028.01, creates a School Financing Review Commission (membership appointed by the Governor and by the Executive Board of the Legislative Council; certain members serve ex officio), and revises when and how school districts may exceed their general fund budget authority under the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act. The State Board of Education must approve, deny, or modify exclusion amounts. The Department of Education defines Network Nebraska telecommunications expenditures used in an exclusion for a district’s first full year of participation. The bill specifies exclusions (e.g., disaster repairs, judgments, special education, special grants, federal impact aid) and retirement-related employer contributions to the School Employees Retirement System and the Class V School Employees Retirement Act; it allows carryover of 2024‑25 employer contribution expenditures into budget authority for FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27. Original §79‑1028.01 is repealed; the act takes effect immediately.- The Executive Board of the Legislative Council will appoint the member described in subdivision (1)(d) each January of odd-numbered years for two-year terms; the initial appointment must occur within 30 days after the act takes effect and will serve until a successor in January 2027. - Members in subdivisions (1)(a)–(c) serve ex officio on the commission. - The Governor must appoint members in subdivisions (1)(e)–(h) within 30 days after the act’s effective date; initial terms begin 30 days after that date, are staggered (some two-year, some three-year initial terms), thereafter three-year terms, and vacancies are filled by the Governor. - Budget change: for school fiscal years 2025–26 and 2026–27, expenditures made in school FY 2024–25 described in subdivision (1)(e)(i) may be carried over and included in general fund budget authority for those two subsequent school years.
109-1-LB304_IntroLB304_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill assigns the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) responsibility for administering the state's social services program, including authority to contract with other social agencies at prevailing rates. DHHS must participate in the federal Child Care Subsidy/Child Care and Development Block Grant program, enforce criminal-history checks for participating providers, allow specified transitional child care assistance, and promulgate rules (certain subdivisions operative July 1, 2025). DHHS must adopt and annually revise a fixed-rate schedule for child-care payments effective October 1 each year. Funding: federal CCDBG funds shall be used to cover costs from the 2021 income-eligibility changes; if insufficient, TANF funds may be used; no General Funds may be used except for administration. DHHS shall collaborate with a private nonprofit on an independent evaluation (if privately funded) and shall develop policy guidelines to permit cash-assistance extensions for extreme hardship.The added phrase "2025 Beginning 2025" appears to set the effective/start date as 2025. For the Department of Health and Human Services, there are no substantive programmatic changes, appropriations, or budget allocations specified in that text. No funding or new appropriations to DHHS are indicated. (Recommend providing the full underlined passage if you want confirmation of impacts beyond the effective date.)
109-1-LB305_IntroLB305_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Revenue- The Department may require an affidavit and any other documentation it deems necessary to substantiate eligibility for the Preceptorship Tax Credit. - The Department determines application completeness, approves qualifying applications, and certifies the amount of credit approved to the licensed physician. - The Department may approve up to $1,000,000 in Preceptorship Tax Credits in any single fiscal year. - The Department may adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the Preceptorship Tax Credit Act. - Separately, the bill specifies that the $5,000 home-purchase tax credit (extremely blighted areas) is subject to recapture by the Department of Revenue.The added text directs the Department of Revenue to administer the Preceptorship Tax Credit Act: require an affidavit and any other documentation, determine application completeness, approve and certify qualifying credits, and promulgate rules to implement the program. It establishes an annual cap of $1 million in credits the department may approve, gives approval priority to rural preceptors, prorates credits when the cap is reached on the same day, and bars transfer or sale of credits. The change is a tax-credit allocation (a $1 million per‑year limit), not a direct appropriation or new cash funding line.
109-1-LB306A_IntroLB306A_Intro_Copy.docxLB306A appropriates General Fund dollars to the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska (Program 781) to support implementation of Legislative Bill 306. It provides $195,000 for FY2025‑26 and $195,000 for FY2026‑27, each from the General Fund, to aid in carrying out LB306.Allocates funding to the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska for Program 781 to implement Legislative Bill 306 (109th Legislature, 1st Session, 2025). Specifically, the addition provides $195,000 from the General Fund for FY2026‑27. The text also references a fund for FY2025‑26 (amount not shown in the excerpt).
109-1-LB306_FinalLB306_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Economic Development, Department of Health and Human Services- Department of Administrative Services: directs DAS to create and publish a public online database of school-district financial information (revenue sources, expenditures, balance sheets from most recent audit reports). The DAS budget administrator must set an implementation date on or before January 1, 2026. School districts must provide annual and historical (back to 2005, if available) audit data; DAS must update the database within 30 days of receipt. - Department of Economic Development: beginning with academic year 2024-25, the Department of Economic Development, in collaboration with the Nebraska State Colleges and University Boards (and in one provision in consultation with the Coordinating Commission), will designate eligible programs/shortage areas for Nebraska Career Scholarships based on periodic workforce reviews. - Department of Health and Human Services: DHHS licensing/approval of foster or residential providers affects student residency determinations. When wards are placed outside their home district, the state shall pay the student's education and required transportation costs under rules and regulations prescribed by DHHS (payments not made in advance).Department of Administrative Services: New requirement to build, host and publish an online database of each school district's financials (revenue sources, expenditures, and balance sheet from the most recent audits). The budget division administrator must set an implementation date on or before Jan 1, 2026. Districts must supply audit-derived data and annual updates (department to refresh within 30 days) and provide historical data back to 2005 when available. Confidential information exempted by law need not be disclosed. Department of Economic Development: No changes in the added text. Department of Health and Human Services: No changes in the added text. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB307_IntroLB307_Intro_Copy.docxLB307 directs two-year General Fund appropriations (amounts shown as placeholders) for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 to fund tuition waivers. It allocates appropriations to: - the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges (Program 48), and - the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska (Program 781). Each appropriation includes designated General Funds to be used only for tuition waivers provided pursuant to the First Responders Recruitment and Retention Act, the In the Line of Duty Dependent Education Act, and Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 80‑411 and 80‑901. The bill contains an emergency clause making it effective upon passage.Adds General Fund appropriations for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 to higher-education governing bodies: the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges (Program 48) and the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska (Program 781). Each receives specified FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 General Fund amounts (placeholders XXX) for tuition waivers. Within those appropriations, designated sums (XXX) for each year are earmarked exclusively for tuition waivers under the First Responders Recruitment and Retention Act, the In the Line of Duty Dependent Education Act, and Neb. Rev. Stat. §§80-411 and 80-901.
109-1-LB308_IntroLB308_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborThe bill establishes the Health Care Staffing Agency Registration Act under the Department of Labor. It defines "Commissioner" as the Commissioner of Labor and "Department" as the Department of Labor. Health care staffing agencies must register annually with the department and pay an annual registration fee of $1,500 per Nebraska location (or a $1,500 statewide fee for health care technology platforms without a physical Nebraska location), payable to the department. The commissioner will administer complaints, investigations, random audits, subpoenas, and enforcement (with appeal rights and representation by department counsel or the Attorney General). The department must maintain a public online database of registrants and may adopt rules. The act becomes operative January 1, 2026, and is added to duties in section 81-401.Summary (Department of Labor focus): - The bill assigns responsibility to the Nebraska Department of Labor (and the Commissioner of Labor) to administer an annual registration program for health care staffing agencies, including health care technology platforms. - Agencies must certify they will not enforce pre‑existing noncompete clauses as a condition of registration. - The department will collect an annual $1,500 registration fee per operating location (or one $1,500 statewide fee for platforms without a Nebraska physical location). - The department must operate a public online registry (approval and expiration/revocation dates), a complaint reporting system, investigate complaints, conduct random audits (≥3 business days’ notice), and exercise subpoena and enforcement powers; legal representation may be provided by department attorneys or the Attorney General. - The bill authorizes the department to adopt rules. No other appropriations or explicit budgetary allocations are specified (fee revenue implied).
109-1-LB309_IntroLB309_Intro_Copy.docxLB309 designates the Department of Environment and Energy as the lead agency to administer the Safe Battery Collection and Recycling Act. The department must review and approve battery stewardship plans (plans due by Jan. 1, 2027), act on plans/amendments within statutory timeframes, host approved plans and annual reports on its website (excluding proprietary information), require notice of producer changes, receive a one-time audit after five years, and review out‑of‑state studies with a report to the Legislature’s Natural Resources Committee by May 30, 2028. The department may adopt rules and enforce plan compliance (denials/appeals under the Administrative Procedure Act). The Battery Stewardship Cash Fund is created, comprised of fees collected under section 4, administered by the department and invested by the state investment officer. Civil penalties are remitted to the State Treasurer.Adds the Department of Environment and Energy as the lead agency to administer the Safe Battery Collection and Recycling Act: review/approve battery stewardship plans (120‑day review; denial/resubmission timelines), require producer membership notifications, publish approved plans/producer lists/annual reports on the department website (excluding proprietary info), and adopt rules. The department must review out‑of‑state studies and submit findings to the Legislature's Natural Resources Committee by May 30, 2028. Creates the Battery Stewardship Cash Fund, made up of fees under section 4, administered by the department and restricted to Act implementation; funds may be invested by the state investment officer under state investment laws. Civil penalties are remitted to the State Treasurer; Attorney General or county attorneys may seek injunctions.
109-1-LB30_IntroLB30_Intro_Copy.docxLB30 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77‑2716 to add a tax subtraction for individuals: for taxable years beginning or deemed to begin on or after January 1, 2025, income from overtime compensation paid under the federal Fair Labor Standards Act is subtracted from federal adjusted gross income. The bill leaves in place numerous existing provisions referencing state and federal entities, including the Tax Commissioner (rulemaking/adjustment authority), the Nebraska Educational Savings Plan Trust (sections 85‑1801–85‑1817), ABLE accounts (77‑1401–77‑1409), the Nebraska long‑term care savings plan, the Medical Debt Relief Fund, the Nebraska National Guard (including 32 U.S.C. duty statuses and federal dual‑status technicians), and federal agencies (U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Office of Personnel Management). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.For taxable years beginning (or deemed to begin) on or after Jan. 1, 2025, individuals may subtract from their federal adjusted gross income (as defined by the Internal Revenue Code) any overtime compensation they received that is paid under the federal Fair Labor Standards Act. The provision references the federal tax code and the FLSA (administered by the IRS and U.S. Department of Labor, respectively). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB310_IntroLB310_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB310 amends §71-519 and repeatedly references the Department of Health and Human Services (department). Key provisions: the department may specify additional newborn screening disorders; it designates the laboratory for testing and receives presumptive and confirmed positive results. The department has authority over use, retention, and disposal of collected blood specimens and related information and must adopt rules (consistent with national lab standards and federal law) governing retention, disposal (including witness-verified records), and permitted public-health uses. The department may charge a reasonable fee to evaluate research proposals and to prepare/supply specimens for approved research. The department must prepare informational pamphlets describing its procedures and permitted research uses. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a parental/guardian opt-out: the Department of Health and Human Services may not require an infant to undergo the subsection (1) screening if the parent or guardian objects. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. Practical effect: DHHS must allow and accommodate parental refusals for the referenced infant screening program, which could affect enrollment or implementation but does not change authorized funding.
109-1-LB311_FinalLB311_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB311 references the Department of Health and Human Services in two contexts: - Motor carrier permits and designations for medicaid nonemergency medical transportation: applications for authority to provide such services under contracts with the Department (or its managed‑care contractors or agents) must involve consultation with the Director of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care (or designee) when the Public Service Commission assesses public convenience and necessity. - Transportation network companies/participating drivers: they may not provide transportation under contract with the Department or its contractors without specific PSC authorization; the commission must grant authorization unless protestants demonstrate existing carriers meet the need. No changes to Department of Health and Human Services funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds that when the commission considers authorizing providers to deliver Medicaid nonemergency medical transportation under a contract with (i) the Department of Health and Human Services, (ii) a Medicaid-managed care organization contracted with the department, or (iii) another agent acting for the department under §75-303.01, the commission must consult with the Division of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care’s Director of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care (or designee). No changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB312_FinalLB312_Final_Copy.docxLB312 amends the Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act to add nurse anesthetists and dietitian nutritionists as eligible for student loans and loan-repayment awards. It revises award limits: student loans capped at $30,000 per academic year (overall caps: $120,000 for medical/dental/doctorate-level mental health; $30,000 for master's-level mental health and physician assistant students); medical resident incentives $40,000 per residency year (cap $120,000); loan repayments set at $30,000/year (up to $90,000) for physicians, psychiatrists, dentists, and psychologists, and $15,000/year (up to $45,000) for physician assistants, nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists, pharmacists, physical and occupational therapists, dietitian nutritionists, and mental health practitioners. The administering department retains authority over agreement terms. Agreements entered by Dec. 31, 2024 must first use federal American Rescue Plan Act funds (no local match required), with those federal funds to be spent by Dec. 31, 2026. Original sections are repealed.The added text expands the list of approved Nebraska programs to explicitly include a nurse anesthesia practice program and a dietitian nutritionist program, and enumerates approved provider categories—specifically naming a nurse anesthetist and a dietitian nutritionist licensed under section 38‑1813. No state agencies or departments are referenced by name in the added language, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations included.
109-1-LB313_IntroLB313_Intro_Copy.docxLB313 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§48-118 and 48-118.04 (Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act), explicitly recognizing the employer's workers' compensation insurer as subrogee and party in third‑party actions. Key changes: - Clarifies that an employer or the workers' compensation insurer is subrogated to employee/dependent claims and may recover amounts beyond paid compensation. - Requires third‑party settlements to be agreed in writing by the employee (or representative) and the employer's workers' compensation insurer (or employer if uninsured), or approved by a court as fair and reasonable. - Specifies court-ordered distribution when parties disagree: deduct recovery expenses, pay one-third of remainder to the employee, reimburse employer/insurer for past and future compensation obligations, with any balance to the employee. Original sections are repealed. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a formula for distributing recovery proceeds: after reasonable collection costs, one‑third goes to the employee (or their representative); next the employer or workers’ compensation insurer is reimbursed for compensation already paid or owed; any remaining balance goes to the employee (or their representative). No government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to appropriations, budget allocations, or funding.
109-1-LB314_IntroLB314_Intro_Copy.docxLB314 amends the Sports Arena Facility Financing Assistance Act (secs. 13-3103, 13-3106). It clarifies eligible uses of state assistance for privately owned sports complexes: repayment of bonds/debt for related public infrastructure or for debt issued by a nonprofit coapplicant (subject to voter approval under §13-3110); leasing facilities to political subdivisions for governmental use (defined as contracts up to 20 years at fair-market rent); and promotion of public sporting events. It caps state-funded promotion at 10 years (arts/cultural events also 10 years) and limits funding to 5 years for complexes in second-class cities or villages. For large public stadiums approved on or after July 19, 2024, state assistance under §13-3108 may fund up to 100% of final project cost. Board approval rules are revised—certain approvals are temporary pending voter approval or issuance of a building permit within 24 months—and board actions require a majority vote including the Governor.Adds a definition of "lease" as any contractual lease between the coapplicants identified in §13-3102(1)(b) for use of an eligible sports arena at fair‑market rent for up to 20 years. Establishes that approvals tied to §13-3103(1)(f) are temporary: they convert to permanent if a building permit for the arena is issued within 24 months of the temporary approval by the board; otherwise the temporary approval voids. No state agencies beyond "the board" (the statute's approving authority) are newly created or referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB315_IntroLB315_Intro_Copy.docxLB315 amends provisions governing biennial reports and occupation taxes for domestic and foreign corporations, adding a sunset for those requirements effective January 1, 2026. The Secretary of State is assigned responsibility to prescribe report forms, collect reports and occupation taxes, send notices, investigate and obtain information (including from state, county, or city officials), and administratively dissolve domestic corporations or revoke foreign corporations’ authority for noncompliance by signing, filing, and serving dissolution/revocation certificates. The existing occupation tax schedule (and the double-rate for foreign corporations, capped at $30,000) is retained. The bill harmonizes statutory language and repeals the prior sections; it contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Added language repeatedly sets a compliance or action deadline of "before January 1, 2026" in multiple places. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB316A_FinalLB316A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueAppropriates General Fund amounts to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to implement Legislative Bill 316 (2025): $441,686 for FY2025‑26 and $84,798 for FY2026‑27. Limits total expenditures from these appropriated funds for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems to no more than $41,300 in FY2025‑26 and $42,700 in FY2026‑27.Appropriates General Fund to the Department of Revenue, Program 102: $441,686 for FY2025‑26 and $84,798 for FY2026‑27 to support implementation of Legislative Bill 316. Limits permanent/temporary salaries and per diems paid from these appropriations to no more than $41,300 in FY2025‑26 and $42,700 in FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB316_FinalLB316_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue- Department of Revenue: Levies a 10% excise tax on retail cannabidiol product sales effective Jan 1, 2026. Retailers must keep electronic sales records as prescribed by the Department of Revenue, file monthly returns by the 20th, and remit tax (department may require electronic filing and EFT). The Department of Revenue will collect the tax and remit receipts at least monthly to the State Treasurer for credit to the Property Tax Credit Cash Fund. - Department of Agriculture (USDA): Bill references the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), USDA licensing and USDA regs under the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 for hemp producer licensing and transport/registration provisions. - Department of Health and Human Services: The Uniform Controlled Substances Act definition designates “Department” as the Department of Health and Human Services. No appropriations included.Adds a definition of "cannabidiol product" as a finished hemp consumer product containing hemp-derived CBD, meeting specified THC limits and excluding synthetically created cannabinoids. Creates a new excise tax effective Jan 1, 2026: a 10% tax on retail sales of cannabidiol products. Department of Revenue duties: prescribe recordkeeping and return forms, require electronic records/filing and EFTs as needed, collect the tax, and remit collections at least monthly to the State Treasurer for credit to the Property Tax Credit Cash Fund. The tax is additional to other state/local taxes and sellers must file monthly returns (due by the 20th) reporting sales and remit payment. No new duties, funding, or appropriations are assigned to the Department of Agriculture or the Department of Health and Human Services in the added text.
109-1-LB317_FinalLB317_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Agriculture, Department of Banking and Finance, Department of Economic Development, Department of Insurance, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Department of Veterans' Affairs, Military DepartmentThe bill assigns multiple administrative, regulatory, and fiscal duties to named agencies. Department of Administrative Services (DAS) must process certification of unpaid obligations, run contract transparency and procurement-preference programs, review landfill disposal‑fee rebate applications, schedule budget transfers (notably $1,000,000 from the Water Resources Cash Fund to the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund), issue warrants, and may direct a $200,000 transfer from the Clean‑burning Motor Fuel Development Fund to the General Fund. Department of Agriculture houses the Riparian Vegetation Management Task Force, gains expanded pesticide rulemaking/enforcement powers (inspections, fines up to $5,000, licensing), participates in species/habitat notice and livestock permitting frameworks, and sits on the Environmental Trust Board. Department of Health and Human Services’ CEO is added to multiple boards/committees, may present evidence at groundwater hearings, and receives specified forfeited sureties and deposits to the HHS Cash Fund for radiation‑site closure (not operating costs). Department of Revenue receives the Litter Fee Collection Fund and expanded ethanol program duties. Transportation, Economic Development, Veterans' Affairs, Military Department, Banking and Finance, Insurance, Labor, and Correctional Services are enumerated stakeholders or receive statutory listings; limited personnel exemptions and session‑law distribution changes are included.Effective July 1, 2025, the Department of Natural Resources is merged into the Department of Environment and Energy, which is renamed the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment; a Chief Water Officer position is created and employees/positions transfer to the new department with continuity of service and bargaining rights. All appropriations and salary limits enacted for Agency No. 29 (DNR) are voided and reappropriated to Agency No. 84 (Department of Water, Energy, and Environment). Unpaid DNR obligations as of June 30, 2025 may be certified as valid encumbrances to the accounting division of the Department of Administrative Services for payment. No substantive changes, funding, or allocations are made for the Departments of Agriculture, Banking and Finance, Economic Development, Insurance, Labor, Correctional Services, Health and Human Services, Motor Vehicles, Revenue, Transportation, Veterans’ Affairs, or the Military Department.
109-1-LB318_IntroLB318_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends duties of the Department of Health and Human Services (the department). Key DHHS mandates and deadlines include: submit a state plan amendment to CMS by September 30, 2025, to cover incarcerated youth (Medicaid, CHIP, and former foster-care youth as specified); earlier and existing directives to seek/submit state plan amendments or waivers for community-based behavioral health, school-based services, continuous glucose monitor coverage, postpartum extension, medical respite facilities (by October 1, 2025), breast pumps and lactation consultations (by January 1, 2025), and translation/interpretation services. Funding provisions: up to $600,000 annually from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for glucose-monitor implementation (excess also from that fund); medical respite and translation services funded by that fund; lactation consultation appropriations intended to be a 145% rate increase over current departmental rates.Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to submit a State Plan Amendment to CMS by September 30, 2025 to secure coverage while detained pending disposition: Medicaid for youth under 21, CHIP for youth under 19, and former foster-care youth up to age 26. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB319_IntroLB319_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services- Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): must pursue all federal SNAP options, maximize federal funding and minimize use of General Funds, employ staff to evaluate options, and submit an annual report (by Dec. 1) to the Health and Human Services Committee detailing options, actions, caseload, costs and expenditures. DHHS must develop a SNAP outreach plan meeting Food and Nutrition Service (USDA) criteria, may accept gifts/grants/donations, partner with counties/nonprofits, seek federal matching funds, and is exempt from implementing the plan if private or federal funds are insufficient to cover implementation or increased caseload. DHHS shall create a TANF‑funded categorical‑eligibility policy (including temporary gross‑income expansion to 165% FPG) and annually report (by Dec. 15) on costs, recommendations, and federal fund availability. - Department of Labor: may administer the SNAP Next Step employment program in partnership with DHHS; recipients 131–165% FPG were to be encouraged to participate (through 9/30/2023). The Legislature intends that the Department of Labor use no General Funds for those processes. - United States Department of Agriculture (Food and Nutrition Service): DHHS must submit the state outreach plan to FNS for approval and request available federal matching funds.Creates a SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) eligibility restriction: anyone convicted of a felony for possession, use, or distribution of a controlled substance (per 21 U.S.C. 862 as of Jan 1, 2025) is eligible for SNAP only if they (1) have completed their sentence or (2) are currently serving parole, probation, or post‑release supervision. Impacts by agency: - Department of Agriculture (USDA/FNS): Primary implementer — must apply and verify the new eligibility standard; may incur administrative verification workload but no explicit funding or appropriation changes are included. - Department of Labor: No direct role or funding changes specified. - Department of Health and Human Services: No funding or appropriation changes specified; no direct programmatic role mandated by this text.
109-1-LB31_IntroLB31_Intro_Copy.docxRequires the State Board of Education to develop and distribute a model policy governing school district use of student surveillance, monitoring, and tracking technology. The model must require districts to inventory tools and provide: vendor names/contact information; purchase and maintenance costs; tool descriptions and privacy protections; opt-out availability; whether data is shared with law enforcement or used for discipline; accommodations for students with disabilities/IEPs; how biometric and personally identifiable information is stored/shared/sold; and available remedies (including under the Consumer Protection Act, the Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act, and section 79-2,104). School districts must post the inventory on their websites and provide hard copies on request. Each school board must adopt a written policy conforming to the model by May 1, 2026, to take effect for the 2026–27 school year. No funding or appropriation changes are specified.The Department of Education (via the State Board of Education) must develop and distribute a model policy on school use of student surveillance, monitoring, and tracking technology. School districts must inventory tools and provide vendor contact info, purchase/maintenance costs, tool descriptions and privacy protections, opt‑out options, law‑enforcement/data‑sharing and disciplinary implications, disability accommodations, biometric/PII storage/sharing/sale practices, and available remedies (including Consumer Protection Act, Political Subdivisions Tort Claims Act, and section 79‑2,104). Districts must post the inventory online and provide hard copies on request. By May 1, 2026, each school board must adopt a written policy conforming to the state model for implementation in school year 2026–27 (with discretion to add provisions). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB320_IntroLB320_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborThe bill assigns specific duties to the Department of Labor: (1) to work with the human trafficking task force to develop or select multilingual informational posters (including a toll‑free hotline) for placement statewide (sec. 81‑1430(3)(a)); (2) to work with the task force and lodging businesses to approve and determine delivery of optional human‑trafficking training for hotel and similar public‑lodging employees (sec. 81‑1431(2)); and (3) to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the hotel/employee training and prevention provisions (sec. 3(4)). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified in the bill.Adds that the task force may collaborate with the Department of Labor and hotels to approve and determine delivery of employee human‑trafficking training. The Department of Labor is authorized to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the section. The provision grants hotels discretion to provide approved training, adopt reporting procedures, and implement prevention policies, and provides limited liability protection for compliant operators. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor are included.
109-1-LB321_IntroLB321_Intro_Copy.docxLB321 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §31-735 governing elections for sanitary and improvement district (SID) boards of trustees. It clarifies agency responsibilities: election commissioners or county clerks receive trustee filings, set the property-record date (≤80 days before the election), and conduct sealed mail-ballot elections (mailing ballots ≥20 days before the election and requiring return by 5 p.m. on election day); clerks of the district must mail election notices ≥65 days before the election; register of deeds records property ownership used to determine voter eligibility. The bill retains provisions for designated corporate/entity representatives, resident vs. all-owner voting classes, and allows boards (per §31-740.01) to reduce trustees from five to three under specified conditions. The original section is repealed. No funding or appropriation changes are included.No government agencies or departments are named in the provided added text. There are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes indicated. The fragment appears to alter a time period reference from "six years" to include "eight," suggesting a possible extension of a duration (e.g., term or eligibility) but lacks context to confirm specifics.
