109-1-LB322_IntroLB322_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB322 explicitly names agency employees in enhanced-offense definitions: it treats employees of the Department of Correctional Services as public safety officers and specifically includes employees of DOCS-operated secure youth confinement facilities when the offender is committed there. It also treats Department of Health and Human Services employees as public safety officers only where the offender is committed under the Sex Offender Commitment Act. The habitual‑criminal mandatory minimum terms are to be served in a Department of Correctional Services adult correctional facility. The bill contains no explicit appropriations, funding, or budget allocations.Summary (focus: Department of Correctional Services & Department of Health and Human Services) - Employees of the Department of Correctional Services are newly listed as "public safety officers" and therefore covered by the bill's enhanced assault offenses and protections. - Employees of the Department of Health and Human Services are added as "public safety officers" only where the offender is committed as a dangerous sex offender under the Sex Offender Commitment Act. - The amendments extend assault definitions/protections (including striking with bodily fluids and related degrees of assault) to these employees where applicable. - No language in the provided additions establishes or changes any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either agency.
109-1-LB323_FinalLB323_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Transportation- Department of Transportation (DOT) bid procedures: for contracts estimated over $250,000 DOT must publish notice once weekly for three weeks in the county newspaper and on its official web page at least 20 days before bid receipt; the web posting alone for 20 days satisfies the notice requirement even if newspaper publication is defective. For contracts of $250,000 or less, DOT may either follow the above procedures or solicit bids from at least three potential bidders and may award if it receives at least one responsive bid. - Adjustment of thresholds: DOT may annually (Oct. 1) adjust the dollar amounts in those bid thresholds by the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics (twelve‑month period ending Aug. 31), rounded up to the next $1,000. - DOT authority and legislative consent: DOT may procure materials, equipment, services, and buildings; it may not construct any building with an estimated cost greater than the adjusted dollar amount in section 81‑1114.01 without legislative consent. - No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds electronic-notice requirements for departmental bid solicitations: agencies must publish notice and post it on their official web page at least 20 days before the bid deadline; temporary web outages do not defeat compliance. Newspaper notices must identify the department's official web page. If the solicitation has been posted on the designated web page for 20 days prior to bid opening, that posting alone will satisfy notice requirements even if the newspaper notice is defective. The text also bars the department from pursuing certain purchases or leases with estimated costs exceeding the adjusted dollar amount for capital construction projects referenced in section 81-1114.01. No changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor or Department of Transportation are included.
109-1-LB324_IntroLB324_Intro_Copy.docxLB324 amends the Business Improvement District Act's protest and notice procedures. Key government actors: city councils conduct hearings, rule on written protests, and may continue hearings; cities must publish hearings, mail notices (with self‑addressed voting postcards when a special assessment or occupation tax is proposed), and administer neighborhood‑association registration rules; county treasurers’ tax rolls identify taxable property owners; registered neighborhood associations receive notice in their requested manner. Proceedings to create or modify a district terminate if, after postcard voting, fewer than 50% of returned postcards from affected record owners (for special assessments) or users of space (for occupation taxes) vote in favor. The bill repeals the original cited sections. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The added language clarifies postcard voting procedures for creation or modification of business improvement districts: postcards must be mailed under §19‑4029.01 to record owners and to users of space; a modified or new district is defeated if fewer than 50% of returning record‑owners (and a corresponding proportion of returning users of space) vote in favor. It also expressly allows self‑addressed postcards and references methods for returning postcards under §§19‑4027 and 19‑4029.04. No state agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB325_FinalLB325_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of InsuranceKey provisions referencing the Department of Insurance (the "department"): - An insurance corporation may waive the statutory requirement that at least one board member be a Nebraska resident for a five-year period upon filing an affidavit with the department affirming specified criteria (including that the corporation’s ultimate controlling entity “as defined by the department” has not changed in ten years). - If the corporation ceases to meet those criteria during the five-year period, it must notify the Department of Insurance specifying which criteria are no longer met and appoint a Nebraska-resident director within six months. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a five‑year waiver process to the statute requiring at least one board member of a domiciled insurer be a Nebraska resident. The insurer may file an affidavit with the Department of Insurance, signed by the board president/chair and notarized, certifying it: has principal offices in Nebraska; is publicly traded (or wholly owned by a publicly traded company); has been domiciled in Nebraska ≥25 years; employs >500 Nebraska‑based, Nebraska‑taxed workers; and whose ultimate controlling entity (as defined by the Department) has not changed in ten years. The affidavit may be filed when criteria are met and renewed after five years. If criteria lapse during the term, the insurer must notify the Department, identify which criteria failed, and appoint a Nebraska resident director within six months. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB326_FinalLB326_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of InsuranceLB326 explicitly defines "Department" as the Department of Insurance and "Director" as the Director of Insurance. Key provisions referencing the Department/Director: - Insurers must respond to a written inquiry from the Department within 15 working days. - Health insurance lead generators and insurers (other than agents, brokers, consultants) must reimburse the Department for the expense of examinations under the Insurers Examination Act. - The Director is authorized to examine, investigate, issue charges/hearings, and to transmit covered claims to the Nebraska Property and Liability Insurance Guaranty Association. - Mutual insurance holding companies must file annual financial statements and a confidential encumbrance disclosure with the Director by March 1 and an independent audit by June 1. The bill contains no explicit state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations to the Department.Adds definitions and regulatory duties relevant to the Department of Insurance: creates/clarifies terms including "customer," "health insurance lead generator," "lead generating device," and "recording." Requires health insurance lead generators to keep books, records and complete sales/verification recordings in an accessible order for Director examination (current year plus two prior years). Expands the association's claims scope to include transferred/assumed policies under specified insolvency conditions, limits association payments for cybersecurity coverage to $300,000 per insured event, and gives the association explicit rights to review, contest, set aside, and defend against pre‑liquidation settlements, releases, judgments, and to assert offsets/defenses. Permits the association to provide covered benefits/services and appoint service providers, and requires exhaustion of state/federal program remedies before association payment. No specific appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations for the Department of Insurance are included.
109-1-LB327_IntroLB327_Intro_Copy.docxLB327 shifts fiscal and administrative responsibility for probation services from counties to the state. Beginning on an implementation date set by the State Court Administrator between July 1, 2026 and July 1, 2027, the state (via appropriations to the Supreme Court) will pay: district probation office operation expenses; office space and facility costs for probation staff; probation staff salaries and travel; IT procurement/management/support; and interpreter services (including auxiliary aids) for non‑English and deaf/hard‑of‑hearing persons. The state already pays drug‑testing and electronic‑surveillance equipment costs except as otherwise provided. Counties must coordinate with the State Court Administrator on the transition. The probation administrator must prepare budget requests for Supreme Court approval and submission for appropriations. The Supreme Court may adopt rules and sets interpreter standards, requiring licensed interpreters for deaf/hard‑of‑hearing persons.Effective between July 1, 2026 and July 1, 2027 (date chosen by the State Court Administrator), the state will assume payment for probation services. Covered costs include district office operations, office space/facilities for probation staff, probation staff salaries and travel, and comprehensive IT procurement/management/support (hardware, peripherals, phones/mobile devices, technical support, software licensing, network and Internet services). These costs are to be paid from funds appropriated to the Supreme Court. County officials must coordinate with the State Court Administrator to ensure a smooth transition of payment responsibilities. The Supreme Court may adopt rules to implement the section.
109-1-LB328_IntroLB328_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of RevenueThe bill assigns the Department of Economic Development (DED) to administer the Affordable Housing Trust Fund and the Site and Building Development Fund. DED must include in its annual status report detailed fund activity, including appropriated funds actually expended and the department’s current administration budget and planned distributions. The Site and Building Development Fund remains administered by DED; the bill reiterates legislative intent to transfer $5 million from the General Fund for each of FY2022‑23 and FY2023‑24 and to appropriate $500,000 from the fund for FY2024‑25 to DED for competitive studies of large commercial/industrial sites. The Department of Revenue (via the Tax Commissioner) is referenced for documentary stamp design, and taxpayers may seek declaratory rulings under Department of Revenue rules.The inserted fragment appears to add a new subsection (m) regarding the Behavioral Health Services Fund, saying (incomplete) that money in the fund “may be retained by the register of deeds.” The text is fragmentary and contains no explicit dollar amounts, appropriations, or line-item budget changes. Impacts on agencies: - Department of Revenue: no explicit appropriation or allocation changes in the provided text. Potential operational/flow impact only if local retention by registers of deeds changes the timing or amount of remittances the Department administratively processes. - Department of Economic Development: not mentioned and no funding or program changes indicated. Recommendation: review the full bill language to confirm scope, any specific retention amounts, and implementation mechanics.
109-1-LB329_IntroLB329_Intro_Copy.docxLB329 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-316.01 (R.S. Cumulative Supp., 2024) to revise definitions and criminalize sexual abuse by school employees. It (1) defines “school contract worker” (persons 19+ who work at State Department of Education–approved or -accredited public, private, denominational, or parochial schools but are not employed by the school) and expressly includes such contract workers within the definition of “school employee”; (2) defines “student” as persons aged 16–19 enrolled or recently attending such schools; and (3) specifies offenses and penalties (first-degree for sexual penetration — Class IIA felony; second-degree for sexual contact — Class IIIA felony; third-degree for a pattern/scheme — Class IV felony) and bars consent as a defense. The bill repeals the original section. No funding or appropriations are included.Adds a definition of "school contract worker" as a person aged 19+ who, while employed elsewhere, works at public, private, denominational, or parochial schools that are approved or accredited by the State Department of Education but is not employed by the school (examples: school resource officer, construction worker, consultant, independent contractor). Also amends subsection (d) to include a school contract worker in the specified clauses. No agencies beyond the State Department of Education are referenced and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB32_FinalLB32_Final_Copy.docxLB32 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §49-1474.01 to clarify disclaimer requirements for political materials. Persons who pay for printed campaign materials must include their name and street address; candidates who pay must include name and street address or a post office box. Radio and television ads must include the payer’s name; stations must keep the payer’s street address or PO box on file for at least six months and divulge it on request. The bill directs “the commission” to adopt rules on disclaimer size and placement and to exempt items (e.g., windshield stickers, yard signs, bumper stickers, campaign buttons, balloons). Violations are Class IV misdemeanors. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds candidate disclaimer requirements: except for individuals using personal resources (or as otherwise allowed), candidates must place their name and street address or PO box on printed campaign materials; radio/TV ads must include the candidate’s name, and the station must retain the candidate’s address on file for at least six months and provide it on request. No government agencies or departments are mentioned and no funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB330_IntroLB330_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB330 amends the revenue distribution statute to direct aviation sales-tax revenue to the Department of Transportation. Specifically, for transactions on or after July 1, 2023, all proceeds of the state sales and use taxes (under §77-2703) on the sale or lease of aircraft (per §3-101) are credited to the Department of Transportation Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund. This change appears in the Revenue Distribution Fund allocation provisions. No dollar amounts or additional DOT appropriations are specified.No provisions in the underlined additions affect the Department of Transportation (no new duties, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DOT). Summary of additions relevant to funding: beginning Oct 1, 2025, statewide sales tax rates are revised (including reduced rates for transactions inside designated Good Life districts and a higher rate on alcoholic liquor). For transactions on or after Oct 1, 2025, 50% of sales/use tax proceeds from alcoholic liquor are credited to a newly created Alcohol Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund (administered by DHHS) and 50% to the Education Future Fund; the Tax Commissioner will determine quarterly credits. The new DHHS fund may be invested by the state investment officer and is dedicated to alcohol addiction prevention and treatment.
109-1-LB331_IntroLB331_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services, Department of RevenueThe bill makes the Department of Revenue (via the Tax Commissioner) administrator of a new statewide consumption tax: registering sellers; collecting, auditing and enforcing liabilities (summonses, liens, seizures, garnishments); designating tax collectors and requiring surety bonds for large sellers; developing tax‑exempt certificates (rules by 9/1/2025; electronic and paper applications available by 10/1/2027); publishing forms and operating a fraud hotline/award program; promulgating remittance, recordkeeping and transitional inventory-credit rules. The Department must maintain employee continuing education, produce an annual report to the Legislature beginning 2029, and may not use assessed tax amounts to evaluate staff. All tax proceeds are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. Tax‑collection agreements are limited to finally assessed (not appealed) taxes and 12‑month terms; interest accrues from entry of the final assessment. Disclosure of tax information outside the Department is criminalized (Class IV felony) with limited enumerated exceptions. The Department of Health and Human Services must certify developmental‑disability eligibility for homestead exemptions on forms prescribed by the Department of Revenue. No explicit appropriations or new budget allocations to either agency are specified.Department of Revenue - Becomes the primary collector/administrator of a new 7.5% statewide consumption tax effective 1/1/2028 (replacing income, sales, property, motor vehicle, and inheritance taxes). - Required to collect proceeds and remit them to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund; State Treasurer disburses per the state's budget; Department of Administrative Services will administer agency-level consumption tax receipts. - New operational duties: create online forms and a tax‑exempt certificate program (rules by 9/1/2025; application available by 10/1/2027); maintain continuing education; publish applicable interest rates; run hotline/whistleblower award program; require receipts; conduct audits, summonses, liens, garnishments and criminal/ civil penalties; establish large‑seller weekly remittance and security rules; permit limited installment agreements; annual report to the Legislature starting 2029. - Administrative limits/benefits: cannot use assessed tax amounts to evaluate employees; specific penalty‑abatement provisions and confidentiality/disclosure rules. Department of Health and Human Services - No substantive new responsibilities or funding changes; only a limited reference to “local public health department” inspectors for declaring property uninhabitable.
109-1-LB332_FinalLB332_Final_Copy.docxLB332 makes multiple regulatory changes affecting state licensing boards and the Department of Health and Human Services (the department). Key agency actions: - Funeral Directing and Embalming: creates an assistant funeral director role subject to collaborative agreements, supervision and recordkeeping under department oversight and adds discipline for noncompliance. - Hearing Instrument Specialists Board/Department: revises definitions, scope (including cerumen removal and required face‑to‑face or reviewed hearing assessments within six months), licensure pathways, temporary training licenses, exam standards, record retention (7 years), employer reporting, and board rule‑making authority. - Board of Pharmacy/public health clinics: modifies board composition; authorizes delegated dispensing at public health clinics with specified practitioner, labeling, pharmacist‑on‑call and refill limits (contraceptives only). - Medicaid/DHHS: mandates coverage expansions (continuous glucose monitors, extended postpartum coverage, electric personal breast pumps and lactation visits, medical respite waivers) and directs funding sources. Fiscal notes: up to $600,000/year from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for CGM expansion; medical respite and lactation consultation funding to be supported as specified; legislative intent to consider state funding of tuition waivers (≥50% of cost) in the biennial budget.Adds regulatory requirements and oversight by "the department" and the licensing "board" for assistant funeral directors and hearing instrument specialists: the board may set exam, practicum and credential criteria; the department may adopt rules, receive annual lists of employed hearing instrument specialists from organizations, determine licensure eligibility/waivers, and require recordkeeping. The text incorporates federal FDA rules (21 C.F.R. 801.422 and 801.109) as standards and references credentialing bodies (National Board for Certification in Hearing Instrument Sciences; International Hearing Society). It also requires consumer disclosures, documentation, and limits (e.g., cerumen removal scope, face‑to‑face assessments). Fiscal language: the Legislature expresses intent to consider continued funding—at least one‑half of the cost of tuition waivers/fees for a state‑college to University of Nebraska Medical Center pathway—through the biennial budget process; no specific appropriation is made.
109-1-LB333_IntroLB333_Intro_Copy.docxLB333 amends Nebraska's Motor Vehicle Operator's License Act to authorize issuance of hazardous materials (HAZMAT) endorsements for intrastate hauling to any person age 18 or older holding a valid commercial driver's license. The bill references and harmonizes state requirements with federal authorities and rules, including the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), 49 C.F.R. provisions, the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners, and federal statutes (Commercial Motor Vehicle Safety Act, Motor Carrier Safety Improvement Act, and USA PATRIOT Act). It also preserves the state's role in authorizing third‑party testers and skills examiners. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a provision allowing any person age 18 or older holding a valid commercial driver's license to be issued a hazardous materials endorsement for intrastate transport. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text.
109-1-LB334_IntroLB334_Intro_Copy.docxLB334 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §32-607 regarding candidate filing forms and filing officers. It specifies the Secretary of State as the filing officer for statewide and multi-county offices (including judges desiring retention) and designates county election commissioners or county clerks for county, city, village, and certain school offices. Candidate forms must list specified contact and qualification information (email optional) and note any civil penalties under the Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act. Critically, the bill requires that the residence address, mailing address, and telephone number on filing forms for judges desiring retention be kept confidential by the filing officer. The original section is repealed. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Requires the candidate filing form for judges seeking retention to have the residence address, mailing address, and telephone number kept confidential by the filing officer. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB335_FinalLB335_Final_Copy.docxLB335 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §85-2303 (In the Line of Duty Dependent Education Act) to revise definitions used in the Act and explicitly add “stepchild” to the definition of “child” for dependents of Nebraska law enforcement officers or firefighters killed in the line of duty. Defined institutions/agencies referenced include the community college system, Nebraska state college system, the University of Nebraska (state university), and volunteer fire departments (as defined in §35-1303). The bill references the In the Line of Duty Dependent Education Benefit (§85-2304) and governing bodies that set tuition and fees. The original §85-2303 is repealed. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds the phrase "or the stepchild," expanding the definition to expressly include a stepchild. No government agencies, departments, or funding/appropriations are mentioned or affected.
109-1-LB336_IntroLB336_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB336 creates a Task Force on Supported Employment. Relevant to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) and Department of Labor (DOL): - Membership: the task force includes as nonvoting members an employee of DHHS’s Division of Developmental Disabilities and an employee of DHHS’s Division of Behavioral Health, each appointed by the Governor, and an employee of the Department of Labor appointed by the Governor. - Deliverable and timing: the task force must submit an electronic report and action plan to the Legislature and Governor by July 1, 2027; the task force terminates December 31, 2027. No sections in the bill appropriate funds or make budgetary allocations to DHHS, DOL, or the task force.Creates a Task Force on Supported Employment that includes nonvoting appointees from the Department of Labor (one employee appointed by the Governor) and two Department of Health and Human Services employees (one each from the Division of Developmental Disabilities and the Division of Behavioral Health, appointed by the Governor). The task force must review prior supported‑employment reports and evaluations, produce an action plan addressing workforce barriers, untapped potential, projected workforce numbers, and effects of work on benefits, and submit a report by July 1, 2027. It terminates December 31, 2027. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB337_IntroLB337_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor Vehicles, Department of TransportationThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) and directs DMV operational and funding changes. Applicants claiming certain motorcycle/helmet exemptions must submit proof of course completion to DMV; DMV must modify its records system by January 1, 2024 to record the course completion date. The bill authorizes a $50 charge for initial/renewal special‑interest plates, with $25 credited to the DMV Cash Fund and $25 to the Highway Trust Fund; a postage/handling fee for mailing plates/registration is credited to the DMV Cash Fund. If plate manufacturing costs exceed the statutory charge, the excess is credited first to the Highway Trust Fund, then to the DMV Cash Fund. Separately, effective July 1, 2023, sales/use tax proceeds on aircraft are credited to the Department of Transportation Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund.Adds all‑terrain vehicles (ATVs) and utility‑type vehicles (UTVs) into the Motor Vehicle Registration Act: DMV must title, register and issue plates for ATVs/UTVs and treat them as "motor vehicles" when registered for highway use under section 60‑6,356. The bill defines UTVs by dimensions (≤74" wide, ≤180" long, four+ non‑highway tires) and retains exclusions (not golf cars/low‑speed vehicles). It allows operation on non‑municipal highways but expressly bars operation on Interstates, state highways, expressways and freeways and permits local ordinances to prohibit use. Operator protection rules (helmets/occupant‑protection or three‑point belts) are clarified. Several registration fee figures appear in the added text ($3, $25, $5) and are inconsistent; no explicit appropriations, budget transfers, or other funding changes for DMV or DOT are specified.
109-1-LB338_IntroLB338_Intro_Copy.docxLB338 (2025) prohibits life insurers, disability insurers, and long-term care insurers in Nebraska from using genetic information — or soliciting genetic test results or actions related to genetic testing — to deny, limit, or rate coverage or impose preexisting-condition exclusions, except when there is a clinical diagnosis. The bill allows insurers to review medical records as part of an application exam, ask about family history, and consider clinical diagnoses. It cites the federal Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (29 U.S.C. §1182) and relies on Nebraska’s statutory definitions in section 48-236. Referred to the Legislature’s Banking, Commerce and Insurance Committee. No state agencies are newly created or assigned duties, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget allocations.Added findings and protections direct that the Legislature endorses genetic testing benefits and, consistent with the federal Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (29 U.S.C. 1182), bars life, disability, and long‑term care insurers — absent a clinical diagnosis — from canceling, limiting, denying coverage, setting different premium rates, soliciting genetic information, or using genetic test results or testing decisions. Exceptions allow insurers to review medical records, ask about family history, and consider clinical diagnoses. Genetic terms adopt definitions in section 48‑236. No state agencies or departments beyond "the Legislature" are newly created or referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB339_IntroLB339_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB339 directs the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to administer the state's social services program and to participate in the federal child care assistance/Child Care Subsidy program. DHHS must promulgate rules implementing specified provider/household provisions (operative July 1, 2025), adopt an annual fixed-rate reimbursement schedule effective October 1, and provide a Feb. 1 annual summary report of prior-year subsidy claims (monthly paid day/partial-day units and aggregate reimbursements by age group). DHHS is to collaborate with a private nonprofit on a privately funded evaluation of prior eligibility changes. For costs resulting from earlier income-eligibility changes (July 1, 2021–Sept. 30, 2026), Child Care and Development Block Grant funds (and, if insufficient, TANF funds) may be used; no General Funds shall be used except for administration.Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to annually (by Feb. 1) produce, for each licensed provider reimbursed under the federal Child Care Subsidy program in the prior calendar year, a claims summary. The report must list by month: paid full-day units for children under 6 and for children 6 and older; paid partial-day units for those same two age groups; and the aggregate reimbursement totals for each age group. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB33_IntroLB33_Intro_Copy.docxLB33 amends the Nebraska Liquor Control Act by redefining terms in sections 53-103.02, 53-103.03, and 53-103.24 to remove nonalcoholic beer from regulation under the Act, harmonize related provisions, repeal the original sections, and outright repeal section 53-160.02. The bill text provided does not explicitly name any state agency or department. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB340_IntroLB340_Intro_Copy.docxLB340 adopts the Asbestos Trust Claims Transparency Act and the Asbestos Claims Priorities and Over‑Naming Reform Act. It directs Nebraska courts to enforce claimant obligations to file all applicable asbestos trust claims, produce trust‑claim materials and affidavits, and allows defendants (not less than 60 days before trial) to move the court to compel additional trust filings. Courts may delay trial, order production, and apply setoffs for amounts paid or payable by trusts; trust materials are admissible and not privileged. The bill permits defendants to seek discovery from asbestos trusts with claimant cooperation. The reform act establishes medical prima facie standards (qualified physicians, AMA Guides), limits discovery until prima facie is shown, restricts consolidation absent consent, and applies to new filings. It amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25‑224 to toll limitations for non‑malignant asbestos conditions until diagnosis meeting the prima facie standard or death. No funding or appropriations are included.Adds procedures requiring claimants to file all asbestos trust claims, produce trust claim materials and affidavits, and supplement them; allows defendants to move courts (and courts to order) additional trust filings, production and a 90‑day delay before trial. Makes trust claim materials and trust governance documents admissible and subject to discovery (claimant cannot assert privilege); permits defendants setoffs for amounts paid or payable by trusts. Establishes medical prima facie standards for impairment and malignant conditions referencing the AMA Guides and American Thoracic Society standards and requires board certification (American Board of Internal Medicine or American Osteopathic Board of Internal Medicine) for certain physicians; courts must hold evidentiary hearings and limit discovery until prima facie proof. Refers to “the court” and asbestos trusts. No executive agencies, departments, appropriations, or budget changes are specified.
109-1-LB341_FinalLB341_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill requires that when a minor is a ward of the state and a settlement is paid in cash, check, draft, or direct deposit, payment be made into a trust account or subaccount established by the Department of Health and Human Services to receive settlement funds for the ward. The account must earn interest for the benefit of the ward, and DHHS must provide notice of the deposit to the ward by personal service or first-class mail. The bill contains no explicit funding, appropriation, or budget allocation for DHHS.The added provisions let a custodian settle a minor’s claim (≤ $40,000, excluding medical liens and fees) without court approval if no guardian/conservator exists, with funds placed in restricted accounts or annuities. For Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): if the minor is a state ward and settlement is paid by cash/check/draft/direct deposit, payment must go into a trust account or subaccount established by DHHS that earns interest “for the benefit of the ward and the department,” and DHHS must notify the ward of the deposit by personal service or first-class mail. Withdrawals from such accounts are limited (court order, custodian direction, upon age 19, or death). No appropriations, budget allocations, or explicit funding changes are specified.
109-1-LB342_IntroLB342_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns it primary regulatory authority over fantasy contest licensing and enforcement. The department may adopt rules (subject to specified limits), conduct background investigations, issue or deny licenses, require geolocation and anti-fraud controls, incorporate and operate a voluntary self‑exclusion program, receive operator reports of prohibited participants, and direct forfeited prizes to problem‑gaming charities. Application and license administration duties and investigations are vested in the department. Fiscal provisions create the Fantasy Sports Consumer Protection Fund, to be administered by the department and credited with all license and application fees; monies in the fund may be invested by the state investment officer. Civil penalties collected by the department are remitted to the State Treasurer for constitutionally prescribed distribution. The bill sets specific fee structures (including a $5,000 application fee and percentage‑based license fees) to fund administration.Defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and gives it primary regulatory, licensing, investigatory, and enforcement authority over fantasy contest operators (rulemaking re: consumer protection, geolocation, anti‑fraud/AML measures, background checks, investigations, referrals to law enforcement), while prohibiting rulemaking that governs individual contest mechanics. The department must process applications, conduct background investigations, issue/deny licenses, and integrate fantasy self‑exclusion into existing programs. Fee/funding provisions: nonrefundable application fee $5,000; initial license fees (existing operators: 10% of prior year adjusted gross receipts or $5,000, whichever is less; new operators: $5,000 plus a supplemental 10% fee on adjusted gross receipts). The Fantasy Sports Consumer Protection Fund is created, administered by the department, to receive license/application fees (invested per state law). Civil penalties accrue to the state; forfeited prizes are directed by the department to problem‑gaming programs.
109-1-LB343_IntroLB343_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor VehiclesLB343 amends section 60-3,104.01 as follows for references to the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): - Changes the specialty license plate application fee from $70 to $40 effective October 1, 2025. Sixty percent of initial and renewal specialty plate fees are credited to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund and forty percent to the Highway Trust Fund. - Allows the DMV to charge a postage and handling fee for mailing plates/registration; that fee is remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund. - Requires the $3 specialty-plate transfer fee be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund. - Assigns DMV duties: provide application forms, deliver plates/certificates (including by mail), furnish temporary license stickers to counties at no cost, and promulgate related rules.For the DMV: the added language sets a new dollar amount effective October 1, 2025 — "forty dollars." The clause distinguishes the period before October 1, 2025 (left unspecified in the added text) and a clear $40 amount beginning October 1, 2025. The amendment does not include any explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Motor Vehicles.
109-1-LB344_IntroLB344_Intro_Copy.docxLB344 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §46-740 regarding groundwater allocation. Key agencies and authorities: the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) retains authority to designate areas as fully appropriated or overappropriated; natural resources districts (NRDs) set allocations and may amend pre‑Nov. 1, 2005 municipal allocations; integrated management plans (IMPs), and controls/incentive programs under §46-715, govern responses to streamflow impacts. The bill bars IMPs, rules, or orders from limiting municipal or nonmunicipal commercial/industrial groundwater use in DNR-designated fully appropriated/overappropriated areas until Jan. 1, 2026, establishes base allocation standards (permit amount under the Industrial Ground Water Regulatory Act or amount necessary for the use, with special treatment for uses <25 million gallons/year), requires IMPs to address consumptive‑use increases that reduce streamflow, and specifies that certain small-use reductions between July 14, 2006, and Jan. 1, 2026, benefit the local NRD. No appropriations or budget changes are included.Adds that municipal water/wastewater allocations made before Nov. 1, 2005 remain in effect but may be amended by the appropriate natural resources district. For allocations made on or after Jan. 1, 2026, it indicates any new or expanded commercial or industrial user served by a municipality is subject to municipal controls (rule or order). Agencies mentioned: natural resources district and municipal authorities. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB345_IntroLB345_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesThe bill references the Department of Administrative Services in Sec. 75-104(2)(a), specifying that Public Service Commission commissioners' mileage reimbursement rate "shall not exceed the mileage rate established by the Department of Administrative Services pursuant to section 81-1176." The same section reiterates that total mileage reimbursements cannot cause expenses to exceed funds appropriated for commissioners' expenses. Separately, the bill amends statutory salaries for several constitutional officers (Lieutenant Governor, Secretary of State, Auditor, State Treasurer, Attorney General) and Public Service Commission commissioners effective January 7, 2027, replacing current amounts with placeholder "XX" figures, indicating future salary adjustments though specific dollar amounts are not provided.Adds effective January 7, 2027 standardized annual salaries (placeholders "XX thousand dollars") for commissioners, the Attorney General, and four constitutional officers (Secretary of State, Auditor of Public Accounts, State Treasurer, Lieutenant Governor). No language in the added text assigns funding, appropriations, or budget allocations to the Department of Administrative Services; the DAS is not directly affected by specified appropriations in this provision (amounts themselves are left as placeholders).
109-1-LB346_FinalLB346_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of TransportationThe bill assigns roles, reporting, and budget responsibilities to DHHS, DAS, DED, DOL, DOT and DMV. DHHS is named ex officio on the Climate Assessment Response Committee, must provide/coordinate staff for the Early Childhood Interagency Coordinating Council, serve as nonvoting ex officio on the Foster Care Reimbursement Rate Committee, report annual child‑welfare service data (including budget allocations), administer a newly created Women's Health Initiative Fund (apply/receive/remit funds to the State Treasurer; investable funds managed by the state investment officer), and become lead agency for the Critical Incident Stress Management Program effective July 1, 2026. DAS assumes duties of the Vacant Building and Excess Land Committee and the Suggestion Award Board beginning July 1, 2026. DOL must produce multilingual human‑trafficking posters and sits on a temporary Nebraska Safety Center advisory council alongside DOT and DMV. DED’s director (or designee) and its Housing Office join broadband and mental‑health advisory bodies. A Rural Broadband Task Force Fund (legislative appropriations/transfers, gifts/grants) is created and terminates July 1, 2026, with remaining balances reverting to the General Fund. Climate committee and children’s behavioral health expenses may be reimbursed from specified state funds.- Department of Administrative Services (DAS): Beginning July 1, 2026, DAS will assume duties of the Suggestion Award Board and the Vacant Building and Excess Land Committee (both terminate July 1, 2026). No funding or appropriation changes are specified. - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): As of July 1, 2026 DHHS will operate the Critical Incident Stress Management program, including coordination, equipment provision, recruitment/training, appointment of a program director (DHHS employee), planning and budget development, program evaluation, quality assurance, regional designation, and rulemaking authority. Also, the State Advisory Committee on Mental Health Services will assume duties of the State Advisory Committee on Substance Abuse Services (the latter terminates July 1, 2026). No explicit new appropriations or budget allocations are stated. - Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Transportation: no changes or funding actions appear in the added text.
109-1-LB347_IntroLB347_Intro_Copy.docxLB347 repeals Neb. Rev. Stat. §75‑148, eliminating the statutory conditions on common carriers’ issuance of securities that were tied to the Public Service Commission. In effect, the bill removes the specific PSC authority/responsibility established by that section to condition or regulate such securities issuances. No changes to agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included in the bill.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB348_IntroLB348_Intro_Copy.docxLB348 directs the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services to receive appropriations of $3,000,000 from the Health and Human Services Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 and $3,000,000 from the same fund for FY2026‑27. Funds are allocated to Program 354 for domestic violence services. The bill contains an emergency clause, making it effective upon passage and approval.Appropriates $3,000,000 from the Health and Human Services Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 and another $3,000,000 from the same fund for FY2026‑27 to the Department of Health and Human Services. Funds are allocated to Program 354 specifically for domestic violence services.
109-1-LB349_IntroLB349_Intro_Copy.docxLB349 primarily amends provisions administered by the Nebraska Power Review Board (the board) and its executive director. Key changes: - Expands defined terms to expressly include "electric energy storage resource" and revises "electric supplier," "private electric supplier," and "privately developed renewable energy generation facility." - Requires board application/approval before constructing or acquiring electric generation facilities, electric energy storage resources, or transmission facilities over 700 volts, while preserving specified exemptions. Privately developed renewable facilities remain exempt if they comply with section 70‑1014.02. - Establishes enforcement procedures administered by the board and its executive director for private electric suppliers who commence construction less than 30 days before required notice: a $500 fine, a 20‑day cure/pay window, mandatory cessation if not cured, and an administrative hearing process (hearing set within 60 days; board decision within 60 days). Hearing costs may be charged to the supplier if found in violation. - Repeals the original versions of the amended sections. No changes to state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a statutory definition of "electric energy storage resource": a resource that can receive and store electric energy for later injection to the grid (6)(a), and expressly excludes devices solely for reactive power (capacitors, synchronous condensers) or equipment solely to power electric vehicles (6)(b). Other inserted phrases appear to be minor textual references to "electric energy storage resources." No government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB34_FinalLB34_Final_Copy.docxLB34 conditions Nebraska’s adoption of year‑round daylight saving time by setting state standard time to UTC−5 (central) and UTC−6 (mountain) once authorized by federal law or order and after three adjacent states do likewise. Federal entities referenced: the Uniform Time Act of 1966, the U.S. Secretary of Commerce, the U.S. Secretary of the Navy, and the U.S. Secretary of Transportation. The bill also prescribes election poll opening/closing times and ballot deadlines by time zone. For state personnel administration, it standardizes sick‑ and vacation‑leave accounting to 11:59 p.m. central time, directs the Director of Personnel to adopt rules, preserves Governor (and the Executive Board of the Legislative Council for legislative employees) discretion to extend leave, and clarifies payment treatment under the Public Employees Retirement Board for forfeited leave. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a state time-standard provision for Nebraska (Central zone = UTC−5; Mountain zone = UTC−6). It references the General Conference on Weights and Measures as the maintainer of Coordinated Universal Time and names the U.S. Secretary of Commerce (in coordination with the U.S. Secretary of the Navy) as the federal official who interprets/modifies UTC for the United States. Operative date is the first Sunday in November after federal authorization or absence of conflict with U.S. law or any order of the U.S. Secretary of Transportation and after three adjacent states adopt a single year‑round time. The provision becomes void if subsection (2) of §49‑1301 becomes operative. No state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB350_IntroLB350_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB350 items referencing the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) and the Department of Correctional Services: - DHHS: Judges may commit defendants to DHHS for competency restoration (state hospital, other state facility, or contract provider). If DHHS proposes treatment by a contract facility/provider it must file a report with the court. If a committed defendant remains in a county jail, DHHS shall reimburse the county for lodging (daily lodging, food, medical services, transportation, other necessary costs) at $100/day for each day after the first 30 days, with annual July 1 CPI-based adjustments. DHHS also provides the emergency protective custody certificate form used by law enforcement. - Department of Correctional Services: Persons taken into emergency protective custody who have prior sex-offense convictions must be admitted to a jail or a Department of Correctional Services facility unless a medical/psychiatric emergency requires a medical facility. [NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.]Adds a procedural requirement that the county attorney must file a copy of the specified document with the court (and where applicable the tribal court or appropriate tribal official). The text appears repetitious/clerical. There are no provisions affecting the Department of Correctional Services or the Department of Health and Human Services, and no new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations included.
109-1-LB351_IntroLB351_Intro_Copy.docxLB351 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §83-338 to define admission priorities for state hospitals for the mentally ill: (a) patients whose hospital care is necessary to protect public health and safety; (b) defendants found incompetent to stand trial who remain lodged in county jail; and (c) persons committed by a mental health board under the Nebraska Mental Health Commitment Act or the Sex Offender Commitment Act, by a district court, or by a tribal court as provided in §§71-964 or 71-1226.01. The Department of Health and Human Services must publish a weekly online report (on or before Nov. 1, 2022) detailing capacity and wait times for state-operated mental health facilities by priority category. The bill repeals the original section. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a requirement that state psychiatric hospitals ("State hospitals for the mentally ill") must prioritize specified patient categories for admission. No other government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget-allocation changes included in the provided text. The clause appears to continue (list item 2), so additional prioritized categories likely follow.
109-1-LB352_IntroLB352_Intro_Copy.docxLB352 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-760.05, directing the State Board of Education and the State Department of Education to implement statewide student-achievement and student-discipline tracking using the department’s student identifier system. The State Board must publish a de-identified, searchable discipline database (by district, building, offense, discipline type, school resource officer/law enforcement involvement, restraint, and seclusion). School districts must report individual student incidents (suspensions, expulsions, alternative placements, physical intervention/restraint/seclusion, offenses triggering long-term discipline, and law-enforcement contact) and designate/publish a discipline data coordinator. The Department must annually analyze and electronically report aggregated and disaggregated achievement and discipline data to the Governor, Legislature, school districts, educational service units, and learning communities and post it publicly. The Commissioner of Education may enforce compliance, including accreditation actions. Original section repealed. No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds requirements for the State Board of Education and the Department of Education to create and publish a de‑identified, publicly searchable student discipline database (searchable by district, school, offense, discipline imposed, school resource officer/law enforcement involvement, restraint, and seclusion). Each school district must designate a discipline data coordinator and post that contact on its website. The department must publish an annual, disaggregated report (by demographics and discipline types and with academic/progress indicators) on its website without identifying individual students. The Commissioner of Education is given enforcement authority to notify noncompliant districts, allow time to cure, and take remedial action—including treating persistent, willful noncompliance as an accreditation rules violation. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are included.
109-1-LB353_IntroLB353_Intro_Copy.docxLB353 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-873 and prohibits labor organizations representing public school employees or employers of public school employees from imposing, in any membership contract entered or renewed after the bill’s effective date, restrictions on when a public school employee may join or terminate membership. The bill retains authorization procedures for payroll deductions (authorization in writing, employee notice, continued effect until revoked) and preserves certification of deduction amounts by the organization, but clarifies that the new timing restriction controls. The original §79-873 is repealed. Applies to school districts and labor/professional organizations; no changes to funding or appropriations. Emergency clause makes the act effective upon enactment.Adds a proviso that the ban on labor organizations placing timing restrictions on when public school employees may join or leave (for contracts entered or renewed after the act's effective date) is subject to any exceptions set out in section 1 of the act. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes indicated.
109-1-LB354_IntroLB354_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill requires the Auditor of Public Accounts to provide the Department of Revenue, by February 1 each year, a list of bond and nonbond tax request amounts from the most recent municipal budgets; the Department will use that information to calculate bond and nonbond tax levies for aid purposes. The bill also removes cities of the first class from eligibility for state aid from the Municipal Equalization Fund and retains provisions for prorated distributions if the Fund is insufficient and crediting any excess to the General Fund.Adds the phrase "or if such municipality is a city of the first class," broadening applicability or qualification to include municipalities designated as cities of the first class. No provisions in the provided text change Department of Revenue funding, appropriations, or budget allocations; no fiscal impact to the Department is indicated.
109-1-LB355_FinalLB355_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of LaborThe bill assigns the Department of Economic Development (DED) responsibility for: distributing state aid to certified development districts (50% equally, 20% prorated by population using the latest federal decennial census or DED determination if unavailable, and 30% by proportional local-government share), verifying local matching dollars, and administering distributions. Under ImagiNE Nebraska, a 0.5% administrative fee on incentives is remitted to the ImagiNE Nebraska Cash Fund, which DED administers and invests to fund program administration. Businesses seeking job-training grants must submit plans to DED; grant recipients are subject to DED audit and annual reporting. DED will update workforce-housing construction cost limits annually using the Producer Price Index from the U.S. Department of Labor (BLS). The Nebraska Innovation Hub Act is amended to define “Department” and “Director” as DED and its Director. No Department of Labor program changes or agency-level appropriations/budget reallocations are made.The added language lets the Department of Economic Development use American Community Survey (ACS) 5‑Year Estimates to determine population when the latest federal decennial census data are not available. No provisions affect the Department of Labor. There are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text.

Stat. §82-309 to specify that the Nebraska Arts Council consists of fifteen members appointed by the Governor from Nebraska citizens known for professional competence and experience in the arts. The statute directs that, in making appointments, consideration be given to recommendations from representative civic, educational, and professional associations and groups concerned with or engaged in the production or presentation of the arts. The bill also repeals the original §82-309. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined/added text was provided. 109-1-LB357_FinalLB357_Final_Copy.docxLB357 restructures administration of the State Racing and Gaming Commission and the Nebraska Racetrack Gaming Act. It expands licensing (adds a separate three‑year racetrack enclosure license; 20‑year operator licenses), requires fingerprint/background checks processed through the Nebraska State Patrol and FBI (applicant pays costs), and mandates market and socioeconomic studies filed with the Governor and the Legislature’s General Affairs Committee. Financial provisions authorize application/license and oversight fees, a one‑time $5 million authorized gaming operator license fee per racetrack (may be paid $1M/year over five years), a $50,000 annual review fee for 20‑year operator licenses, and a 20% gross gaming revenue tax. The bill creates/renames the Racetrack Gaming Fund to receive fees and certain horseracing receipts, transfers the Racing Cash Fund into it, and directs investment earnings to the General Fund beginning Oct. 1, 2024; the Commission remits fines/taxes to the State Treasurer for statutory distribution. It also revises equine‑activity liability exceptions and repeals multiple specified statutes.Adds authority for Nebraska State Fair Board, county fair boards, county agricultural societies, and qualifying nonprofit livestock/horse exposition organizations to apply to the Racing and Gaming Commission for a racetrack enclosure license (3‑year term; $10,000 application and $10,000 renewal fee). Existing horseracing licensees are deemed licensed until the commission rules. Applicants must submit fingerprints to the Nebraska State Patrol, which will forward them to the FBI and report results to the commission. Fiscal changes: the State Treasurer must transfer any money in the Racing and Gaming Commission’s Racing Cash Fund on the act’s effective date to a new Racetrack Gaming Fund. Provisions reference license-fee structures (including an initial $5 million fee payable in $1 million annual installments) and allocation of license fees and gross tax receipts to the commission.
109-1-LB358_IntroLB358_Intro_Copy.docxLB358 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §83-178 (Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act). It directs the Department (and its director) to establish and maintain individual files for committed offenders and requires file review before classification, transfer, preparole, or parole decisions. Committed offenders may access their own individual file by written request to the facility chief executive officer and may obtain medical records from the provider under §§71-8401–71-8407; the department may withhold mental‑health/psychological records when appropriate. The Office of Public Counsel retains inspection authority under §§81‑8,240–81‑8,254 but must have offender consent to access medical/mental‑health records and may not further disclose those records except as authorized by law. No funding or appropriation changes.Adds a provision letting a committed offender access his or her individual file by written request to the facility’s chief executive officer. No specific state agency or department is named, and there are no funding, appropriations, or budget allocation changes included.
109-1-LB359_IntroLB359_Intro_Copy.docxLB359 states the Legislature’s intent that the Department of Health and Human Services increase rates for child welfare aid. The bill is declarative in intent; no specific rate changes, funding amounts, appropriations, or new budget allocations are contained in the text provided. Introduced by Senator M. 109-1-LB35_IntroLB35_Intro_Copy.docxLB35 amends procedures for privately developed renewable energy facilities, emphasizing roles for state and local agencies. Key agency provisions: - "Board" (and its executive director) receives developer notices, issues exemption acknowledgments within 10 days, may sue in the name of the State for failure to meet decommissioning security requirements, and receives copies of bonds/instruments. - Private developers must consult the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission to identify measures to avoid or mitigate impacts to protected species. - Developers must enter joint transmission development agreements with the electric supplier that owns transmission ≥60 kV and comply with applicable regional transmission organization processes. - Facilities near military installations must meet 15 C.F.R. 7.4 related foreign-adversary restrictions or NERC critical-infrastructure requirements. - Local governmental entities may enact decommissioning rules that supersede state bond requirements. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The added text is only the phrase "Will, upon reaching commercial operation, be." It does not reference any government agency or department and contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB360_IntroLB360_Intro_Copy.docxLB360 (2025) limits homeowner association regulation of political signs by specifying categories of signs that associations may prohibit or remove: signs larger than 4'×6', signs with language or graphics judged offensive to an ordinary person, signs accompanied by music/sounds or streamers or otherwise distracting to motorists, and signs that violate any law. Associations may remove signs that violate restrictive covenants not preempted by the bill. No state agencies or departments are referenced, and no funding or appropriations changes are included.Adds four prohibitions on signs: larger than 4×6 feet; containing language/graphics offensive to an ordinary person; accompanied by music/sounds, streamers, or otherwise distracting to motorists; or that violate any law. Also explicitly permits a homeowner association to remove signs that violate restrictive covenants not barred by this section. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are affected.
109-1-LB361_IntroLB361_Intro_Copy.docxLB361 amends the Nebraska Fair Employment Practice Act to (1) prohibit covered employers from discriminating or retaliating against individuals who report work‑related injuries, bring claims, or seek remedies under the Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Act, and to state that the Act’s remedies are supplemental to workers’ compensation; and (2) establish a right to jury trial in civil actions under the Act, explicitly including cases against state and governmental agencies. Section 48-1126 is revised to confirm state and government agencies may be sued under the Act like other employers. Sections 48-1125 and 48-1126 are amended and the originals repealed. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are provided.Adds that it is unlawful for a "covered entity" to discriminate or retaliate against someone for reporting a work‑related injury, filing a claim, or seeking remedies under the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act. States that rights and remedies under the Nebraska Fair Employment Practice Act are supplemental to those under the Workers' Compensation Act. Establishes a right to a jury trial in any civil action under the Fair Employment Practice Act, explicitly including suits against state and governmental agencies. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included. The language is incorporated into sections 1–3 of the act.
109-1-LB362_FinalLB362_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue- Department of Health and Human Services: directs DHHS to oversee Nebraska’s 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline—including contracting for counselors, call‑center operators, and providers—and to coordinate with the Public Service Commission to ensure 988 connectivity and interoperability with the 911 system. - Department of Revenue: requires the Department of Revenue to set the prepaid wireless surcharge annually (effective Jan. 1) based on prior July 1 charge levels, post at least 90 days’ advance notice of changes online, and provide the Public Service Commission surcharge calculation and collection data on request. - Funding: designates the prepaid wireless surcharge as the sole funding obligation for 911 service, telecommunications relay service, and universal service for prepaid wireless; creates a 911 Service System Fund but includes no direct appropriations or budgetary allocations to DHHS or the Department of Revenue.Adds standards and goals for a statewide next‑generation 911 system: interoperability, security, common standards, capacity to receive/process/analyze all 911 request types, integrate additional data, and share info among PSAPs. Establishes staggered three‑year terms for committee members beginning in 2025. Exempts providers from collecting the wireless surcharge for customers served under the Nebraska Telephone Assistance Program who do not receive a monthly billing statement. No direct appropriations, budget allocations, or new funding lines are specified. Potential impact for the Department of Revenue: reduced wireless surcharge collections from exempt NTAP customers (not quantified). No explicit changes to the Department of Health and Human Services’ funding or responsibilities appear in the added text.
