109-1-LB364_FinalLB364_Final_Copy.docxAmends Neb. Rev. Stat. §37-342. Retains the commission's authority to enter long-term leases, lease-purchase agreements, or other agreements for state park purposes. Requires the commission to obtain approval from the Legislature — or, when the Legislature is not in session, the Executive Board of the Legislative Council — before issuing an indication of intent to incorporate land or facilities owned or developed by a local governmental subdivision into the state park system. When seeking that approval, the commission must provide an estimated fiscal impact that specifies the extent costs can be paid from cash funds and the extent likely to require General Fund appropriations. Repeals the original section.Adds a clause specifying that when the Legislature is not in session, authority (or action) may be exercised by the Executive Board of the Legislative Council. The text repeats the same clause; no executive agencies beyond the Legislative Council are mentioned and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB365_IntroLB365_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB365 directs the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to take multiple Medicaid actions and makes specific funding intentions: - By Jan 1, 2026, DHHS must provide coverage and reimbursement for self-measured blood pressure monitoring services (device, cuffs, training, data collection). - By Jan 1, 2025, DHHS must cover electric personal-use breast pumps and a minimum of ten lactation consultation visits; the Legislature intends the appropriation for those visits equal a 145% increase over DHHS’s current lactation consultation rate. - By Jan 1, 2024, DHHS must cover and reimburse necessary translation/interpretation services and maximize federal funding; those services are to be funded by the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund. - By Jan 1, 2023, DHHS must provide continuous glucose monitor coverage; effective Aug 1, 2024 eligibility expands. The Legislature intends up to $600,000 annually be appropriated from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for that expansion (excess also funded from the Fund). - By Oct 1, 2023, DHHS must seek federal approval to extend postpartum Medicaid coverage to at least six months. - By Oct 1, 2025, DHHS must submit a waiver/state plan amendment to designate two medical respite facilities for homeless adults in the expansion population; those services shall be funded by the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund and DHHS must report annually after approval.Requirement for the Department of Health and Human Services to, by January 1, 2026, provide coverage and reimbursement under the medical assistance program for self-measure blood pressure monitoring services for all eligible recipients. Covered services must include a validated blood pressure device, appropriately sized (and replacement) cuffs, patient education/training on device setup/use, calibration and measurement procedures, and patient/caregiver data reporting to providers for treatment planning. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocation language is included.
109-1-LB366_IntroLB366_Intro_Copy.docxLB366 creates a Legislative Economic Analysis Unit and a Chief Economist within the Legislature to review regulatory economic impacts. State agencies (boards, commissions, departments, etc.) must publish proposed rules, notify the Legislature and Chief Economist, and submit cost‑benefit analyses (including public vs. private jobs impacts) and related information before filing rules with the Secretary of State. Agencies must classify rules as major or nonmajor. The Unit must report on each major rule to the subject committee within 15 legislative days, assessing procedural compliance, private‑sector impacts, and the regulatory impact analysis. Major rules cannot be published by the Secretary of State until ratified by the Legislature or 60 legislative days pass; the Governor may approve limited emergency early effective dates with required findings. The bill amends Administrative Procedure Act definitions and preserves limited judicial review. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds procedures requiring agencies to electronically submit proposed rules to the Legislature and the Chief Economist and to publish notice in a statewide newspaper before filing with the Secretary of State. Agencies must provide copies, concise statements, a major/nonmajor classification with justification, related regulatory actions and their economic effects, proposed effective dates, and cost‑benefit analyses (including jobs added/lost, public vs. private). The Legislative Economic Analysis Unit must report on each major rule to the relevant legislative committee within 15 legislative days, assessing procedural compliance, regulatory impact, and effects on private‑sector mandates; agencies must cooperate. Major rules generally cannot be sent to the Secretary of State or take effect until ratified by the Legislature or after 60 legislative days, unless the Governor seeks earlier effect and publishes a written emergency/federal‑funding justification. Courts may review whether statutory requirements were completed. No funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB367_IntroLB367_Intro_Copy.docxLB367 amends the Uniform Credentialing Act to (1) add a new section prohibiting licensed providers under the Medicine and Surgery, Mental Health, Nurse, Pharmacy, and Psychology Practice Acts from providing conversion therapy to persons under 19, (2) define conversion-, gender-identity-, and sexual-orientation-conversion therapy and carve out clergy/religious-capacity exceptions, and (3) make violations both a ground for discipline by the Department (with board recommendation) and a deceptive trade practice under the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act. The bill also clarifies that Department disciplinary procedures and notice/hearing processes apply, and extends these disciplinary grounds to pharmacy technician registrations overseen by the Department and board. It prohibits expenditure of state or political-subdivision funds for providing, referring, or insuring conversion therapy.Adds a prohibition barring credentialed providers under the Medicine and Surgery, Mental Health, Nurse, Pharmacy, and Psychology Practice Acts from providing conversion, gender identity, or sexual‑orientation conversion therapy to anyone under 19. Defines those therapies and exempts clergy acting in a purely religious/pastoral (non‑healthcare) capacity. Violations are designated deceptive trade practices under the Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act (subject to its remedies/penalties). Crucially, the state and its political subdivisions are forbidden from expending funds to conduct or refer for conversion therapy or to provide health‑benefit coverage for it.
109-1-LB368_IntroLB368_Intro_Copy.docxLB368 creates the Nebraska Youth in Care Bill of Rights and assigns specific duties to the state child welfare agency (referred to in the bill as "the department"), guardians ad litem, caseworkers, and the courts. Key agency-related provisions: - The department must facilitate sibling joint placement/visitation (per §43-1311.02), reunification and family visitation as required by state/federal law, provide transition plans and post-adoption information (per §43-1311.03), maintain confidentiality consistent with law, and ensure access to vital documents. - Caseworkers must be trained on the rights, deliver paper notices to youth aged 14+, discuss rights on defined timelines (within 72 hours, within two weeks, then quarterly), and explain grievance procedures. - Guardians ad litem must discuss rights within two weeks of appointment and every six months, and raise suspected infringements to the court. - The department must acknowledge grievances within three business days and provide appeal information under the Administrative Procedure Act. - The Nebraska Strengthening Families Act Committee (§43-4716) will monitor implementation. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Adds detailed child-welfare duties and oversight. Key government actors named or implicated: - "The department" (child welfare agency) must facilitate sibling placements/visitation, reunification, family visitation, confidentiality, access to vital records, transition plans for youth (including parenting youth), and explain denials; must acknowledge foster‑care grievances within three business days and provide grievance/Administrative Procedure Act review information. - Caseworkers must be trained on and provide paper notices of youth rights, discuss them on set timelines, and obtain acknowledgments. - Guardians ad litem (appointed under §43‑272.01) must discuss rights soon after appointment and semiannually and raise alleged infringements to the court. - Courts and the Nebraska Strengthening Families Act Committee (§43‑4716) will monitor implementation. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB369_IntroLB369_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB369 amends section 43-2101 to address decisionmaking for youth in agency custody. It provides that 18-year-olds may make health-care decisions without parental consent except when they are in the custody of the Department of Health and Human Services pursuant to a juvenile court order. It further allows persons under 19 who are committed to the Department of Correctional Services for secure care to consent to and make decisions about their medical care, mental health services, and related services during commitment without parental consent, subject to section 71-6902. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds two consent rules: (c) Individuals 18+ may consent to their own health care without parental/guardian permission, unless they are in the custody of the Department of Health and Human Services under a juvenile court order. (d) Persons under 19 who are committed to the Department of Correctional Services for secure care may consent to and make decisions about their medical, mental‑health, and related services for the duration of the commitment, except as otherwise required by section 71‑6902. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB36A_FinalLB36A_Final_Copy.docxLB36A appropriates funds to the Nebraska Department of Environment and Energy (Program 513) to implement Legislative Bill 36. It directs (1) $51,585 from the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund for FY2025‑26 and (2) $109,036 from the same fund for FY2026‑27. It caps total expenditures from these appropriations for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems at $30,264 for FY2025‑26 and $63,554 for FY2026‑27.Appropriates funds from the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund to the Department of Environment and Energy, Program 513: $51,585 for FY2025‑26 and $109,036 for FY2026‑27 to support implementation of Legislative Bill 36 (109th Legislature, 2025). Limits permanent and temporary salaries and per diems charged to these appropriations to no more than $30,264 in FY2025‑26 and $63,554 in FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB36_FinalLB36_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB36 defines "department" as the Department of Transportation and designates the Nebraska DOT as authority over the state highway system and federal‑aid primary road designations (subject to U.S. Secretary of Transportation approval). The DOT may redesignate, relocate, or recreate routes with State Highway Commission advice and the Governor’s consent, considering traffic, costs, safety, and economic factors. The bill authorizes the DOT to acquire land, interests and easements (including by eminent domain) for highway purposes; to establish and operate mitigation banks or in‑lieu‑fee programs for compensatory mitigation; to enter cooperative agreements and adopt related rules; and requires payment in lieu of ad valorem taxes for mitigation property acquired after July 1, 2026. No explicit appropriations or budget allocations to the DOT are included.Adds authority for the Department of Transportation to establish, use, and operate a mitigation bank or in‑lieu‑fee program to provide compensatory mitigation for transportation projects it administers (impacts to threatened/endangered species or habitat, wetland dredge/fill, and habitat restoration/creation/enhancement/preservation). State regulatory agencies must give priority to the department's mitigation bank when reviewing mitigation plans. The department may enter cooperative agreements with public or private parties and may acquire real property for the program—including by purchase, gift, or eminent domain. Owners of mitigation bank property acquired after July 1, 2026 must pay a sum in lieu of lost ad valorem taxes to the county. The department may adopt rules. No explicit new appropriations or line‑item funding changes are specified.
109-1-LB370_IntroLB370_Intro_Copy.docxLB370 amends the Nebraska Student-Athlete Name, Image, or Likeness Rights Act. Relevant government entities: postsecondary institutions (as defined in §85-2403) and public postsecondary institutions are specifically addressed — the bill requires written contracts for payments ≥ $5,000 involving a name/image/likeness collective, postsecondary institution, or third party, and provides that public postsecondary institutions may be sued under this Act only to the extent allowed by the State Tort Claims Act, State Contract Claims Act, or State Miscellaneous Claims Act, with a one-year limitations period. The Supreme Court is referenced for attorney admission as qualified professional representation. Agency agreements are generally not public records. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds definitions (Parties; Third party) and new compliance rules under the Nebraska Student‑Athlete Name, Image, or Likeness Rights Act. Mentions state or federal civil courts (as grounds for disqualifying an athlete agent if charges/convictions exist) and references "section 48‑3604" and "this state" regarding agency‑agreement public‑record status and agent licensure. Requires written contracts when anticipated annual NIL payments to a student‑athlete meet or exceed $5,000, specifying payer identity, total compensation, payment timing, athlete obligations, term dates, revision/termination options, and nonpayment terms. Prohibits certain payments by agents (e.g., loans to induce representation) and voids contracts offering upfront benefits for future NIL rights. No changes to government funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB371_FinalLB371_Final_Copy.docxLB371 (2025) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§25-3502 and 25-3503 (Uniform Civil Remedies for Unauthorized Disclosure of Intimate Images Act). Key changes: expands “depicted individual” and “intimate image” definitions to cover images created by computer generation or digital manipulation; treats such nonconsensual computer-generated/digitally manipulated images as potentially “private”; clarifies consent, identifiability, and harm standards; and preserves causes of action against persons who intentionally or recklessly disclose private intimate images. The bill repeals the prior versions of those sections. No state agencies, departments, appropriations, or budgetary changes are referenced.Adds language expanding covered material to explicitly include content produced "by means of computer generation or digital manipulation" and clarifies clause (C) to cover images or content "created by means of computer generation or digital manipulation without the consent of the depicted individual" (and an alternate phrasing concerning information displayed in connection with an intimate image). No government agencies, departments, appropriations, or funding changes are mentioned.
109-1-LB372_FinalLB372_Final_Copy.docxLB372 repeals sections 2-3813, 2-3814, and 81-2,181, removing statutory provisions governing grain inspections, the Nebraska Origin and Premium Quality Grain Cash Fund, and labeling requirements for honey. The bill text does not explicitly name any state agency or department. By repealing the cash fund statute, it effectively abolishes that dedicated funding mechanism; no new appropriations or other budget allocations are provided in the bill.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB373_FinalLB373_Final_Copy.docxLB373 amends Nebraska road statutes (sections 39-1410, 39-1722, 39-1724, 39-1725). Key agency actions and roles: - County board: may open section-line roads when public good requires; may propose/vote to vacate or abandon public roads (two-thirds vote required); must specify disposition conditions; must file certified vacating resolution with the county register of deeds within 30 days. - County highway superintendent (or designee): may be directed to study road use and submit written reports retained by the county clerk. - County surveyor or a licensed professional land surveyor: must perform work to perpetuate government corners and plant monuments; lost corners located per state survey statutes. - Governing body of metropolitan/primary/first-class cities and their planning and public works directors: prior approval required for vacations/abandonments within city zoning jurisdiction; must receive mailed notice before hearings. - Townships: may receive offers to relinquish roads in township-operating counties. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds procedures empowering county boards to propose vacating or abandoning previously declared public roads (those under former section 39-1410), allows such actions without requiring a study, and requires the county board to set a public hearing (time/date/place) and mail notices to affected persons (per section 39-1724). It also assigns duties to a directed superintendent or designated person to carry out tasks such as causing survey monuments to be placed. References include sections 23-1907, 23-1908, 39-1722 and 39-1724. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB374_IntroLB374_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill expressly defines, for FBI interpretation related to criminal background checks, that the term "department" in section 38-131 means the Division of Public Health of the Department of Health and Human Services. This is in the context of fingerprinting and national criminal history record checks for initial licensure applicants. No appropriations, budget allocations, or other funding changes for the Department of Health and Human Services are included.Creates a Licensed Midwives Practice Act administered by the Department of Health and Human Services (the department) and a five‑member Board of Licensed Midwives. The department is responsible for licensing and determining applicant qualifications (including CPM credentialing and education standards), issuing/renewing licenses, and enforcing the Act per board rules. The board will adopt practice standards, testing and medication authorizations (e.g., oxytocin), consent form and newborn screening requirements. The department shall establish and collect initial licensure and renewal fees as provided in sections 38‑151 to 38‑157. Licensed midwives may practice without supervision or collaborative agreements. No new appropriations, budget allocations, or other funding changes are included in the added text.
109-1-LB375_IntroLB375_Intro_Copy.docxLB375 creates the Grocer Reinvestment Option Fund, to be administered by the department (agency name not specified). The department may use up to 15% of fund money for administrative costs, adopt rules, and must report annually to the Legislature (first report due October 31, 2025) on projects funded, geographic distribution, applicant identities, and resulting new investment. The fund will consist of legislative transfers and private gifts/grants; monies available for investment are to be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The bill expresses legislative intent to appropriate an unspecified amount for FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27. Grants must be spent within three years; unspent grant funds are recouped and remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund.Creates the Grocer Reinvestment Option Fund, administered by “the department,” with up to 15% of fund money allowed for the department’s administrative costs. The fund may include legislative transfers plus gifts, grants, and private contributions. Available funds must be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The Legislature intends to appropriate [XXX] for FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27 to implement the Act. The department must report annually (first due Oct. 31, 2025) on projects, locations, applicants, and new investment. Grants must be spent within three years; unspent disbursed grant funds will be recouped, remitted to the State Treasurer, and credited to the General Fund. The department may adopt implementing rules.
109-1-LB376_FinalLB376_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill assigns multiple operational, reporting, and funding responsibilities to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) and assigns budget oversight roles to the Department of Administrative Services (DAS). DHHS duties include receiving physician abortion reports and publishing an annual public report; annual program reporting (due Dec. 1) and continued Nebraska Prenatal Plus reporting through Dec. 15, 2029; receiving/furnishing mental‑health/commitment data for the firearm‑purchase database; investigating facility infectious‑disease notifications; operating the lead‑poisoning program and statewide cancer registry; and developing a developmental‑disabilities quality improvement plan with goals/benchmarks included in the biennial budget to the DAS Director. DHHS must create an amino‑acid elemental‑formula assistance program (up to 50% of OOP, max $12,000/12 months) and apply for a 1915(c) waiver to run a capped family support program ($10,000/applicant, ≤850 participants) with ARPA funds as available. Medical‑assistance/managed‑care contract limits are tightened (admin ≤12%, profit ≤3%, MLR 85%, incentives ≤2%). Specified ICF/DD and other allocations include $55,000 admin, $312,000 community services, and $1,000,000 to the General Fund. Appropriations: cigarette‑tax‑derived HHS Cash Fund monies (registry ≤$200,000; research limits) and a required $7,000,000 transfer from that cash fund to the General Fund as directed by the DAS budget administrator. DAS will receive agency budget forms, enforce deadlines, collaborate on DHHS goals/benchmarks, administer allotments and position authorizations, and may review long‑vacant positions.The added language mainly extends and clarifies statutory deadlines and scope-of-practice limits: it cross‑references post‑fertilization age limits in section 71‑6915; authorizes an "advanced technician" to visualize intubation and to perform the acts of an emergency medical technician‑intermediate through December 31, 2025; and pushes multiple statutory deadlines to dates including December 31, 2025; December 31, 2027; June 30, 2028; and December 15, 2029. Affected citations include sections such as 71‑6915, 71‑510, 68‑1735.01, 81‑3133.01, and 81‑649.02. The text contains no explicit references to the Department of Administrative Services or the Department of Health and Human Services, and it does not make any appropriations, budget allocations, or funding changes for either agency.
109-1-LB377_FinalLB377_Final_Copy.docxLB377 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §37-101 governing the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission. The commission remains nine members (one from each of eight districts plus one at-large), appointed by the Governor with the consent of a majority of the Legislature. Members must be Nebraska residents and citizens, district appointees must reside in their districts, at least three must be engaged in agricultural pursuits, and no more than five may share the same political party. Members serve four-year terms beginning January 15 and serve until successors qualify; appointments to fill vacancies are for the remainder of the term and do not count as a full term. No person who has served three full terms is eligible for reappointment. The Governor may remove members after a hearing; removal actions are filed with the Secretary of State. The bill repeals the original section. No funding or appropriation changes are included.I can’t summarize because you didn’t include the underlined (added) text — you only sent “three.” Please paste the underlined excerpt here (or upload the bill and indicate the section). 109-1-LB378_IntroLB378_Intro_Copy.docxLB378 requires every public or private two- or four-year college or university in Nebraska to file quarterly reports with the Attorney General and electronically to the Legislature detailing "reportable funding" (> $50) received from defined foreign sources. Reports must include amount, purpose, whether ongoing, foreign source identity and address, and copies of related contracts/agreements. Tuition payments by a natural person foreign payer on behalf of an individual are exempt. The Attorney General will prescribe the report format, post reports on the AG website, and enforce the law. Enforcement includes civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation and forfeiture of any reportable funding not disclosed. No appropriations or budget changes are included.Adds a quarterly reporting requirement for Nebraska public and private two‑ and four‑year colleges and universities to disclose to the Attorney General (and electronically to the Legislature) all “reportable funding” from defined foreign sources (broadly: foreign governments, foreign legal entities, non‑U.S. individuals, and their agents) over $50. Reports must include amounts, purpose, donor identity, contracts/MOUs and whether funding is ongoing. The Attorney General must prescribe report format, post reports on the AG website, and enforce the provision, with civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation and forfeiture of unreported funds. Payments by a foreign natural person for an individual’s tuition are exempt. No appropriations or budget allocations for agencies are specified.
109-1-LB379_IntroLB379_Intro_Copy.docxLB379 amends section 68-1724 (Welfare Reform Act). It specifies cash assistance for recipient families with children is limited to a total of twenty-four months, with the time limit extended if the state fails to meet terms of the self‑sufficiency contract. The bill requires the department to develop policy guidelines to permit additional cash assistance for families facing extreme hardship and to revise self‑sufficiency contracts and extend assistance when no job is available. It establishes cost‑shared, work‑related child care assistance up to 200% of the federal poverty level prior to October 1, 2026, and 185% thereafter, with family contributions up to 20% of gross income. No specific appropriations, new funding amounts, or budget allocations are included.No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriations, or budget allocation changes. The added text is an editorial adjustment: it hyphenates "twenty-four month" to "twenty-four-month."
109-1-LB37_IntroLB37_Intro_Copy.docxLB37 adopts the Railroad Safety Act and amends the Public Service Commission's (PSC) jurisdiction to explicitly include railroad carrier safety pursuant to the Railroad Safety Act and specified statutory sections (74-918, 74-919, 74-1323, 75-401 to 75-430). The bill defines railroad safety terms, limits trains carrying hazardous substances on federally defined main lines to 8,500 feet, creates a civil-liability rule for trains exceeding 7,000 feet, and states the PSC lacks authority over railroad labor relations. The Federal Railroad Administration is referenced for main-line tonnage definitions. The act is operative July 1, 2026, repeals the prior version of section 75-109.01 and section 17-225. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Added provisions reference and rely on federal agencies and rules: definitions incorporate terms from 49 C.F.R. and 49 U.S.C., and "main line" is tied to timetables filed with the Federal Railroad Administration. The bill designates the Public Service Commission as "Commission" but expressly states the Railroad Safety Act does not give the Commission jurisdiction over railroad labor relations or collective‑bargaining matters. New operational limits include an 8,500‑foot maximum train length on state main lines and a civil‑litigation rule preventing reduction of plaintiff recovery for comparative fault where a train over 7,000 feet caused injury. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.

Specified amounts in this program are designated for state aid only. 109-1-LB380_FinalLB380_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill directs the Division of Medicaid and Long-Term Care of the Department of Health and Human Services to: (1) require medicaid managed-care contractors to comply with federal/state laws and EPSDT requirements for mental health and substance-use services; (2) make contractor surveys, financial analyses, contract audits, and parity reports and results public; (3) ensure access parity and provider access through review of claims, reimbursement procedures, network adequacy, and rate adequacy; (4) establish monthly electronic communications with all Medicaid providers about managed-care contract amendments; (5) define network adequacy; and (6) annually post the Division’s network adequacy assessment criteria and each MCO’s compliance on the Department website. No specific appropriations or budget allocations to the Department are specified.Summary (Dept. of Health and Human Services focus): Adds detailed audit and program‑integrity protections and obligations. Program integrity contractors must provide written justification to a provider before an audit; limit records requests to documents proportional to the audit; give 90 days to adjust mis-billed claims; provide ≥10 business days’ notice for onsite audits; and include a detailed written notice of any alleged overpayment (beneficiary, dates, amount, claim IDs, evidence, payment method, recovery method, appeals info, and a 60‑day non‑recoupment period after notice). Contractors may not recoup until appeals are exhausted unless a department‑verified “credible allegation of fraud.” Contractors must supply appeal procedures, contact info, and answer provider inquiries within 10 business days. The Division of Medicaid and Long‑Term Care must enforce MH/SUD parity, ensure access and rate/network adequacy, publish contractor audits/parity reports, define network adequacy, provide monthly electronic provider communications about MCO contract changes, and annually post network adequacy criteria and MCO compliance. No explicit funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB381_IntroLB381_Intro_Copy.docxLB381 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §68-974 (Medical Assistance Act) to tighten program-integrity requirements for the Department (DHHS) and its contractors and to formalize coordination with the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and Medicaid managed care organizations. Key provisions: limit claim review to one year from date of payment (except fraud); require written justification to providers to commence audits, 180-day determination letters, 10 business days' notice for onsite audits, and minimum response windows for records; exclude capitated managed‑care claims from recovery-audit scope and require coordination among DHHS, contractors, and MCOs; ban most extrapolated overpayments; require annual contractor performance metrics posted on the department website and a December 1 annual report to the Legislature. No appropriation or budget allocation changes are specified.Adds audit and notice protections tied to "the department" and its contractors (program integrity contractor; audit/recovery contractor). Key agency/contractor requirements: - The audit-initiating entity must provide clear written justification to the provider before commencing an audit. - Adjustments to payments barred after one year from payment except for provider fraud. - Records requests must be limited to documents relevant and proportional to the services audited (per subsection (12)). - Onsite audits must be scheduled with at least ten business days' advance notice; documentation cannot be required sooner than 90 days after a provider's request. - Written adverse findings/recoupment notices from the department/contractor must include ten specified items (beneficiary, dates, amount, claim number, detailed basis/evidence, payment method, claims-adjustment procedure, appeal right, recovery method, and a 60-day wait before recoupment). - Program integrity contractors may not recoup until appeals are exhausted (except credible fraud) and must provide appeal procedures, contact info, and respond to provider inquiries within ten business days. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.

It provides $2,000,000 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for FY2025-26 and $2,000,000 from the same fund for FY2026-27. Each fiscal-year appropriation is designated as $2,000,000 in Cash Funds for state aid and may only be used for that purpose. The bill prohibits using these appropriated funds for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates to the Department of Health and Human Services (Program 571) $2,000,000 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for FY2025‑26 and $2,000,000 for FY2026‑27 (total $4,000,000 across the biennium) to support implementation of Legislative Bill 382 (109th Leg., 2025). Each annual appropriation is designated as $2,000,000 Cash Funds restricted for state aid only. The funds may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB382_FinalLB382_Final_Copy.docxLB382 amends funding and reimbursement for aging services. It expands uses of the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund to include reimbursement of actual costs for eligible activities and services under section 81-2222 and retains investment/crediting provisions (State Treasurer returns; state investment officer investments; earnings credited to the General Fund beginning Oct. 1, 2024). The Legislature intends to appropriate $2,000,000 in FY2025-26 and $2,000,000 in FY2026-27 from that fund to the state's eight area agencies on aging (equal shares). Section 81-2224 is amended to require "the department" to reimburse each designated area agency on aging 75% of actual costs from (1) state appropriations (including the specified fund), (2) federal allocations (e.g., Older Americans Act), and (3) other funds; payments are monthly and prorated if funds are insufficient.Adds legislative intent to appropriate $2,000,000 in FY2025‑26 and $2,000,000 in FY2026‑27 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund to the state's eight area agencies on aging. Funds are for providing or reimbursing actual costs of eligible activities and services as defined in section 81‑2222 and will be distributed equally to each of the eight agencies. References cash fund appropriations described in section 2 of the act.
109-1-LB383_FinalLB383_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor VehiclesThe bill amends multiple statutes affecting the three agencies as follows: - Department of Motor Vehicles: Sec. 8 (amending 25-21,302) requires inquiry of DMV records when seized motor vehicles or titled vessels may show recorded owners or liens; responses must be used to identify and name owners or lienholders in forfeiture petitions. - Department of Health and Human Services: Adds “a Department of Health and Human Services employee” to the list of protected persons under the racketeering/predicate-offense statute (making assaults on DHHS employees prosecutable under that provision). DHHS is named as the reporting recipient for sexual-assault victims under 18, may receive information from criminal-justice agencies for child-abuse/neglect investigations, and is identified as a provider of sex-offender treatment during incarceration. - Department of Correctional Services: DCS must order mental-health evaluations at least 180 days before scheduled release to assess whether certain offenders qualify as dangerous sex offenders; results and an affidavit must be sent to the Attorney General and relevant county attorneys. Evaluations may be required where inmates refused or failed in-prison sex-offender treatment. No appropriations, funding increases, or agency-specific budget allocations for DMV, DHHS, or DCS are included.No specific new duties, appropriations, or budget allocations are directed to the Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, or the Department of Motor Vehicles. - Department of Correctional Services: The bill creates/clarifies offenses and penalties for child sexual abuse material (Class III felony for offenders under 19, Class ID for adults, Class IC for repeat offenders) and references forfeiture statutes—these could increase incarceration demand but include no funding or appropriation language. - Department of Health and Human Services: No substantive provisions or funding changes affecting DHHS in the added text. - Department of Motor Vehicles: A “digitized identification card” is defined (mirrors data on an operator’s license), but the bill does not assign duties to DMV or provide funding. Attorney General enforcement and civil penalties (up to $2,500 per violation) are included; penalties go to the State Treasurer.
109-1-LB384_IntroLB384_Intro_Copy.docxLB384 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-1633 (Property Tax Request Act). It applies to political subdivisions (counties, cities, school districts, community colleges) and adds a requirement that a majority of the elected members of each participating subdivision's governing body attend joint public hearings on proposed property-tax-request increases above the allowable growth percentage. County clerks (or designees) organize the joint hearings; county assessors receive electronic submissions by September 4 and coordinate printing with a service designated by the county board. The bill preserves existing postcard-notice procedures: initial printing charged to the county general fund and the creation/mailing costs (including staff time, materials, postage) apportioned proportionately to participating political subdivisions. The original section is repealed.Adds the phrase "a majority of the elected members of the governing body of." Stat. §87-302 (Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act), expanding and clarifying categories of deceptive trade practices — including false privacy-policy statements; restrictions on installing or activating file‑sharing programs on others’ computers; treating each misbranded individually packaged substance as a separate violation; prohibiting publication/monetization of sexually explicit, obscene, or harmful-to-minors material when participants are minors, trafficking victims, or nonconsenting (with a telecommunications/broadband exception); and barring certain right-to-list home sale agreements. 109-1-LB386_IntroLB386_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services- The bill expands the definition of "administrator" to expressly include an administrator of a Department of Correctional Services facility (or designee). - Multiple provisions authorize holding persons taken into emergency protective custody, or subjects in sex-offender commitment proceedings, in a Department of Correctional Services facility as an appropriate location for admission or custody; dangerous sex offenders may be held in DOC facilities and shall not be admitted to a medical facility for emergency custody unless a medical or psychiatric emergency requires it. - The written emergency-custody certificate required from law enforcement must be prescribed and provided by the Department of Health and Human Services; copies are forwarded to the county attorney. - No direct appropriations or specified budget amounts for either agency appear.Creates the Regional Mental Health Expansion Pilot Program administered by the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice to fund one county law enforcement agency to add mental‑health beds regionally. The commission must develop grant eligibility, application and audit rules, identify grant funding, and may adopt rules; it will coordinate with the Attorney General. No specific appropriation or dollar amounts are included. Department of Correctional Services: added as an explicit potential placement site ("Department of Correctional Services facility") and is referenced in provisions allowing admission to jails/other correctional facilities under the pilot and permitting videoconferenced evaluations/hearings. Department of Health and Human Services: not directly altered or allocated funding in the added text; existing references to medical facilities and section 71‑919 remain, and videoconferencing for evaluations/hearings is authorized.
109-1-LB387_IntroLB387_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB387 amends §83-170 (Nebraska Treatment and Corrections Act) to explicitly define "Department" as the Department of Correctional Services and "Director" as the Director of Correctional Services. It clarifies "facility" to mean any institution operated by the department and retains "person committed to the department." The bill adds definitions for "restrictive housing" and "solitary confinement," describing confinement conditions applicable to inmates in department-operated facilities, and references the Director of Supervision and Services (per §83-1,101). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB388_FinalLB388_Final_Copy.docxLB388 amends procedures for judicial nominating commissions and assigns roles to state officials and the Nebraska State Bar Association. Key agency actions and changes: - Governor: appoints Supreme Court judge members, citizen members, and fills citizen-member vacancies. - Nebraska Supreme Court / Clerk of the Supreme Court: Clerk manages electronic or mailed lawyer-member nominations and ballots (via the Court’s attorney licensure portal), publishes hearing notices, delivers certified results, and assures ballot secrecy. Supreme Court judge designated to each commission chairs meetings (no vote). - Executive Council of the Nebraska State Bar Association: nominates or appoints alternate lawyer members, fills alternate-lawyer vacancies upon Clerk notification, and supplies candidates when electronic nominations are insufficient. - Secretary of State and Attorney General: serve on the ballot-counting board with the Clerk (or their alternates). Other provisions: four-year terms, alternates fill vacancies in order, eight voting members required at votes, hearing timelines (first hearing within 60 days; nominations to Governor within 90 or 120 days), automatic termination for residency or party-registration changes. No appropriations or funding changes.Adds procedural rules and agency roles for judicial nominating commissions. Key agencies: Nebraska Supreme Court (attorney licensure portal — electronic receipt of applications by Oct. 1 of even-numbered years), Clerk of the Supreme Court (authorized to fill vacancy by moving up alternates using certified prior election results and to notify the Executive Council), the Judicial Nominating Commission, the Executive Council of the Nebraska State Bar Association (to designate lawyers to fill vacancies when notified), the Nebraska State Bar Association, and the Governor (receives candidate names). New rules: electronic filing deadline, priority order for filling vacancies (alternate of same party → nonpartisan alternate → Clerk-selected alternate by prior vote totals), requirement that lawyer commissioners resign before seeking a judgeship, and residency-change release. No funding or appropriation changes.
109-1-LB389_IntroLB389_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill directs state distributions beginning in 2029 to offset educational service units' lost property-tax revenue after elimination of their levy authority. For 2029 each ESU's payment equals its property taxes for tax year 2027 increased by 3.5%; for 2030 and thereafter the amount equals the prior year's distribution increased by 3.5%. The Department of Revenue is charged to annually determine and certify each ESU's distribution amount to the State Treasurer and the ESU. Distributions are made in two equal payments, on or before March 31 and August 31.Key points affecting the Department of Revenue (DOR): - Starting FY 2028-29, educational service units (ESUs) lose authority to levy property taxes. - Beginning in 2029 the state must pay ESUs amounts to offset lost levy revenue: for 2029 each ESU receives its tax‑year 2027 levy amount increased by 3.5%; for 2030 onward each ESU receives the prior year's distribution increased by 3.5%. - The DOR is required to annually calculate each ESU's distribution amount and certify those amounts to the State Treasurer and the ESU. - Payments are made in two equal installments: on or before March 31 and on or before August 31. - The provision creates a recurring state payment obligation to ESUs but contains no separate appropriation language or specified funding source in the added text.
109-1-LB38_FinalLB38_Final_Copy.docxThis bill restructures administration of the Geologists Regulation Act around the Board of Geologists (seven gubernatorial appointees) and clarifies agency roles and procedures. Key agency actions and changes: - Board of Geologists: establishes membership, five-year terms, qualifications for professional‑geologist members, authority to adopt rules, a code of practice, issue licenses, enroll geologist‑interns, grant certificates of authorization to organizations, issue temporary permits, set and publish examinations (including Nebraska‑specific exam), maintain a roster, designate emeritus members, hold disciplinary hearings, employ counsel, and notify the Secretary of State of revocations/suspensions/probations. Board may charge fees and set exam fees to recover costs. - Governor: appoints board members; may remove for cause. - Secretary of State: prohibited from issuing corporate certificates of authority, registering business names or trade marks that use “geology” unless the board has issued an organizational certificate of authorization or eligibility letter. - Attorney General: serves as legal advisor; board may also retain counsel. Fiscal provisions: fee caps established (licensure ≤ $300, geologist‑intern enrollment ≤ $100, certificate of authorization ≤ $300, emeritus ≤ $100) and an additional administrative collection fee up to $100. Board member reimbursement governed by §§81‑1174 to 81‑1177. No direct appropriations or new budget allocations are included.Adds and expands duties, membership, and fee authorities for the state board administering the Geologists Regulation Act. Key government actors: the Nebraska board (which issues licenses, certificates of authorization, temporary permits, and prepares a Nebraska-specific exam); the Governor (appoints board members); college/university presidents (may recommend one faculty member for appointment); and the National Association of State Boards of Geology (board may adopt its exams/guidelines). Statutory cross‑references govern reimbursement and record‑distribution fees (sections 81‑1174 to 81‑1177 and 84‑712 to 84‑712.09). Funding/fee changes: application/renewal and certificate fees are nonrefundable; the board may add up to $100 to cover administrative collection costs; it may charge for roster copies and may waive first reexamination fees. No general appropriations or budget allocations are added.

109-1-LB391_FinalLB391_Final_Copy.docxCreates the Give to Enable Support Act and a Give to Enable Support Cash Fund administered by the State Treasurer, who will accept private contributions (no General Fund transfers), invest fund balances via the state investment officer under existing state investment law, and implement the Give to Enable Support Program beginning January 1, 2026. The Treasurer will accept annual applications (Jan 1–June 1), establish accounts for qualifying individuals using fund distributions, and adopt rules. The bill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-2716 to permit a state income tax subtraction for contributions to the Give to Enable Support Cash Fund (not deductible federally), subject to existing $5,000 married filing separate / $10,000 per return limits, thereby creating a state tax expenditure. No specific appropriations or General Fund allocations are made.Creates the Give to Enable Support Cash Fund and the Give to Enable Support Program, both administered and implemented by the State Treasurer beginning January 1, 2026. The Treasurer will accept only private contributions into the cash fund (explicitly prohibiting transfers from General Funds) and the state investment officer will invest any available fund balances under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The Treasurer will accept annual applications (Jan 1–June 1), approve as many as funding allows, establish accounts by April 1 following approval, fund each account at least at the minimum required to open, and may adopt implementing rules. No specific appropriations or dollar amounts are listed.

109-1-LB394_IntroLB394_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureLB394 updates the Weights and Measures Act's incorporated NIST/NCSNM handbooks and requires copies of those handbooks be filed with the Secretary of State, the Clerk of the Legislature (electronically), and the Department of Agriculture. The bill contains no provisions that explicitly change funding, appropriations, or budget allocations to the Department of Agriculture.Department of Agriculture — Weights & Measures: The bill increases inspection/testing fees (effective 2025) for specified devices. Examples shown: up to 35‑lb capacity scales $37 → $43; loading‑rack meters $110 → $128; liquid petroleum gas meters $135 → $157; liquid fertilizer/herbicide meters $125 → $145; liquid feed meters $125 → $145; cryogenic meters $176 → $204; mass‑flow (all liquid) $252 → $293; electric vehicle chargers $294 → $340. 109-1-LB395_IntroLB395_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor VehiclesLB395 amends juvenile record‑sealing statutes to impose specific duties for three agencies: - Department of Motor Vehicles: courts must send notice of a sealing order to the DMV when the sealed record includes impoundment or a prohibition to obtain a license or permit under §43‑287. Sealing orders must include contact information for each government agency subject to the order. - Department of Health and Human Services: courts must notify DHHS if the juvenile was a ward or DHHS was a party. DHHS may access sealed records for intake, case plans, evaluations, federal reporting, supervision/protection of persons placed with the department, and for specified licensing/certification purposes, and may release information as needed to perform those duties. - Department of Labor: required to create a website link informing employers they may not ask about sealed records and that employment applications must state applicants are not obligated to disclose sealed records. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Adds two provisions: (1) when a juvenile record is sealed upon termination of probation, the sealing explanation must inform the juvenile they are prohibited from possessing a firearm under §28‑1204.05; (2) authorizes law enforcement to check whether applicants under age 25 have prior juvenile adjudications for felonies or misdemeanor domestic violence when applying for concealed‑handgun permits or certificates to buy/transfer handguns. No budget, funding, or appropriation changes. Department of Labor: no direct effect. Department of Health and Human Services: possible minor administrative role if it or its contractors handle juvenile‑record notifications, but no funding change. Department of Motor Vehicles: no direct effect.
109-1-LB396_FinalLB396_Final_Copy.docxLB396 amends procedures for public power entities and related agencies. It requires public power districts, public power and irrigation districts, rural power districts, and agencies created under sections 18-2426 to 18-2434 to prepare annual written proposed budgets showing prior two years’ revenues and expenditures, current-year estimates, and a fiscal-policy summary. Proposed budgets must be posted at the entity’s principal headquarters at least seven days before the board adoption meeting; a newspaper notice (at least seven days prior) must state availability and location. Any interim changes must be added at headquarters before the meeting, the public must be allowed to testify, a written record kept, and post-adoption change summaries made available. LB396 also requires districts’ CPA audits to be filed with the Auditor of Public Accounts within 180 days after year-end. No funding or appropriation changes are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.

109-1-LB398_FinalLB398_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Department of Veterans' AffairsThe bill makes multiple agency-specific changes: - DMV: reduces organizational license‑plate fee from $70 to $40 (effective Oct 1, 2025); 60% of initial/renewal fees go to the DMV Cash Fund, 40% to the Highway Trust Fund. Allows postage/handling and $3 transfer fees (to DMV Cash Fund); authorizes electronic‑reporting fees for wrecker/salvage dealers. Creates new veteran/military/Purple Heart/disabled‑veteran/alternate plates (eligibility verified via the DVA registry). Sets plate fees ($5 alphanumeric to the Nebraska Veteran Cemetery System Operation Fund; $40 personalized with 25% to DMV Cash Fund and 75% to that cemetery fund). Revises driver‑record revenue splits (41 2/3% DMV Cash Fund; 25% General Fund; 33 1/3% Records Management Cash Fund), directs $4 per record to the Operator’s License Services System Replacement and Maintenance Fund, and creates that fund (investment earnings credited to the General Fund beginning Oct. 1, 2024). Expands DMV duties, system buildout, fee schedules, and staff training/background checks. - Dept. of Veterans' Affairs: provides its registry for plate eligibility; establishes Veterans Employment Program Fund and Pets for Vets Cash Fund (funded by section 35 and appropriations; investable). - Dept. of Transportation: may investigate railroad‑crossing complaints, hold hearings, order crossings/relocations; landowners pay half of special crossing costs exceeding $1,500. - Dept. of Health and Human Services: Choose Life plate fees go to the HHS Cash Fund to supplement TANF; DHHS will administer an Organ and Tissue Donor Awareness and Education Fund funded by specified plate proceeds. - Dept. of Revenue: may receive SSNs for specified purposes; the Wildlife Conservation Fund may cover administration costs for the income‑tax designation program and will receive a General Fund transfer equal to designated contributions (amount set by the Tax Commissioner).Summary of added provisions affecting named agencies: - Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): New and revised specialty/alternate plates (Space Force, disabled veteran, Purple Heart, Cornhusker spirit, Arbor Day, Choose Life, Donate Life, etc.), new fee structures (e.g., $40 personalized disabled‑veteran/Purple Heart fee; $70 Cornhusker fee), allocations of collected fees to the DMV Cash Fund and designated recipients, a $1 registration fee for commercial fertilizer trailers (effective Jan 1, 2026), RV registration fee tiers, and CDL/medical‑certification compliance rules requiring DMV to update CDLIS records (including marking drivers “not‑certified,” downgrades and cancellations) with deadlines by June 23, 2025. - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): Choose Life plate proceeds are credited to the Health and Human Services Cash Fund to supplement TANF federal funds. - Department of Transportation (DOT): Nebraska Cornhusker Spirit plate fees direct part of proceeds to the Highway Trust Fund. - Department of Veterans’ Affairs: Plate eligibility references VA service‑connected disability determinations; fee revenue (from certain personalized veteran/Purple Heart plate fees) directs 75% to the Nebraska Veteran Cemetery System Operation Fund to support veterans’ cemetery operations. - Department of Revenue: No direct changes or appropriations affecting the Department of Revenue are included.
109-1-LB399_FinalLB399_Final_Copy.docxLB399 amends the Mutual Finance Assistance Act (secs. 35-1204–35-1205). Key agency/entity effects: - Authorizes mutual finance organizations formed under the Interlocal Cooperation Act or Joint Public Agency Act; agreements must run three years, require each member to levy the same agreed property tax rate within their boundaries for one of the three tax years (not necessarily the same year), and limit levies to no more than that rate in the other years. Levies exclude bonded indebtedness and lease-purchase contracts in existence on or after July 1, 1998. - Revises qualification for distributions from the Mutual Finance Assistance Fund to rural/suburban fire protection districts and mutual finance organizations by setting the outside‑city assumed‑population threshold at 60% of a county’s assumed population and detailing the Census‑based assumed population calculation (referencing section 77‑3,119). - Operative date: October 1, 2025. No specific appropriations or dollar amounts are changed; the bill alters eligibility and levy rules affecting fund distributions.The added text contains no references to any government agencies or departments and makes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. 109-1-LB39_IntroLB39_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and FinanceLB39 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §8-124.01 to require a bank to notify the Department of Banking and Finance within 30 days of a vacancy on its board of directors. The bill repeals the original §8-124.01. 109-1-LB3_IntroLB3_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill amends procedures for selecting Nebraska's presidential electors and assigns specific duties to state officials. - Governor: must serve certificates of appointment by registered or certified mail; notify electors of meeting time/location; include a security feature and vacancy/amendment language in the state's certificate of ascertainment submitted under 3 U.S.C. 5; fill vacancies if electors fail to elect replacements by 3 p.m. - Secretary of State: receives convention certifications; provide each elector a list and a presidential/vice‑presidential ballot; examine and accept only ballots consistent with each elector’s pledge; affix the state seal to abstracts. - Board of State Canvassers: open county abstracts, prepare and sign the statewide abstract, and treat the presidential canvass as the return of votes for party electors—electors receiving the highest statewide votes are deemed elected. Other: bill expressly provides for five presidential electors and requires electors to pledge to vote for the statewide highest‑vote presidential/vice‑presidential candidates. 109-1-LB400_IntroLB400_Intro_Copy.docxLB400 amends the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act (section 48-1,110) to create rebuttable presumptions that certain cancers in firefighters are compensable as arising out of employment. Key provisions: - Presumes cancers diagnosed during employment are work-related. - For retired firefighters: a rebuttable presumption applies if diagnosis occurs within a period (not to exceed 60 months) beginning at last work date and extending three months per full year of service (applies to professional retirees before Jan 1, 2026, and all volunteer retirees). - For professional firefighters retiring on/after Jan 1, 2026: presumption lasts post-separation equal to years worked if under 20 years’ service; if 20+ years, presumed at any time in life. - Purchased retirement service credit cannot be used to calculate years of service for these presumptions. - Post-retirement claims under the new post-2026 rule are limited to medical benefits only. The bill repeals the original section 48-1,110. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Adds specific carcinogen findings and workers'‑comp presumptions for firefighters. Benzene and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are listed as known carcinogens linked to uterine cancer; certain hydrocarbons are linked to urinary tract and ureteral cancers. The bill allows case‑by‑case inclusion of other agents, including those classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as Group 1 or 2A. It creates rebuttable presumptions that cancers diagnosed during employment (and in specified post‑retirement windows) arose out of firefighting service, with differing timeframes for retirees (rules vary for retirements before/after Jan 1, 2026 and for volunteers). Purchased service credit cannot be used to calculate service years. Claims under the post‑retirement presumption are limited under the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act to medical benefits only. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB401_IntroLB401_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor Vehicles, Department of RevenueThe bill makes two agency-specific tax changes. For the Department of Motor Vehicles, it reduces the penalty for late sales/use tax returns to $5 when the penalty is being collected by a county treasurer or the DMV (replacing the standard 10% or $25 penalty). For the Department of Revenue, it exempts publicly traded partnerships (treated as partnerships) from the partnership remittance rule provided the partnership files an annual information return with the Department reporting unit-holder name, address, taxpayer identification number, and other requested information. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either agency are included.Department of Revenue: - Requires notices (including notices of proposed deficiency) to include a written statement detailing the facts, circumstances, and reasons the Tax Commissioner relied on when determining a taxpayer did not report the correct tax or did not make an overpayment. - Clarifies that for returns filed for taxable years beginning (or deemed to begin) on or after Jan 1, 2022, a specified credit may be claimed in the same taxable year for which the election is made, regardless of when the tax is paid to Nebraska or deducted federally. Department of Motor Vehicles: - No changes or references. Funding/appropriations: - No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB402_IntroLB402_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of RevenueLB402 amends the Gambling Winnings Setoff for Outstanding Debt Act to add the Department of Labor as a claimant for unemployment-benefit overpayments and to authorize the Department of Labor to submit certified debts ($25+) to the electronic collection system. The Department of Revenue, in consultation with the Department of Health and Human Services and the Department of Labor, must develop and implement the secure collection system; outstanding state tax liability is defined to include liabilities administered by the Department of Revenue, the Department of Labor, and the Department of Motor Vehicles. Remittances are to be credited pro rata: first DHHS-certified debts, then Department of Labor-certified debts, then outstanding state tax liability. DHHS, the Department of Labor, and the Department of Revenue share confidentiality, notification, hearing, and rulemaking duties. No funding or appropriation changes are specified.Department of Labor - Authorized to establish/set off casino, pari‑mutuel, sports wagering, and cash‑device winnings against debts assigned to it for unemployment overpayments (section 48‑663.01). - May submit certified debts of $25+ to collections (unless legitimately disputed); overpayment debts submitted continuously and may fluctuate with actual amounts. - Upon Department of Revenue remittance notification (sec. 9‑1306), Labor must notify the obligor within 20 days, providing basis, intent to apply winnings, 30‑day contest right and hearing address; mailed hearing requests are effective on mailing. Labor must hold hearings, adjust amounts if incorrect, and allow appeals under the Administrative Procedure Act. Department of Revenue - Role limited to remittance/notification under sec. 9‑1306; no funding changes. Department of Health and Human Services and Department of Motor Vehicles - No additions or funding/appropriation changes referenced.
109-1-LB403_IntroLB403_Intro_Copy.docxCreates an Office of Grants in the executive branch, led by a Director of Grants appointed by the Governor (serving at the Governor’s pleasure) after a nationwide search; the Director must have at least ten years’ experience in writing or managing federal grants. The office may hire additional staff “for which adequate funding is available.” Duties: identify national (including federal) grant programs for state agencies, political subdivisions, and in-state private organizations; assist those entities with identification, application, and compliance; and by July 1, 2026 (and annually thereafter) adopt and update a statewide plan to maximize grant funding. The office must submit an annual electronic report to the Legislature summarizing the plan, legislative impacts on grant eligibility, entities served, and resulting awards and dollar amounts. No specific appropriations or budget allocations are set.Creates an Office of Grants in the executive branch. The Governor appoints a Director (serving at the Governor’s pleasure) who must have ≥10 years’ experience with federal grants and be chosen after a nationwide search; the Director may hire staff “for which adequate funding is available.” The office will identify national/federal grant programs for state agencies, political subdivisions, and in-state private organizations and assist those entities with identification, applications, and compliance. It must produce a statewide plan to maximize grant funding by July 1, 2026, update it annually, and submit an annual electronic report to the Legislature (due July 1) summarizing the plan, analyzing effects of recent state legislation on federal grant eligibility, listing entities served, and reporting awards obtained and total dollars. No specific appropriations or budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB404_IntroLB404_Intro_Copy.docxLB404 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29-2263 (probation). Key provisions: - Courts must specify probation terms (≤5 years for felony/second-offense misdemeanor; ≤2 years for first-offense misdemeanor) and provide notice at sentencing that the offender may be eligible to have the conviction set aside; the State Court Administrator is directed to develop standardized advisement language and any necessary forms. - The court may discharge a probationer on application of a probation officer, the probationer, or on its own motion. - New: the court may extend the term of probation on joint application of the probation officer and the probationer, within existing statutory limits. - Clarifies that probation officers may impose administrative sanctions with the probationer’s full knowledge and consent as authorized by existing statutes. No agencies other than the State Court Administrator, courts, and probation officers are referenced. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds authority for a court, upon joint application by the probation officer and the probationer, to extend the probation term subject to the limits already set in subdivision (1)(a). Affects the court and probation personnel; no specific state agencies or departments are newly created or referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.
109-1-LB405_IntroLB405_Intro_Copy.docxLB405 amends §53-123.17 of the Nebraska Liquor Control Act (and repeals the original section), clarifying provisions for local entertainment district licenses. Key governmental actors and responsibilities: - Local governing bodies (city or village councils): may designate or revoke entertainment districts, file designations with the Commission, regulate districts by ordinance, impose an occupation tax within their liquor license jurisdiction, and cancel licenses for cause. - Nebraska Liquor Control Commission: receives filings, must be notified of applications, provides application copies to local clerks, and processes/decides appeals from local cancellations. - Clerks of local governing bodies: receive the $300 additional entertainment district license fee payable by applicants. No state appropriations or other budgetary changes are made.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB406_IntroLB406_Intro_Copy.docxLB406 revises section 2-1201 to define and restate provisions for the State Racing and Gaming Commission. Key agency/authority items: members (seven) are appointed by the Governor and subject to legislative confirmation; the Governor may remove members for cause. Membership composition, term lengths, geographic and partisan limits, vacancy filling, and prohibitions on financial interests in licensed racetrack enclosures or authorized gaming operators (per the Nebraska Racetrack Gaming Act) are specified. Compensation is set at $1,000 per month, adjustable every two years by up to the CPI change; members are reimbursed for expenses per sections 81-1174 to 81-1177 and must be bonded/insured under section 11-201. The original section is repealed.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB407_IntroLB407_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesThe bill amends placement restrictions to bar use of the "secure youth confinement facility operated by the Department of Correctional Services." Under amended section 43-251.01, juveniles described in subdivision (3) of §43-247 may not be placed in an adult correctional facility, the DOCS-operated secure youth confinement facility, or a youth rehabilitation and treatment center. Juveniles described in subdivisions (1), (2), or (4) of §43-247 may not be assigned or transferred to an adult correctional facility or the DOCS-operated secure youth confinement facility. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services are included.Adds procedures for juveniles aged 13–15 charged with certain enumerated felonies: juvenile court has exclusive original jurisdiction; after disposition a county attorney may move to transfer the case to district court; the court must hold a hearing within 15 days, the juvenile has counsel, and the court will retain the case unless the county attorney proves by a preponderance that the juvenile is not amenable to rehabilitation. Decisions must be issued within 30 days and are immediately appealable on an expedited schedule. If granted, charges are filed in district court and the juvenile is arraigned as an adult; statutes of limitation are tolled for one year after transfer or final appeal. Admissions by the juvenile are generally inadmissible except for specified uses. No provisions change funding, appropriations, or the Department of Correctional Services' budget.
109-1-LB408_IntroLB408_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the Special Education Teacher Forgivable Loan Program Act to be administered by "the department" (administrative authority designated in the bill). The department may award forgivable loans to eligible students attending Nebraska state colleges or the University of Nebraska (up to 25 loans per academic year per eligible institution). Loans cover remaining in‑state tuition after federal/state aid and require a contract obligating recipients to begin teaching special education in Nebraska within one year of graduation and teach five consecutive years (or an equivalent number of years). The department manages forgiveness (20% per compliant year over five years or pro rata if fewer loan years), deferments by rule, and collection with 5% simple interest on unpaid balances. Repayments are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The State Board of Education may adopt rules. No specific appropriation or funding source is provided.Creates the Special Education Teacher Forgivable Loan Program to be administered by "the department" (state education department implied). The department may award forgivable loans (up to 25 per eligible institution per year) to cover remaining in‑state tuition after recipients apply for federal financial aid and state scholarships/grants. Recipients enter contracts with service and forgiveness terms (20% forgiven per compliant year over five years, pro rata if fewer loan years); deferments may be allowed under department rules. Failed obligations incur simple interest at 5% and repayments are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The State Board of Education may adopt program rules. No specific appropriation or funding source is provided.
109-1-LB409_IntroLB409_Intro_Copy.docxLB409 amends membership and reporting provisions for the Nebraska Power Review Board. Appointments remain by the Governor with legislative approval and four‑year terms, but once one current member vacancy/term occurs the five‑member board must include: at least one engineer, one attorney, and at least one licensed journeyman electrician who is affiliated with a nonprofit labor organization holding a 501(c)(5) exemption and selected from a list provided by that organization, plus two additional persons. Conflicts restrictions and recusal timelines remain. The bill preserves member pay rates and caps (standard members $100/day to $7,000/yr; the Southwest Power Pool Regional State Committee designee $250/day to $35,000/yr; SPP‑related pay capped at $40,000/yr) and reimbursement rules. The board must submit a biennial report with annual data to the Governor, Clerk of the Legislature (electronically), and the Department of Environment and Energy, which will consider the data in its own reports. Original section repealed. [NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.]The amendment changes the board’s composition once the first member appointed under subsection (1)(a)(iii) vacates or their term expires after the bill’s effective date. At that point the board will be reduced/defined to five members: at least one engineer, one attorney, one licensed journeyman electrician who is affiliated with a nonprofit labor organization for electrical workers holding a 501(c)(5) exemption and chosen from that organization’s recommended list, and two additional persons. No specific government agencies, departments, or funding/appropriation changes are mentioned.
109-1-LB40_IntroLB40_Intro_Copy.docxLB40 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §21-193 (Uniform LLC Act) to require notice of organization, certificate amendments, mergers, conversions, or domestications to be published for three successive weeks in a legal newspaper of general circulation near the LLC’s designated office. Notices must include the information required by §21-117(b); brief resumes of amendments/transactions must be published the same way. Voluntary dissolution notices remain subject to §21-150. Proof of publication must be filed with the Secretary of State; late publication with subsequent filing validates prior and subsequent LLC acts. The bill repeals the original section.
