109-1-LB410_IntroLB410_Intro_Copy.docxLB410 (2025), introduced by Sen. J. Cavanaugh and referred to the Legislature’s Banking, Commerce and Insurance Committee, requires health insurance coverage for prosthetics and orthotics as prescribed. The bill defines "orthotic" as a custom‑fitted or custom‑fabricated medical device applied to correct deformity, improve function, or relieve disease symptoms, and "prosthetic" as artificial limbs and associated components, including replacements when required by changes in a patient's condition. The text contains no references to state agencies or departments and includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds definitions for this section: "orthotic" is a custom‑fitted or custom‑fabricated medical device applied to the body to correct deformity, improve function, or relieve disease symptoms; "prosthetic" means artificial legs and arms and associated components, including replacement devices needed due to changes in the patient's physical condition. No government agencies or funding/appropriations are mentioned.
109-1-LB411_IntroLB411_Intro_Copy.docxLB411 amends the Nebraska Teacher Recruitment and Retention Act (section 79-8,114). It directs the department (Nebraska Department of Education) to automatically provide annual retention grants beginning July 1, 2025, with amounts tiered by years of full‑time Nebraska teaching: $2,500 (years 1–6), $3,000 (years 7–15), and $4,000 (year 16 onward). It creates a one‑time $5,000 high‑need retention grant for teachers who, on or after July 1, 2025, obtain an endorsement in special education, mathematics, science, technology, or dual‑credit and sign a contract to teach in that endorsement area. A teacher may receive only one high‑need retention grant; teachers who received such a grant before July 1, 2025, are ineligible for the new $5,000 grant. The bill repeals the original section and takes effect immediately under an emergency clause. No specific appropriation language is included.Effective July 1, 2025, "the department" must automatically provide teacher retention grants. Eligible teachers receive: $2,500/year in years 1–6, $3,000/year in years 7–15, and $4,000/year from year 16 onward. A one-time $5,000 high-need retention grant is available (on or after July 1, 2025) for teachers who obtain an endorsement in special education, mathematics, science, technology, or dual-credit and sign a one-year contract to teach in that endorsement area at a Nebraska school. Each teacher may receive only one high-need grant; teachers who already received a high-need grant before July 1, 2025, are ineligible for another. The provision names only "the department" as the administering entity; no new funding, appropriation, or budget allocation is specified in the added text.
109-1-LB412_IntroLB412_Intro_Copy.docxLB412 amends Nebraska paternity law to (1) expand definitions (child under 18; support includes reasonable education) and (2) allow a person claiming to be a biological father to file a complaint to intervene in juvenile-court proceedings where the juvenile court has jurisdiction. Procedural provisions reference district courts (including cases under the Uniform Interstate Family Support Act), county courts, separate juvenile courts, and sheriffs for service. The bill: waives filing fees for the intervention complaint; authorizes juvenile courts to order genetic testing and require the child’s availability for testing; and permits the juvenile court to allocate genetic-testing costs to the complainant, the county, or the state at its discretion. It bars intervention by persons whose parental rights have been terminated.Adds definitions and decision-making guidance for juvenile courts in paternity/genetic-testing matters. Key points: - "Child" is defined as a person under 18 years, regardless of being born out of wedlock. - The juvenile court may order genetic testing or establish paternity and may consider: the child's age; the child's relationship with any presumptive parent; the child's relationship with any parent whose rights are established; the child's relationship with the complainant; whether establishing paternity would benefit or harm the child; and any other relevant factor the court deems appropriate. - Only the juvenile court (a government judicial body) is implicated; no other agencies or departments are mentioned. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB413_IntroLB413_Intro_Copy.docxLB413 amends section 70-655 (Chapter 70, art. 6) governing public power districts, public irrigation districts, and public power and irrigation districts. It explicitly authorizes district boards to set rates for electricity, water, storage and other commodities (including ethanol and hydrogen) and permits rate differentiation by objective criteria (e.g., load size, firm/nonfirm service, technology risk, length of commitment). Boards may negotiate special commercial/industrial rates (effective ≤5 years); where a customer has a state or political‑subdivision economic development agreement with >500 kW and ≥60% annual load factor, negotiated rates must include a production component at least equal to incremental production cost. Following mergers, districts may maintain different predecessor rates for up to five years if supported by cost‑of‑service or rate studies. No appropriations or budget changes are included.Summary: The added provision permits rates and charges to be tiered or varied according to objective factors—specifically load size, load factor, whether service is firm or nonfirm, technology risks, length of service commitment, and other objective criteria. No government agency or department is named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB414_FinalLB414_Final_Copy.docxLB414 establishes a state suicide mortality review team and requires it to enter a cooperative agreement with the Nebraska Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) to share and store review-related data. Upon request by the bill’s director, a county attorney or the Attorney General may issue subpoenas for records (to be entered into NVDRS and provided to the team as aggregate narratives). The team has five business days to obtain requested records and may access coroner/autopsy reports, law enforcement (including probation and corrections) reports, medical and mental‑health records, EMS and prescription‑monitoring data, school and employment records, toxicology, and next‑of‑kin interviews. Prosecuting attorneys may permit law enforcement to withhold records that would jeopardize prosecutions. All team materials are confidential and largely immune from subpoena or use in court. Annual reports are due April 1 to the Clerk of the Legislature and the Department of Health and Human Services. No funding or appropriations are specified.Adds authority and procedures for suicide mortality review teams to establish a cooperative agreement with the Nebraska Violent Death Reporting System to share and store review-related data. At a director's request, a county attorney or the Attorney General may issue subpoenas for listed records (coroner/autopsy, law enforcement/probation/corrections, medical and mental‑health records, EMS, prescription monitoring, toxicology, employment, school, next‑of‑kin interviews); subpoenaed material must be entered into the Violent Death Reporting System and provided to the team as an aggregate narrative. Agencies must provide requested records within five business days unless law enforcement, with prosecuting attorney approval, withholds records that would impede a criminal investigation. Review team records are confidential and generally exempt from subpoena/discovery; team members have testimonial protections. Beginning April 1, 2026, and annually, the team must report to the Clerk of the Legislature, Department of Health and Human Services, and nonprofits with specified case data and recommendations. No funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB415_FinalLB415_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of RevenueLB415 (as described) makes two agency-specific changes. It designates the Department of Labor as the “Department” under the Nebraska Healthy Families and Workplaces Act and authorizes the Commissioner of Labor to issue citations, assess administrative penalties, provide hearings and enforcement, and block state contracts for unpaid citations. It requires the Department of Revenue, in consultation with DHHS, the DMV, and the Department of Labor, to create an electronic gambling‑winnings setoff system: DHHS may certify child‑support debts; the DMV and Labor may submit outstanding state liabilities; operators must check the system and remit setoffs to Revenue, which credits DHHS‑certified debts first, then other state liabilities (including unemployment overpayments per amended 48‑665). No appropriations or budget allocations for these agencies are included.- Department of Labor: Adds an explicit definition that “overpayment” includes unemployment insurance overpayments (sec. 48-663.01) and repeatedly names DOL as an agency that may be owed outstanding state liabilities eligible for collection or setoff (including offsets against gambling winnings). Also clarifies paid‑sick‑time accrual timing (after 80 hours) and that sick leave provided in early 2025 counts toward 2025 employer obligations (policy impact, not agency funding). - Department of Motor Vehicles: Is expressly listed among agencies that may hold outstanding state liabilities and participate in setoff/collection processes (including gambling winnings setoff). - Department of Revenue: The bill ties obligor definitions to section 77-2701.25 (Dept. of Revenue setoff authority), expanding the types of debts subject to that process. - Department of Health and Human Services: No substantive additions affecting DHHS in the added text. No new appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB416_IntroLB416_Intro_Copy.docxLB416 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25-21,185.11 to clarify the effect of releases, covenants not to sue, or similar agreements. Key changes: a release discharges the released party from liability to the claimant but reduces the claimant’s claim against other liable parties by the released party’s share as determined by the trier of fact; a released party may not be made or remain a party to the action (or may be dismissed), though that party’s negligence remains relevant under §25-21,185.09; and releases do not abrogate joint-and-several liability of remaining defendants. The original section is repealed. No state agencies or departments are referenced, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budgetary provisions.Adds a new subsection clarifying that a release, covenant not to sue, or similar agreement between a claimant and one or more liable parties does not eliminate the joint and several liability of any other person liable on the same claim. No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB417_IntroLB417_Intro_Copy.docxLB417 assigns and clarifies responsibilities across multiple state education entities. Key provisions: - Board of Regents, University of Nebraska: given powers and duties to administer the Nebraska Promise Program. - Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education: to administer the College Promise Fund, distribute funds to community and state colleges, develop an appeals process, and implement intent to fully fund annual tuition waivers equal to the total value of waivers provided. Fund receipts may include legislative transfers; the state investment officer will invest fund balances under existing state investment law. - Community colleges and state colleges: must waive remaining tuition (after federal grants and state scholarships) for eligible Nebraska residents (income < $65,000) per program rules. - State Board of Education and State Department of Education: update statewide assessment/reporting systems; the board to recommend national and portable career‑readiness assessments (including National Career Readiness Certificates) and ensure no‑cost administration; the department to use the student identifier system to track and annually report achievement and discipline data to the Governor, Legislature, districts, ESUs, and learning communities. - Governor: appoints a technical advisory committee (appointments confirmed by the Legislature).Adds administration and funding mechanics and assessment duties to state education entities. Key points: - Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education will administer a new "College Promise Fund" to reimburse community colleges and state colleges for tuition waivers; the fund consists of legislative transfers and is intended to be fully funded each year equal to the total value of waivers. The state investment officer may invest fund balances under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Colleges must waive 100% of remaining tuition after federal grants and state scholarships; Cooperating Commission will provide an appeals process. - The State Board (and "the department") will recommend nationally recognized career‑readiness assessments (leading to a National Career Readiness Certificate) beginning 2025–26. School districts must report individual student scores per state procedures; assessments are provided at no cost to twelfth‑grade public students.
109-1-LB418_IntroLB418_Intro_Copy.docxLB418 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §38-1424 (Funeral Directing and Embalming Practice Act) to explicitly allow a nonlicensed funeral director and embalmer to officiate at a funeral ceremony. The bill retains existing disciplinary grounds tied to violations of state law or rules of "the department or other body having regulatory powers" (i.e., the agency charged with enforcing the Act) and clarifies that licensed practitioners may continue pre-need sales under the Burial Pre-Need Sale Act. Introduced to and reviewed by the Legislature’s Health and Human Services Committee, the bill repeals the prior version of §38-1424. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a provision permitting a nonlicensed funeral director and embalmer to officiate at a funeral ceremony. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no stated changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB419_FinalLB419_Final_Copy.docxLB419 amends veterans law and affects the Department of Veterans’ Affairs and related officers. It expands eligibility for Nebraska veterans homes to include Nebraska National Guard service, explicitly including active duty for training, and clarifies surviving spouses/parents must meet two‑year Nebraska residency and be unable to earn a livelihood. The Director of Veterans’ Affairs (or deputy/designee) retains authority to receive, approve or disapprove Nebraska Veterans’ Aid Fund applications originating from local post service officers, county veterans service officers, state service officers, or recognized veterans organizations, with a one‑claim/30‑day limit (funeral exception). The bill reiterates that staffing and state service office expenses require specific legislative appropriation and may not come from the $12 million trust or its interest; trust principal reverts to the State Treasury on completion.Adds eligibility language covering veterans (including those on active duty for training) who need long-term care at a Nebraska veterans home. Requires applications be filed through a service officer or a state service officer. Limits applicants to one claim per 30-day period, with an exception allowing an additional claim for funeral expenses. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB41A_FinalLB41A_Final_Copy.docxLB41A appropriates funds to the Department of Health and Human Services to implement Legislative Bill 41 (2025), designated to Programs 344 and 348. - Program 344: FY2025‑26 — $8,798 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund and $19,223 federal; FY2026‑27 — $7,655 Cash and $16,305 federal. - Program 348: FY2025‑26 — $69,777 Cash and $85,802 federal; FY2026‑27 — $72,860 Cash and $86,780 federal. All specified amounts are earmarked for state aid only. Appropriated funds may not be used for permanent or temporary salaries or per diems for state employees.Department of Health and Human Services — Appropriations to implement LB 41 (109th Legislature, 1st Sess., 2025): - Program 344: FY2025‑26 — $8,798 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (Cash) and $19,223 federal funds; FY2026‑27 — $7,655 Cash and $16,305 federal. - Program 348: FY2025‑26 — $69,777 Cash and $85,802 federal; FY2026‑27 — $72,860 Cash and $86,780 federal. All amounts are designated for state aid only and may not be used for permanent/temporary salaries or per diems for state employees.
109-1-LB41_FinalLB41_Final_Copy.docxLB41 (2025) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §71-502.03 to modify statutory requirements for blood testing of pregnant women related to communicable diseases. The bill also includes a legislative statement of intent regarding payment for certain blood tests for pregnant women but does not specify appropriations, funding amounts, or new budget allocations. The measure was introduced Jan. 9, 2025, referred to the Legislature’s Health and Human Services Committee, and repeals the original version of the section.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB420_IntroLB420_Intro_Copy.docxLB420 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §84‑1501 to define composition and appointment rules for the Public Employees Retirement Board (PERB). The board will have nine appointed members plus the state investment officer as a nonvoting, ex officio member. Seven appointees must be active or retired participants from systems administered by PERB (School Employees Retirement System, Nebraska Judges Retirement System, Nebraska State Patrol Retirement System, Retirement System for Nebraska Counties, State Employees Retirement System, and a Class V school retirement system teacher). Two appointees must be non‑state employees with ≥10 years’ experience in organizational management or actuarial/benefit‑plan administration. Appointments are made by the Governor with Legislative approval; terms are staggered and vacancies filled by gubernatorial appointment. 109-1-LB421_IntroLB421_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB421 requires authorized gaming operators to check the state's collection system (per the Gambling Winnings Setoff for Outstanding Debt Act) before paying sports-wagering winnings. If a winner has a debt or outstanding state tax liability, the operator must deduct the identified amount and remit the deducted funds to the Department of Revenue to be credited against that liability under section 9-1306. The bill also revises gaming-tax distributions. For non-sports gross gaming revenue: 75% to the State Treasurer (2.5% Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund, 2.5% General Fund, 70% Property Tax Credit Cash Fund) and 25% to the county treasurer (county or split with city/village). For sports-wagering gross revenue: remitted to State Treasurer as 3% Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund, 3.5% Racetrack Gaming Fund, 3.5% Racing Cash Fund, and 90% Property Tax Credit Cash Fund.Added provisions define online sports wagering/platform providers, require wagering to be run by authorized gaming operators (licensed racetrack or partner), permit servers outside Nebraska subject to federal law, limit operators to one platform/provider, and require operators/providers to submit platform controls to the Racing and Gaming Commission under a specified review timeline before offering wagering. For the Department of Revenue: sports-wagering gross gaming tax collected under section 9-1203 is to be remitted to the State Treasurer and allocated: 3% to the Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund, 3.5% to the Racing and Gaming Commission’s Racetrack Gaming Fund, 3.5% to the Racing Cash Fund, and 90% to the Property Tax Credit Cash Fund. No direct appropriations to the Department are added.
109-1-LB422_FinalLB422_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB422 amends the Nebraska Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act to require transfer-on-death deeds to include a warning that the Department of Health and Human Services may require revocation of the deed by the transferor, the transferor's spouse, or both, in order to qualify or remain qualified for Medicaid assistance. The bill also notes that designated beneficiaries may be personally liable to account for Medicaid reimbursement to the extent of the property's value. No provisions in the bill make changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Health and Human Services.The added language requires transfer-on-death deeds executed after the act’s effective date to include a warning that property insurance may expire 30 days after the transferor’s death unless the beneficiary is added as an insured. It specifies coverage ends at the earlier of the policy period’s normal end, the beneficiary obtaining other coverage, or 30 days after death only if the premium for days beyond the policy period is paid. No provisions affect the Department of Health and Human Services and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB423_IntroLB423_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentLB423 places the Job Training Cash Fund under the direction of the Department of Economic Development, requiring the department to establish subaccounts for Cash Reserve Fund transfers and for training grants for small employers, with prior-year investment earnings allocated to that subaccount. The department must give preference to training activities and grants that occur in enterprise zones or federal opportunity zones and to specified rural or high-poverty-area businesses. The bill maintains the Intern Nebraska Cash Fund and authorizes the Department of Economic Development, or its contractors, to use up to 5% of any appropriation for administrative services. It directs the State Treasurer to transfer any unobligated Intern Nebraska Cash Fund balances to the General Fund on or before June 30, 2026, and allows transfers between the Job Training Cash Fund and the General Fund at the Legislature’s direction.The bill directs the State Treasurer to transfer any unobligated balances in the Intern Nebraska Cash Fund to the General Fund on or before June 30, 2026, in amounts and on dates specified by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services. For the Department of Economic Development, this reduces or eliminates remaining cash‑fund resources held for the Intern Nebraska program, potentially decreasing available program funding; no new appropriations or budget allocations to the Department are specified in the added text.
109-1-LB424_IntroLB424_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB424 references the U.S. Department of Labor in defining "inflation rate" as the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U), as prepared by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics, for the 12‑month period ending August 31 of the year the property tax bill is determined. That CPI‑U figure is used to set the "allowable growth percentage" (the lesser of the inflation rate or 3%) that caps annual increases in individual property tax bills. The bill contains no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor.The added provision caps year‑to‑year property tax bill increases at the lesser of (a) the inflation rate or (b) 3%. It defines “inflation rate” as the 12‑month change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U) as prepared by the U.S. Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics for the period ending August 31 of the tax year. Improvements to a parcel are excluded from the cap. There are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes for the Department of Labor or BLS in this text; the Department’s role is limited to supplying the CPI‑U data used to calculate the cap.
109-1-LB425_IntroLB425_Intro_Copy.docxLB425 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-3506 to expand homestead tax-exemption eligibility and adjust documentation requirements. The bill adds a new category (effective January 1, 2026) for veterans rated at least 80% but less than 100% service‑connected disabled; the exemption for that category is a percentage of the exempt amount equal to the veteran’s VA disability percentage. The United States Department of Veterans Affairs is the certifying agency for disability status. Applications: veterans in subsection (2)(a) require VA certification every five years; applicants in (2)(b)–(g) must apply annually, but VA certification is required only in years evenly divisible by five. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a property tax exemption tied to a veteran’s VA disability rating: for homesteads described in the new subdivision, a percentage of the exempt amount equal to the veteran’s disability percentage is exempt from taxation. Effective January 1, 2026, eligible recipients include veterans discharged honorable or general who receive compensation from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs for service‑connected disability of at least 80% but less than 100%, and qualifying surviving spouses (unremarried or remarried after age 57); excludes those already eligible for total exemption under sections 77‑3526 to 77‑3528. No state agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB426_IntroLB426_Intro_Copy.docxLB426 amends school statutes to authorize a voluntary American flag education program (grades 5–8) administered by school districts (school boards, superintendents, and committees on American civics) and permits funding via lottery education funds or private donations. It revises distribution of State Lottery Operation Trust Fund moneys used for education: for FY2024-25 through FY2028-29 transfers are prescribed by percentage to specific state funds (e.g., 8% Behavioral Training Cash Fund; 2% College Pathway; 7% Community College Gap Assistance; 10% State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund; 3% for distance-education incentives and flag education programs; 58% to Nebraska Opportunity Grant Fund, et al.). Through FY2023-24 funds remained in the Nebraska Education Improvement Fund with specified FY2023-24 allocations and a transfer of its balance (less a small reserve) to the Behavioral Training Cash Fund. Auditor of Public Accounts reporting and a Dec. 31, 2027 Education Committee recommendation on post‑2029 allocations are required. Funds may be invested by the state investment officer; agencies may retain portions for administrative costs.Creates an optional one‑hour American flag education program for students between 5th and 8th grade as part of social studies, covering the U.S. Flag Code, the thirteen folds, flag etiquette/presentation, and flag history. Programs may be developed with local recognized veterans organizations (see §80‑401.01). Each student receives a 3'×5' American flag and a flag etiquette booklet. Program costs are to be paid with lottery funds pursuant to §79‑3501 or private donations. Text also references flag education programs under subdivision (4) of §79‑724.
109-1-LB427_IntroLB427_Intro_Copy.docxLB427 directs the State Treasurer to create and administer a Student Savings Account Support Fund and to establish individual educational savings accounts for K–12 students in approved or accredited public, private, denominational, or parochial schools. The state investment officer will invest fund balances under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Beginning July 1, 2026, the Treasurer (or a third‑party manager under the Treasurer’s supervision) must transfer $1,500 per enrolled student each fiscal year from the Support Fund into each student’s account (available by July 15 or 30 days after application). The State Board of Education must publish and adjudicate a list of qualified educational expenses on the State Department of Education website and may adopt rules. The Treasurer monitors accounts, audits for misuse, refers suspected fraud to the Nebraska State Patrol, and requires restitution; terminated account balances revert to the General Fund.Creates a Student Savings Account program administered by the State Treasurer (or a third‑party manager under the Treasurer's supervision). The State Board of Education must publish a list of qualified educational expenses on the State Department of Education website and hear appeals to add items. The State Treasurer will open individual accounts starting July 1, 2026; each fiscal year $1,500 per enrolled K–12 student will be transferred from the newly created Student Savings Account Support Fund into each student's account. Funds are invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The Treasurer will monitor, audit, and investigate misuse and report crimes to the Nebraska State Patrol; improperly used funds require restitution. Unused/terminated accounts revert funds to the General Fund. The State Board may adopt implementing rules.
109-1-LB428_FinalLB428_Final_Copy.docxLB428 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-532 to impose procedural and parental-rights requirements on school districts and school personnel regarding student surveys. For surveys asking about drug, vape, alcohol, or tobacco use, districts must notify parents/guardians/educational decisionmakers at least 15 days prior via the school's electronic notification system or mail and describe question types, purpose/age-appropriateness, data use, access, privacy protections, and result disclosures. Parents may request a copy, review the survey in person, or exempt their child. Schools may not disclose students' personally identifiable information except as required by law, and surveys requesting sexual information are prohibited for grades K–6. The bill cites consistency with federal statutes/regulations (FERPA, PPRA, COPPA, and the Children’s Internet Protection Act) and repeals the original §79-532. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds parental-notice, review, opt-out, and privacy rules for school surveys about drug, vape, alcohol, or tobacco use. School districts must notify parents/guardians/educational decisionmakers at least 15 days before survey administration via the school's electronic system or mail, describe survey content/purpose/privacy/access/disclosure, allow parents to request a copy, review it in person, or exempt their child, and bar disclosure of students' personally identifiable information except as required by law. Prohibits surveys asking sexual information for K–6 students. Cross-references federal PPRA (20 U.S.C. 1232h), COPPA (15 U.S.C. 6501 et seq.), and CIPA regulation (47 C.F.R. 54.520) as of Jan 1, 2025 — implicating the U.S. Department of Education, FTC, and FCC responsibilities. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are added.
109-1-LB429_IntroLB429_Intro_Copy.docxLB429 restricts how school boards interact with professional employees' organizations (defined as groups for professional development or liability protection). It requires school boards to provide equal access to any professional employees' organization that requests use of school employees' physical or electronic mailboxes; equal permission to display materials or send representatives to employee meetings or orientation events; and equal ability to post signage or materials (e.g., bulletin boards, posters, pamphlets). The bill also prohibits a school board from naming or referring to a school day or break using any organization's name. No state agencies beyond school boards are referenced and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.Adds definitions for "professional employees' organization" (an organization for professional development or liability protection) and "school employee" (administrators, student teachers, paraprofessionals, teachers, administrators employed by a school board). Requires school boards to provide equal access to any professional employees' organization for physical/electronic mailboxes, attendance or representation at employee meetings/orientations, and posting signage/materials (bulletin boards, posters, pamphlets). Prohibits school boards from naming any school day or break after a professional employees' organization. No state agencies or departments beyond school boards are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB42_FinalLB42_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB42 explicitly defines “Department” as the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). It authorizes DHHS to prescribe nurse aide training curricula, adopt and promulgate related rules and regulations, and approve training courses (to be consistent with federal requirements). DHHS is also the agency to which a person listed on the Nurse Aide Registry may petition to remove a conviction finding after one year. The bill contains no provisions specifying changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a definition clarifying that "Service provider" is a person certified by the Department of Health and Human Services to provide developmental disabilities services, and that this applies to providers under the Medicaid Comprehensive Developmental Disabilities Waiver (as defined in §71-6501). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB430_IntroLB430_Intro_Copy.docxLB430 amends Student Discipline Act provisions governing short‑ and long‑term suspension and adds an exception to the prohibition on suspending pre‑K–2 students. Changes require principals to investigate and, within 24 (up to 72) hours of a short‑term suspension, send the student and parent/guardian a written statement to the principal/superintendent describing the conduct, reasons for action, prior interventions, available school resources, and an actionable plan to keep the student in school; principals must document efforts to conference with parents. Elementary schools may suspend pre‑K–2 students only if the student brings a deadly weapon (per §28‑109) to school/related vehicle/activity or engages in violent behavior capable of causing physical harm. Long‑term suspension/expulsion/mandatory reassignment notices must also include resources, an actionable reentry plan, hearing rights (including completing missed work without attending alternative programs), record and witness access, and a hearing request form. Original sections are repealed. No appropriations or funding changes.Adds required information schools must include when addressing student misconduct: documentation of prior actions taken to discontinue or alleviate the behavior; resources the school can provide or recommend to assist the student; and an actionable plan for handling future behavior aimed at maximizing strategies to keep the student in school. Also adds language covering bringing prohibited items onto campus and engaging in violent behavior capable of causing physical harm to another student or school employee. No specific government agencies or departments are mentioned and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB431_IntroLB431_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB431 amends the Uniform Controlled Substances Act (sections 28‑401 and 28‑405) to explicitly define "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and to reference the Secretary of Health and Human Services in an exclusion for anabolic steroids. Steroids approved by the Secretary for nonhuman implant use (e.g., cattle) are excluded from the anabolic steroid definition, while prescribing or dispensing those substances for human use remains regulated as anabolic steroids. No appropriations, funding, or budget changes for the Department are included.Adds a statutory definition of "kratom" as products or ingredients that: (a) contain any part of the mitragyna speciosa leaf when the plant contains the alkaloids mitragynine or 7‑hydroxymitragynine, or (b) are synthetic materials containing those alkaloids. The bill also inserts "Kratom" into the enumerated list at subsection (46)(f); a subsequent fragmentary insertion "(g) substances their substance" appears unclear/errant. There are no provisions in the quoted text assigning duties, regulatory authority, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations to the Department of Health and Human Services. No direct DHHS fiscal impacts are indicated in this excerpt.
109-1-LB432_IntroLB432_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB432 assigns primary responsibility for carrying out death sentences to the Department of Correctional Services and its Director. The bill (a) defines “Department” and “Director”; (b) makes the department responsible for selecting the execution method (lethal injection or nitrogen hypoxia) and for creating, modifying, and maintaining a written execution protocol; (c) authorizes the Director to select substances or equipment, designate and train an execution team, and supervise executions at a department facility; (d) makes execution-team identities confidential; (e) empowers the Director to seek military assistance and requires the Director to return execution proceedings to the sentencing court. No appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are included.Adds definitions and administrative authority for the Department of Correctional Services and its Director: defines “Department” and “Director,” and defines “lethal injection” (IV injection) and “nitrogen hypoxia” (inhalation of pure nitrogen). Gives the Director authority to determine the method of execution (lethal injection or nitrogen hypoxia), select equipment for nitrogen hypoxia, and designate qualified persons to administer substances under the execution protocol for lethal injection. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB433_IntroLB433_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and Finance, Department of Insurance, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Veterans' AffairsLB433 amends exemptions from the State Personnel System and retirement membership rules as follows: - Department of Banking and Finance and Department of Insurance: Deputies and examiners (per sections 8‑105 and 44‑119) are exempted from the State Personnel System, except those who remain covered. - Department of Correctional Services: Chief executive officers of all facilities and the department medical director are exempt; personnel employed as pharmacists, physicians, psychiatrists, or psychologists by the department are also exempt. - Department of Health and Human Services and Department of Veterans' Affairs: Personnel employed as pharmacists, physicians, psychiatrists, psychologists, service‑area administrators, or facility operating officers are exempt. Specific veterans' home chief executive officers are listed as exempt. - Department of Labor: If the contributory retirement plan/contract under section 48‑609 is terminated, active Department of Labor participants will be granted vesting credit for years of participation. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The added language makes deputy directors and attorneys in the Departments of Banking and Finance, Insurance, Labor, Correctional Services, Health and Human Services, and Veterans' Affairs (and all other state agencies) hired after the bill’s effective date subject to at‑will employment. Directors set their salaries, subject to gubernatorial approval and credential-based levels. Current incumbents may elect to become at‑will (the election is irreversible); until they do they remain in the State Personnel System. Separately, returning temporary employees with less than a 120‑day break must rejoin the retirement system within 30 days, and the temporary‑employee definition is expanded to cover certain legislative limited‑term, grant‑funded, and special‑project hires. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are changed.
109-1-LB434_FinalLB434_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB434 amends State Fire Marshal statutes and explicitly provides that fees for fire-safety inspections of foster family homes (per amended section 81-505.01(2)) may be paid by the Department of Health and Human Services. The bill does not include any direct appropriations to DHHS or otherwise change DHHS budget allocations.Adds a late‑submittal fee tied to DHHS certification processing: a flat $100 plus 50% of the applicable plan‑review fee, payable in addition to the plan‑review charge. Fee receipts are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the designated account (fund not specified in the excerpt). The amendment also references dates (Sept. 1, 2025; Aug. 31, 2025) and monetary figures ($5,000) and a “no more than sixty” limit, but the excerpt does not make the specific cap, appropriation, or target fund clear. 109-1-LB435_IntroLB435_Intro_Copy.docxBill LB435 amends the Conveyance Safety Act, reallocating duties to the Conveyance Advisory Committee to advise the State Fire Marshal on rules, qualifications, temporary licenses, enforcement, continuing education providers, and disciplinary actions. The State Fire Marshal is authorized to adopt/update conveyance safety standards, grant case-by-case equivalency requests (appealable under the Administrative Procedure Act), register conveyances, and require certificates of inspection before first use. The State Fire Marshal employs a state elevator inspector (and deputies) and establishes inspector qualifications. Licensing applications for elevator mechanics and contractors are submitted to the State Fire Marshal and must permit criminal-history checks via the Nebraska State Patrol/FBI. Owners may satisfy inspection requirements via approved third-party inspection and insurance filings. Procedural provisions for complaint investigations by the State Fire Marshal or state elevator inspector are clarified. Original sections listed are repealed. No appropriations or funding changes.Adds requirements involving the State Fire Marshal and state licensing for elevators. Equivalency requests must go to the State Fire Marshal (or designee) and include: a third‑party inspection certificate submitted to the State Fire Marshal, a conveyance insurance policy and statement that it is insured, and payment of an administrative fee established pursuant to section 81‑5,214. Applications for an elevator mechanic license must include name, address, contact email, and telephone. Elevator contractor applications must include subsection (3) info, business name/address, estimated employee count with workers’ compensation evidence (if applicable), proof of general liability/personal injury/property damage insurance, a description of accidents over $1,000, and the name/phone/license number of a Nebraska licensed elevator mechanic employed or contracted in writing. No appropriations or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB436_IntroLB436_Intro_Copy.docxLB436 amends Nebraska’s Regulation of Health Professions Act, clarifying roles and procedures for the Department’s director, the division, the Health and Human Services board, and regulatory entities under the Uniform Credentialing Act. Key provisions: - Director, with board advice, appoints technical committees; for unregulated professions committees consist of six appointed members plus a board member chair; for scope-change reviews the existing regulatory entity serves as the technical committee. Composition limits and impartiality requirements specified. - Division directed to adopt rules establishing standards for application of review criteria. - Committees must use scientific evidence, hold public fact‑finding hearings, comply with the Open Meetings Act, and file written findings and recommendations (including least‑restrictive regulation when applicable). No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds procedural and substantive oversight requirements tied to the Uniform Credentialing Act. For regulated health professions, the profession’s regulatory entity must serve as the “technical committee” for scope‑of‑practice change applications, consult with applicant groups and opponents, assess risks, and recommend solutions. For unregulated professions or those without a regulatory entity, a separate review process is indicated. The additions require adoption/promulgation of rules, evaluation of education/training and competency safeguards, and assurance that the state has means to verify qualifications and discipline licensees. No changes to funding, appropriations, or specific state departments/agencies or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB437_IntroLB437_Intro_Copy.docxLB437 repeals the Nebraska Health Care Certificate of Need Act and numerous related statutes. It amends sections 71-20,103 and 71-20,105 to harmonize review procedures under the Nonprofit Hospital Sale Act, specifying that the department shall review applications and issue decisions within set timeframes. The Attorney General retains a role to elect review within twenty days and, if elected, complete review within sixty days. The bill eliminates obsolete provisions and repeals a long list of statutory sections. Operators must deduct any identified debts or outstanding state tax liabilities and remit those deducted amounts to the Department of Revenue to be credited against the debtor’s liability per section 9-1306 and the Gambling Winnings Setoff for Outstanding Debt Act. The bill also revises tax distributions. For non-sports gaming revenue: 75% to the State Treasurer (2.5% Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund; 2.5% General Fund; 70% Property Tax Credit Cash Fund) and 25% to local government (county or county/city split). For sports-wagering revenue: 2.5% Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund; 5% Racing and Gaming Commission’s Racetrack Gaming Fund; 27.5% Property Tax Credit Cash Fund; 20% General Fund; 45% Education Future Fund.The added language permits online sports wagering (through authorized racetrack-based operators or their contracted platform providers) and subjects gross gaming revenue from sports wagering to the tax in section 9-1203. The Department of Revenue’s role is to collect/remit that tax to the State Treasurer, to be credited as follows: 2.5% to the Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund; 5% to the Racing and Gaming Commission’s Racetrack Gaming Fund; 27.5% to the Property Tax Credit Cash Fund; 20% to the General Fund; and 45% to the Education Future Fund.
