109-1-LB439_IntroLB439_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Revenue- The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue (Sec. 2). - Qualifying taxpayers must apply to the Department of Revenue for the new Property Tax Circuit Breaker credit and may be required to provide documentation as determined by the department (Sec. 3(5)(e)). - The department must approve qualifying applications within 30 days and certify the approved credit amount to the taxpayer (Sec. 3(6)); taxpayers must attach that department-issued certification to their income tax return (Sec. 4). - The Department of Revenue is authorized to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the act (Sec. 6). - The bill preserves Department of Revenue recapture authority for an existing homebuyer credit (Sec. 77-2715.07(7)(d)). - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Summary (Department of Revenue focus): - The bill names the Department of Revenue as the administering agency for the new Property Tax Circuit Breaker Act (effective for taxable years beginning or deemed to begin on/after Jan 1, 2026). - The Department must receive and review applications, which must include residence address, property tax or rent paid, federal AGI, assessed value (for owners), and any other documentation the Department requires. - If eligible, the Department must approve and certify the credit amount to the taxpayer within 30 days; taxpayers attach that certification to their income tax return. - The Department is authorized to adopt rules and regulations to implement the Act. - No changes to Department funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB43_FinalLB43_Final_Copy.docxLB43 amends Nebraska electric-siting statutes to add definitions (including “foreign adversary” per 15 C.F.R. 791.4) and narrows “military installation” to specified USAF silos and bases (31 C.F.R. citations). It requires owners of generation or >700‑volt transmission projects within ten miles of such installations to certify to the board (and its executive director) that no electronic-related equipment/components are manufactured by a foreign adversary, with a NERC compliance exemption for suppliers meeting North American Electric Reliability Corporation standards. Privately developed renewable facilities remain exempt from board review if they notify the board 30 days before construction, submit decommissioning plans and security, consult the Game and Parks Commission, and execute joint transmission development agreements with transmission owners or RTO processes. The board may preapprove limited use of foreign-adversary components and may sue the State for decommissioning noncompliance. No appropriations or budget changes are included. The act is an emergency measure.Adds requirements for electric suppliers and facility owners near military installations to notify or certify to "the board" that their generation/transmission facilities contain no electronic equipment or components manufactured by a defined "foreign adversary" (per 15 C.F.R. 791.4 as of Feb 7, 2025). Identifies covered military sites by reference to 31 C.F.R. sections (as of Jan 1, 2025), including U.S. Air Force ballistic missile silos and bases. Owners of facilities tied to the transmission grid at ≥100 kV and meeting nameplate/injection thresholds must alternatively certify compliance with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) critical infrastructure protection standards. The board may preapprove use of foreign‑adversary equipment only if no reasonable alternative exists and avoiding it would cause greater harm. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB440_IntroLB440_Intro_Copy.docxLB440 (Education Leave and Support Act) assigns administration to the State Department of Education and creates two state funds managed with investments by the state investment officer under applicable state investment acts. Beginning Jan. 1, 2026, a 0.35% payroll fee on certificated teachers’ taxable wages (collected quarterly from employees) plus an equal employer match is remitted to the State Treasurer and credited to the State Education Leave Fund. The department will reimburse school districts (starting July 1, 2026) for substitute-teacher costs for the first six weeks of a teacher’s FMLA leave, up to actual daily costs as determined by the department; reimbursed teachers need not use accrued leave during that period. Excess (>20% of projected needs) is transferred by the State Treasurer to a new Education Retention Fund for shortages and professional development. The department must adopt procedures, report annually to the Legislature, and funds are audited by the Auditor of Public Accounts.Creates a new payroll-funded State Education Leave Fund administered by the State Department of Education (the department). Beginning Jan 1, 2026, a 0.35% payroll fee will be withheld from covered teachers’ taxable wages; school districts must collect it and remit quarterly to the State Treasurer and also remit an equal employer match. Receipts are credited to the State Education Leave Fund, invested by the state investment officer under existing state investment acts. Funds reimburse districts (beginning July 1, 2026) for substitute-teacher costs for the first six weeks of a teacher’s FMLA leave (capped at actual daily cost as set by the department); affected teachers need not use accrued leave for those six weeks. The department must adopt application/disbursement procedures and report annually to the Legislature. Surplus funds (>20% of projected needs) are transferred by the State Treasurer to a new Education Retention Fund, also administered by the department, to address shortages and professional development. Misuse requires repayment and penalties; the Auditor of Public Accounts must audit the Leave Fund annually.
109-1-LB441_IntroLB441_Intro_Copy.docxLB441 amends the Building Construction Act (section 71-6401) to authorize state agencies, counties, cities, and villages that require building-permit inspections to permit virtual inspections under conditions specified by the bill. Authorized inspectors must be credentialed with the issuing state agency, county, city, or village, or be third-party inspectors registered or licensed with the State of Nebraska; self-inspections are excluded. Virtual inspection eligibility: residential buildings under three stories and 10,000 sq ft, with onsite personnel listed and live interaction required (except nonstructural reinspections, which may use video/photo). All permit or structural inspections must be performed by authorized inspectors, and inspection records must be made public if the structure is standing when requested. No appropriations or funding changes are included. The original section is repealed.Adds definitions and inspection rules for entities issuing building permits: "authorized inspector" (credentialed by the state agency, county, city, or village issuing permits, or a third‑party inspector registered/licensed with the State of Nebraska; excludes self‑inspectors) and "inspection records" (pass/fail results with reasons tied to the permit address). Requires state agencies, counties, cities, or villages to allow virtual inspections for residential buildings under three stories and under 10,000 sq ft if the permit holder provides an onsite personnel list and the inspection is live with both parties; nonstructural reinspections may use photos/video. Mandates use of an authorized inspector for building or structural inspections and makes inspection records public if the structure remains standing. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB442_IntroLB442_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to administer the state social‑services program and authorizes the department to contract with other social agencies for services. The department must provide child‑care assistance to families with incomes from 130% to 400% of federal poverty level beginning October 1, 2026, and must adopt rules and regulations implementing program requirements. Funding is provided by a 0.52% payroll tax (employer 0.39%, employee 0.13%); General Funds are prohibited from covering state costs, including administration, arising from the income‑eligibility changes beginning October 1, 2026. The department shall set and annually revise a fixed-rate schedule for child‑care payments, not to exceed providers’ private rates, with possible separate rates for infants and children with special needs.DHHS duties and funding changes — summary: - DHHS will administer statewide social services and may contract for service delivery; ADC statutory maximums apply only to public assistance grants, not social services. - Beginning Oct 1, 2026, DHHS must extend child‑care assistance to families with incomes from 130% to 400% of FPL and adopt rules implementing eligibility and provider requirements. - Eligibility details: after 12 continuous months, 10% of household gross earned income is disregarded at redetermination; assistance is cost‑shared on a sliding scale with family contributions capped at existing transitional child‑care cost‑sharing rates (as of Jan 1, 2025). - Operational rules (effective Oct 1, 2025): employer/employee accommodation and enrollment flexibilities for households with provider employees. - Funding: a 0.52% payroll tax (0.39% employer / 0.13% employee) will fund the program. General Funds are prohibited from covering state costs (including administration) arising from the 2026 income‑eligibility expansion. - DHHS must set annual fixed reimbursement rate schedules for providers and prioritize highest assistance for qualified apprentices.
109-1-LB443_IntroLB443_Intro_Copy.docxLB443 amends the Nebraska Criminal Code to create the offense of unlawful squatting and assigns specific duties to law enforcement. If an officer has probable cause (e.g., personal property indicating abandonment or a nonpermanent structure), the officer must issue a warning citation. The citation directs the recipient to appear within three business days before a designee of the officer’s law enforcement agency and produce documentation authorizing residency (deed, title, rental agreement, proof of payments; photos/electronic copies accepted). Failure to appear or produce authentic documentation permits arrest; conviction is a Class I misdemeanor. No state agencies, departments, or budget appropriations are named or altered, and no funding changes are included.Adds an offense of unlawful squatting: knowingly entering and residing on another’s land without consent with intent to claim or appropriate it. Law enforcement officers with probable cause (e.g., signs of abandonment or nonpermanent structures) must issue a warning citation that requires the recipient, within three business days, to appear before a designee of the issuing law enforcement agency to present documentation authorizing residency (deed, title, rental agreement, proof of payments; photos/electronic copies acceptable). Failure to appear or presenting inauthentic/nonauthorizing documentation permits arrest; conviction is a Class I misdemeanor. The only government entity referenced is the issuing law enforcement agency (and its designee). No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB444_IntroLB444_Intro_Copy.docxLB444 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §75-307 to require the commission to administer proof-of-coverage, bonding, self-insurance or other security filings for certificated intrastate motor carriers, motor carriers transporting household goods under §75-304.03, and motor carriers transporting railroad employees under §75-304.04. The commission retains discretion to set amounts, require bonds or policies to cover property losses, and classify carriers by operational hazards and household-goods value. The bill adds an explicit minimum of $1,000,000 in uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage per occupant for required policies and continues to exempt transportation network companies. The measure repeals the original section. No changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.Adds a requirement that "the commission" must set required insurance policy rates to include a minimum of $1,000,000 in uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage per occupant. No specific state agency beyond "the commission" is named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB445_IntroLB445_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Transportation- Establishes the State Building Construction Alternatives Act to be administered by the state building division of the Department of Administrative Services (DAS), including procurement processes (design‑build, construction manager‑GC) and discretionary payment of stipends to unsuccessful design‑build proposers. - DAS must adjust the dollar threshold for projects subject to bid every four years beginning Jan 1, 2026, using a construction cost index. - The DAS division will remit rental proceeds to the State Building Revolving Fund and the State Building Renewal Assessment Fund and administer the State Emergency Capital Construction Contingency Fund. - Disbursements from the Nebraska Arts Council Cash Fund are to be made on warrants drawn by the Director of Administrative Services. - Buildings/grounds owned, leased, or operated by the Department of Correctional Services and nonoffice leased facilities for the Department of Transportation are exempt from certain DAS facilities‑administration duties. - The bill contains no new explicit appropriations.- Department of Administrative Services (DAS): Adds/clarifies DAS authority and procedures under the State Building Construction Alternatives Act to use design‑build and construction manager–general contractor procurements. Requires short‑listing, minimum two proposers when possible, detailed RFP content, confidentiality of alternative technical concepts, stipend payments to unsuccessful responsive proposers (with stipend conferring IP to the state), mandatory cost weighting of at least 50% in evaluations, staged negotiations with ranked proposers, and authority to cancel or re‑solicit. DAS must adjust specified dollar thresholds every four years beginning Jan 1, 2026, using a chosen construction‑cost index. Also adds reporting obligations to provide a report upon request to the Appropriations Committee, Building Maintenance Committee, or any legislator. - Department of Correctional Services: No changes apparent. - Department of Transportation: No changes apparent. - Funding/appropriations: No direct changes to appropriations or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB446_IntroLB446_Intro_Copy.docxBill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §71-602. It directs the department responsible for vital records to update standard registration and certification forms to support registration, statistical research or quality improvement, and consistency with federal forms. It expands authorized recipients of health data and statistical research information to include the United States Public Health Service (or its successor), government health agencies, statewide quality improvement initiatives, and researchers approved through a department-established application process. The department must publish at least annual, de-identified analyses of information received on its website. Confidentiality is preserved and any release under the section does not convert the information into public records. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a requirement that the responsible state agency publish at least annually on its website information about statewide quality improvement initiatives and a clear, expedited application process for those initiatives. No specific agency is named and no funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB447_IntroLB447_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of LaborLB447 amends the Community Development Law to define "workforce housing" and requires the Department of Economic Development to annually update the construction cost caps for owner-occupied and rental units based on the most recent Producer Price Index for All Commodities published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either agency are included.Added language requires redevelopers (and their contractors/subcontractors) on specified redevelopment construction projects to employ laborers, mechanics, and apprentices through registered apprenticeship programs and to comply with those programs’ standards — or if a registered apprenticeship program does not respond to a request within 15 business days. It defines “labor hours” (excluding foremen, superintendents, owners, and bona fide executive/administrative/professional employees per 29 C.F.R. part 541); “qualified apprentice” (represented by a 501(c)(5) organization and employed in a program whose training facility is in this state); and ties “registered apprenticeship program” to the federal definition in 26 U.S.C. 3131(e)(3)(B). No changes to Department of Economic Development or Department of Labor funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB448_IntroLB448_Intro_Copy.docxLB448 renames and revises Nebraska's postconviction relief framework as the Postconviction Relief Act. Key agency/office impacts: - District courts: retain original jurisdiction, may appoint up to two attorneys for postconviction proceedings, order disclosure of prior trial/appellate counsel files, and grant hearings or relief. Proceedings are civil; orders on motions are final judgments appealable to appellate courts. - County attorneys: must be served notice of postconviction motions. - County boards: required to pay appointed counsel's fees and reasonable expenses in the full amount fixed by the district court. - Appellate courts, Nebraska Supreme Court, and U.S. Supreme Court: referenced for finality, timelines, and retroactivity of newly recognized constitutional claims. - Law enforcement and prosecutors: bill provides for disclosure and discovery obligations (details in act). Substantive changes include adding actual innocence as a statutory ground, a one-year filing limitation with enumerated tolling exceptions, and narrow excusal of defaults for manifest injustice.Adds the "Postconviction Relief Act," creating statutory postconviction relief grounds: (1) constitutional denial/infringement rendering a judgment void or voidable under the Nebraska or U.S. Constitution, or (2) actual innocence. Defines actual innocence standards: new evidence (e.g., exculpatory DNA, alternative-suspect evidence, impeachment of state's witnesses, or undermining forensic science) and a clear-and-convincing showing that the new evidence likely would have changed the outcome. Specifies when forensic evidence is "undermined" and defines foundational and applied validity. Allows courts to excuse procedural defaults or time limits to prevent manifest injustice if a colorable actual-innocence claim exists. Preserves ineffective-assistance-of-trial-counsel claims not raised on direct appeal. Permits district courts to order prior trial/appellate counsel to provide complete case files to the prisoner. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB449_IntroLB449_Intro_Copy.docxLB449 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §39-1365.01 to revise requirements for the department responsible for the state highway system (the Department of Transportation). The department must develop a specific, long-range state highway system plan, annually formulate and assign project priorities, and present the plan and the §39-1365.02 report to the Legislature by December 1 for referral to the appropriate standing committees. The plan must (1) designate portions of the system as expressways and (2) account for highway revenue by each district under §39-1102, requiring that at least 70% of revenue raised in a district be allocated to projects within that district. The bill repeals the original section.Adds a district-based accounting and allocation rule for highway revenue (referencing section 39-1102). It requires revenues raised by each highway district to be tracked by district and mandates that at least 70% of a district’s revenue be allocated to projects within that same district. No specific agencies or departments are named in the text; operational responsibility would fall to the agency that currently administers highway revenues (e.g., the state transportation/highway authority). No new appropriation amounts are specified—the change is a restriction on how existing district-raised highway revenue must be allocated.
109-1-LB44_IntroLB44_Intro_Copy.docxLB44 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29-3001 governing postconviction relief. It preserves that motions are filed in the sentencing court, that notice must be served on the county attorney, and that proceedings are civil with costs taxed as in habeas corpus cases. The one-year limitation for filing a verified postconviction motion is retained but its triggering events are clarified/expanded: timing may run from the conclusion of direct appeal, discovery of the factual predicate, removal of a state-created impediment, recognition of a new constitutional right by the Nebraska Supreme Court or U.S. Supreme Court (if made retroactive), denial of certiorari or affirmance by the U.S. Supreme Court (with a 30-day district court notice requirement after petitioning for certiorari), or the date the prisoner turns 21. No state agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed.Adds a new subsection (f) specifying that the relevant date is the date the prisoner reaches 21 years of age. No government agencies, departments, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned or affected.
109-1-LB450_IntroLB450_Intro_Copy.docxLB450 amends the Property Assessed Clean Energy Act to (1) add grid resiliency and renewable energy to legislative findings and (2) revise definitions and municipal procedures. Key government-related changes: municipalities (defined as counties, cities, or villages) may create clean energy assessment districts and act as district governing bodies; counties may not create districts overlapping a city or village’s corporate or extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction. Municipalities must hold a public hearing (published in a legal newspaper at least ten days prior) before creating a district. Ordinances or, for counties, resolutions must include a public-purpose finding, a model assessment-contract form (municipality, property owner, and optional third‑party lender), designation of an official authorized to sign contracts, application/eligibility rules, assessment collection procedures, and fixed interest/repayment requirements for residential projects. No appropriations or budget allocations are specified.Adds a definition of "grid resiliency improvement" as any acquisition, installation, or modification (on public or private property) intended to anticipate, prepare for, withstand, respond to, and rapidly recover from major power disruptions. Examples listed: backup power generators; backup generators powered by renewable energy; solar panels with battery storage; and smart grid technology. No government agencies or departments are referenced and no funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB451_IntroLB451_Intro_Copy.docxLB451 amends transfer and administration rules for unclaimed property and the Capitol Restoration Cash Fund. It directs the State Treasurer to, on or before November 1 each year 2025–2034, transfer any Unclaimed Property Trust Fund balance in excess of $1 million so that the first $1 million goes to the Capitol Restoration Cash Fund and any remaining balance to the Permanent School Fund (transfers revert to the Permanent School Fund beginning 2035). The bill authorizes the State Treasurer to deduct unclaimed-property administrative costs into a newly created Unclaimed Property Cash Fund and requires investment of available balances by the State Investment Officer under existing investment acts. It updates the Capitol Restoration Cash Fund statute to explicitly allow transfers from the Unclaimed Property Trust Fund and the Nebraska Capital Construction Fund, assigns administration to the fund administrator and commission, and authorizes fund use for Capitol restoration, collections, promotion, and HVAC project management. The Auditor of Public Accounts and Department of Revenue confidentiality provisions are retained.Adds annual transfer requirements for the State Treasurer: on or before November 1 each year 2025–2034, any Unclaimed Property Trust Fund balance over $1,000,000 must be split — the first $1,000,000 to the Capitol Restoration Cash Fund and any remaining excess to the Permanent School Fund. Beginning in 2035, any Unclaimed Property Trust Fund balance over $1,000,000 must be transferred to the Permanent School Fund. Agencies mentioned: State Treasurer and the Legislature (which may direct the fund). Funds affected: Unclaimed Property Trust Fund (and Unclaimed Property Cash Fund), Capitol Restoration Cash Fund, and Permanent School Fund. No other specific appropriations or dollar amounts beyond the $1,000,000 threshold are specified.
109-1-LB452_IntroLB452_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesBill LB452 declares the Legislature’s intent to appropriate funds to the Department of Health and Human Services: $500,000 in FY2025-26 and $500,000 in FY2026-27 from federal funds. The amounts are designated as Federal Funds (specifically federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds) and are earmarked solely for court-appointed special advocate state aid. The bill includes an emergency clause, making it effective upon passage and approval.The Legislature intends to appropriate $500,000 in FY2025-26 and $500,000 in FY2026-27 in federal funds to the Department of Health and Human Services for state aid. Each year’s appropriation specifically designates $500,000 Federal Funds for Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) state aid and restricts use exclusively to that purpose. The funding source is federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) in both fiscal years.
109-1-LB453_FinalLB453_Final_Copy.docxLB453 amends Nebraska guardianship and conservatorship statutes. Key agency provisions: - Nebraska State Patrol: required to submit applicants' fingerprints to the FBI and provide criminal history reports to the State Court Administrator; reports must be filed with the court at least 10 days before appointment unless waived or expedited. Applicants pay fingerprint/background-check costs. Financial institutions and trust companies are exempt. - State Court Administrator and courts: receive and review the federal criminal-history reports before signing appointment orders. - Public Guardian/Public Guardianship Act: may serve as temporary guardian/conservator; if the Public Guardian has exceeded caseload ratios (per section 30-4115), courts must appoint individual limited temporary guardians subject to availability of funds appropriated under section 81-3141. Appointments stop when those funds are exhausted. - Counties/county boards: must pay approved expenses/fees for appointed limited temporary guardians and may apply under section 81-3141 for reimbursement. Temporary guardians/conservators are not required to submit fingerprints.Authorizes the Nebraska State Patrol to submit applicants’ fingerprints to the Federal Bureau of Investigation for a national criminal history check and to provide the resulting criminal history report to the State Court Administrator. Requires the State Patrol to forward fingerprints to the FBI and to issue the report to the State Court Administrator. Costs: the applicant must pay the actual cost of fingerprinting and the criminal background check. No state funding or appropriation changes specified.
109-1-LB454_FinalLB454_Final_Copy.docxLB454 amends duties and funding provisions for the Department (and its Division of Behavioral Health) and regional behavioral health authorities (RBHAs). RBHAs retain planning, budgeting, contracting, reporting, audit coordination, and uniform fee-policy duties; they may only provide division-funded services after competitive bidding (or if no qualified providers) with director authorization and a division contract. The bill permits a behavioral health services provider, with department approval, to add new services or expand capacity if it meets department network enrollment standards, is enrolled with the department and RBHA, and is contracted with the RBHA. The Behavioral Health Services Fund remains administered by the division, containing legislative appropriations and other receipts (transfer to the General Fund permitted by Legislature). Money from section 76-903 is designated for housing-related assistance for very low-income adults with serious mental illness or substance abuse disorder; if obligations are met, up to 20% may be allocated to RBHAs for housing acquisition/rehabilitation. The division will allocate funds by formula, contract with RBHAs, and investments are handled by the state investment officer.Adds that a behavioral health services provider may, with approval by "the department," begin new behavioral health services or expand existing capacity only if the provider: (a) meets the department's network enrollment standards, (b) is enrolled as a network provider with both the department and a regional behavioral health authority, and (c) holds a contract with a regional behavioral health authority. Agencies mentioned: the department and regional behavioral health authorities. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are included.
109-1-LB455_IntroLB455_Intro_Copy.docxLB455 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-144.01 to make employer/insurer injury reports filed with the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court confidential and not subject to public inspection, while prescribing limited exceptions. The Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court (and its administrator) remains the filing and access control authority; the administrator will prescribe forms for employee waivers and inspection requests. An employee may waive confidentiality (waiver stays in effect across employers unless revoked). Permitted disclosures include the employee (or authorized attorney/agent), the employer/insurer/risk pool/third-party administrator (or their attorneys/agents) with written authorization, attorneys involved in claims or litigation, state or federal investigators or statistical compilations, redacted employer injury counts, pleadings/exhibits filed with the court, nonprofit condolence uses for workplace deaths, or by court order. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds confidentiality rules for reports filed with the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court. Key agency references and duties: - Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court: reports are confidential except as provided; the court may deny inspection unless an exception applies. - Administrator of the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court: prescribes the form and manner for employees to waive confidentiality and for making inspection/copy requests. - State or federal government: may obtain reports for investigations, examinations, or to compile statistical information. Permitted disclosures include when the employee waives confidentiality, the employee (or their attorney/agent), the employer/insurer/risk pool/TPA (or their counsel/agent), certain insurers'/TPAs' attorneys handling related claims, court filings/exhibits, redacted employer injury statistics, nonprofit grief outreach, or by court order. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB456_IntroLB456_Intro_Copy.docxLB456 amends §48‑146.02 of the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act. It authorizes three‑judge panels of the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Court to seek suspension or revocation of a workers' compensation insurer's authorization from the Director of Insurance, to suspend/revoke a risk management pool's group self‑insurance authority under the Intergovernmental Risk Management Act, or to revoke a self‑insurer's approval under §48‑145, without affecting preexisting liabilities. The Attorney General, at the compensation court administrator's request, may file show‑cause motions, be treated as a party, present evidence, and appear before the panel; the presiding judge appoints panel judges and does not serve. The bill enumerates insurer/pool/self‑insurer practices that trigger action, permits the compensation court to examine records of insurers, pools, self‑insurers, adjusters, third‑party administrators, and agents (subject to work‑product and attorney‑client privilege), and allows the court to adopt implementing rules. No funding or appropriation changes are included.I don’t see the underlined text — you only provided “(5)”. Please paste the actual added text (or attach the bill page/section). When you do, I’ll produce a ≤150‑word summary focused on: - any government agencies/departments named, - changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations, - any new duties or transfers of authority to agencies, - effective dates or reporting/oversight requirements. If you prefer, paste the entire subsection (5) and I’ll extract and summarize just the additions.
109-1-LB457_FinalLB457_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services, in consultation with the State Department of Education, to develop model anaphylaxis policies for use by school districts and licensed child care programs. DHHS must solicit input from relevant medical professionals, parents, school staff, and others; include emergency response protocols, individualized health-care plans, communication strategies, and exposure-reduction measures; review and update the models at least every three years; and post them on the applicable department's website. The model policies may be used as guides for required local policies. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DHHS are included in the bill.The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) must, in consultation with the State Department of Education, develop and publish on its website model anaphylaxis policies for school districts and licensed child care programs. Policies are to be created with input from medical and educational stakeholders and must include emergency treatment protocols, individualized health care plan guidance, communication strategies, exposure-reduction strategies, and child/parent communication guidance. DHHS must reexamine and update the models at least every three years. The bill imposes no new appropriations, funding, or budget allocations to DHHS in the added text.
109-1-LB458_IntroLB458_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB458 (amending section 77-1804) requires county treasurers to forward an electronic copy of the list of real property subject to tax sale to the Property Tax Administrator. The Property Tax Administrator must compile a statewide list and publish the compiled list on the Department of Revenue’s website. The bill contains no explicit appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue.No provisions change Department of Revenue appropriations or create new funding/allocations for the Department. Substantive additions affecting tax/tax-deed processes: establishes an administrative $150 charge to the property owner upon issuance of a certificate; directs periodic review (every five years beginning 2030) of an existing $20 fee; clarifies timelines and procedures for tax-deed applications by purchasers and land banks (including a 9‑month application window after specified post‑sale periods and a 2‑year vacancy determination for certain cases); enumerates objective criteria for classifying property as vacant and abandoned and requires an affidavit to the county treasurer. Also adds housing/zoning changes (duplexes, accessory dwelling units) but no Department of Revenue budget or appropriation changes.
109-1-LB459_IntroLB459_Intro_Copy.docxLB459 assigns responsibilities to the Nebraska Department of Environment and Energy, declares legislative intent, and establishes a Home Weatherization Clearinghouse. The bill directs the Clearinghouse to perform duties related to home weatherization programs and coordination, subject to requirements of any relevant federal, state, or local grant program. The provided text does not specify any appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations.Adds a proviso that the provision applies only when expressly required by the applicable federal, state, or local grant program. No specific agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB45_IntroLB45_Intro_Copy.docxLB45 amends statutes governing the Nebraska Training and Support Cash Fund and the Nebraska Worker Training Board. Key agency references and funding changes: - Nebraska Training and Support Cash Fund: maintained as an investable fund (state investment officer). Expenditures require the Governor's written authorization upon the Commissioner of Labor’s recommendation; the Legislature may direct transfers to the General Fund. Interest from the State Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund is credited to the cash fund. - Uses expanded to explicitly include awarding grants under section 3 (grants for job programs for historically underserved youth) and to cover administrative costs; an Administrative Costs Reserve Account within the fund must be allocated to cover anticipated administrative expenses. - Nebraska Worker Training Board composition specified (includes Commissioner of Labor, Director of Economic Development, Commissioner of Education, community college representative). The board must prepare annual program guidelines for fund-supported workforce activities. - The Department (Labor) must publish an annual report detailing administrative expenditures; no unrelated departmental costs may be charged to these allocations. No specific appropriation amounts are included.Adds authority to award grants under section 3 of the act pursuant to subdivisions (2)(c)–(f) of section 48-622.02, specifying use of grant administrative funds for application review, program auditing, and data management. It bars allocating any portion of administrative costs to unrelated departmental expenses. The (unnamed) department administering the grants must publish an annual report itemizing administrative expenditures to ensure transparency. No specific dollar amounts, appropriations, or funding increases are included.
109-1-LB460_IntroLB460_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB460 includes multiple statutory transfers from the State Settlement Cash Fund to other funds to be executed "on such dates and in such amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services." Those directed transfers are: $876,998 to the General Fund (on or before June 30, 2018); $1,756,639 to the General Fund (on or before June 30, 2019); $125,000 to the Legal Education for Public Service and Rural Practice Loan Repayment Assistance Fund (on or before April 30, 2018); $150,000 to that same loan repayment fund (on or before July 9, 2018); and $600,000 to the newly created Nebraska Council on Economic Education Cash Fund (on or before July 1, 2025).Creates the Nebraska Council on Economic Education Cash Fund for University of Nebraska Board of Regents expenses, to be invested by the state investment officer. The Legislature intends to appropriate $300,000 from this cash fund to the Board of Regents in FY2025-26 and $300,000 in FY2026-27. The State Treasurer is directed to transfer $600,000 from the State Settlement Cash Fund into the new cash fund on or before July 1, 2025; the timing and amounts of that transfer are to be set by the budget administrator of the Budget Division of the Department of Administrative Services. No direct appropriations to DAS are made.
109-1-LB461_IntroLB461_Intro_Copy.docxLB461 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §16-1027 governing municipal firefighter retirements. Key institutional provisions: - Retirement committee: establishes optional annuity benefit forms to be provided under the funding medium for the retirement system. - Retirement system: may purchase annuity contracts for retirees and may distribute paid-up contracts; payment of lump sums or distribution of contracts terminates system obligations. - Cities and city councils: may adopt lump-sum distribution options for pre-1997 retirees; if annuity cost comparisons differ by >5%, the retirement committee reviews and the city council, after a hearing, sets the lump-sum amount. - Funding: if a firefighter’s retirement value is insufficient to provide a statutorily required minimum pension, the city must use funds from the retirement system’s unallocated employer account to make up the shortfall. The bill repeals the original section.Adds language listing permissible payment frequencies — "annual payments, quarterly payments, monthly payments, or" — expanding/clarifying timing options. No government agencies, departments, or budgetary appropriations or funding changes are referenced.
109-1-LB462_IntroLB462_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill explicitly references the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) as follows: it defines “Department” to mean DHHS; requires DHHS to establish a statewide toll-free child abuse/neglect reporting number; requires DHHS to provide or approve mandatory-reporter training (with a free online training to be created by Oct. 1, 2027 and updated at least every five years) and to adopt implementing rules by Oct. 1, 2027; directs DHHS to retain all reports and related records in a child protection tracking system for statistics and future investigations; assigns DHHS responsibility to assign counties to child advocacy centers and to share/coordinate initial responses and information with law enforcement; and provides for DHHS (Division of Children and Family Services) representation on county child abuse investigation and treatment teams. Juvenile-court jurisdiction includes juveniles voluntarily relinquished to DHHS or DHHS-licensed placement agencies. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds duties for the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): by October 1, 2027 DHHS must provide or approve mandatory reporter training on child abuse/neglect (to be completed within 90 days of starting and every two years thereafter), create a free publicly available online version of that training (developed in consultation with experts on implicit bias and culturally diverse families), update it at least every five years, and adopt rules and regulations to implement the section. Training topics include identification, reporting, trauma‑informed responses, implicit bias/cultural competency/race‑conscious reporting, and alternatives/community resources. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB463_IntroLB463_Intro_Copy.docxLB463 expands school safety duties and grant authorities primarily for the State Department of Education (SDE) and the state school security director. Key agency actions and funding changes: - Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (Dept. of Health/Medicaid oversight) may now fund grants for costs associated with school cardiac emergency response plans. Investment earnings credited to the General Fund beginning Oct. 1, 2024. - The state school security director (SDE) must develop a cardiac emergency response plan template and collect district safety plans; SDE also to provide training for cardiac emergency response teams. - SDE may administer grants (districts and educational service units; ESUs may apply on behalf of nonpublic schools) to purchase AEDs and implement plans; the Commissioner prescribes application forms. - Annual, non‑identifying reporting to the Legislature required (due Dec. 1). - Intent to appropriate $10 million from the School Safety and Security Fund to SDE to run the grant program. The State Investment Officer invests fund balances.Adds requirements that the legislature establish a cardiac emergency response plan template for schools and define related terms. Agencies/entities mentioned: "the department" (charged with providing training for cardiac emergency response team members serving public and nonpublic schools), school boards (required to annually review/evaluate each district plan), and local emergency medical services providers (required coordination). The template mandates AED placement and routine maintenance, designation and training of staff (coaches, nurses, athletic trainers), annual drills, and team activation protocols. The bill authorizes grants for costs associated with implementing the plan pursuant to section 7, but contains no specific appropriation amounts.
109-1-LB464_IntroLB464_Intro_Copy.docxLB464 (109th Legislature, 2025) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-101 to create and prohibit "organized retail crime," define related terms, establish penalties based on aggregated retail market value (which is an element prosecutors must prove beyond a reasonable doubt), allow aggregation of losses across victims in the same scheme, and specify that representing merchandise as stolen is criminal even if it was not actually stolen. The bill repeals the original §28-101. The bill was referred to the Judiciary Committee. No state agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the text.No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes. Substantive additions: prior conduct relevant to classification is limited to acts within ten years of the current offense. The statute allows aggregating the retail market value taken under a single organized retail crime scheme from one or more victims in the same indictment/complaint for offense classification, but the same amounts cannot be counted toward more than one offense. Aggregate retail market value is made an essential element that must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt. It also eliminates the defense that merchandise was not actually stolen/embezzled/converted if it was explicitly represented as such.
109-1-LB465_IntroLB465_Intro_Copy.docxLB465 amends statutes governing transportation network companies (TNCs). It directs the commission (which administers motor carrier regulation) to allow TNCs to choose either an annual flat fee up to $25,000 or a per‑vehicle fee up to $80, with the commission setting fee amounts so total collections do not exceed costs of administration and enforcement. Fees are due Jan 1 (delinquent Mar 1); initial permits issued on or after July 1 pay 50%. Collections are remitted to the State Treasurer within 30 days. The State Treasurer must credit TNC fees to the Transportation Network Company Regulation Cash Fund for enforcement; fees for other regulated motor carriers remain credited to the General Fund. The bill also requires personal vehicles used under the cited provisions to comply with the Motor Vehicle Registration Act and repeals the original sections.Adds language authorizing an annual flat fee, capped by an annual per‑vehicle fee (i.e., a per‑vehicle ceiling on such annual fees). No specific government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB466_IntroLB466_Intro_Copy.docxLB466 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-245 (Nebraska Juvenile Code) to revise definitional terms. Key agency references and changes: - Office of Dispute Resolution: "Approved center" must be approved by the Director of the Office of Dispute Resolution. - Department of Correctional Services: "Staff secure juvenile facility" expressly excludes institutions operated by the Department of Correctional Services. - Referral/approval authority: Restorative justice facilitators must be approved by the referring county attorney, city attorney, or juvenile or county court judge. - Other cross-references remain to juvenile, county, and district courts and to mental health treatment facilities (per §71-914). The bill also clarifies that "alternative to detention" does not include placements using physical construction or hardware to restrain movement (except manually controlled delayed egress ≤30 seconds) and redefines "young adult" as older than 18 but younger than 21. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.I can’t summarize from just the fragment “younger than.” Please paste the full underlined (added) text or upload the bill excerpt. 109-1-LB467_IntroLB467_Intro_Copy.docxLB467 amends the Utilization Review Act (sections 44-5416 to 44-5431) to require health carriers and utilization review agents to implement and maintain a prior-authorization application programming interface (API) by January 1, 2028, consistent with federal regulation 45 C.F.R. 156.223(b) as it existed January 1, 2025. The API requirement does not apply to prior-authorization requests for drugs (drug defined by 45 C.F.R. 156.221(b)(1)(v) as of January 1, 2025). The bill updates the statutory citation to include this new section and repeals the original section 44-5416. No state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Requires health carriers and utilization review agents to implement and maintain a prior authorization API by January 1, 2028, to conform with 45 C.F.R. 156.223(b) as it existed on January 1, 2025. Exempts prior authorization requests for drugs; “drug” is defined by 45 C.F.R. 156.221(b)(1)(v) as of January 1, 2025. The text cites federal regulations (45 C.F.R.) but does not name specific federal agencies or create new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB468A_IntroLB468A_Intro_Copy.docxAppropriates $5,000,000 from the Securities Act Cash Fund for FY2025-26 and $5,000,000 from the same fund for FY2026-27 to the Department of Banking and Finance, Program 66, to implement provisions of Legislative Bill 468 (109th Legislature, 2025). Each fiscal-year appropriation is designated as Cash Funds for state aid and must be used only for that purpose. The bill prohibits using these appropriated funds for permanent or temporary employee salaries and per diems. Contains an emergency clause making the act effective upon enactment.Appropriates $5,000,000 in FY2025-26 and $5,000,000 in FY2026-27 from the Securities Act Cash Fund to the Department of Banking and Finance, Program 66, to assist implementation of Legislative Bill 468 (109th Legislature, 2025). Each year's appropriation is designated as Cash Funds for state aid and must be used solely for that purpose. The funds expressly may not be spent on permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB468_IntroLB468_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Insurance, Department of Revenue- Department of Administrative Services: The budget division administrator may direct State Treasurer transfers from the Securities Act Cash Fund to the General Fund — $29 million on or before June 30, 2026, and $23 million on or before each June 30, 2027, 2028, and 2029. - Department of Insurance: Securities registration fees are credited to the Department of Insurance Cash Fund. The Director must transmit insurance premium tax receipts annually: 50% to the State Treasurer, 30% to the General Fund, 10% to the Mutual Finance Assistance Fund, and 10% to counties (by population), subject to specified exceptions. - Department of Revenue: Retains discretion to review county assessor sale determinations, must publish compiled delinquent-sale lists online, will collect/adjust the renewable-energy nameplate-capacity tax and remit proceeds to county treasurers, and the 3% collection fee is credited to the Department of Revenue Property Assessment Division Cash Fund.Department of Revenue - New duty: beginning Jan 1, 2027 and annually thereafter, DOR must adjust a specified tax rate by the average annual percentage change in total statewide property taxes over the most recent 10 years (round to nearest dollar). - Creates a 1% tax on clear market value of property (or beneficial interests) received by each person in excess of $100,000 for decedents dying on/after July 1, 2025; proceeds are to be distributed to counties (credit to county general funds) according to certified property-tax shares, with 10% allocated to counties by population share. - Legislative intent to review specified fees every five years beginning 2030. Department of Administrative Services - No direct funding, appropriation, or new duties identified. (Mileage referenced to section 33-117; no appropriation change.) Department of Insurance - No changes, funding, or new responsibilities identified. Funding/appropriations - $5 million annually from the Securities Act Cash Fund to be distributed to counties proportionally by population beginning July 1, 2025.
109-1-LB469_IntroLB469_Intro_Copy.docxLB469 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §76-1401 (Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act) to impose a duty on the State Court Administrator to develop a form that must be included in eviction notices. The bill directs the State Court Administrator (judicial branch administrative office) to prepare that form. The act repeals the original section. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB46_IntroLB46_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human Services- Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): required to apply for SNAP options to maximize federal funding and minimize General Fund use; hire staff and submit an annual report to the Legislature (Dec. 1) detailing options, actions, caseload and costs. DHHS must develop a state outreach plan meeting Food and Nutrition Service (USDA) criteria, may accept gifts/grants, partner with counties/nonprofits, submit the plan to USDA FNS for approval and request federal matching funds, and may be exempt from implementing the plan if private/federal funds are insufficient. DHHS shall create a TANF-funded categorical eligibility policy (temporary 165% gross income limit through 10/1/2025) with annual evaluation reports (Dec. 15). DHHS shall establish a Restaurant Meals Program (subject to federal approval), operational by July 1, 2026. - Department of Labor: to the extent federal funds are available, partner on the SNAP Next Step Program encouraging eligible households (131–165% poverty) to participate until 9/30/2023; Legislature intends no General Funds be used by the Department of Labor for these processes.Summary (underlined additions): - Department of Agriculture: Requires the Department of Agriculture (the “department”) to establish a Restaurant Meals Program as part of SNAP, subject to any required federal state-plan approval. Eligible households (elderly/disabled and their spouses per 7 U.S.C. 2012(j), and homeless individuals per 7 U.S.C. 2012(l)) may redeem SNAP benefits at private vendors that contract with the department to provide concessional-priced meals under 7 U.S.C. 2018(h). The program must be operational by July 1, 2026, and the department may adopt rules to implement it. - Department of Labor & Department of Health and Human Services: No changes, responsibilities, or funding/appropriation directives for these agencies are included in the added text. - Funding/appropriations: The addition contains no new appropriations or budget allocations.
109-1-LB470_FinalLB470_Final_Copy.docxLB470 authorizes attorneys to substitute unsworn declarations "under penalty of perjury" for sworn declarations, verifications, certificates, statements, or affidavits required by law in cases where the attorney's signature is required—except for depositions, oaths of office, or oaths required to be taken before a specified official other than a notary public. The bill prescribes the exact declaration language for executions inside and outside Nebraska. No specific state agencies or departments are named; the text references the laws of the State of Nebraska and notary publics. The bill does not include any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds that whenever law requires an attorney’s sworn declaration, verification, certificate, statement, oath, or affidavit (other than for depositions, oaths of office, or oaths before officials other than a notary), an attorney may instead submit an unsworn written declaration signed and dated under penalty of perjury. Provides two model forms: one for execution outside Nebraska referencing Nebraska laws, and one for execution within Nebraska. No state agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.
109-1-LB471_IntroLB471_Intro_Copy.docxLB471 prohibits state agencies and other state entities from restricting the use, purchase, or sale of any motor vehicle (per §39-101) based on the energy source powering any vehicle component (including propulsion or accessory functions). It imposes the same prohibition on counties, cities, and villages. The bill also bars the Department of Environment and Energy from seeking (or causing to be sought) a waiver under the federal Clean Air Act that would allow Nebraska to adopt vehicle emissions standards more stringent than those required by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included in the bill.Prohibits any state agency or other state entity, and any county, city, or village, from restricting the use, purchase, or sale of motor vehicles based on the vehicle’s energy source (including propulsion or other powered functions). Directs the Department of Environment and Energy not to seek (or cause to be sought) any Clean Air Act waiver to adopt vehicle-emission standards more stringent than those required by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB472_IntroLB472_Intro_Copy.docxLB472 creates the Office of Regulatory Management within state government, led by a Director appointed by and serving at the pleasure of the Governor. The office will supervise a baseline, publicly published catalog of agencies' regulatory requirements and publish biennial reports showing changes and estimated compliance costs for a median Nebraska citizen or business. All state departments, agencies, offices, and divisions must conduct internal reviews (initial reviews due within six months) and provide evaluations, needs assessments, and supporting due diligence to the office on request; updates are required every two years or within 60 days of a request. The office reviews agencies' identification of systemic problems, requires cost–benefit and monetized/nonmonetized estimates, may request reevaluation if best practices were not used, and must publish its assessments. The office may not authorize or reject other agencies' regulatory actions. No funding appropriations or budget allocations are specified in the bill.Creates the Office of Regulatory Management under a Director appointed by and serving at the pleasure of the Governor. The office will supervise a baseline, publicly published catalog of all regulatory requirements, require every Nebraska state agency/department/office/division to conduct and submit internal reviews (initially within six months, then biennially or within 60 days of request), and publish a biennial report estimating changes and compliance costs for the median citizen or business. The office will collect, assess, and publish agencies' evaluations and due diligence for new rules, can ask agencies and the Governor to reevaluate rulemaking if best practices weren’t used, but cannot approve or block agency regulations. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB473_IntroLB473_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and FinanceLB473 expands the Department of Banking and Finance’s authority under the Nebraska Money Transmitters Act. It establishes new fees (including a $50,000 charter fee for digital asset depositories and a $500 investigative fee for branch/merger/conditional‑charter requests), retains a $1,500 nonrefundable license application fee and specified minimum investigative fees, and grants the Director rulemaking, cost‑recovery and proportionate‑fee authority. The department may accept third‑party or multistate exams/audits, use analytic systems, and participate in multistate supervision. Licensees must provide records and pay examination costs; failure to respond within 21 days can trigger fines (up to $5,000 per violation) and investigation cost charges. The department may issue a notice of cancellation if a licensee fails to maintain its surety bond. All fees and charges collected are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Financial Institution Assessment Cash Fund; fines are remitted per Article VII, §5. No other appropriations or budget changes are specified.The added provisions (Nebraska Money Transmitters Act) designate the Department of Banking and Finance (and its Director) as the supervising authority, expanding its powers to: enter agreements with federal/state regulators and multistate organizations; use the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System/Registry and analytical/examination tools; accept third‑party audits and out‑of‑state exam reports; conduct and coordinate examinations (including multistate processes); require records, background checks, reports, bonds, net‑worth and permissible‑investment standards; and impose fees, costs, fines, suspensions, and enforcement orders. Financial flows: all fees, charges and costs collected under the Act are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Financial Institution Assessment Cash Fund; fines are remitted to the State Treasurer for constitutional distribution. No separate new appropriations or line‑item budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB474_FinalLB474_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and Finance, Department of Insurance, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB474 substantially expands the Department of Banking and Finance’s regulatory, licensing, examination, enforcement, and fee authorities for money transmitters, digital asset depositories, installment loans/sales, and residential mortgages (including use of NMLS, background checks, privacy/breach rules, rulemaking, cease‑and‑desist, fines, and charging examination/investigation costs to licensees). The bill prescribes new fee and bond requirements (including a $50,000 digital‑asset depository charter fee and higher money‑transmitter application/renewal fees), permits annual assessments on regulated institutions, and directs fees and fines to the State Treasurer (crediting the Financial Institution Assessment Cash Fund or otherwise as required). The Department of Insurance gains flexibility to approve nonstandard policy provisions and must establish, by Jan 1, 2026, a tax (up to 6%) on non‑Medicare HMO direct‑writing premiums, remitted to the Medicaid Access and Quality Fund. DHHS is exempted from offering corrective action plans when a provider is formally restricted and must seek federal approval by Aug 1, 2025 for Medicaid Access and Quality Act funding.Department of Banking and Finance (DBF) - Expands DBF authority under a new Nebraska Money Transmitters Act: defines terms, establishes licensing, examination, background-check, net‑worth and surety bond (≥$100k or 100% of average daily liability, cap $500k) requirements, permissible investments, reporting, enforcement (fines up to $5,000/day), multistate supervisory participation, use of Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System and Registry, and acceptance of third‑party audits/exams. - Sets money transmitter fees: $1,500 application; $750 annual renewal. - Implements parallel provisions for the Nebraska Installment Loan and Sales Act: DBF is the regulator; license/application/branch/renewal fees and surety bond ($50,000) schedules and enforcement powers spelled out (e.g., application fees: sales $150, loan $500; renewal/branch fees listed). - All license fees/charges credited to the Financial Institution Assessment Cash Fund; fines remitted to the State Treasurer per Article VII, §5. Department of Insurance - Requires policyholders (policies issued/delivered on/after Jan 1, 2026) receive electronic or mailed notice at least 15 days before termination/lapse for nonpayment; assignees get equivalent standing. Department of Health and Human Services - No substantive budget, appropriation, or funding changes; only a brief definitional reference to "provider"/visiting faculty permits (section 38‑2045) without funding effects.
109-1-LB475_IntroLB475_Intro_Copy.docxLB475 (Riepe) amends Nebraska’s controlled‑substance law by classifying tianeptine as a controlled substance, revising Schedules III–V to list numerous drugs, and cross‑referencing federal standards. The bill cites the Drug Enforcement Administration (U.S. Department of Justice) exempted‑products/anabolic‑steroid list (as of Jan. 31, 2022) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and 21 U.S.C. §355 (FD&C Act §505) for FDA‑approved product exclusions (e.g., dronabinol). It repeals Neb. Rev. Stat. §28‑405 (R.S. Cumulative Supp., 2024) and was referred to the Judiciary Committee. No state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds "Tianeptine" as item (62) to an enumerated list of substances. The inserted text does not reference any government agencies, departments, or programs, nor does it make or change any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB476_IntroLB476_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureLB476 authorizes any person to notify the Department of Agriculture (or the Attorney General) of violations or potential violations of the Foreign‑owned Real Estate National Security Act. The Department of Agriculture is designated to investigate such violations; if the Director of Agriculture has reasonable suspicion a violation occurred, the Director must refer the matter to the Attorney General or to outside counsel retained by the Department for enforcement. The bill permits use of outside counsel retained by the Department. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are specified.No provisions affect the Department of Agriculture. The added text clarifies that property interests are exempt from being voided, divested, or otherwise subject to the Foreign‑owned Real Estate National Security Act if they were acquired while the holder was authorized to work in the U.S. (per 8 C.F.R. 274a.12) or acquired while the holder was not a nonresident alien; that protection continues even if the holder later becomes a nonresident alien. The exemption does not apply to restricted entities or their agents/trustees. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Agriculture are included.
109-1-LB477_IntroLB477_Intro_Copy.docxLB477 amends the Workplace Privacy Act (sections 48-3502 and 48-3503). It bars employers from requiring employees or applicants to provide usernames/passwords, log into personal internet accounts, add employers to contacts, or change account privacy settings. It also prohibits mandatory use of apps or wearable electronic devices to track employee location, travel patterns, or contacts, except during a pandemic state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor under §81-829.40 — and then only for on‑site contact tracing during work hours, with data destroyed within 48 hours after the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s recommended tracing period. Data that associates an employee with tracked employer property must be stored by an independent third party and accessed only by warrant. The bill references the Governor and the CDC. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a prohibition on employers requiring employees to use or wear electronic tracking apps/devices, with a narrow exception if the Governor issues a pandemic state‑of‑emergency proclamation under §81‑829.40 that expressly allows employer contact tracing. Conditions: tracing only on employer premises during work hours; collected data excluded from personnel files and destroyed within 48 hours after the end of any tracing period recommended by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Data linking an employee to tracked property must be stored by an independent third party and is accessible only by warrant. The Governor (state executive) and the CDC are the only government entities specifically referenced. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB478_FinalLB478_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureReferences to the Department of Agriculture are in section 53-304. The bill directs that the Winery and Grape Producers Promotional Fund be located in the Department of Agriculture for administrative purposes. Revenue sources credited to the fund include winery charges ($20 per 160 gallons), certain shipping-license fees (manufacturer and retail direct-sales shipping license fees), excise taxes, and gifts/grants. The Department, at the direction of and in cooperation with the Nebraska Grape and Winery Board, shall use the fund to develop and maintain research, marketing, promotion, and related programs for grapes, fruits, berries, honey, and other agricultural products for the wine industry, including funding experts in viticulture and enology. Funds may be invested, carried over between fiscal years, and used only for the statute’s specified purposes (subject to transfers under section 2-5604).Summary (Department of Agriculture focus): The added provisions authorize the liquor commission to issue auction permits to auction houses for selling alcoholic liquor from closed retailers or private in‑state collections, require auction notification and inventories, and empower the commission to adopt rules. They also authorize shipping licenses for out‑of‑state wholesalers to ship only to licensed Nebraska wholesalers; such licensees must pay the fee required by sections 53‑124 and 53‑124.01, which the commission remits to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The primary source of supply must reaffirm brands annually by July 1 (renewals open 90 days prior); the commission may charge a renewal fee up to $30. Retailers with an out‑of‑state shipping license are exempt from a specified reporting requirement. Impact on Department of Agriculture: none — no provisions, appropriations, or budget allocations are directed to the Department of Agriculture.
109-1-LB479_IntroLB479_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB479 amends section 77-27,132 to direct that, for transactions occurring on or after July 1, 2023, all proceeds of sales and use taxes imposed under section 77-2703 on the sale or lease of aircraft (per section 3-101) be credited to the Department of Transportation Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund. The bill takes operative effect October 1, 2025, and repeals the original version of section 77-27,132.The underlined additions consist only of the date "October 1, 2025" and the term "one‑half." There are no explicit references to the Department of Transportation, nor any changes to DOT funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in that added text. The language does not specify what "one‑half" applies to.
109-1-LB47_IntroLB47_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Economic Development and assigns it several duties. The department must establish a Small Business Investment Program to award grants to microloan delivery and technical-assistance organizations and innovation hubs, coordinate statewide microlending support, leverage nonstate funds, and may use awards for match requirements, revolving loan funds, or guaranty funds. The department may award up to $3,000,000 annually under that program. Under the Small Business Assistance Act the department must create and administer grant programs (start-up grants up to $25,000; existing small-business grants up to $12,500) and contract with private entities to provide counseling in redevelopment areas and qualified census tracts. The department must submit biennial reports to the Governor and Legislature and may require reporting from contractors and grant recipients.Adds and clarifies definitions and scope for the Department of Economic Development: establishes "economic redevelopment area" (areas with average unemployment ≥150% of the state rate and ≥20% poverty by census tract) and defines "qualified census tract" by cross‑reference to 26 U.S.C. 42(d)(5)(B)(ii)(I) as of Jan 1, 2025. Expands covered parties to include private entities located in those areas and entities with which the department contracts. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB480_IntroLB480_Intro_Copy.docxLB480 amends the Water Recreation Enhancement Act. It broadens legislative findings and authorized projects for Lake McConaughy, the Lewis and Clark State Recreation Area, and Niobrara State Park to include marina construction and other projects that expand water access and recreational opportunities. The bill vests the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission with authority to administer these projects, including entering contracts (construction, management, legal, audit, consulting) and public‑private partnerships, and directs the commission to engage local stakeholders. It encourages political subdivisions holding Federal Energy Regulatory Commission licenses to enter into land use/lease/purchase arrangements (with covenants/easements to ensure FERC compliance). It also bars Game and Parks commissioners and employees (and their immediate family members) from having financial interests in related real‑estate transactions or contracts. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Added language authorizes use of projects to increase recreational opportunities and enjoyment of Niobrara State Park and to fund infrastructure improving access to recreational areas and water access. No specific state agencies or departments are named in the added text, and it does not itself change or specify funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB481_IntroLB481_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and assigns the department these duties: establish the Foster Child Scholarship Program (HOPE Scholarships) beginning in 2025-26; annually notify educational decisionmakers about the program; adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the Act; and electronically submit annual reports (first due December 1, 2026) to the Governor and Legislature detailing number of recipients, total scholarship amounts, and specified demographic data. The Legislature intends to appropriate $200,000 from the General Fund to the department for each of fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27 to carry out the Act.The Department of Health and Human Services (department) must establish the Foster Child Scholarship Program to award HOPE Scholarships beginning 2025–26 for foster children and their biological siblings to attend qualifying private, nonprofit Nebraska schools. The department may adopt rules, must annually notify educational decisionmakers about the program, and shall not gain governance authority over participating schools. Reporting: by Dec. 1, 2026 and annually thereafter the department must electronically report to the Governor and Legislature the number of recipients, total scholarship dollars awarded, and recipient demographics (income, grade, race/ethnicity, geography). The Legislature intends to appropriate $200,000 from the General Fund to the department for each of FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB482_IntroLB482_Intro_Copy.docxLB482 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §44-359 (insurance). It preserves the trial and appellate courts’ authority to award a reasonable attorney fee to a plaintiff who obtains judgment on most insurance-policy or fraternal benefit society claims (fees taxed as costs), but clarifies language regarding the fee being awarded in addition to the plaintiff’s recovery. It adds an express exclusion: the fee rule does not apply when the plaintiff’s claim arises from a post-loss assignment of rights or benefits in a property-damage claim by a property owner. The bill contains no changes to state agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds an exception clarifying that subsection (1) does not apply when a plaintiff's right to sue comes from a post‑loss assignment of rights or benefits tied to a property owner's claim for damage to insured property. No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes.
109-1-LB483_IntroLB483_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesThe bill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-416 to specify that any person convicted of violating the controlled-substances provisions, if sentenced to the Department of Correctional Services, must attend appropriate drug-abuse treatment and counseling while incarcerated. No provisions in the bill reference funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services.No provisions in the added text reference the Department of Correctional Services or change its authorities, operations, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The additions instead: define permissible cannabis products (including a 300 mg delta-9 THC limit and pill/tincture forms), clarify THC and hemp definitions, make the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission members also serve on the Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission, and establish exemptions for conduct or transport lawful under the Nebraska Medical Cannabis Patient Protection Act/Regulation Act. No DOC-specific language or fiscal changes are included.
109-1-LB484_IntroLB484_Intro_Copy.docxLB484 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-1359 (2024 supplement) to revise definitions for “agricultural land and horticultural land,” excluding land associated with a building or enclosed structure and expressly including wasteland in common ownership/management. It expands “agricultural or horticultural purposes” to include land under conservation easements (per the Conservation and Preservation Easements Act) and land enrolled in unspecified federal or state programs that pay for removal from production. The bill also clarifies treatment of platted/subdivided parcels and defines “farm home site” and “farm site.” No state agencies are specifically named and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.The added text simply inserts a numbered subsection “(1) ;” and contains no substantive language. It mentions no government agencies, departments, programs, budget items, appropriations, or funding changes. No fiscal or administrative impact is specified.
