109-1-LB485_IntroLB485_Intro_Copy.docxLB485 requires that personal identifying information of train crew members in reports and in communications with law enforcement arising from railroad fatalities be redacted from public reports and maintained confidentially by law enforcement and others in possession of those records. Unredacted copies may be accessed as needed by: the host or employing railroad; persons with court-ordered authorization; and law enforcement officers, prosecutors, or Public Service Commission staff when necessary for performance of duties. The bill also exempts train crew members from having to display an operator’s license to law enforcement during locomotive or train operations. “Train crew member” is defined to include engineers, conductors, brakemen and other crew operating on rails. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Requires that personal identifying information of train crew members in railroad-fatality reports and related communications be redacted from public reports and kept confidential by law enforcement and others who possess the records. Unredacted copies are accessible to: the host/employing railroad; persons authorized by court order; and law enforcement officers, prosecutors, or Public Service Commission staff when access is necessary to perform their duties. Establishes that a train crew member (engineer, conductor, brakeman, or any other locomotive/train crew member) is not required to display an operator’s license to law enforcement while operating a train in the state. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB486_IntroLB486_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB486 directs the Department of Health and Human Services to implement a standard reimbursement rate for service providers under the Aged and Disabled Personal Care Services waiver. The rate must align with the CBIZ Optumas rate study dated December 7, 2022, and be rebased at least once every two years. The bill does not specify any appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations.DHHS must establish and implement a standard reimbursement rate for providers under the Aged and Disabled Personal Care Services waiver. The rate must align with the CBIZ Optumas rate study dated December 7, 2022, and must be rebased at least every two years. The provision assigns implementation responsibility to the Department; it does not specify any new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB487_IntroLB487_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the Restitution and Redress for Redlining Task Force (seven members: two appointed from the Commission on African American Affairs and others by congressional district) — Governor appointments subject to confirmation by the Legislature's relevant standing committee. The Attorney General must provide administrative, technical, and legal assistance; state agencies and the State Treasurer must cooperate and may furnish confidential information. Task force may hire staff, contract for research, and is entitled to state travel reimbursement. The task force and its Restoration Study Fund terminate November 1, 2028. Fiscal provisions: proceeds of the tax under §77-4303 are redirected to the Restoration Study Fund from enactment until Nov. 1, 2028 and expended by the task force. The Marijuana and Controlled Substances Tax Administration Cash Fund may transfer monies to the Restoration Study Fund until Nov. 1, 2028. After Nov. 1, 2028, tax proceeds distribution resumes: 5% to the administration cash fund; 50% of the remainder to counties (County Drug Law Enforcement and Education Funds); remaining funds to the Nebraska State Patrol Drug Control and Education Cash Fund. Funds are invested by the state investment officer; Tax Commissioner administers the tax.Creates the Restitution and Redress for Redlining Task Force with seven gubernatorial appointees (subject to legislative standing‑committee confirmation) and requires cooperation from state agencies. Agencies/departments specified: Commission on African American Affairs (two members), the Office of the Governor, the Legislature (standing committee), district courts (to compel testimony/subpoenas), all state agencies (must provide information), the Attorney General (administrative/technical/legal assistance), the State Treasurer (custodian of a new Restoration Study Fund), and the State Investment Officer (invests fund assets under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act). Members serve without pay but may receive expense reimbursement per state travel statutes. Funding: establishes the Restoration Study Fund to be credited by legislative transfers, gifts/bequests, and expressly permits transfers from the Marijuana and Controlled Substances Tax Administration Cash Fund; the task force may expend the fund for its work. Task force terminates November 1, 2028.
109-1-LB488_IntroLB488_Intro_Copy.docxLB488 amends criminal and juvenile probation procedures and assigns responsibilities to key agencies: - Office of Probation Administration: authorized to create a statewide graduated‑response matrix, provide implementation and ongoing training to probation officers, and promulgate rules and regulations (including ensuring prompt court review of custodial sanctions). - Probation officers/Chief probation officers: may impose administrative or custodial sanctions, arrest probationers without a warrant when flight risk or danger exists, and take juveniles into temporary custody in similar circumstances. - Peace officers: obligated to assist and assume custody of probationers or juveniles when called by a probation officer. - County attorneys and sentencing/juvenile courts: must be promptly notified via written reports after arrests or detentions and decide whether to file motions to revoke probation or authorize release. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a duty requiring peace officers to arrest and assume custody of a probationer when requested by a probation officer. It also requires peace officers to take juveniles into temporary custody upon a probation officer's request for assistance, referencing subsection (6) of §43‑286.01. No state agencies beyond "peace officer" and "probation officer" are newly created or mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB489_IntroLB489_Intro_Copy.docxLB489 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §70-1012 to limit activity around higher‑voltage electric facilities to entities defined as "electric supplier" in §70-1001.01 and to require board approval before such an electric supplier constructs or acquires electric generation facilities or transmission lines/facilities carrying more than 700 volts. Existing exemptions (intra‑service‑area extensions, limited replacement generation, acquisition of lines ≤115 kV with notice, and qualified facilities) are retained. The bill also states a prohibition on certain (unspecified in the excerpt) entities from operating, maintaining, constructing, or acquiring transmission lines and related facilities. No state agency appropriations or other funding changes are included.Adds the phrase "an electric as defined in section 70-1001.01," i.e., it incorporates the statutory definition found at §70-1001.01. No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.
109-1-LB48A_FinalLB48A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB48A appropriates $1,000,000 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), Program 33, for FY2025‑26 and $1,000,000 for FY2026‑27 to aid in carrying out Legislative Bill 48 (2025). Expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from these appropriated funds are capped at $60,000 for each of FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27.Appropriates $1,000,000 from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund to DHHS (Program 33) for FY2025‑26 and another $1,000,000 for FY2026‑27 to support implementation of Legislative Bill 48 (109th Leg., 1st Sess., 2025). Caps total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems charged to these appropriated funds at $60,000 in each fiscal year.
109-1-LB48_FinalLB48_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) is directed to establish a Family Resource and Juvenile Assessment Center Pilot Program in cities of the metropolitan class. The pilot must operate 24/7, be developed with local grassroots organizations and impacted youth/family advisors, and terminate five years after the act's operative date. DHHS must create the designation process for centers, require comprehensive self-assessments and data systems tied to national standards, and conduct an annual evaluation of program impact on youth, families, community trust, and juvenile justice involvement. Funding: designated centers may receive up to $500,000 annually per center from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund (no General Funds if those funds are unavailable). Up to 10% of program funds, capped at $50,000/year, may be used for administration. The Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund statute is amended to include this pilot program as an authorized use.DHHS must create a Family Resource and Juvenile Assessment Center Pilot Program in metropolitan cities (24/7 operation; terminates five years after the act’s operative date). DHHS will set a designation process with quality standards, require centers to complete self‑assessments (e.g., national Standards of Quality), implement outcome data systems, and provide ongoing post‑service supports (mentoring, check‑ins). Funding: designated centers may receive up to $500,000 per center annually from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund; if those funds are unavailable, General Funds cannot be used. Administrative spending for the pilot is capped at 10% of program funds, up to $50,000 per year. DHHS must perform annual program evaluations to inform future policy.
109-1-LB490_FinalLB490_Final_Copy.docxLB490 amends the Motor Vehicle Certificate of Title Act and assigns operational duties to the Department (motor vehicle authority), county treasurers, and the Director of Motor Vehicles. Key agency actions: the Department must implement and operate an electronic title-and-lien system, prescribe forms and certificate numbering, provide system access to licensed dealers and lienholders, note and cancel liens electronically, and issue titles after lien releases. County treasurers must transmit an electronic copy of issued titles to the Department, maintain indices and seals, notify the Department and first lienholders when liens are noted or cancelled, and may destroy records after five years. The Director sets implementation dates for electronic-title provisions; some title eligibility changes begin Jan. 1, 2026. The bill references existing fees for lien notation but contains no new appropriations or specified funding changes.Adds exclusions and title/lien rules for certain farm equipment: utility trailers; beginning Jan 1, 2026, self‑propelled equipment used exclusively to apply fertilizer/chemicals, floater‑spreader implements, implements of husbandry used mainly for tilling, harvesting or feeding livestock; and, beginning Jan 1, 2026, power‑unit hay grinders or power unit/ grinder combinations when operated without cargo. Confirms that security interests previously perfected under UCC Article 9 retain priority as of their original perfection date. Requires certificate‑of‑title holders to surrender titles to allow lien notation; allows secured parties to obtain a title in the owner’s name and note a lien per sections 60‑144 and 60‑164 if owner fails to obtain title. No agencies or funding/appropriation changes are mentioned.
109-1-LB491_IntroLB491_Intro_Copy.docxLB491 amends §72-819 to direct the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission to award grants to a federally recognized Indian tribe to construct, develop, and manage a Chief Standing Bear museum and visitor center. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate up to $7 million from the Museum Construction and Maintenance Fund in FY2025-26 for construction and up to $7 million in FY2026-27 for exhibit fabrication and historical interpretation for that project. The Commission is also directed to construct and manage a museum at Fort Robinson State Park, with intent to appropriate up to $7 million from the same fund in FY2025-26. The Commission may enter an MOU or contract with the Nebraska State Historical Society for museum development and exhibits. The original section is repealed.Adds a funding cap of "Not more than seven million dollars for fiscal year 2026‑27." No specific government agency or department is named; the provision sets a $7 million maximum appropriation/allocation for FY 2026‑27.
109-1-LB492_IntroLB492_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB492 explicitly references the Department of Health and Human Services in section 43-247(7), confirming juvenile court jurisdiction over any juvenile voluntarily relinquished pursuant to section 43-106.01 to the Department of Health and Human Services or to a child-placement agency licensed by the Department. The bill makes no express changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Health and Human Services.Adds/clarifies that a "habitually truant" child (age 13–16) accrues 20+ unexcused absences with documented loss of educational attainment. Creates a defense to adjudication if, after subtracting excludable absences, the child has fewer than 20 unexcused days. New exclusions: absences caused by lack of adequate transportation; school failure to coordinate agreed interventions/attendance supports; physical or mental illness excused by a parent/guardian (with or without a doctor’s note); or other excusal by the school or court. Referrals must identify which unexcused absences, if any, were excused by a parent/guardian for physical or mental illness. No Department of Health and Human Services funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB493_IntroLB493_Intro_Copy.docxNo state agencies or departments are referenced in LB493, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes. Summary: LB493 adopts the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (an anti‑SLAPP framework). It permits a defendant to file a special motion for expedited dismissal within 60 days of service, stays related proceedings and limits discovery while the motion is pending, requires courts to hear and rule on motions within specified 60‑day deadlines, and grants an appeal as of right from denials. The bill mandates awards of court costs, reasonable attorneys’ fees, and litigation expenses to prevailing moving parties, provides severability, declares an emergency, and outright repeals sections 25‑21,241 through 25‑21,246, R.R.S. Neb.Adds procedural protections under the Uniform Public Expression Protection Act: filing a special motion triggers a stay of proceedings (including discovery and hearings) with limited discovery exceptions and carve-outs for unrelated motions and emergency public‑health/safety injunctions. Courts must hear the motion within 60 days (or later for good cause), and rulings can be appealed as of right within 21 days. The court must dismiss with prejudice if the moving party shows the Act applies and the respondent fails to rebut or to establish a prima facie case; prevailing movants are entitled to court costs, reasonable attorney fees, and litigation expenses. No government agencies, departments, or changes to funding/appropriations/budgets are mentioned.
109-1-LB494_IntroLB494_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesThe bill directs the State Treasurer to transfer $750 million from the General Fund to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund in fiscal year 2024‑25, with the timing and installment amounts to be set by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services.Summary of added provisions (Department of Administrative Services: none specified) - New certification/transfer rule: If one-year/ two-year revenue calculations meet specified positive/negative conditions, the Tax Commissioner must certify a calculated positive amount to the State Treasurer, who will transfer that amount to the Cash Reserve Fund. - Property tax relief funding (effective FY2025-26): The Legislature intends that the General Fund will transfer whatever amount is necessary to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund to provide the property tax credits required by section 77-7305. Credits will appear on property tax statements and offset school district taxes. The total relief equals a defined minimum amount, plus any additional transfers to the fund made under section 77-4602 for that tax year. No language in the added text references the Department of Administrative Services or directs any appropriations or budget changes to that agency.
109-1-LB495_IntroLB495_Intro_Copy.docxLB495 amends the Property Tax Request Act (Neb. Rev. Stat. §§77‑1632 and 77‑1633). It narrows the scope of the special joint‑hearing and expanded notice procedures in §77‑1633 to "county, city, or school district," removing community colleges from that definition. As a result, county clerks, county assessors, county boards, and participating political subdivisions (counties, cities, school districts, learning communities, sanitary and improvement districts, natural resources districts, and educational service units) will still follow §77‑1633 joint public‑hearing, postcard‑mailing, website‑posting, cost‑allocation, and reporting duties, but those requirements no longer apply to community colleges, which remain subject to the standard §77‑1632 hearing/notice process. The bill contains an emergency clause and takes effect on enactment. No changes to appropriations or funding allocations are made.The added text consists only of the repeated conjunction “or.” It mentions no government agencies or departments and makes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. There is therefore no substantive policy or fiscal impact to summarize.
109-1-LB496_IntroLB496_Intro_Copy.docxAmends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-6,111 to clarify roadway rules for animals and livestock. Riders/drivers of animals, animal-drawn vehicles, farm tractors, and implements of husbandry retain the rights and duties of vehicle drivers and must, when obstructing traffic, pull to the nearest shoulder. Defines "livestock" (horse, mule, donkey, cattle, swine, sheep, goat) and imposes four duties on motorists encountering persons leading/herding livestock: use caution when approaching/passing, promptly stop if given a distress signal (unless stopping would cause an accident), turn off the engine if requested, and yield the right of way to the livestock. Repeals the original section. No state agencies or departments are named, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a new subsection defining "livestock" (horse, mule, donkey, cattle, swine, sheep, goat) and imposes duties on drivers encountering people leading/herding livestock on highways: exercise caution when approaching/passing; stop if given a distress signal (unless moving is necessary to avoid an accident); turn off the engine if requested; and yield the right of way to livestock. No government agencies, departments, or changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are referenced.
109-1-LB497_IntroLB497_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB497 references the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) in residency and payment provisions for students placed outside their home district. Key DHHS-specific items: - If a ward is placed outside his/her resident district and does not reside in a foster family home licensed or approved by DHHS, the state shall pay the student's education and required transportation costs to the receiving district or approved institution "under rules and regulations prescribed by the Department of Health and Human Services" (payments not in advance). - A ward who resides in a foster family home licensed or approved by DHHS is generally deemed a resident of the district where they resided when becoming a foster child, unless §§43-1311/1312 dictate otherwise. - Residential settings operated by providers certified or licensed by DHHS are addressed for residency determinations. No direct DHHS appropriations or new budget allocations are specified in the bill.Added language requires a school board to admit, without charge, a student who is enrolled in a private, denominational, parochial, or a school that has opted out of accreditation, for part‑time enrollment solely to participate in extracurricular activities per §79‑2,136, when the student’s resident district does not offer the activity and the admitting district is the closest that does. There are no references to the Department of Health and Human Services, nor any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for that agency.
109-1-LB498_IntroLB498_Intro_Copy.docxCreates timing and funding rules administered by the state education department and other state fiscal offices under the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act. Key agency actions and budget changes: - Department (state education department) must certify foundation aid amounts and district budget authority on or before June 15, 2025, and March 1 each year thereafter, and report necessary funding levels to the Governor, the Appropriations Committee, and the Education Committee; certifications are sent to the Director of Administrative Services, the Auditor of Public Accounts, and local systems. - Foundation aid: $1,500 per formula student for FY2023-24 and FY2024-25; from FY2025-26 forward the per-student amount is indexed annually by CPI‑U. 24% of total foundation aid is paid from the Education Future Fund. - Treatment: certified state aid shown as budgeted non‑property‑tax receipts and deducted before calculating local property tax requests; aid distributed in ten monthly payments (Sept–June), with small payments lumped in December. - Any certifications for FY2025-26 completed prior to the act’s effective date are null and void. - Appropriations Committee must include the amount necessary to fund the certified state aid in its budget recommendations. - Emergency clause: effective on passage.Adds a formula for foundation aid beginning in school fiscal year 2025‑26: each district's aid equals the prior year’s foundation aid per formula student, increased by the percent change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI‑U) for the previous calendar year as published by the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics, multiplied by the district’s number of formula students. No specific appropriation amounts are set; the change ties future state payments to the BLS CPI‑U.
109-1-LB499_FinalLB499_Final_Copy.docxLB499 amends statutes governing the Crime Victim’s Reparations Committee (Reissue Revised Statutes §§81-1802 to 81-1804). Key changes: public members’ terms now begin October 1; to establish staggered service, one of the two public members appointed under subdivision (2)(b)(i) and one of the two appointed under subdivision (2)(b)(ii) will serve initial two-year terms, with all subsequent terms being four years; vacancies are filled for the remainder of the term; and members whose terms have expired may continue to serve until a successor is appointed. The bill repeals the original sections. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds that each public member’s term begins October 1. It specifies that one of the two public members appointed under subdivision (2)(b)(i) of section 81-1802 and one of the two appointed under subdivision (2)(b)(ii) of section 81-1802 will serve initial two‑year terms; thereafter members serve four‑year terms. No state agencies or departments are newly created or mentioned beyond the cross‑reference to section 81‑1802, and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB49_IntroLB49_Intro_Copy.docxLB49 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-405 to clarify limits on school districts’ authority to restrict access to school property and activities. It defines “ban and bar action” and provides that such actions may be enforced as criminal trespass under §§28-520 to 28-522. The State Board of Education is directed to develop and distribute a model ban-and-bar policy by January 1, 2026. The policy must require that bans and bars be used only for immediate, significant threats to safety or to enforce court orders and that actions be limited in scope. The bill affects school districts and school boards; no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Requires the State Board of Education to develop and distribute a model "ban and bar" policy by January 1, 2026. The addition defines "ban and bar action," "Board," "school board," and "school district," and says school districts' authority to restrict access is subject to the act's limitations. The model policy must limit bans/bars to responses to an immediate, significant threat to people or to facilitate enforcement of a court order and must limit their scope. It also notes such actions may be enforced under criminal trespass statutes (sections 28-520 to 28-522). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB4_IntroLB4_Intro_Copy.docxLB4 amends state telecom law to add and clarify the Public Service Commission's (PSC) jurisdiction over the new Telecommunications Exchange Deregulation Act. The PSC may require carrier disclosures, protect claimed confidential proprietary data, adopt rules, and must decide petitions to deregulate an exchange within 90 days. Only an electing local exchange carrier may petition; deregulation criteria use U.S. Census population data (U.S. Bureau of the Census) or presence/coverage of competing voice-service carriers. Deregulated carriers are relieved of carrier-of-last-resort, quality-reporting, and most pricing obligations. Transitioning carriers lose eligibility for Nebraska Telecommunications Universal Service Fund support for deregulated exchanges, and the PSC must, where feasible, reduce their fund allocations accordingly. The bill also repeals and replaces the prior sections it amends.Summary: The bill empowers the state "commission" (the telecommunications regulator) to require carrier disclosures, protect proprietary information under section 84-712.05, adopt rules, and decide exchange deregulation (final order within 90 days). It directs the commission to use the most recent U.S. Bureau of the Census data for population determinations. Financially, transitioning carriers lose eligibility for Nebraska Telecommunications Universal Service Fund support for deregulated exchanges, and the commission must, insofar as the funding formula permits, reduce those carriers' fund allocations to account for deregulated exchanges. The commission also may reclassify carriers and oversee discontinuance and related proceedings.
109-1-LB500_IntroLB500_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the 21‑member School Financing Review Commission. Statutory members include the Commissioner of Education (or designee), the Property Tax Administrator (or designee), a gubernatorial appointee, three nonvoting legislative members (including members of the Education and Revenue Committees), a postsecondary education representative, a member of the Educational Service Unit Coordinating Council, multiple school board members and administrators from Class III–V districts, a certificated teacher, and six at‑large members. The commission must deliver a final report to the Governor, the State Board of Education, and the Legislature by December 1, 2025; thereafter it will review state education mission goals, the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act implementation, and issue adequacy-of-funding reports biennially (every even‑numbered year July 1, 2028–2034). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified. The act takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.Creates a 21‑member School Financing Review Commission including: the Commissioner of Education (or designee), a Governor appointee, three nonvoting legislative members (including members of the Education and Revenue Committees), the Property Tax Administrator (or designee), a postsecondary finance expert, an Educational Service Unit Coordinating Council member, specified school board members and administrators from Class III–V districts, a certificated teacher, six at‑large members, and others. The commission must submit a final report to the Governor, State Board of Education, and Legislature by December 1, 2025; thereafter it will biennially (July 1, even years 2028–2034) report on adequacy of school funding. Duties include reviewing State Department of Education goals and implementation of the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB501_FinalLB501_Final_Copy.docxLB501 amends procedures and deadlines for assessing real property that suffers "significant property damage." Key government actors and changes: - Property owners must report damaged property to the county clerk by July 15; Tax Commissioner prescribes the form. - County assessors must inspect reported properties and submit a report to the county board of equalization by July 20. - County boards of equalization adjust assessed value to the value at the time of damage, may meet June 1–July 25 (or to Aug 10 with an extension), and must notify owners; protests may be filed with the board (30 days) and appealed to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission (30 days). - Mobile homes moved under §77-3708 with accelerated tax may seek refunds under §77-1734.01 for reductions ordered by the county board. - Assessors, sheriffs, constables, city council members, and village trustees must notify county treasurers of removals/demolitions; county treasurers are excepted from immediate tax collection/distress for damaged property. - Emergency effective date. No funding or appropriation changes.Adds requirements for the county assessor to inspect and review all properties for which owners file reports under this section and to submit a comprehensive report to the county board of equalization by July 20 of the current assessment year. The report must use a form prescribed by the Tax Commissioner and include all such property-owner reports. No agencies beyond the county assessor, county board of equalization, and the Tax Commissioner are mentioned, and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB502_IntroLB502_Intro_Copy.docxLB502 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-1714 (Farm Labor Contractors Act) to clarify criminal penalties: violations of §48-1711 or §48-1712 are Class II misdemeanors; intentional defacement, use, permitting use, or acting without a farm labor contractor license is a Class II misdemeanor; and a seed corn producer or farm labor contractor who violates §48-1715 is guilty of a Class IV misdemeanor. The bill repeals the original section. No state agency or department is named in the bill text, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a criminal penalty: any seed corn producer or farm labor contractor who violates section 48-1715 is guilty of a Class IV misdemeanor. No government agencies or departments are referenced and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB503_IntroLB503_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Revenue- "Department" is defined as the Department of Revenue. - The Department of Revenue receives county applications for "American energy friendly" designation, must act within 30 days to grant designation, and maintain an up-to-date list of applicant/designated counties on its website. The department may adopt rules to implement these provisions. - The department is directed to collect the nameplate capacity tax, enforce this tax statute, and may promulgate necessary rules and regulations. - Owners must file annual nameplate capacity reports with the Department by March 1; taxes are due April 1 and paid quarterly. - The department will prorate any increased nameplate capacity tax based on the number of days it designated a county as American energy friendly in a year. - The Department must separately identify tax proceeds and remit them to the county treasurer within 30 days of receipt.The added text defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns these responsibilities to it: receive county applications for "American energy friendly county" designation; decide and notify counties within 30 days if statutory requirements are met; maintain an up‑to‑date list on its website of counties that have applied/been designated; adopt rules and regulations to implement the program; and apply a proration rule for the increased nameplate‑capacity tax in the first year a county gains or loses designation (tax increase prorated to days designated). No new appropriations, funding lines, or budget allocations for the Department are specified.
109-1-LB504A_IntroLB504A_Intro_Copy.docxAppropriates state General Fund dollars to the Nebraska Attorney General, Program 507, to implement Legislative Bill 504. Amounts: $72,149 for FY2025‑26 and $147,752 for FY2026‑27. Includes spending caps on permanent and temporary salaries and per diems drawn from these appropriations: maximum $50,000 in FY2025‑26 and $103,000 in FY2026‑27. Funds are explicitly designated to aid the Attorney General in carrying out LB504.Appropriates General Fund amounts to the Nebraska Attorney General (Program 507) to implement Legislative Bill 504: $72,149 for FY2025‑26 and $147,752 for FY2026‑27. Limits total expenditures from these appropriations for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems to no more than $50,000 in FY2025‑26 and $103,000 in FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB504_FinalLB504_Final_Copy.docxThis bill creates the Age-Appropriate Online Design Code Act. State enforcement: the Nebraska Attorney General may pursue civil penalties (up to $50,000 per violation) beginning July 1, 2026; collected penalties are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution. Federal and state references: the bill relies on Federal Trade Commission guidance to define “dark patterns,” uses Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI data to adjust revenue thresholds biennially, and exempts data subject to federal regimes (GLBA Title V, HITECH, HIPAA section 264 regulations) and certain clinical-trial protections (including FDA requirements). Government entities (federal, state, tribal, local) are excluded from the Act. The Act is operative January 1, 2026.Adds references to federal and state agencies: Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI used to adjust the $25 million revenue threshold); Federal Trade Commission (FTC) — its determinations of "dark patterns" as of Jan 1, 2024 apply and COPPA/FTC rules are incorporated; federal statutes/regulators (GLBA Title V, HITECH, HIPAA regulations) exempt certain data; Food and Drug Administration and International Council for Harmonisation standards govern clinical trial data exemptions. State enforcement: Nebraska Attorney General may bring actions (but not seek civil penalties under the act until July 1, 2026). Civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Nebraska's Constitution.
109-1-LB505_IntroLB505_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill expresses legislative intent to appropriate $10,000,000 in FY2025‑26 and $10,000,000 in FY2026‑27 (Federal Funds) to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program No. 347 (Public Assistance). The appropriation is to include funds from the federal Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program for grants to nonprofit organizations that (1) provide food assistance, (2) distribute food in ten or more Nebraska counties, and (3) qualify for the Emergency Food Assistance Program administered by the United States Department of Agriculture. The act takes effect immediately upon passage due to an emergency clause.DHHS — Program No. 347 (Public Assistance) receives an intent appropriation of $10,000,000 in Federal Funds for FY2025‑26 and $10,000,000 for FY2026‑27. The appropriation is from the federal TANF block grant and is to be used for grants to nonprofit organizations that (1) provide food assistance, (2) distribute food in ten or more Nebraska counties, and (3) are eligible for the Emergency Food Assistance Program (TEFAP). Department of Agriculture — no direct state budget/appropriation changes; the bill only references the federal USDA‑administered TEFAP as an eligibility criterion for grant recipients.
109-1-LB506_IntroLB506_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the Landlord and Tenant Radon Awareness Act requiring lessors to provide prospective tenants and tenants with radon information and a specified disclosure form. Defines "radon measurement specialist" and "radon mitigation specialist" as individuals licensed under the Radiation Control Act. "Lessor" expressly may include a government agency or subdivision. The State of Nebraska is referenced as strongly recommending radon testing and mitigation. Security deposits may not be withheld to pay for radon testing or mitigation, except where a tenant installed an uncertified mitigation system without the lessor's consent. Applies to leases entered on or after the act's effective date. No funding, appropriations, or new agency creation are included.Adds the "Landlord and Tenant Radon Awareness Act," defining terms (dwelling unit, lease, lessor, mitigation, radon, radon hazard defined as ≥4 pCi/L, radon measurement specialist, radon mitigation specialist, tenant). Requires lessors to provide a specified radon-disclosure form to prospective and current tenants (at application and upon request) and to provide radon test results within ten days of receipt. Notes radon measurement/mitigation specialists must be licensed under the Radiation Control Act. The lessor definition explicitly includes "government agency, or subdivision thereof," and the State of Nebraska is cited as recommending testing/mitigation. Prohibits withholding security deposits to pay for radon testing/mitigation except where a tenant improperly installed an unapproved mitigation system; requires itemized statements if withholding occurs. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB507_IntroLB507_Intro_Copy.docxLB507 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-1129 to specify services resident school districts must provide for children with disabilities. Responsibilities fall to the school board and include: reimbursing parents/guardians for transportation at the mileage rate in §81-1176 (for actual miles; when one parent transports multiple eligible children payment is based on one child; no payment for untraveled miles); providing transportation when a child must attend an out-of‑district facility or requires special transportation; supplying certified visiting teachers for homebound children; and offering correspondence or other instructional methods approved by the Commissioner of Education. The nonresident school district may provide transportation by mutual agreement with the district of residence. The bill references reimbursement tied to the statutory mileage rate but contains no separate appropriations or new funding allocations.The added phrase "enrolled in the school district" simply qualifies the subject (likely students) as being members of a local school district. It names no state or federal agencies or departments and includes no language changing funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. No fiscal or administrative agency assignments are specified.
109-1-LB508_IntroLB508_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §55-117 and affects the Nebraska National Guard, the Governor, the Adjutant General, and local police authorities. It (1) limits ordering the Nebraska National Guard into active combat for federal service to instances when the U.S. Congress has declared war or has lawfully called forth the Guard under the U.S. Constitution; (2) requires the Governor to review all current federal orders placing Guard members into active combat for compliance and, if noncompliant, to take action to immediately return those members to Nebraska; (3) requires the Governor to report findings and actions to the Legislature’s Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee within 30 days of completing the review; and (4) defines "active combat." No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds limits and procedural duties concerning the Nebraska National Guard and federal activation. Key agencies mentioned: the Nebraska National Guard, the Governor, the United States Congress, and the Legislature's Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee. New provisions: the Guard may not be ordered into "active combat" unless Congress has declared war or cited the Guard to execute federal laws, suppress insurrection, or repel invasions per the U.S. Constitution. The Governor must review all current federal orders placing Guard members into active combat, return any members if an order is noncompliant, and report the review and actions to the Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee within 30 days of completing the review. "Active combat" is defined in three parts. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB509_IntroLB509_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Revenue- The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Revenue. - The Department of Revenue is authorized to certify and revoke certification of scholarship-granting organizations under the Opportunity Scholarships Act and to receive required notifications from those organizations. - Scholarship-granting organizations must notify the Department of intended tax-credit amounts; the Department must determine within 30 days whether the intended amount exceeds the annual credit limit and inform the organization (and thus the donor) of availability. If a contribution is not received in the required window, the Department will remove that amount from its calculations. - The Department will process notifications in receipt order against annual tax-credit limits (initially $25 million for 2025–2027, adjustable thereafter up to $100 million under specified rules). - The Department of Revenue may recapture a specified housing purchase tax credit if eligibility conditions are not met.Creates the Opportunity Scholarships Act and designates the "Department" as the Department of Revenue. The Department of Revenue must certify and may revoke certification of scholarship‑granting organizations, process organizations' notifications of intended donor tax credits, notify organizations within 30 days if intended credits would exceed availability, and track/remove notified amounts when contributions are not received. The Act establishes nonrefundable Nebraska income tax credits (individuals, pass‑throughs, corporations, estates/trusts) with per‑taxpayer caps (generally the lesser of contribution, 50% of tax liability, or $100,000; estates/trusts $1,000,000) and five‑year carryforward. It sets an aggregate annual credit cap: $25 million (2025–27) with formulaic growth to a $100 million max. No explicit appropriations or new Department budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB50_FinalLB50_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB50 amends section 77-6204 to require the county treasurer to distribute all revenue received from the Department of Revenue (pursuant to §77-6203) as follows: 5% to the community college area where the renewable energy facility is located; the remainder to local taxing entities that would have otherwise received personal property tax revenue from depreciable personal property used directly to generate electricity from wind, solar, biomass, or landfill gas. The bill also explicitly prohibits the Department of Revenue from retaining any revenue collected under sections 77-6201 to 77-6204 for distribution, use, transfer, pledge, or allocation to or from the General Fund.Adds a 5% carve‑out of specified renewable energy generation facility revenue to the community college area where the facility is located, with the remainder to be distributed pursuant to the existing subdivision (1)(b) scheme. For the Department of Revenue, this is an allocation change in revenue distribution responsibilities—no new appropriation or separate funding line is created. The net effect is that other recipients under subdivision (1)(b) will receive slightly less overall funding because 5% is redirected to the local community college area.
109-1-LB510_IntroLB510_Intro_Copy.docxLB510 amends revenue statutes governing Good Life Transformational Projects and Good Life Districts. Key agency roles and changes: - "The department" (statutory reviewing authority under these chapters) retains sole authority to approve, modify boundaries, transmit application materials to affected cities/villages, hold hearings, adopt commercially reasonable development/design standards, and terminate districts only under specific investment‑commitment thresholds and not before three years. - Cities/villages may become applicants, must approve boundary removals/standards in certain cases, and must obtain voter approval before appropriating local revenue to a Good Life District program. - Nebraska State Fair Board facilities are excepted from gaming exclusions. - Fiscal changes: state sales tax reductions for transactions in Good Life Districts are limited to portions within municipal corporate limits and, beginning July 1, 2025, apply only after the city/village has imposed at least a 2.75% local sales or occupation tax. Applicants must certify that any diverted state sales tax will be offset or exceeded by new sales tax on development. Emergency clause makes law effective on passage.Beginning July 1, 2025, state sales tax treatment for Good Life Districts changes: the state rate (per §77-2703) becomes 5.5% generally, but transactions within the portion of a Good Life District inside a city or village are taxed at 2.75% — only after that city/village imposes a local sales or occupation tax of at least 2.75%. Transactions in Good Life Districts will be subject to the reduced state rate referenced in §77-2701.02(7). The bill directs "the department" to accept evidence from property owners or cities and to deem such parties the official Good Life District applicant for all related statutes, and prohibits the department from terminating a Good Life District within three years of its establishment. Cities or villages are prohibited from using eminent domain to acquire district property for transfer or sale to private parties. No explicit appropriations or other budget line-item funding changes are specified.
109-1-LB511_IntroLB511_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor VehiclesThe bill directs DHHS to lead education, awareness, and outreach campaigns addressing healthy families, pornography, and prostitution, and explicitly enumerates DHHS employees among protected persons in expanded racketeering-related assault offenses. DHHS must also execute affiliation agreements with "qualified third parties" that provide services to domestic violence and sexual assault victims under the Protection from Domestic Abuse Act. The Department of Correctional Services must provide persons committed for registrable offenses written Sex Offender Registration Act notice before release, obtain a signed copy, retain it, and forward a copy to the registrant and the Nebraska State Patrol registration division. The DMV must (1) be queried for title and lien information when vehicles subject to forfeiture are seized and (2) include written Sex Offender Registration Act notice on operator and commercial license applications. No specific appropriations or budget allocations for these agencies are identified.Summary of added provisions affecting specified agencies: - Department of Correctional Services: New duty to provide written notification to persons required to register under the Sex Offender Registration Act—require the person to read and sign the form, retain a signed copy, and provide copies to the registrant and the Sex Offender Registration and Community Notification Division of the Nebraska State Patrol. - Department of Health and Human Services: No substantive additions or funding changes affecting DHHS in the added text. - Department of Motor Vehicles: No substantive additions or funding changes affecting DMV in the added text. - Funding/appropriations: Legislature intends to appropriate $100,000 (General Fund) for FY2025-26 to the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice for grants to law enforcement and $25,000 (General Fund) for FY2025-26 to the Nebraska State Patrol to implement sex-offender registration changes.
109-1-LB512_IntroLB512_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB512 defines "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services and assigns the department responsibility for collecting reports on provision of abortion‑inducing drugs. Physicians must file a report with the department within 30 days after the end of the calendar month in which the drug was provided. The department must produce a standard reporting form. Required report fields include physician name; drug name and dates; follow‑up visit date; documentation of adverse events; follow‑up treatment; and referral purpose. Reports must exclude personally identifying information. The bill contains no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations for the department.The added Chemical Abortion Safety Protocol Act requires physicians to file de-identified reports with the Department of Health and Human Services within 30 days after the end of the month in which an abortion-inducing drug was provided. Reports must use a department-produced standard form and include the physician’s name, drug(s) and dates, follow-up visit date (follow-up required 3–14 days post‑provision), documented adverse events, any follow‑up treatment, and referral purpose. The department may adopt rules/regulations specifying additional required information. Reports must exclude personally identifying patient information. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB513A_FinalLB513A_Final_Copy.docxThis bill appropriates funds to multiple state judicial and administrative agencies to implement LB513, and takes effect immediately due to an emergency clause. - Supreme Court: - Program 3: $26,838 (FY2025‑26); $53,775 (FY2026‑27). Salary/per diem caps: $23,631 and $47,616. - Program 4: $21,976; $44,023. Caps: $19,242 and $38,774. - Program 6: $250,398; $501,519. Caps: $218,585 and $440,449. - Program 7: $205,999; $412,530. Caps: $179,257 and $361,202. (All Supreme Court amounts from the General Fund.) - Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Court (Program 526): $21,574 (FY25‑26) and $43,211 (FY26‑27) from the Compensation Court Cash Fund; caps $18,736 and $37,753. - Tax Equalization and Review Commission (Program 131): $12,051 and $24,283 from the General Fund; caps $10,465 and $21,087.Appropriates funds to implement Legislative Bill 513 (109th Leg., 1st Sess., 2025): - Supreme Court — Program 3: $26,838 (FY2025‑26) and $53,775 (FY2026‑27) from the General Fund; salary/per diem caps $23,631 and $47,616. - Supreme Court — Program 4: $21,976 (FY2025‑26) and $44,023 (FY2026‑27) from the General Fund; salary/per diem caps $19,242 and $38,774. - Supreme Court — Program 6: $250,398 (FY2025‑26) and $501,519 (FY2026‑27) from the General Fund; salary/per diem caps $218,585 and $440,449. - Supreme Court — Program 7: $205,999 (FY2025‑26) and $412,530 (FY2026‑27) from the General Fund; salary/per diem caps $179,257 and $361,202. - Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Court — Program 526: $21,574 (FY2025‑26) and $43,211 (FY2026‑27) from the Compensation Court Cash Fund; salary/per diem caps $18,736 and $37,753. - Tax Equalization and Review Commission — Program 131: $12,051 (FY2025‑26) and $24,283 (FY2026‑27) from the General Fund; salary/per diem caps $10,465 and $21,087.
109-1-LB513_FinalLB513_Final_Copy.docxBill LB513 raises statutory salaries for the Nebraska Supreme Court's Chief Justice and associate justices. It sets salaries at $225,055.35 (effective July 1, 2024), $228,431.18 (effective July 1, 2025) and $231,857.65 (effective July 1, 2026). Salaries are payable in equal monthly installments. The bill reiterates that the Chief Justice and Supreme Court judges may not hold any other compensated public office or accept compensated federal appointments during their terms. The bill repeals the prior version of section 24-201.01, designates July 1, 2025 as the operative date, and includes an emergency clause making the act effective upon passage and approval. No separate appropriation language is provided.Sets the annual salary for the Chief Justice and all Supreme Court judges at $228,431.18 effective July 1, 2025, and $231,857.65 effective July 1, 2026. This is a scheduled judicial pay increase (a $3,426.47 rise, about 1.5%), impacting the state judiciary’s payroll and likely increasing related appropriations in the Supreme Court/judiciary budget.
109-1-LB514_IntroLB514_Intro_Copy.docxLB514 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §14-102 to expressly authorize cities of the metropolitan class, by ordinance, to regulate housing authorities. New municipal powers include requiring code enforcement and pest control on housing authority–owned/controlled properties; regular inspections; mandatory registration of housing authority-managed units under any city rental-registration ordinance; establishment of penalties for code or management failures; and monthly reporting from the housing authority to the city council. The bill repeals the original section. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds authority for a metropolitan-class city to regulate its housing authority. Requirements include: city code enforcement and pest control for all housing-authority‑owned/controlled properties; regular inspections of all managed properties; mandatory registration under the city's rental registration ordinance; penalties for code violations and mismanagement; and monthly updates to the city council. Government entities referenced: the housing authority, the metropolitan-class city (and its code enforcement function), and the city council. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB515_IntroLB515_Intro_Copy.docxLB515 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §38‑28,104 (Pharmacy Practice Act). It specifies required information on non‑controlled (legend) drug prescriptions before dispensing (patient identifier or “for emergency use”/“for use in immunizations,” drug name, strength, dosage form, quantity, authorized refills, directions, date, prescriber's name, and written signature if applicable). It also allows pharmacists to provide an emergency refill (up to a 30‑day supply or the most recent refill amount, whichever is less) when refill authorization cannot be obtained, provided: (1) the pharmacist documents the prescription from a label, pharmacy record, or common database; (2) the drug is not a controlled substance; (3) it is a maintenance medication; and (4) interruption of therapy would harm the patient. No state agencies or appropriations are named or altered.Adds authority for pharmacists, when unable to promptly obtain refill authorization from the prescriber, to dispense an emergency refill up to a 30‑day supply (or the amount of the most recent refill, if less) provided they: obtain prescription information from a prescription label, any pharmacy’s prescription record, or a common database; the drug is not a controlled substance; the drug is a maintenance medication; and, in the pharmacist’s professional judgment, interruption of therapy would be harmful. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB516_IntroLB516_Intro_Copy.docxLB516 directs the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) statutory framework be amended by outright repeal of sections 68-130 and 81-1139.01, Reissue Revised Statutes of Nebraska. The bill removes a statutory requirement tied to counties to provide office space for DHHS and eliminates those identified obsolete provisions. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included or changed in the bill.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB517_IntroLB517_Intro_Copy.docxLB517 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-2,144 to expand duties and reporting requirements tied to the State School Security Director (appointed under §79-2,143) and the State Department of Education. School districts must provide the director with accreditation-related safety/security plans, annual inspection information for protective door assemblies, door-locking systems, and double-entry doors, and any other security information requested (subject to withholding under §84-712.05(9)). The director will set minimum standards (to the State Board of Education), establish protective-door-assembly standards requiring annual inspections by qualified inspectors, conduct statewide school-security assessments, oversee behavioral/mental-health training per §79-2,146, and administer the School Safety and Security Reporting System Act. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a requirement that school districts/school boards maintain annual inspection information for protective door assemblies, door‑locking systems, and double‑entry doors, and establishes standards requiring each school board to cause annual inspections of applicable protective door assemblies by a trained inspector with appropriate knowledge/training/experience in door assemblies and building security. Defines "protective door assemblies" to include doors with panic or fire‑exit hardware; door assemblies in exit enclosures; electronically controlled egress doors; and doors with special locking arrangements (e.g., delayed‑egress, sensor‑released, elevator‑lobby). No state agency or funding/appropriation changes are specified.
109-1-LB518_IntroLB518_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB518 amends section 83-1,100.03 and requires the Department of Correctional Services to consult with the Board of Parole in adopting rules to reduce inmates who serve full sentences and are released without supervision. The department must provide a validated risk-and-needs assessment used in parole decisions and help ensure parolees receive a minimum of nine months of supervision. The bill also requires the department and the board to jointly submit an annual electronic report (due February 1) to the Legislature, Supreme Court, and Governor documenting: the percentage of department inmates released without supervision; characteristics of those released (felony class, offense type, most recent risk assessment, reentry-plan status, reasons for release); and department/board recommendations to reduce such releases. No funding or appropriation changes are included.The added text requires that the specified report be submitted electronically and sets out three required components—"(a) Describe," "(b) Document," and "(c) Provide"—though the excerpt does not include the substantive content of those items. There is no reference in the provided underlined language to the Department of Correctional Services, nor any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB519_FinalLB519_Final_Copy.docxLB519 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §83-4,114.02 to require the Nebraska Department of Correctional Services to provide independent confirmatory testing, upon inmate request, before imposing disciplinary measures for drug or alcohol violations. The requirement covers positive urinalysis results and any positive screening, field, presumptive, or spot test of items suspected of being or containing contraband drugs. If the confirmatory test remains positive, the inmate must pay the cost of that test. The bill repeals the original section. No new appropriations are included; cost recovery is imposed on inmates when confirmation is positive.The added language (subsection (1)(a)–(b)) expressly includes “urinalysis” and “any screening test, field test, presumptive test, or spot test of an item suspected of being or containing a contraband drug.” No government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes in the excerpt.
109-1-LB51_FinalLB51_Final_Copy.docxLB51 ratifies and adopts the National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact (34 U.S.C. 40316) to enable authorized interstate exchange of criminal history record information for noncriminal-justice purposes. The bill designates the Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety to execute the compact for Nebraska and names the superintendent (or a designee) as the state's compact officer responsible for administering the compact. The Nebraska State Patrol is designated the state repository for criminal history record information, charged with carrying out compact duties and authorized to adopt rules, regulations, and procedures for cooperative exchange with federal authorities. The compact remains effective until specifically renounced by statute and does not alter existing Nebraska obligations under state law (including the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act). No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds state approval and ratification of the National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact (34 U.S.C. 40316). The Superintendent of Law Enforcement and Public Safety must execute the compact and (or the superintendent’s designee) serves as Nebraska’s compact officer to administer it. The Nebraska State Patrol is designated as the state repository for criminal history record information, authorized to take necessary actions, adopt rules and procedures, and coordinate criminal-history exchanges with the federal government for noncriminal-justice purposes. Ratification remains effective until explicitly renounced by statute. The provision preserves existing Nebraska State Patrol duties under state law (including the Security, Privacy, and Dissemination of Criminal History Information Act) and does not change public access rules. No funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB520_IntroLB520_Intro_Copy.docxLB520 amends provisions affecting bed and breakfast establishments and assigns duties to state agencies. The State Fire Marshal must incorporate bed-and-breakfast-specific provisions into the State Fire Code, review plans, enforce the Code via inspections and orders, and apply existing plan‑review fee authority. The bill requires the (state) department that administers the Nebraska Pure Food Act to offer a food‑handling certification exam and to enforce food safety requirements for bed and breakfasts (storage, temperatures, prohibitions, sanitation, etc.). New fire‑safety mandates include smoke/heat alarms, emergency lighting, egress requirements (or sprinklers), extinguishers, and kitchen fire suppression for larger operations; establishments have 18 months to add a secondary egress or a sprinkler system. No changes to state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a definition of "bed and breakfast" and extensive health and safety requirements. It repeatedly assigns roles to "the department" (unnamed): approving alternative thawing methods, prescribing food-safety standards (temperatures, storage, prohibited home-canned goods, use of pasteurized Grade A milk), offering and administering the food-handler certification exam, and requiring certification for operators. Fire/safety rules require smoke/heat detectors, emergency lighting, primary and secondary egress (with exemptions if sprinklered), an 18‑month compliance window to add egress or sprinklers, specified fire extinguishers, and commercial kitchen fire-suppression hoods for B&Bs serving hot meals to more than ten guests. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB521_FinalLB521_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Motor VehiclesThe bill directs the Secretary of State and the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to enter an agreement to match the statewide voter registration list with DMV records to verify applicant information, including citizenship. Under the agreement the DMV must: enter a Social Security Administration agreement per 42 U.S.C. 405(r)(8); provide a combined voter-registration application for issuance/renewal of operator’s licenses and state ID cards; electronically transmit registration data (including digital image and signature) to county election officials; and notify election officials when a registrant surrenders a Nebraska license/ID to another state for cancellation. The Secretary of State may contract with the Department of Administrative Services for storage and distribution of printed election forms. No appropriations or budget changes for either agency are specified.No underlined additions specifically name or change responsibilities, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Administrative Services or the Department of Motor Vehicles. Relevant additions: - The Secretary of State may purchase/lease/contract for petition-processing software (not for signature verification) — no DAS procurement or appropriation language included. - New or clarified election procedures require verification of voter photographic identification for early voting and other ballot-verification steps (photographic ID referenced), which may indirectly involve DMV-issued IDs but imposes no new DMV duties or funding. In short: no direct statutory or budgetary impacts on DAS or DMV in the added text.
109-1-LB522_IntroLB522_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB522 adds annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLA) to Nebraska workers’ compensation weekly income benefits lasting longer than 12 months (amending sections 48-121 and 48-122.01), effective beginning 2026. The COLA percentage is defined as the greater of 1% or the twelve‑month percent change in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers as prepared by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics. The Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Court determines the applicable COLA each January 1 and automatically applies the adjustment every twelve months. The bill contains no appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations.Adds automatic cost-of-living adjustments (COLA) to weekly workers’ compensation income benefits that continue beyond 12 months, effective Jan 1, 2026. COLA each year = greater of 1% or the 12‑month change in the CPI‑W (BLS, U.S. Dept. of Labor); the Nebraska Workers’ Compensation Court will determine the annual COLA. Benefits will be adjusted every 12 months (rounded up to next whole dollar) but not to exceed the applicable statutory maximums in sections 48‑121.01 and 48‑122. Section 48‑122.03’s maximum limitation will not bar COLA increases under section 48‑122. No changes to Department of Labor appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB523_IntroLB523_Intro_Copy.docxLB523 establishes the Student Teacher Compensation Act. The State Department of Education must create a stipend program providing $4,000 per student‑teaching semester to eligible student teachers who apply. The department must annually report to the Legislature and Governor on numbers of applicants and recipients and aggregate demographic and educator‑shortage area data (no individual or school identifiers). The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate funds annually to the State Department of Education for stipends; the department may also pursue grants, private donations, or federal funding. The State Board of Education may adopt rules and determine acceptable accredited teacher education programs (accreditation recognized by the U.S. Department of Education). The act is operative July 1, 2025, and contains an emergency clause.Creates the "Student Teacher Compensation Act" (sections 1–7). Key agencies: the State Department of Education must establish a stipend program and provide $4,000 per student‑teaching semester to eligible, applying student teachers; the State Board of Education may adopt rules and determine acceptable accrediting agencies (those recognized by the U.S. Department of Education). The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate funds annually to the State Department of Education for these stipends; the department may also pursue grants, private donations, or federal funding. Reports under the Act must not identify individual persons or schools providing feedback. No total appropriation or budget allocation amount is specified.
109-1-LB524_IntroLB524_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB524 directs the State Treasurer to transfer $1,000,000,000 from the General Fund to the Education Future Fund in fiscal year 2023‑24 and $250,000,000 in fiscal year 2024‑25 on such dates and in such amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services. These provisions tie the timing and amounts of those specified transfers to instructions from DAS's budget division.The added text requires the department to automatically distribute retention grants to the employing school district, which must then pass the funds to eligible paraeducators. It establishes paraeducator eligibility and grant amounts: $1,000 for paraeducators contracted and averaging ≥28 hours/week in school years 2025‑26 or 2026‑27, with proportional (prorated) amounts for those averaging <28 hours. No specific appropriation, funding source, or budget allocation for the Department of Administrative Services is identified in the added language.
109-1-LB525_IntroLB525_Intro_Copy.docxLB525 enacts the Agricultural Data Privacy Act. Key government roles and fiscal provisions: - Attorney General: granted exclusive enforcement authority to sue controllers or processors for injunctive relief or civil penalties (penalty amount left unspecified in the bill). - State Treasurer: required recipient of any civil penalties, to be distributed per Article VII, section 5 of the Nebraska Constitution. - Attorney General duties: must publish controller/processor responsibilities and consumer rights on the AG website and provide an online complaint submission mechanism. The bill disallows a private right of action. No appropriations or other budget allocations are specified.Creates the "Agricultural Data Privacy Act" to regulate agricultural data (definitions, consent, rescission) and limit controllers' and processors' use, sale, or conditioning of services on such data; bans contract provisions waiving these rights and disallows a private right of action. The Attorney General is given exclusive enforcement authority to seek injunctive relief and civil penalties (amount left as a placeholder). All civil penalties must be remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution per Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution. The Attorney General must publish guidance on controller/processor responsibilities and consumer rights on the AG website and provide an online complaint mechanism. No specific funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB526_FinalLB526_Final_Copy.docxLB526 authorizes public power suppliers—defined as public power districts, municipal electric utilities, or other government entities providing electric service—to impose reasonable, non‑discriminatory requirements on cryptocurrency mining operations (facilities ≥1 MW) to cover infrastructure upgrade costs. Permissible measures include requiring direct payment or a letter of credit and imposing terms or conditions, but only after the supplier performs a load study to determine costs and impacts. Prospective miners must notify and meet interconnection requirements of the local supplier. Suppliers must publish on their websites the number of mining operations under their jurisdiction and each operation’s annual energy usage. Suppliers may interrupt service per existing rate schedules and policies. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.Adds a regulatory framework for "cryptocurrency mining operations" (≥1 MW) handled by "public power suppliers" — defined as public power districts, municipal electric utilities, or other government entities that provide electric service. Public power suppliers may require miners to pay for or secure (e.g., letter of credit) infrastructure upgrade costs and may impose terms and conditions, provided requirements are fair, reasonable, and not unduly discriminatory. Suppliers must conduct a load study before imposing requirements. Prospective operators must notify the local supplier and meet its interconnection rules. Each supplier must publish on its website the number of mining operations it oversees and each operation’s annual energy usage. Suppliers may interrupt service to miners per established rate schedules/policies. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB527A_FinalLB527A_Final_Copy.docxLB527A appropriates funds to the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services to implement LB527. For Program 344 it provides $5,765,385 from the Medicaid Access and Quality Fund and $12,279,638 federal funds for FY2025‑26, and $11,758,984 (cash) and $25,045,347 (federal) for FY2026‑27 — all designated for state aid only. For Program 348 it provides $57,392,193 (Medicaid Access and Quality Fund) and $105,013,007 (federal) for FY2025‑26, and $117,056,172 (cash) and $214,182,801 (federal) for FY2026‑27 — also for state aid only. Neither appropriation may be used for permanent/temporary salaries or per diems. The act takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.Appropriates funds to the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services for implementation of LB 527 (Programs 344 and 348). Program 344: FY2025-26 — $5,765,385 from the Medicaid Access and Quality Fund and $12,279,638 federal; FY2026-27 — $11,758,984 cash and $25,045,347 federal. Program 348: FY2025-26 — $57,392,193 cash and $105,013,007 federal; FY2026-27 — $117,056,172 cash and $214,182,801 federal. All listed cash and federal amounts are designated as state aid only. The appropriations may not be used for permanent or temporary state employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB527_FinalLB527_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services- The bill directs that beginning no later than January 1, 2027, $5,000,000 annually shall be used to obtain federal financial participation to pay a monthly per‑member fee of at least $75 to qualified primary care providers who meet criteria established by the Department of Health and Human Services to serve as primary care medical homes for target populations. Use of these funds is subject to required federal approvals. - The Department of Health and Human Services is authorized to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations necessary to implement the Medicaid Access and Quality Act.Creates the "Medicaid Access and Quality Act" and tasks the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to implement it, adopt rules, and set provider criteria. The act directs rate enhancements for nonhospital physical‑health providers—emphasizing evaluation & management, labor-and-delivery, and rural services—and specifies intent that Medicaid practitioner fee‑schedule rates and related General Fund appropriations not be reduced below the July 1, 2024 levels. Funding: beginning no later than Jan 1, 2027, $5 million annually will be used to secure federal matching funds to pay a monthly per‑member fee (not less than $75) to qualified primary‑care medical homes; any remaining funds go to the medical assistance program and CHIP. All uses require applicable federal approvals.
109-1-LB528_IntroLB528_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentDefines the Department of Economic Development ("department") and charges it with establishing a grant program to procure annual licenses for preexisting three-dimensional, game-based learning platforms for middle and high schools (science/chemistry/physical science/mathematics focus). Grants are funded with lottery funds pursuant to §79-3501 and awarded from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund (administered by the State Department of Education). The department will set application criteria, approve developer applications, require full statewide district access, restrict funds to license procurement (not R&D), and must award grants by July 1 annually. The department must file an annual report to the Clerk by December 1 and may adopt rules. Funding allocation: of the 10% transferred under §79-3501, 8.75% is reserved for these subsection (2) grants and 1.25% for subsection (1) grants.Summary (Department of Economic Development): - “Department” is defined as the Department of Economic Development. - The department may approve grants to purchase annual licenses for preexisting learning platforms; grant funds may not be used for platform research or development. - Eligible platforms must align with State Board of Education academic standards for middle/high school, comply with ISO 27001 data-security standards, and show experience with statewide implementation. - Grants approved by the Department of Economic Development are to be awarded from the State Department of Education Improvement Grant Fund, administered by the State Department of Education. - No specific appropriation amounts or new budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB529_FinalLB529_Final_Copy.docxLB529 amends the State Procurement Act (section 73-803) to revise definitions used for procurement. It clarifies that "division" refers to the materiel division of the Department of Administrative Services and redefines "state agency" to exclude the University of Nebraska, the Nebraska state colleges, the Nebraska Investment Council, the courts, the Legislature, and any officer or agency established by the Nebraska Constitution. The change is applied to actions on or after July 19, 2024. The bill repeals the prior version of section 73-803 and declares an emergency, making the act effective upon passage. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Mentions the Nebraska Investment Council and specifies that the bill’s amendments to this subdivision apply to any action taken on or after July 19, 2024. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB52_FinalLB52_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends Neb. Rev.
