Stat. §81-1850 to (1) require county attorneys to forward victims' names/addresses to the Department of Correctional Services (DCS) and the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) (among others) after a felony conviction; (2) require DCS and DHHS to include victims' names in offender files (not public record) and to respond to written victim notification requests; (3) require DCS (or county corrections agencies) to notify victims of furloughs/releases (≥24 hours), transfers to community status, community-based program start/termination, escapes/returns, discharges (when practicable ≥30 days prior), sentence-credit/release-date calculations, sentence reductions, and victims' rights to submit statements; (4) require county attorneys to notify DCS of Mental Health or Sex Offender Commitment petitions and DCS to forward victim information to DHHS; (5) require DHHS to notify victims of commitment-related escapes, discharges/disp osition changes, furloughs/releases, and program participation; (6) direct DCS and DHHS to adopt implementing rules; and (7) exempt victims' contact information held by DCS/DHHS from public disclosure. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Added (underlined) language expands the enumerated list of covered offenses to include manslaughter; motor vehicle homicide; first- and second-degree assault (including by strangulation/suffocation); terroristic threats; stalking; first-degree false imprisonment; sexual abuse by a school employee; first-degree sexual assault of a child; child enticement by electronic communication; sexual abuse of a protected individual; domestic assault (first/second degree); and sex and labor trafficking (including minors). There are no appropriation, funding, or budget-allocation provisions in the added text. Operationally, the Department of Correctional Services could see increased caseloads/incarceration demands and DHHS may face greater need for victim services, treatment, and case management, but no direct fiscal or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB530A_FinalLB530A_Final_Copy.docxAppropriates $134,000 from the Supreme Court Automation Cash Fund to the Nebraska Supreme Court (Program 570) for FY2025‑26 to implement provisions of Legislative Bill 530. No funds are appropriated for FY2026‑27. The appropriation may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates $134,000 from the Supreme Court Automation Cash Fund to the Nebraska Supreme Court (Program 570) for FY2025‑26 and $0 for FY2026‑27 to support implementation of Legislative Bill 530 (109th Legislature, 1st Session, 2025). Funds may not be used to pay permanent or temporary state employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB530_FinalLB530_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of TransportationThe bill makes the following agency-specific changes: - Department of Correctional Services (DOCS): prohibits placing juveniles in DOCS secure youth confinement facilities and excludes DOCS institutions from the “staff secure juvenile facility” definition; requires inmates sentenced to DOCS convicted under controlled-substance provisions to receive drug treatment/counseling; DOCS may access sealed juvenile records for individuals committed to or under its care. - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): permits peace officers to deliver juveniles taken into custody for certain noncriminal matters to DHHS for temporary placement, supervision, and emergency medical/behavioral consent (custody ends if no court order within 48 hours); courts must notify DHHS when DHHS was a party or the juvenile was a ward; DHHS may access and disclose sealed juvenile records as needed for intake, case planning, evaluations, reporting, supervision, and licensing. - Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): courts must transmit abstracts of juvenile convictions/adjudications affecting driving privileges and notify the DMV when sealed records include impoundment or prohibitions on obtaining licenses/permits. - Department of Transportation (DOT): authorized to temporarily reduce posted maximum speed limits under specified conditions, require electronic/digital signage and notices, adopt rules, and maintain related policies and records. - Department of Labor: must provide a website link informing employers they may not ask about sealed records and ensure employment applications state applicants need not disclose sealed records. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Department of Labor: No substantive changes or funding/appropriation items affecting the department. Department of Correctional Services: Electronic monitoring tampering is added as a Class I misdemeanor and applies to devices required by court order or as a condition of parole — DOCS roles are implicated but no new duties or funding are specified. Department of Health and Human Services: No substantive changes or funding/appropriation items affecting the department. Department of Motor Vehicles: Courts may order driver bans and suspend (up to 2 years) or revoke (15 years) operator's licenses for convictions involving tampering with electronic monitoring devices; orders are to be administered at sentencing/final judgment/probation revocation. No new DMV funding is specified. Department of Transportation: New authority to temporarily reduce posted speed limits for weather, traction, emergencies or congestion, effective only when shown on electronic/digital signs; reductions in 5 mph increments (policy may allow different increments), no minimum speed while reduced, recordkeeping and a requirement to develop policy and adopt rules. No appropriations or budget allocations included.
109-1-LB531_IntroLB531_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentLB531 prohibits the Department of Economic Development from requiring projects that receive funding from the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to comply with the International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) as prescribed. The bill also creates an exception to the existing requirement that buildings constructed with state funds meet the 2018 IECC. No provisions in the bill change funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Economic Development or the Affordable Housing Trust Fund.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB532_IntroLB532_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor- The bill defines "Department" as the Department of Labor. - The Department of Labor is directed to maintain a public database of violations of sections 1–9 on its public website. - The Department of Labor may adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement sections 1–9. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor are included in the bill.Summary (Department of Labor focus): - "Department" is defined as the Department of Labor and is assigned enforcement and administrative duties for sections 1–9. - The Department must investigate alleged employer violations of E‑Verify/work‑authorization rules, issue determinations, provide contested‑case hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act, and notify licensing agencies of final violations. - It must maintain a public online database of violations and may adopt rules to implement the sections consistent with federal law. - The Department may assess/collect reinstatement fees (greater of its investigation/enforcement costs or $1,000) and set additional suspension periods for violations involving five or more unauthorized aliens. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB533_IntroLB533_Intro_Copy.docxLB533 amends the Pharmacy Benefit Manager Licensure and Regulation Act. It defines "clinician-administered drug" and requires specialty pharmacies that ship such drugs to comply with federal requirements (including USP general chapter 800 and the Drug Supply Chain Security Act), provide 24/7 access to a pharmacist or nurse, accept refill requests per PBM/health carrier utilization procedures, and obtain signature on deliveries to health care providers. Requesting providers must give five business days' notice of delivery. PBMs and health carriers must establish an appeal/exception process when delivery commitments fail or immediate one-time use is needed. The bill designates "Director" as the Director of Insurance and becomes operative January 1, 2026. No funding or appropriations are included.Adds definitions and rules for "clinician‑administered drug" and "specialty pharmacy." Specialty pharmacies that ship these drugs must follow federal drug‑shipment rules (including USP chapter 800), provide 24/7 access to a pharmacist or nurse, accept refill requests per PBM/health carrier procedures, and follow DSCSA track‑and‑trace rules when compounding. Providers must give delivery date/time/place at least five business days ahead; shipments to providers require signature. PBMs and health carriers that mandate use of a specialty pharmacy must provide an appeal/exception process when delivery fails or immediate, irreparable harm would result without a one‑time use of an in‑stock drug. PBMs/health carriers may not require specialty pharmacies to dispense clinician‑administered drugs to patients for patient transport to providers. No specific government agencies are newly created or funded; federal statutes (USP standards and the Drug Supply Chain Security Act) are referenced. No funding or appropriation changes.
109-1-LB534_FinalLB534_Final_Copy.docxLB534 directs payment of settled claims and authorizes agency account write-offs. Claims settled by the Attorney General or State Claims Board are to be paid through Agency 65 as follows: Program 536 (General Fund) $1,195,691.75; Program 592 (General Fund) $827,500.00; Program 593 (Workers' Compensation Claims Revolving Fund) $1,260,000.00; Program 594 (State Insurance/Revolving Fund) $1,446,454.12. The Director of Administrative Services is authorized to draw warrants and the State Treasurer to pay upon receipt of releases. The State Claims Board approved write-offs by state agencies: Department of Veterans' Affairs $14,983.58; Department of Motor Vehicles $14,296.88; Department of Transportation $120,741.50; Department of Labor $90,339.82; Nebraska Public Employees Retirement Systems $49,591.34; Department of Environment and Energy $53,256.46; Department of Health and Human Services $1,424,360.66. The act takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.Adds appropriations to pay settled claims and directs payment processing through Agency 65 (Programs 536, 592, 593, 594). Key funding changes: - General Fund appropriations: $1,195,691.75 for miscellaneous/line-of-duty claims (Program 536) and $827,500.00 for indemnification claims (Program 592) — total General Fund $2,023,191.75. - Workers' Compensation Claims Revolving Fund: $1,260,000.00 for workers' comp claims (Program 593). - State Insurance Fund: $1,446,454.12 for tort claims (Program 594). The Attorney General and State Claims Board settlements are authorized for payment; the Director of Administrative Services and State Treasurer are directed to issue warrants upon receipt of releases. The State Claims Board approved write-offs for: Dept. of Veterans' Affairs; Dept. of Motor Vehicles; Dept. of Transportation; Dept. of Labor; Nebraska Public Employees Retirement Systems; Dept. of Environment and Energy; Dept. of Health and Human Services (total write-offs $1,767,570.24).
109-1-LB535_IntroLB535_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB535 expressly references the agencies as follows: - Public safety officer definition added: includes employees of the Department of Correctional Services; includes employees of the Department of Health and Human Services only when the offender is committed as a dangerous sex offender under the Sex Offender Commitment Act (sec. 3). - Section 28-934 expands covered locations to include secure youth confinement facilities operated by the Department of Correctional Services when the offender is committed to such a facility. - Section 29-2221 continues mandatory imprisonment in a Department of Correctional Services adult correctional facility for habitual offenders and adds assault under section 4 of this act to the offenses that can trigger enhanced habitual criminal mandatory minimums. No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.Summary (Dept. of Correctional Services & Dept. of Health and Human Services) - The added language explicitly classifies employees of the Department of Correctional Services as "public safety officers," extending the bill’s enhanced assault provisions to DOC staff. - Employees of the Department of Health and Human Services are included as "public safety officers" only when the offender is committed under the Sex Offender Commitment Act as a dangerous sex offender. - The bill broadly raises protections for covered workers (on-duty) against serious injury, use of dangerous instruments, and assaults involving bodily fluids. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either department are included.
109-1-LB536_IntroLB536_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentThe bill defines "Department" as the Department of Economic Development. It directs the Department to accept grant applications from eligible manufacturers from October 1, 2025, through November 1, 2025, consider applications in order received, approve qualifying applications subject to available funding, and notify applicants. The Department will administer the newly created Manufacturing Modernization Pilot Investment Fund, which consists of legislative transfers and other gifts/grants and will fund grants (each up to $250,000, matching private funds). The Department may adopt rules and regulations to implement the Act. The Legislature intends to appropriate [XXXX] dollars from the General Fund to carry out the Act.The added provisions designate the "Department" as the Department of Economic Development and make the department responsible for administering the new Manufacturing Modernization Pilot Investment Fund and grant program. The department must accept applications Oct 1–Nov 1, 2025, consider them in receipt order, approve eligible applicants subject to available funding, and may adopt rules to implement the program. Grants are matched one-to-one by private funds, capped at $250,000, and may not fund projects begun before application; recipients who lose eligibility must repay grants. The Fund is created to receive legislative transfers and gifts and will be invested by the state investment officer. The bill expresses legislative intent to appropriate [XXXX] dollars from the General Fund (amount unspecified).
109-1-LB537_IntroLB537_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB537 directs the Department of Labor to administer the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund and to provide workforce development grants, to be awarded evenly among Nebraska’s three congressional districts. Grants must be used for job skills, money management, communication, job preparation, and placement; applicants must demonstrate one-to-one private matching. Grant recipients must report to the Department of Labor on job placement and self-sufficiency outcomes for individuals served. The Legislature intends to transfer $1,500,000 from the General Fund to the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund for FY2025-26 for the department to provide these grants.The Department of Labor must award workforce development grants evenly across the three congressional districts. Grants may be used for job skills, money management, communication, job preparation, and job placement. Applicants must show one-to-one private matching funds. Grant recipients must report to the department on job placement and self‑sufficiency outcomes. The Legislature intends to transfer $1,500,000 from the General Fund to the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 to fund these grants.
109-1-LB538A_IntroLB538A_Intro_Copy.docxAppropriates General Fund sums to the Nebraska State Department of Education, Program 25, to implement Legislative Bill 538. Allocation: $138,227 for FY2025‑26 and $137,431 for FY2026‑27. Caps permanent and temporary salaries and per diems charged to these appropriations at $66,197 for FY2025‑26 and $68,348 for FY2026‑27.Appropriates General Fund amounts to the State Department of Education (Program 25) to implement Legislative Bill 538: $138,227 for FY2025‑26 and $137,431 for FY2026‑27. Caps permanent and temporary salary and per diem expenditures from these appropriations at $66,197 for FY2025‑26 and $68,348 for FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB538_IntroLB538_Intro_Copy.docxLB538 requires school boards and governing boards of postsecondary institutions to adopt written discrimination and harassment policies that explicitly address antisemitism. It establishes Title VI coordinator roles in state education entities: the bill creates/assigns a Title VI coordinator within the State Department of Education and directs the Coordinating Commission on Postsecondary Education to designate/employ a Title VI coordinator. The commission’s statutory staffing authority is amended to include that designation. The commission’s coordinator must monitor discrimination and harassment (including antisemitic conduct), investigate complaints under the new policies, and file an annual report. The bill does not include any express changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.The Coordinating Commission on Postsecondary Education must designate a Title VI coordinator. That coordinator will monitor discrimination and harassment in public institutions, including antisemitic discrimination as defined elsewhere in the act. Duties include investigating all complaints of discrimination or harassment under the policy required by section 3 and filing an annual report. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB539_IntroLB539_Intro_Copy.docxLB539 amends Nebraska handgun statutes and reallocates responsibilities for criminal-history checks to the Nebraska State Patrol. The Patrol is restricted to receiving only information necessary to determine fitness for concealed-carry permits or firearm transfer disqualifications and must provide only to an applicant’s local chief of police or sheriff whether the applicant is disqualified. Entities (including mental-health boards) reporting in good faith are granted immunity from liability. The bill creates a Class II misdemeanor for knowingly causing the Patrol to request checks without reasonable belief an application exists and retains a Class IV felony for materially false statements or false identification in handgun transactions. Multiple statutory sections are repealed; no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds that criminal history record information (CHRI) checks for firearms or explosives purposes apply to persons qualified for a concealed carry permit under § 69-2430 or otherwise subject to CHRI checks by law. No specific government agency or department is named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB53_IntroLB53_Intro_Copy.docxLB53 declares the Legislature’s intent not to criminalize pregnancy or punish people for pregnancy outcomes and establishes both criminal and civil immunity for individuals regarding their own pregnancy outcomes (including stillbirth, miscarriage, intentional termination, or any non–live-birth outcome). The bill does not mention or direct any specific state agencies or departments, nor does it include any funding, appropriations, or budgetary provisions.Adds a prohibition on citation, arrest, or prosecution for any person based on the outcome of their own pregnancy (including stillbirth, miscarriage, intentional termination, or any non–live birth) and grants civil‑action immunity for such pregnancy outcomes. No government agencies, departments, or changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are referenced.
109-1-LB540_IntroLB540_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureLB540 explicitly defines "Department" as the Department of Agriculture and "Director" as the Director of Agriculture (or designated representative). It creates the Nebraska Apiary Advisory Board, to be chaired by the Director of Agriculture, with board members appointed by the Director and the Director responsible for filling vacancies. The board may include an invited University of Nebraska entomology representative. Members serve without compensation but are eligible for expense reimbursement pursuant to existing statutes (sections 81-1174 to 81-1177). The bill contains no new appropriations or other funding changes directed to the Department of Agriculture.Creates the Nebraska Apiary Advisory Board under the director (Department of Agriculture). The director appoints and chairs the board, fills vacancies, and may invite (but not require) one University of Nebraska entomology/apiculture representative. Membership must include at least one commercial beekeeper, one beekeeper active in a club, and one hobbyist/sideliner beekeeper. Members serve without compensation but may receive expense reimbursement under sections 81-1174 to 81-1177. The board will identify research gaps, prioritize needs to improve managed and wild bee health/habitat, recommend actionable protection and recovery steps, review related statutes/policies, and guide education/outreach. The Board of Regents must create a full-time apiculture educator in the UNL extension service. No new appropriations or specific funding/budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB541_IntroLB541_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Motor VehiclesThe bill requires the Secretary of State to contract with the Department of Administrative Services for storage and distribution of official voter registration forms. It directs the Secretary of State and the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) to enter an agreement to match statewide voter registration data with DMV records (including citizenship verification); the DMV must also enter an agreement with the Social Security Commissioner. The DMV must make voter registration applications available at issuance/renewal of operator’s licenses and state ID cards, electronically transmit registration data to county election officials within specified timeframes, and provide electronic images/signatures from DMV records for voter registration purposes. The Secretary of State will use DMV data to verify ID numbers on mailed early-voting ballot requests and will supply DMV with voter ID requirement information. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either agency are specified.No provisions directly reference or assign duties or funding to the Department of Administrative Services or the Department of Motor Vehicles. There are new election requirements that may indirectly affect DMV (as the primary issuer of “valid photographic identification” now required for voter registration, ballot requests and returns), but the bill does not create new DMV responsibilities or appropriate funds. It also does not change DAS authorities or include any appropriations or budget allocations for either agency. Key added election provisions (context only): defines “hand count”; requires photographic ID for registrants and voters; sets secure ballot drop‑box standards (lighting, signage, tamper resistance, 24‑hour video surveillance, inspections, repairs, and 22‑month recording retention); mandates watermark and signature verification for early ballots; requires independent IT assessment and a hand count of at least 25% of ballots for verification.
109-1-LB542_IntroLB542_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB542 contains no explicit references to the Department of Transportation. The bill amends statutes on metropolitan utilities district authority and on utility-facility relocation for highway projects, but it does not name or directly address the Department of Transportation, nor does it include any appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations directed to that agency.Adds a definition of “qualifying utility facility” that expressly covers utility facilities located in, over, along, or under: Interstate highways (and urban extensions), highways formerly designated as Interstates, any highway, parts of the state highway system, and roads/right‑of‑ways under county, city, or village primary authority. “Utility facility” is expanded to include commercial broadband supplier facilities (per §86‑5,104) and community antenna television service facilities (per §18‑2201). The provision operates “notwithstanding any rule, permit, agreement, franchise, or other authorization or law to the contrary.” For the Department of Transportation, this clarifies the types of facilities that may occupy DOT-managed rights‑of‑way and could restrict the applicability of existing permitting/authorization processes; no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB543_IntroLB543_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor VehiclesLB543 authorizes the Department (DMV) to deliver license plates or registration certificates by mail or alternative shipping and permits the DMV to charge a postage-and-handling fee limited to actual cost; that fee is remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund. The bill also: (1) establishes a $50 annual nonrefundable fee for requesting a single front-or-rear plate, remitted to the Highway Trust Fund; (2) maintains a per-plate fee cap (not to exceed $4.25) and changes the remittance destination for fees under §60-3,102 from the Highway Trust Fund to a License Plate Cash Fund beginning with the 2029 issuance cycle; and (3) retains duplicate-registration and replacement-plate fees ($1 and $2.50).Key DMV changes (effective on an implementation date set by the director on or before Jan. 1, 2029): - Allows registrants to choose annual or multiyear (2- or 3-year) registrations; multiyear renewals require payment of fees and taxes for each year, including fees under sections 60-3,141 and 60-3,156. - Permits the department to mail license plates or registration certificates to applicants or county treasurers via secure delivery; if mailed to the applicant the department may charge a postage/handling fee limited to actual cost. That fee is remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund. - Allows operation/towing with proof of registration for 30 days without a mailed plate. - Beginning with the 2029 plate issuance cycle, all fees collected under this section are to be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the License Plate Cash Fund.
109-1-LB544_IntroLB544_Intro_Copy.docxLB544 amends the Employment Security Law (section 48-601) to disqualify an individual from unemployment benefits for any week in which the individual (1) fails to respond to a job offer within two business days or (2) fails to appear for a scheduled job interview without notifying the prospective employer. The bill requires the department that administers the Employment Security Law to establish an online portal, an email address, and a telephone hotline for employers to report such failures and mandates that the department verify employer-submitted information before denying benefits. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Creates new eligibility rules for unemployment benefits: an individual is disqualified for any week they (1) fail to respond to a job offer within two business days or (2) fail to appear for a scheduled interview without notifying the prospective employer. The department is required to establish a website portal, an email address, and a telephone hotline for employers to report such failures, and must verify employer-submitted information before denying benefits. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB545_IntroLB545_Intro_Copy.docxLB545 (Rountree) would create statutory immunity from civil liability for injury or death arising from use of donated menstrual products when those products are used as prescribed, and includes definitions of terms used. The bill was referred to the Judiciary Committee. No state agencies or departments are named, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budgetary provisions.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB546_IntroLB546_Intro_Copy.docxLB546 amends §81‑829.40 to restate and clarify the Governor’s authority and duties in disasters, emergencies, and civil defense emergencies. It specifies the Governor’s general direction and control of emergency management and the Nebraska Emergency Management Agency (NEMA); requires proclamations to describe affected areas and be filed with NEMA, the Secretary of State, and local government clerks; and confirms activation of state, city, village, county, and interjurisdictional emergency management organizations and plans. The Governor is affirmed as commander in chief of the militia and may suspend regulatory statutes and employ all available state and local resources. The bill repeals the original section and takes effect immediately. No funding or appropriation changes are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB547_IntroLB547_Intro_Copy.docxLB547 amends Nebraska tax statutes to modify veteran-related exemptions. It aligns the definition of "disabled veteran" with federal law (5 U.S.C. §2108 as of Jan 1, 2025) and requires that a veteran’s disability or blindness be recognized by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs as service‑connected. Changes affect (1) a motor vehicle tax exemption for one vehicle owned/used by a disabled or blind veteran who was discharged or separated with an honorable characterization, and (2) a property (mobile home) tax exemption for disabled or blind veterans discharged with honorable or general (under honorable conditions) characterizations. The bill becomes operative January 1, 2026, repeals the original sections, and contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a definitional provision: “veteran” is defined to have the same meaning as in 5 U.S.C. 2108 as that section existed on January 1, 2025. No federal agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB548_IntroLB548_Intro_Copy.docxLB548 authorizes political subdivisions (e.g., municipalities) that own and operate natural gas distribution systems to enter contracts to sell natural gas to Nebraska-based industrial consumers whose facilities require at least 3 billion BTU per day on an average day. Contracts must be for a minimum two-year term (excluding renewals). The industrial customer must not be a customer of any investor‑owned or other governmentally‑owned gas system for the operations receiving service at the time the contract is made. For contract purposes, the facility location is deemed within the political subdivision’s service area. No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds authorization allowing any political subdivision that owns and operates a natural gas system (e.g., a municipal or other government utility) to contract to sell natural gas to industrial consumers located in Nebraska that average at least 3 billion BTU/day. Key provisions: contracts must run at least two years (excluding renewals); the industrial customer must not already be served by any investor‑owned or governmentally‑owned gas system for the operations to receive the service at time of contracting; and the customer’s facility is deemed within the political subdivision’s service area solely for the contract. No specific state agencies, appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are established or changed.
109-1-LB549_IntroLB549_Intro_Copy.docxLB549 amends §§79-804, 79-805, and 79-814.01 to permit local school boards to employ (including as volunteers) chaplains—defined as licensed/ordained clergy trained for secular settings—without holding state teaching or administrative certificates. School boards must adopt policies on employment, discipline, continued education, and termination. Chaplains are subject to criminal history checks conducted by the Nebraska State Patrol (including FBI fingerprint checks at the Commissioner of Education's request); the Commissioner may deny eligibility for employment based on specified convictions. The State Department of Education/Commissioner retains notification and eligibility functions; county treasurers’ withholding and board personal-liability provisions in §§79-804/79-805 are made inapplicable to chaplains. Boards set applicant fees for background checks, limited to actual direct costs. Requests for closed hearings invoke the Open Meetings Act. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a definition of "chaplain" and authorizes local school boards to employ (including volunteers) chaplains to provide academic, career, emotional, and behavioral supports without requiring a state teaching or services certificate. Chaplains must undergo a criminal history record check pursuant to section 79-814.01 and pay any required fees; the Commissioner of Education may deny eligibility based on that check and, if denied, the school board may not employ the individual. School boards must adopt policies governing employment, discipline, continued education, and termination of chaplains. The provision does not compel boards to hire chaplains and excludes chaplains employed under section 1 of the act. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB54_IntroLB54_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB54 directs appropriations to the Department of Health and Human Services for FY2025-26 to increase reimbursement rates for developmental disability service providers by 11%. Specifically: - An appropriation of $XXX from the General Fund to DHHS, Program 424, solely to implement the 11% reimbursement increase. - An appropriation of $XXX from Federal Funds to DHHS, Program 348, solely to implement the 11% reimbursement increase. The bill includes an emergency clause; it takes effect upon passage.Appropriates unspecified amounts (listed as $XXX) for FY2025‑26 to the Department of Health and Human Services to fund an 11% increase in reimbursement rates for developmental disability service providers. One appropriation is from the General Fund to Program 424 and a separate appropriation is from Federal Funds to Program 348. Both appropriations are restricted and must be used solely to implement the 11% rate increase.
109-1-LB550_IntroLB550_Intro_Copy.docxLB550 requires Nebraska public school districts to adopt a policy excusing students to attend released‑time courses for religious instruction. For excused periods, students are counted as attending their district for purposes of school funding and compulsory attendance. Districts may award academic credit for such courses only after secular, neutral evaluation comparable to similar courses and without testing religious content or denominational affiliation. Released‑time courses may not be held on district property unless permitted under a neutral equal‑access policy that opens property to community groups. The bill preserves equal access to district funds/benefits for sponsoring entities and allows aggrieved parties to sue the responsible school district for damages, equitable relief, and attorney’s fees. An emergency clause makes the act effective immediately.Adds rules governing "released time" courses and the school district's obligations. Key government entity: the school district. Changes affecting funding/finance: a student excused to attend a released time course must be counted as attending the home school for purposes of school funding and attendance calculations. Operational requirements: districts may grant academic credit using secular evaluation criteria and must treat requests neutrally regarding religious content. Districts must not deny released time sponsors equal access to any funds, benefits, or services the district makes available to community groups. Enforcement: aggrieved persons may sue the school district for actual damages, equitable/declaratory relief, and reasonable attorney’s fees and litigation costs. No new statewide appropriations or specific departmental budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB551_IntroLB551_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB551 amends section 85-1511 to require community college boards to file two annual audits with the Auditor of Public Accounts, the Coordinating Commission, and the Department of Administrative Services: (1) a comprehensive fiscal-year audit of books, accounts, all revenue sources, and the county-certified property valuation — filed by November 15; and (2) a comprehensive audit of full-time-equivalent student enrollment and reimbursable educational units (including three most-recent years’ verified totals used for aid calculations) — filed by August 15. The bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Added text bars the Board of Regents, the Nebraska State Colleges Board of Trustees, and community college boards from creating or authorizing new academic tenure for anyone not tenured before the act’s effective date. Each board must adopt written policies on employee agreements; acceptable dismissal grounds (including just cause, program discontinuance, financial exigency); annual faculty evaluations; minimum standards of practice; standards for review/discipline; and dismissal procedures. The Department of Administrative Services is not referenced and there are no appropriations, funding, or budget changes affecting DAS in the added language.
109-1-LB552_IntroLB552_Intro_Copy.docxLB552 prohibits public postsecondary institutions in Nebraska from maintaining a "diversity, equity, and inclusion" (DEI) office or conducting DEI programs that (a) influence hiring apart from color‑blind/sex‑neutral processes, (b) provide differential treatment or special benefits based on race, color, ethnicity, gender identity, or sexual orientation, (c) implement policies/procedures or programs referenced to those traits, or (d) require participation or condition enrollment/functions on such programs. "Appropriate governing board" is defined as the Board of Regents (University of Nebraska), the Board of Trustees (Nebraska State Colleges), or a community college governing board. The bill also prohibits spending public money on DEI offices/programs. Exceptions include sexual‑harassment training, attorney‑staffed compliance offices, grant/accreditation statements, demographic data collection, scholarly research, recognized student activities, and short‑term guest speakers. Employees may sue for injunctive relief; no appropriations or funding changes are specified.Adds definitions and restrictions affecting public postsecondary institutions governed by the Board of Regents (University of Nebraska), Board of Trustees (Nebraska State Colleges), and community college governing boards. Defines "diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) office/program" and prohibits requiring participation in DEI programs or spending public money on DEI offices/programs. Preserves exceptions allowing sexual‑harassment training; legal offices staffed by attorneys for compliance; grant- or accreditation-related statements; data collection; scholarly research; recognized student organization activities; and short-term guest speakers. Allows employees to sue institutions for violations and obtain injunctive relief. No specific appropriations or new budget allocations are made.
109-1-LB553_IntroLB553_Intro_Copy.docxLB553 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§71-5662, 71-5663, 71-5665, and 71-5668 to add dietitian nutritionists to eligibility for Rural Health Systems and Professional Incentive Act student loans and loan-repayment programs. The bill directs the (unnamed) commission to include dietitian nutritionist practice when designating health profession shortage areas. The Department (responsible for program administration) will execute exempt agreements with recipients and local entities and make loan-repayment payments directly. State and local entities provide equal funding for repayments, subject to caps: $30,000/year (physicians, psychiatrists, dentists, psychologists) and $15,000/year (physician assistants, nurse practitioners, pharmacists, physical and occupational therapists, dietitian nutritionists, and mental health practitioners). Student-loan limits remain (e.g., $30,000/academic year; certain program total caps). ARPA federal funds continue to be prioritized for specified agreements and may be used without local matching for the covered period.Adds enumerated program categories in Nebraska (including a Dietitian Nutritionist program) and a list of authorized provider types — explicitly including "a dietitian nutritionist licensed under section 38-1813" — plus several qualification/eligibility provisos (be, not, enter... ). No specific state agency or department is named in the added text beyond the statutory licensing reference (section 38-1813). No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB554_IntroLB554_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB554 creates the Nebraska Health Professions Commission and explicitly designates the chief medical officer of the Department of Health and Human Services (or the chief medical officer’s designee) as a commission member. The bill does not include any explicit changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Creates the Nebraska Health Professions Commission to review credentialing and scope-of-practice proposals, hold public factfinding hearings, collect and analyze workforce, public health, quality, access, and affordability data, and issue annual recommendations to the Legislature. For the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): the commission must include the DHHS chief medical officer or a designee; it must file its report with the board, the DHHS director, and the Health and Human Services Committee chair; and it may monitor/evaluate public health and health‑care quality impacts of enacted changes. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB555_IntroLB555_Intro_Copy.docxLB555 amends the Funeral Directing and Embalming Practice Act to create an assistant funeral director credential, requiring a collaborative agreement and supervision by a licensed funeral director, recordkeeping, and prohibition on embalming (violation results in immediate termination of the agreement and employment). The bill adds failure to comply with the collaborative agreement as a grounds for disciplinary action under section 38-1424 and subjects credentials to discipline pursuant to section 38-196 and applicable department or other regulatory body rules. It repeals the prior versions of amended sections and includes an emergency clause. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds an assistant funeral director classification under the Funeral Directing and Embalming Practice Act: assistants may perform principal funeral-directing functions (services, interments, family arrangements, daily management) but may not perform embalming. A licensed funeral director must enter into and supervise a written collaborative agreement with each assistant and retain records of the agreement and the assistant’s functions. Violation of the embalming prohibition or failure to comply with section 8 results in immediate termination of the collaborative agreement and employment in Nebraska. No state agency or department is named, and no funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB556_IntroLB556_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB556: agency provisions - Department of Correctional Services: The bill clarifies that a "staff secure juvenile facility" expressly excludes any institution operated by the Department of Correctional Services. It also prohibits placement, assignment, or transfer of specified juveniles to adult correctional facilities or the secure youth confinement facility operated by the Department of Correctional Services. - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): Peace officers taking juveniles into temporary custody under specified statutes must deliver custody to DHHS when not released. DHHS must place the juvenile in the least restrictive temporary setting, supervise placement, and may consent to emergency medical, psychological, or psychiatric treatment; DHHS has no further authority absent a court order. Temporary DHHS custody ends if no court order is issued within 48 hours. For mental‑health emergency custody, officers may place juveniles at a mental health facility or deliver them to DHHS and must complete a department‑prescribed certificate. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.The added language clarifies juvenile-detention procedure: for felony arrests, the probation officer must recommend detention, release, or an alternative and forward intake info to a judge, who consults the officer and may consider (but is not bound by) the factors in §43-260.01. For non-felony arrests, the statute specifies criteria under which detention is unnecessary (no serious threat, no recent willful failures to appear) and when detention is immediately necessary (e.g., fleeing law enforcement, absconding from placements/home, violent or multiple property offenses, threats). It also notes circumstances requiring agreement of the juvenile’s counsel and the county or city attorney. No provisions reference the Department of Correctional Services or the Department of Health and Human Services, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB557_IntroLB557_Intro_Copy.docxLB557 amends multiple education statutes. Agencies and bodies affected include the State Department of Education, State Board of Education, Commissioner of Education, learning community coordinating councils (and achievement subcouncils), school boards, resident and option school districts, and the Legislature’s Education Committee. Key provisions affecting agencies and funding: - Option districts must notify parents/resident districts (within ten days); the Commissioner prescribes application/withdrawal forms; rejected applicants receive written reasons and appeal instructions to the State Board. - Parents of students denied option enrollment are eligible for a $2,500 educational support payment for the applicable school year. - Resident districts must provide transportation for option students with disabilities; the State Department of Education reimburses those costs per existing statute (79-1144). - Net option funding formula (FY2023-24 onward) is revised: net option funding = net option students × (statewide average basic funding per formula student − foundation aid per formula student). - The State Department must annually certify school-building free/reduced-price lunch percentages (community eligibility identified student percentage multiplied by 1.6). - Learning community coordinating councils retain levy and fund-administration authorities and must report to the Education Committee.Adds procedures tied to option enrollment and educational support payments. School districts must use a random selection process that considers student/parent interest and may not use criteria that discriminate (race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, protected classes); listed factors include residential address and district capacity. It creates a process for requesting an educational support payment pursuant to subsection (3). If a student's option enrollment application is rejected by the district, the parent or guardian is eligible for a $2,500 education-support payment for that school year. The changes reference certification under section 79-2120 and section 79-769 (learning community/school building data). No explicit appropriation language appears.
109-1-LB558_FinalLB558_Final_Copy.docxLB558 (introduced by Sen. von Gillern; referred to the Revenue Committee, read Jan 22, 2025) establishes an "Infrastructure Review Task Force" concerning transportation infrastructure and assigns duties to that task force. The provided excerpt does not name any state agencies or departments, nor does it specify membership, reporting requirements, deadlines, or any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. Further bill text would be required to identify responsible agencies or any fiscal impacts.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB559_FinalLB559_Final_Copy.docxLB559 adds financial transaction offenses (including unlawful installation/use of skimmer devices and a continuing criminal‑enterprise enhancement) to Nebraska’s forfeiture statute and creates a Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund. The Attorney General will administer the Fund, which consists of assets forfeited from financial transaction offenses (per section 28‑1601). Money in the Fund may be invested by the state investment officer under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Victims may apply to the Attorney General for reimbursement; the Attorney General determines eligibility and may prorate payments if funds are insufficient. Funds remain in the Fund for at least 36 months or until application resolution, after which remaining monies are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under the Nebraska Constitution. Prosecuting authorities must specifically plead forfeiture in charging papers; district courts conduct pretrial and post‑conviction evidentiary forfeiture hearings and may allow intervention.Creates the Financial Fraud Victims' Reimbursement Fund, to be administered by the Attorney General. The fund will consist of assets forfeited from financial transaction offenses (per §28-1601(8)(b)(ii)). The state investment officer shall invest available funds pursuant to the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. Victims may apply to the Attorney General for reimbursement; the AG determines eligibility and amounts, and will distribute pro rata if claims exceed available funds. Funds tied to a specific offense remain in the fund until the later of 36 months after transfer or resolution of applications filed in that period; afterward remaining funds are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution under Neb. Const. art. VII, §5. No separate appropriations or other budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB55_IntroLB55_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill states legislative intent to appropriate $1,500,000 for FY2025‑26 from the Hospital Quality Assurance and Access Assessment Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) for the Medical Assistance program. Funds are to reimburse non‑hospital mental health providers serving Medicaid‑eligible participants who are also Medicare‑eligible when the Medicare rate for behavioral health services is lower than the then‑current Medicaid rate. The bill also expresses intent to sustain Medicaid rates for such mental health providers under Program 348 (Medical Assistance).DHHS: Legislative intent to appropriate $1,500,000 for FY2025‑26 from the Hospital Quality Assurance and Access Assessment Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services (Program 348, Medical Assistance). Funds are designated to reimburse non‑hospital mental health providers who serve Medicaid‑eligible, Medicare‑eligible (dual‑eligible) participants when Medicare reimbursement is lower than then‑current Medicaid rates for behavioral health services. The language also expresses intent to sustain Medicaid rates for those mental health providers serving dual‑eligible participants under Program 348.
109-1-LB560_FinalLB560_Final_Copy.docxLB560 amends §81-3725 to revise the Nebraska tourism grant programs administered by "the commission" and its executive director. Key agency-related provisions: - The commission continues marketing-assistance grants for national/international-caliber events; applicants must document out-of-state draw, marketing plans, tracking methodologies, and potential press coverage. - The commission must establish an innovative tourism grants program (marketing, planning, basic support, regional cooperation) and prohibits use of awards for equipment or capital facility development/improvements. - Eligibility for innovative grants is expanded to include projects that increase nonlocal, in-state visitors or both nonlocal in-state and out-of-state visitors. - Funding cap: the commission may award up to $500,000 in innovative tourism grants to any city or village per fiscal year. - The executive director will convene a technical review committee (minimum three members representing public sector, private sector, and citizens) to score applications and forward recommendations to the commission. Grants recipients must submit final reports within 90 days; the commission shall adopt rules. The original section is repealed.Adds a requirement that "the commission" administering the innovative tourism grant program may award up to $500,000 in such grants to any eligible city or village per fiscal year. No other agencies or appropriation sources are specified.
109-1-LB561_FinalLB561_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationThe bill assigns the Department of Transportation (DOT) these responsibilities and authorities: issue overweight raw‑milk vehicle permits under section 60‑6,298; make permit applications available in county treasurers’ offices; create a statewide “bridge map” (by Jan. 1, 2026), publish it on DOT’s public website, and review it annually; revoke individual permits for violations and revoke all overweight raw‑milk permits if DOT determines federal aid is at risk; initiate legal actions to recover bridge‑repair costs when overweight raw‑milk vehicles damage prohibited bridges, with recovered monies remitted to the Roads Operations Cash Fund; and grant limited vehicle‑length exceptions to meet axle‑weight limits. The bill also contemplates DOT’s existing permit fee and application processes.Creates an “overweight raw‑milk vehicle” permitting regime administered by the Department of Transportation (DOT). Key DOT duties and powers: - Define and enforce permit conditions (permit under §60‑6,298); vehicles limited to 107,500 lbs and must meet axle/group limits under the federal bridge formula (23 U.S.C. 127, as of 1/1/2025). - Must carry and obey a DOT “bridge map” of prohibited bridges, which DOT must create by Jan 1, 2026, review annually, and publish online. - May revoke individual permits for violations (with written notice and APA appeal rights) and may revoke all permits if permits jeopardize federal aid. DOT can authorize interstate travel only with FHWA written approval. - DOT may sue to recover bridge‑repair costs from responsible owners; recovered funds are credited to the Roads Operations Cash Fund. - DOT may grant vehicle‑length exceptions to meet axle weight limits. No new appropriations or other budget allocations are specified beyond crediting recovered repair proceeds to the Roads Operations Cash Fund.
109-1-LB562_IntroLB562_Intro_Copy.docxLB562 amends Game and Parks statutes administered by the Nebraska Game and Parks Commission and touches the Department of Motor Vehicles (Director of Motor Vehicles) and county treasurers. Key agency provisions and fiscal changes: - Commission authority: establishes/resets permit types and caps fees (resident annual motor-vehicle permit ≤ $50; nonresident = 2× resident; temporary resident permit ≤ $10; nonresident = 2× resident). Active-duty military permit set at $5. Commission to set exact fees by rule; may offer temporary reduced rates. - Permit issuance: permits may be sold via commission offices, vending, authorized vendors, county offices, and permit agents; permit agents may collect and retain an issuing fee per section 37-406. - Mountain sheep permits: resident application fee ≤ $34; auctions may authorize up to two additional permits; auction proceeds restricted to perpetuation/management of mountain sheep, elk, and deer. - Motorboat registrations/stamps: three‑year registration fees specified by class; up to $10 of each registration may be used for the Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Program. Non‑Nebraska boats must buy an AIS stamp ≤ $30 plus issuance fee (section 37-406); stamp proceeds remitted to the State Game Fund. - DMV role: implementation date and enhanced owner identification/data requirements for boat registration.Adds that an issuing fee will be charged pursuant to section 37-406 and that the number of permits issued shall not exceed the number awarded under subsection (2). Clarifies that a partner, officer, shareholder, or beneficiary may be designated as the qualifying landowner by a partnership, corporation, or trust under rules in subdivision (2)(a). No specific government agencies or departments are named, and no changes to appropriations, budget allocations, or new funding are included beyond the cross-reference to the existing fee statute.
109-1-LB563_IntroLB563_Intro_Copy.docxLB563 amends the Motor Vehicle Registration Act (sections 60-301, 60-302, 60-3,101, and 60-3,104) to define "commercial fertilizer trailer" and authorize the Department (the agency charged by the Act) to issue permanent trailer license plates for such trailers. It: (1) adds the new definition; (2) exempts these permanent plates from the six‑year reissuance/validation‑decal cycle; (3) requires return of the permanent plate to the Department if the registrant no longer owns the trailer; and (4) makes the registrant liable for the full registration fee on renewal for trailers still owned. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed. Original statutes are repealed and provisions harmonized.Adds a definition of "commercial fertilizer trailer" — a trailer owned by an individual or business that sells agricultural fertilizer or chemicals. Establishes that permanent trailer license plates issued under section 6 must be returned to "the department" if the registrant no longer owns the trailer, and that the registrant remains liable for the full registration fee for any commercial fertilizer trailer still owned at renewal. No agencies beyond "the department" are named and no funding or appropriation changes are included.
109-1-LB564_IntroLB564_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB564 directs the State Treasurer to transfer $750 million from the General Fund to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund in fiscal year 2024–25 “on such dates and in such amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services.” The bill also states the Legislature’s intent that transfers in fiscal year 2025–26 and each year thereafter equal the prior year’s transfer increased by $150 million.The amendment changes the timing of a $150,000,000 appropriation for the Department of Administrative Services from a two‑year 2025–26 allocation to a single fiscal year 2025 allocation. Total funding is unchanged at $150 million; the revision only shifts when the department may receive or obligate the funds. No new funding amount, source, or additional line-item detail is provided in the underlined text.
109-1-LB565_IntroLB565_Intro_Copy.docxLB565 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §84-901.03 (Administrative Procedure Act) to impose new transparency, notice, and procedural requirements on state agencies. Agencies must post guidance documents and an annual online index of current rules and guidance, and deliver that index electronically to the Clerk of the Legislature by December 31 each year. Each guidance document’s first page must contain a specified advisory notice and an estimated fiscal-impact description for state agencies, political subdivisions, and regulated entities. The bill creates a 60-day agency-response requirement for written requests to revise, repeal, or convert guidance into rules and requires publication of related agency decisions. It bars issuing guidance between July 1, 2025, and July 1, 2027, except for federal compliance, prohibits guidance more stringent than federal law, and revokes guidance/provider bulletins from July 1, 2022–July 1, 2025 unless federally required. No appropriations or budget changes are included. An emergency clause makes the act effective upon enactment.- Agencies must include a description, with estimated quantification, of fiscal impacts on state agencies, political subdivisions, and regulated persons/businesses. - State agencies are barred from issuing guidance documents from July 1, 2025, through July 1, 2027, except when needed to comply with new or amended federal rules. - Guidance documents may not impose requirements stricter than federal law. - All guidance documents and provider bulletins issued between July 1, 2022, and July 1, 2025, are revoked pending formal rulemaking under the Administrative Procedure Act, unless explicitly required for federal compliance. - No explicit changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are made.
109-1-LB566_IntroLB566_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB566 includes a recapture provision assigning authority to the Department of Revenue to recapture the residential purchase income tax credit if the claimant sells or transfers the residence or stops using it as a primary residence within five years after the end of the taxable year the credit was claimed. The bill contains no provisions making changes to Department of Revenue funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB567_IntroLB567_Intro_Copy.docxLB567 directs the Nebraska State Board of Education to adopt a model policy on community engagement. School districts are authorized (but not required) to adopt local policies consistent with that model. No state agencies beyond the State Board of Education and local school districts are referenced, and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB568_IntroLB568_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Veterans' AffairsLB568 affects the following agencies: - Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): directs DMV to issue new alternate and organizational plates (including Arbor Day), manage delivery/temporary stickers, and collect related fees. Key fee allocations: organizational plates $70 (60% to Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund, 40% to Highway Trust Fund); $3 transfer fee credited to DMV Cash Fund; alphanumeric alternate plates $5 credited to the designated recipient; personalized-message alternate plates $40 (25% to DMV Cash Fund, 75% to designated recipient); Nebraska Cornhusker spirit plates $70 (60% to DMV Cash Fund, 40% to designated recipient). DMV may charge postage/handling (credited to DMV Cash Fund); manufacturing cost overruns credit the Highway Trust Fund first. - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): Choose Life plate proceeds credited to the Health and Human Services Cash Fund to supplement TANF; DHHS to administer the Organ and Tissue Donor Awareness and Education Fund (receives Donate Life plate revenues and other contributions). - Department of Revenue: Wildlife Conservation Fund may pay Department of Revenue (and other agencies) for expenses administering the income tax designation program; State Treasurer transfers equal to designated contributions are specified. - Department of Veterans' Affairs: will administer a Veterans Employment Program Fund and a Pets for Vets Cash Fund (both funded by designated plate proceeds) to support veteran recruitment and pet-adoption grants.- Department of Motor Vehicles: required to design and issue a long list of new alternate plates (Arbor Day, Breast Cancer, Choose Life, Czech Heritage, Donate Life, Down Syndrome, Josh the Otter, Mountain Lion, Native American, Cornhusker Spirit, Nebraska History, Pets for Vets, Prostate Cancer, Wildlife, etc.). Czech Heritage plate fees go to the DMV Cash Fund. Nebraska Cornhusker Spirit Plates carry a $70 fee; 60% of that fee is credited to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund and 40% to the Spirit Plate Proceeds Fund. - Department of Health and Human Services: fees from Choose Life Plates are credited to the Health and Human Services Cash Fund to supplement TANF federal funds. - Department of Revenue: no changes or funding/appropriation actions evident in the added text. - Department of Veterans' Affairs: no direct appropriation or administrative duties specified. Pets for Vets Plates create proceeds for a Pets for Vets Cash Fund to support veterans, but no explicit transfer to the Department of Veterans’ Affairs is stated. - Additional: Home of Arbor Day Plate Cash Fund is created and administered by the University of Nebraska Board of Regents for arboretum grants.
109-1-LB569_IntroLB569_Intro_Copy.docxLB569 amends §38-1216 of the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act to add a statutory duty for the Nebraska Board of Emergency Medical Services to undertake a review and evaluation of the act and statewide emergency care needs and to submit an annual electronic report to the Nebraska Legislature. The required aggregate report items include: counts of EMS telephone/call volumes (by organizational status and primary caregiver level), regional average response times, patient age ranges, complaint types, provider impressions, patient dispositions, number of active Nebraska‑licensed EMS providers, and comparisons with other national regions or states. The bill repeals the prior version of §38-1216. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Requires an annual statewide report compiling aggregate EMS data for Nebraska, including: total EMS telephone calls; calls by EMS organizational status; calls by primary patient caregiver level of care; average regional response times; patient age ranges; nature of complaints; provider impressions; patient dispositions; number of active licensed EMS providers in Nebraska; and comparisons with other national regions/states. No specific government agency or department is named to produce the report, and no funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB56_IntroLB56_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationThe bill requires that information from post‑mortem alcohol/drug testing (for drivers or pedestrians who die within four hours of a motor vehicle crash) be included in reports under sections 60‑6,101 to 60‑6,104 and be tabulated monthly by the Department of Transportation. It specifies that this information — including the identity of the deceased and measured alcohol/drug levels — is public and may be released or disclosed as provided by the department. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Transportation are included.Adds a new subsection requiring medical facilities and mortuaries to comply with a peace officer’s request to draw blood from a driver or pedestrian described in subsection (1). No provisions reference the Department of Transportation, and the amendment contains no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations affecting DOT.
109-1-LB570_IntroLB570_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to award nursing scholarships of $2,500 per semester to students who meet specified eligibility (Nebraska residency; enrollment or intent to enroll in an approved in‑state nursing program leading to an associate degree, diploma, certificate, or accelerated BSN; intent to practice as an LPN, RN, or nurse aide; and a written two‑year work commitment in Nebraska), subject to available appropriations. The Legislature states intent to appropriate $5,000,000 to DHHS for fiscal year 2025–26 for this purpose.The Department of Health and Human Services will award $2,500 per semester scholarships to eligible nursing students, subject to available appropriations. Eligibility: Nebraska residency; enrollment or intent to enroll in an approved Nebraska nursing program (associate, diploma, certificate, or accelerated BSN); intent to practice as an LPN, RN, or nurse aide after program completion; and a written agreement to work in Nebraska for two years after completion. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate $5 million to DHHS for FY2025‑26 for this scholarship program.
109-1-LB571_IntroLB571_Intro_Copy.docxLB571 (2025) requires public power districts that operate a defined benefit pension plan to begin, January 1, 2026, paying a cost-of-living adjustment to retirees who are not eligible for Social Security. The adjustment must equal the annual COLA determined by the federal Social Security Administration. No state agencies other than public power districts and the federal SSA are referenced; the bill contains no express appropriations, funding allocations, or budgetary provisions.Effective Jan. 1, 2026, any public power district that operates a defined benefit pension plan must provide retirees who are not eligible for Social Security a cost‑of‑living adjustment equal to the annual COLA set by the federal Social Security Administration. The only federal agency mentioned is the Social Security Administration. The text does not include any specific funding, appropriation, or budget allocation language.
109-1-LB572_IntroLB572_Intro_Copy.docxLB572 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act to authorize school districts to exceed their general fund budget authority to cover stipends paid to student teachers or interns completing supervised practicums (defined in §79-875). It also amends the School District Property Tax Limitation Act to exempt the portion of a district’s property tax request needed to pay those stipends. The State Board of Education retains authority to approve, deny, or modify budget-exclusion amounts; the bill references the Department (Nebraska Department of Education) in other distance-education provisions. No specific appropriations or dollar amounts are set in the bill.Adds a permitted expenditure allowing funds described in subsection (a) or (b) to be used to pay stipends to student teachers or interns (as defined in §79‑875) who are completing a supervised teaching practicum in Nebraska public or private schools. The change references subdivision (1)(o) of §79‑1028.01. No specific dollar amounts, new appropriations, or agency budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB573_IntroLB573_Intro_Copy.docxLB573 creates the Meat and Poultry Workers and Contractors Protection Act. Key agency roles and actions: - The bill repeatedly tasks the "commissioner" (as used in the bill) to receive and investigate complaints, develop a compliance monitoring process within 90 days, assess civil penalties up to $15,000 for violations, and bring civil actions on behalf of aggrieved workers or contract growers. - Covered industrial operators must submit disaster mitigation plans to the commissioner and, after a disaster-mitigation event, provide workers and affected contract growers workers' compensation coverage, severance, and lost-revenue payments; violations trigger commissioner enforcement and private suits (unpaid compensation plus liquidated damages and attorney fees). - The commissioner must require operators with ≥25 employees to provide employees information about federal collective-bargaining/FLSA rights (29 C.F.R.; 29 U.S.C.). - The commissioner shall appoint a Workers and Contractors Task Force (specified membership including two nonvoting members from the Legislature’s Agriculture Committee) that reports annually to the commissioner and Legislature. No appropriations or agency budget allocations are specified.Creates enforcement and oversight duties for a state "commissioner" (investigate complaints, develop a compliance-monitoring process within 90 days, assess civil penalties up to $15,000, and bring court actions). References federal OSHA and the Nebraska Workers' Compensation Act for worker protections and compensation. Requires covered operators to submit disaster mitigation plans and provide worker severance/compensation and contract-grower lost‑revenue payments (private obligations). Requires employers with ≥25 employees to provide workers information on collective‑bargaining rights under 29 C.F.R. and the Fair Labor Standards Act. Establishes a Commissioner‑appointed Workers and Contractors Task Force (includes union and agricultural representatives, an attorney, and two nonvoting members from the Legislature’s Agriculture Committee) to meet regularly and report annually to the commissioner and Legislature. No state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB574_IntroLB574_Intro_Copy.docxLB574 establishes procedural rights and protections for certified firefighters and emergency personnel (including EMTs and paramedics) during formal investigations ordered by a commanding officer. Key provisions require written complaint summaries before interviews, audio-recording of interviews, confidentiality of complaint materials (unless disclosure is legally required or consented), notice of investigation outcomes, access to personnel and training records, representation by legal or union representatives, prohibition of compulsory polygraph exams, ability to seek damages for false complaints, grievance rights, access to mental health services, and employer obligations for safe working conditions, training, equipment, and support. No state agencies or departments are identified, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget allocations.Adds firefighter procedural and workplace rights: definitions; requirements for formal investigations (timely completion; written complaint summary before interviews; right to legal/union representation; audio-recorded interviews; written notice of outcomes; confidentiality of complaints/statements/recordings; ability to seek damages for false complaints; grievance review; no compelled polygraphs). Establishes rights to safe working conditions, training, equipment, support, and job-related mental health services; confidentiality of personal information; off-duty political activity; and access to personnel and training records. No specific government agencies or departments are named and no funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB575_IntroLB575_Intro_Copy.docxLB575 amends the Property Tax Request Act (77-1633) and property tax levy limits (77-3442). Key agency actions and fiscal effects: - County clerk: must organize joint public hearings (one per county) between July 14–24 after 6 p.m.; notify county assessor and participating political subdivisions by July 4. - County assessor: receive electronic submission of required information by July 4 and forward postcard data to a printing service designated by the county board. - County general fund: pays initial cost to print postcards; subsequent creation and mailing costs (including staff time, materials, postage) are charged proportionately to participating political subdivisions based on parcel counts. - Levy change: adds a cap requiring a political subdivision’s levy, when total taxable valuation rises, be limited so it raises no more property tax revenue than the prior year unless two-thirds of the governing body vote to exceed it. - Dept. of Natural Resources and DOT’s Division of Aeronautics remain referenced for existing levy exceptions. - Emergency clause: effective on enactment.Adds a new levy restriction (subsection (12)) on political subdivisions: if a subdivision’s total taxable valuation rises year-to-year, its property tax levy is capped at the amount required to raise the identical dollar amount of property tax revenue it raised the prior year. A subdivision may exceed that cap only by an affirmative two‑thirds vote of its governing body. References an exception in section 77‑3444. No specific state agencies or departments are named, and no direct appropriations, funding lines, or budget allocations are created—this is a constraint on local property tax revenue growth.
109-1-LB576_IntroLB576_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §86-903 to (1) require the Department of Revenue to determine the prepaid wireless surcharge annually (effective January 1) based on the charges described in subsection (2) as of the preceding July 1 and (2) require the Department to post at least 90 days' advance notice of any surcharge change on its website. It also requires the Department to provide prepaid wireless surcharge calculation and collection data to the Public Service Commission upon request. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department are included.Adds an appropriation of one dollar, under subsection (1), to maximize operational support for all public safety answering points (PSAPs) statewide. No other Department of Revenue funding changes, allocations, or budget details are specified.
109-1-LB577_IntroLB577_Intro_Copy.docxLB577 amends statutes (including sections 71-436.02 and 38-2847) affecting the Department of Health and Human Services to revise licensure and operational requirements for remote dispensing pharmacies. Changes require remote dispensing to occur under real-time audiovisual supervision by a Nebraska‑licensed pharmacist employed by a supervising pharmacy; dispensing must cease if the audiovisual link fails. The remote site must share the same pharmacist in charge as the supervising pharmacy, with that pharmacist ensuring at least one onsite visit per calendar month. The supervising pharmacist may delegate tasks but remains responsible for drug utilization review, final verification, supervision of remote dispensing, and must attempt counseling on all new prescriptions. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
