109-1-LB578_IntroLB578_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Correctional Services- Department of Correctional Services (DCS) - Committed offenders employed by DCS or others must be paid at least the state minimum/Wage and Hour Act levels (amends 83-183.01). - DCS must open deposit accounts for wage-earning committed offenders; adopt rules on labor conditions, due process, and restitution collection; treat sentencing restitution orders as authorizations to withhold/transfer funds; and report annually to the Legislature on restitution collection (83-183, 83-183.01, 83-184.01). - On release, offenders receive control of their deposit account funds (minimum one-third at release; full payment within six months) (83-187). - The Reentry Cash Fund is administered by DCS; funds credited pursuant to section 33-157 and donations and used for tuition, fees, and reentry/reintegration costs for offenders in the incarceration work camp (83-917). - Department of Labor - The bill cites the U.S. Department of Labor’s Dictionary of Occupational Titles for occupational classification under the Wage and Hour Act (48-1202(4)).- Extends Wage and Hour Act protections to inmate employment, explicitly including offenders employed by the Department of Correctional Services (DOC) and local jails — wages must meet or exceed Wage and Hour Act minimums. This treats the State and its political subdivisions (including DOC) as employers for those purposes. - Requires DOC to open deposit accounts for committed offenders earning wages (per §83-183.01) and directs that inmates be given full control of those accounts. - Requires DOC and jails to follow Occupational Safety and Health Act requirements and related regulations even if the federal law may not formally apply. - Establishes Jail Standards Board rules on hours, pay, due process, and restitution collection, plus annual electronic reporting to the Legislature; administrators must provide data to the board. - No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB579_IntroLB579_Intro_Copy.docxLB579 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§84-712 and 84-712.01 to (1) prohibit charging fees for public-record requests made by members of the Legislature and (2) impose timing requirements on custodians. Custodians (public bodies, public entities, public officials, and state agencies) must, within four business days of receiving a written request, provide an estimated cost and either access/copies (if equipment is available), a written denial with required information, or a written explanation when fulfillment cannot be completed within four business days, including the earliest practicable fulfillment date and a chance to narrow/prioritize the request. Requesters then have ten business days to respond; absent a response the custodian will not proceed. The bill also preserves that state agencies offering records via the §84-1204 portal obtain fee approval under §§84-1205.02–84-1205.03 and may include approved portal fees. No appropriations or budgetary allocations are contained.Adds language exempting members of the Legislature from fees for requests under this section — “No fee shall be charged under this section for a request made by a member of the Legislature,” with an exception referenced in subdivision (3)(i)/subsection (3). No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB57_IntroLB57_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB57 states the Legislature's intent to appropriate funds to the Department of Health and Human Services for Medicaid assisted‑living facility rates (Program No. 348). It specifies $7,926,576 for FY2025‑26 ( $3,345,808 General Funds; $4,580,768 Federal Funds) and $8,243,639 for FY2026‑27 ($3,479,640 General Funds; $4,763,999 Federal Funds). The amounts are designated to increase Program 348 Medicaid assisted‑living facility rates under Nebraska’s aged and disabled home and community‑based 1915(c) waiver to a daily rate of $88.24 for FY2025‑26 and $91.78 for FY2026‑27 for both rural and urban assisted‑living waiver days.Intent to appropriate to the Department of Health and Human Services: - FY2025-26: $7,926,576 total ( $3,345,808 General Fund; $4,580,768 Federal Funds). - FY2026-27: $8,243,639 total ( $3,479,640 General Fund; $4,763,999 Federal Funds). Funds are designated for Program 348 to raise Medicaid assisted‑living facility rates under Nebraska’s aged and disabled home-and-community‑based 1915(c) waiver to a daily rate of $88.24 in FY2025‑26 and $91.78 in FY2026‑27 for both rural and urban assisted‑living waiver days.
109-1-LB580_IntroLB580_Intro_Copy.docxLB580 reappropriates any remaining funds in the Lead Service Line Cash Fund to the Nebraska Department of Environment and Energy for FY2025‑26 to be used for lead service line replacements pursuant to Neb. Rev. Stat. §71‑5328. Remaining funds not allocated for qualified labor training organizations are reappropriated to the Department specifically to provide grants to metropolitan utilities districts for lead service line replacements under §71‑5328. The bill contains an emergency clause and takes effect upon enactment.Any remaining balances in the Lead Service Line Cash Fund are reappropriated for FY2025-26 to the Department of Environment and Energy to fund lead service line replacements under §71-5328. Remaining funds not reserved for qualified labor training organizations are similarly reappropriated to the Department to provide grants to metropolitan utilities districts for those replacements.
109-1-LB581_IntroLB581_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB581 appropriates $3,000,000 from the General Fund to the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services for FY2025‑26. The funds are designated for behavioral health services for youth in facilities that include an early childhood development center.Appropriates $3,000,000 General Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services for FY2025‑26. Funds are designated for behavioral health services for youth housed in a facility that includes an early childhood development center. This is a FY2025‑26 one‑year GF appropriation to DHHS.
109-1-LB582_IntroLB582_Intro_Copy.docxLB582 amends the Mechanical Amusement Device Tax Act and the Nebraska Tourism Commission Promotional Cash Fund statute. - Tax administration: Beginning July 1, 2025, distributors (or operators without a revenue-sharing distributor) must pay a quarterly tax on each cash device; the Tax Commissioner prescribes the reporting form and the department collects the tax. - Tax rate and allocations: 15% of net operating revenue per device. Receipts are remitted to the State Treasurer and credited: 5% to the Charitable Gaming Operations Fund (enforcement/central server), 2.5% to the Compulsive Gamblers Assistance Fund, 20% to the General Fund, 47.5% to the Education Future Fund, 17.5% to the Property Tax Credit Cash Fund, and the remaining 7.5% to the county treasurer where the device is located (split between county and city/village as applicable). - Tourism fund: The Nebraska Tourism Commission Promotional Cash Fund will consist of revenues submitted by vendors/retailers under section 81-3728 and advertising sales; the commission administers expenditures under the Nebraska Visitors Development Act and the state investment officer may invest fund balances. Operative Oct. 1, 2025; original sections repealed.The added language directs percentage-based allocations to the Education Future Fund. It lists several percentage figures (including 47.5%, 17.5%, 7.5% and other figures shown as 15, 5, and 20). No other government agencies or departments are named, and no specific dollar amounts, new appropriations, or overall budget totals are included.
109-1-LB583_IntroLB583_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue, Department of Veterans' Affairs, Military Department- Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): DHHS will administer the Child Care Grant Fund (funded in part by section 76-903) and award grants (up to $15,000) to licensed child care providers, community organizations, or schools; DHHS also houses the Medicaid Fraud Settlement Fund and 25% (and a 5% category) of the state portion is transferred to the Health Care Homes for the Medically Underserved Fund, which the bill also makes eligible to receive documentary-stamp-tax receipts under section 76-903. - Department of Veterans' Affairs (DVA) / Military Department: DVA will administer the Military Installation Development and Support Fund (receiving section 76-903 receipts), must require at least a 50% match for projects, and ensure at least $100,000/year to DVA for a statewide skillbridge strategy and $100,000/year to community providers of veteran mental-health services. "Military installation" explicitly includes facilities under the Nebraska Military Department. - Department of Economic Development (DED): DED will administer the Affordable Housing Trust Fund (receiving section 76-903 receipts) and may prioritize projects funded from the Economic Recovery Contingency Fund. - Department of Revenue: Tax Commissioner/Department of Revenue will design documentary-stamp tax stamps and may issue declaratory rulings; the department may not overturn a county assessor's sale qualification without review confirming an error. - Funding allocations from the $3.30 documentary-stamp tax (per section 76-903): $1.05 to Affordable Housing Trust Fund; $0.25 to Site and Building Development Fund; $0.25 to Homeless Shelter Assistance Trust Fund; $0.40 to Behavioral Health Services Fund; $0.05 to Economic Recovery Contingency Fund; $0.05 to Military Installation Development and Support Fund; $0.05 to Innovation Hub Cash Fund; $0.05 to Health Care Homes for the Medically Underserved Fund; $0.40 to Child Care Grant Fund. - Economic Recovery Contingency Fund transfers (timed): $30 million to Inland Port Authority Fund (by five business days after April 17, 2024); $750,000 to Museum Construction and Maintenance Fund (by Dec 31, 2024); $15 million (by Dec 31, 2025); $7 million (Jan–Jun 2026); remaining unobligated funds on July 31, 2026, to Inland Port Authority Fund.- Department of Health and Human Services: Child Care Grant Fund expanded to fund licensed child-care providers for staff retention/recruitment incentives and capital expenses; DHHS must contract with a statewide organization to run application, review and technical assistance. Behavioral Health Services Fund and Health Care Homes for the Medically Underserved Fund also receive dedicated transfers. - Department of Veterans' Affairs: receives at least $100,000/year to contract with community organizations to create a statewide SkillBridge/attraction program for veterans; an additional ≥$100,000/year is directed to veteran mental‑health services via community organizations. - Military Department / Military Installation Development and Support Fund: receives a dedicated allocation (0.05 per dollar) to support community organizations serving veterans per subsection (2) of §55‑901. - Department of Revenue: identified as the source of transfers (sec. 76‑903 and §43‑2623) that allocate specified per‑dollar shares among multiple funds. - Department of Economic Development: a 0.05 per‑dollar allocation is directed to an Economic Recovery Contingency Fund to establish/operate an office to pursue and coordinate grant funding on behalf of the state (funding allocation noted; administering agency not specified).
109-1-LB584_IntroLB584_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB584 authorizes (section 29-2204(5)) a court that wants more detailed information before imposing sentence to commit an offender to the Department of Correctional Services. While so committed, the Department must conduct a complete study of the offender as provided in section 29-2204.03. The bill contains no provisions altering funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services.Summary for Department of Correctional Services: - The bill revises felony sentencing language for Classes IA, IB, IC, ID, II and IIA (clarifying maximum and minimum terms) and adds a new subsection requiring that when the offender was under 18 at the time of the offense, the court must set the sentence's minimum and maximum as provided by section 28-105.02. - No provisions in the added text alter funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services.
109-1-LB585_IntroLB585_Intro_Copy.docxLB585 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-2404.02 to adjust Community-based Juvenile Services Aid Program administration and funding. It preserves a 10% General Fund set‑aside (excluding administrative funds) for a common data set and evaluation—allocated between the commission and the University of Nebraska at Omaha, Juvenile Justice Institute (UNO JJI) per historical percentages—and adds a second 10% set‑aside for grants to community-based organizations located in qualified census tracts with annual budgets ≤ $1 million that prevent juvenile crime prior to justice-system involvement. The remainder is apportioned by commission rule using a county/tribal youth population formula; the commission may require up to a 5% local match. The commission maintains the data set and provides it to UNO JJI for evaluation. Rulemaking and reporting obligations involve the commission, UNO JJI, Office of Probation Administration, directors of relevant juvenile programs, and the Nebraska Association of County Officials.- Allocates 10% of the annual General Fund appropriation to the Community‑based Juvenile Services Aid Program (excluding administrative funds) to grant-making for community‑based organizations located in IRS-defined qualified census tracts (26 U.S.C. 42(d)(5)(B)(ii)(I) as of Jan 1, 2025) with annual budgets ≤ $1 million, focused on preventing juvenile crime before system involvement. - Establishes distribution criteria to prioritize organizations with staff who have lived juvenile‑justice experience, smaller budgets, location in qualified census tracts, and the demographics of populations served. - Directs the University of Nebraska at Omaha, Juvenile Justice Institute, to assist grant recipients in developing logic models and evaluation measures to assess program impact.
109-1-LB586_IntroLB586_Intro_Copy.docxLB586 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §32-944 (Election Act) to require county sheriffs and directors or designated staff of city/county jails and detention centers to implement facility-specific plans ensuring voting access for individuals unable to vote in person. Plans must address training, notification of voting/registration/curing procedures, reasonable access, a designated jail location for ballot return (collected by two registered voters of different parties), and deadlines. County election commissioners or county clerks must adopt procedures consistent with the Election Act and rules of the Secretary of State. Noncompliance by a sheriff or facility director is subject to a civil penalty set by the district court and payable by the county. The bill repeals the original §32-944. No funding or appropriations are included.Requires county sheriffs (or facility directors/designated staff) to: provide jailed eligible voters access to verify/change/register to vote, supply information on ballot-return methods/locations/deadlines, provide a jail location where ballots may be returned to two registered voters of different parties, and offer a process to cure ballot deficiencies. Election commissioners or county clerks must adopt procedures consistent with the Election Act and rules promulgated by the Secretary of State. Noncompliance by a county sheriff/director/designated staff is subject to a civil penalty set by the district court where the jail is located, payable by the county. No new appropriations or budget allocations are specified beyond the county-payable civil penalty.
109-1-LB587_IntroLB587_Intro_Copy.docxLB587 amends Nebraska’s Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act to shorten tenant termination timelines and expand tenant remedies for landlord noncompliance. Key changes: shortens the repeat‑breach termination notice to seven days; clarifies termination procedures if a landlord remedies a breach before the termination date; adds landlord failures to remediate known mold or pest infestations to the list of breaches; authorizes tenants to purchase remediation supplies/services and deduct actual costs from rent; allows recovery for diminution in rental value and for damage to tenant personal property; excuses rent during noncompliance; and permits recovery of substitute‑housing costs and attorney’s fees for deliberate failures. No state agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget provisions.Adds tenant remedies when a landlord fails to remediate a known mold problem or pest infestation: tenants may purchase supplies or services to remediate and deduct actual, reasonable costs from rent, and may recover damages for diminution in value of their personal property caused by the landlord's deliberate or negligent noncompliance. The text also clarifies applicability of the remedies subsections. No government agencies, departments, or budget/appropriation changes are mentioned.
109-1-LB588_IntroLB588_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §43-512 to specify Department of Health and Human Services (department) responsibilities: accepting written applications for aid to dependent children; conducting investigations and referring findings to the county or authorized attorney where parental support is available; and determining allowance and monthly assistance amounts. Payments remain by unit size per §68-1713, and beginning September 10, 2025 the maximum monthly payment level is to be calculated and tied to the annual inflation factor. The department must adopt rules providing services to prevent dependency, establish work incentive/ training programs, and issue rules implementing transitional benefits (five-month transitional payments, child care, and up to 12 months medical assistance) consistent with federal law. Authorized attorneys may be department employees. No appropriations or budget allocations are specified.The added language sets a specific effective/calculation date of September 10, 2025 and requires the referenced value to be adjusted annually using the statutory "annual inflation factor." There is no explicit appropriation, new funding amount, or budget allocation for the Department of Health and Human Services in this underlined text. In short: procedural indexing to inflation beginning 9/10/2025; no direct DHHS funding change included.
109-1-LB589_IntroLB589_Intro_Copy.docxLB589 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-1142. Key agency actions and fiscal changes: - State Board of Education: establishes the percentage cap for support‑service reimbursable costs (not to exceed 10% minus the Legislature’s set‑aside percentage). - Department (Nebraska Department of Education): reimburses school districts, cooperatives, and ESUs 80% of total allowable excess special‑education costs; may prorate payments if General Fund appropriations (minus set‑asides) are insufficient, with remaining portions of the 80% drawn from the Education Future Fund. - State Treasurer and Director of Administrative Services: Treasurer certifies available General Fund and Education Future Fund balances monthly; Director draws warrants for payments. - Department must set aside separate appropriation amounts for special‑education and support‑service reimbursements based on estimates and may audit claims. - Districts must provide four days professional leave for special‑education staff (supported by substitutes). - Department must report annually (by Nov. 15) to the Governor and the Appropriations and Education Committees on costs and reimbursements. - Repeals the original section.Adds that substitute costs tied to special education programs are allowable and reimbursable. Requires each school district to provide special education staff four days per year of on-site professional leave, supported by substitute personnel, solely to complete essential documentation for students on their caseloads. No specific state agency is named and no dollar amounts or new appropriations are specified.
109-1-LB58_FinalLB58_Final_Copy.docxLB58 repeals Nebraska's statutory provisions governing jeweler's liens by outright repealing sections 52-301, 52-302, 52-303, and 52-304, Reissue Revised Statutes of Nebraska. No state agency or department is referenced in the bill. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB590_IntroLB590_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationThe bill authorizes the Department of Transportation to, by rule and regulation, establish, use, and operate a mitigation bank or an in-lieu fee program in accordance with applicable state and federal law. The program’s stated purpose is to provide compensatory mitigation for incidental take of threatened or endangered species and their habitat. The statute also requires that a state or local agency or private party that owns a mitigation bank pay a sum in lieu of ad valorem taxes lost by the county. The bill contains no direct appropriations or other budget allocations to the Department of Transportation.Department of Transportation is authorized to adopt rules to establish, operate, and use a mitigation bank or in‑lieu fee program consistent with state and federal law to provide compensatory mitigation for incidental take of threatened/endangered species and their habitat from permitted activities. The program’s purpose includes restoring, creating, enhancing, or preserving habitat, applying fair and practicable mitigation ratios to offset project impacts, and achieving a net increase in conservation functions and values for affected species and resources. Financially, owners of mitigation banks (state/local agencies or private parties) that acquire land for habitat purposes must pay a sum in lieu of ad valorem taxes to compensate counties for lost property tax revenue. No direct DOT appropriations or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB591_IntroLB591_Intro_Copy.docxLB591 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§45‑1003 and 45‑1004 to expand licensing requirements under the Nebraska Installment Loan Act. It requires any person (not a financial institution) who, at or after the time a loan is made by a financial institution, markets, owns, holds, acquires or services that loan to obtain a license. It also clarifies that a license from the department is required to make installment loans or to service, hold or acquire ownership interests in such loans or otherwise engage with borrowers. The bill exempts affiliates whose in‑state activities are limited solely to securitization where servicing rights remain with the licensee or transfer to a financial institution, licensee, or permittee, and defines “affiliate” and “control.” No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds the short phrase "or that services, or interest ," to the bill text. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in this addition.
109-1-LB592_FinalLB592_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesThe bill requires the State Treasurer and the Accounting Administrator of the Department of Administrative Services to determine the appropriate state fund types for the ABLE program to comply with federal law and state policy. It directs the State Treasurer to annually report, prior to transferring funds, the amounts transferred from the ABLE Expense Fund to the State Investment Officer's Cash Fund to the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services (and electronically to the Legislative Fiscal Analyst). Program startup and operating costs are to be paid from the Treasury Management Cash Fund (and transfers from the expense fund as permitted), in amounts authorized by legislative appropriation.The added clause makes amounts in the referenced account immune from levy, execution, judgment, garnishment or other judicial seizure to satisfy debts of the account’s beneficiary or owner. It is an asset-protection provision that overrides other law. There are no provisions in this text altering Department of Administrative Services funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB593_FinalLB593_Final_Copy.docxLB593 (introduced by Sen. Moser; Natural Resources Committee) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §66‑1226 to adopt updated standards for automotive spark‑ignition engine fuel and repeals the original section. The provided text names no state agency or department responsible for implementation, and it contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB594_IntroLB594_Intro_Copy.docxLB594 amends §60‑6,179.01 regarding handheld wireless device use while driving. Exemptions explicitly apply to personnel performing official duties: law enforcement officers, firefighters, ambulance drivers, and emergency medical technicians; employees or contractors of utility service providers responding to utility emergencies; and drivers communicating with emergency services during an emergency. The section does not apply to commercial motor vehicle operators where §60‑6,179.02 governs. Violations remain traffic infractions with points assessed on the operator’s license pursuant to §60‑4,182 and fines of $200 (first), $300 (second), and $500 (third+). No state agency appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds exceptions to the ban on physically holding or supporting a handheld wireless device while driving: exempts employees or contractors of utility service providers responding to utility emergencies and persons communicating or attempting to communicate with emergency services. Also clarifies the prohibition does not apply when the device is used without touching it or to initiate a function with a single touch. No government agencies or departments are named and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.
109-1-LB595_IntroLB595_Intro_Copy.docxCreates the Research Excellence Cash Fund to be administered by the University of Nebraska. The fund will consist of gifts, grants, bequests, and transfers authorized by the Legislature and may be used to support research-based investments in data, data collection, and ongoing research important to the Nebraska economy (explicitly including the Nebraska Mesonet). Any fund balances available for investment are to be managed by the state investment officer pursuant to the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. No specific dollar appropriations are included. The bill takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.Creates the Research Excellence Cash Fund, to be administered by the University of Nebraska. The fund will consist of gifts, grants, bequests, and transfers authorized by the Legislature and may be used for research investments in data, data collection, and ongoing research critical to Nebraska’s economy (explicitly including the Nebraska Mesonet). Any funds available for investment must be invested by the state investment officer pursuant to the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. No specific appropriation amounts are provided.
109-1-LB596_IntroLB596_Intro_Copy.docxLB596 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §25-2228 to recognize publication of legally required notices on websites or applications of digital news publications that do not have a print edition and to treat such online publication for the required number of days/weeks as legally sufficient. It retains that notices may continue to be published in newspapers and reiterates the existing requirement (effective Oct. 1, 2022) that newspapers or digital news publications post notices on a statewide repository website established and maintained by a majority of Nebraska newspapers; failure to post there does not invalidate a notice. The bill repeals the original section. No state agencies or departments are named, and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds language allowing required notices or publications to be met by posting on a digital news publication’s website or application for the prescribed number of days or weeks (including when no print edition exists). No government agencies, departments, or changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are referenced.
109-1-LB597_IntroLB597_Intro_Copy.docxLB597 amends the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act and assigns actions to multiple state agencies. - State Department of Education: determine and certify state aid to the Director of Administrative Services, Auditor of Public Accounts and local systems (certification dates set June 15, 2025 and March 1 thereafter) and report required funding to the Governor, Appropriations Committee and Education Committee. - Education Future Fund: fund 24% of total foundation aid. - Property Tax Administrator / Tax Commissioner: county assessors to certify taxable value by Aug. 20 (amendments by Aug. 31); PTA to certify adjusted valuations by Oct. 10; Tax Commissioner to hear objections, certify corrections by Jan. 1, and permit appeals to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission. - Director of Administrative Services: draw warrants for lump‑sum state aid upon State Board approval. Fiscal changes: foundation aid (through 2024-25: $1,500 per formula student; from 2025-26 onward: greater of $1,500 per student or 7.5% of basic funding); inclusion of foundation aid as a formula resource reduced to 60% from 2025-26; agricultural land adjusted valuation reduced from 72% to 65% from 2025-26; local effort rate for certification reduced by ten cents beginning 2025-26. Certifications for 2025-26 completed before the act’s effective date are null and void.Adds new school-aid mechanics effective FY2025-26. Foundation aid to each school district will be the greater of $1,500 per formula student or 7.5% of basic funding under §79-1007.16. For state aid certification (§79-1022) the local effort rate is set at the maximum levy under §77-3442(2)(a) minus $0.10; for final aid calculations (§79-1065) the local effort rate is the rate that, when multiplied by total adjusted valuation of taxable property in local systems receiving equalization aid under the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act (TEEOSA), yields the amount needed when combined with state appropriations and other actual local receipts (§79-1018.01). "Local effort rate yield" is defined as each local system’s adjusted valuation times that rate. Adjusted valuation for FY2025-26 onward is fixed at 65% of actual value (§77-1359/77-1363) and 65% of special valuation (§77-1343). The Legislature is referenced as the source of state appropriations.
109-1-LB598_IntroLB598_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB598 assigns several specific roles to the Department of Administrative Services (DAS). The State Department of Education must certify state aid amounts to the Director of Administrative Services on or before June 15, 2025, and March 1 annually. The State Treasurer is directed to transfer $1.0 billion (FY2023‑24) and $250 million (FY2024‑25) from the General Fund to the Education Future Fund on dates and in amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of DAS; the bill expresses intent for $250 million annually thereafter. For special education reimbursements, the State Treasurer notifies the Director of Administrative Services of available funds in the General and Education Future Funds, and the Director draws warrants against those appropriations.No provisions in the added text change duties, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Administrative Services. Substantive additions affect the Department of Education: school districts may apply (by Jan 15) for Education Future Fund payments to cover extraordinary limited-English-proficiency (LEP) costs, with a formula-based maximum payment and pro rata reduction if fund balance is insufficient; payments issued by Jan 31. Beginning FY 2025‑26, the department must also reimburse districts/cooperatives for additional costs of students served under Section 504 at the same percentage used for special education reimbursement, establish reporting/documentation procedures, and treat this as additional (not replacement) funding.
109-1-LB599_IntroLB599_Intro_Copy.docxLB599 (2025) directs the Nebraska State Board of Education to adopt a prescribed cybersecurity policy applicable to schools. The bill identifies the State Board of Education as the responsible agency for promulgating that policy. No other state agencies are named, and the bill as provided contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB59_FinalLB59_Final_Copy.docxLB59 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §2-3224 governing natural resources districts. It authorizes district funds to be disbursed not only by written instrument signed by the treasurer (or an authorized designee) but also by electronic payment systems, explicitly including electronic funds transfers and automated clearinghouse transfers. The bill requires any written authorization permitting another to sign for the treasurer be filed with the district secretary. If the treasurer’s bond does not cover losses caused by authorized signatories, a corporate surety bond must be procured and filed, approved by two district officers other than the treasurer. The secretary must report bond filings or changes at each board meeting. The original section is repealed. No appropriations or budget allocations are included.Adds language specifying acceptable payment methods—either a check signed by the treasurer or use of electronic payment systems including electronic funds transfers and automated clearinghouse transfers—and provisions allowing the treasurer to authorize another person to sign on the treasurer’s behalf. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB5_IntroLB5_Intro_Copy.docxLB5 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-470 to broaden legal immunity for use, prescribing, dispensing, and administration of opioid antagonists (e.g., naloxone) and defines covered actors and entities. It protects: health professionals licensed under the Uniform Credentialing Act; family/friends and school personnel who obtain/administer an opioid antagonist; emergency responders (licensed under the Emergency Medical Services Practice Act or via the EMS Interstate Compact) using supplies from their EMS organization; and peace officers or law enforcement employees using agency-provided supplies. Protected persons are immune from administrative action, criminal prosecution, and (with exceptions for willful, wanton, or gross negligence) personal civil liability. The bill defines law enforcement agencies (police departments, town marshals, sheriffs, Nebraska State Patrol) and law enforcement employees, and clarifies that organizational liability is not affected. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included. The prior section is repealed.Adds a definition of "opioid antagonist" to mean naloxone hydrochloride or any opioid antagonist approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration for emergency reversal of known or suspected opioid overdose. No government funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB600_IntroLB600_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationKey Department of Transportation (DOT) provisions in LB600: - DOT (or its agents) may remove vehicles/objects from highways/shoulders without owner consent when impeding traffic and is immune from liability for damage. - DOT may reduce maximum lawful speed limits (temporarily) for weather, traction, emergencies, or congestion; such reductions require electronic/digital signage, five-mph increments, no minimum speed during reductions, and DOT must adopt policy, keep records (including per-highway limits and changes), and may promulgate rules. - DOT may enforce school-crossing and highway-work-zone speed limits using speed control enforcement systems and may contract with certified operators. - DOT (or local authorities) shall assess civil penalties for camera-enforced violations; DOT must create guidance for administrative fee calculation. - DOT must erect/maintain signage on controlled-access highways regarding yielding to stopped vehicles. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Summary (Department of Transportation): - DOT may remove vehicles/objects obstructing highways or shoulders and is not liable for removal damage. - DOT may temporarily lower posted speed limits for fog, precipitation, smoke, dust, traction issues, emergencies, or congestion; reductions must be displayed on electronic/digital signs, set in 5 mph increments, with no minimum speed, and DOT must adopt policy, keep records, and may adopt rules. - DOT may use (or authorize/contract for) photographic/radar/laser speed-control systems to enforce school crossing and highway work-zone speeds subject to conditions (active school warning lights or presence of workers, signage). Thresholds: citations for >6 mph over in school zones, >11 mph over in work zones. - Systems require independent annual calibration and operator daily logs. Civil penalties are assessed and remitted to the State Treasurer. - No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DOT are specified.
109-1-LB601_IntroLB601_Intro_Copy.docxLB601 (DeBoer) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29‑2101 to clarify and enumerate the statutory grounds for granting a new trial after a conviction, explicitly listing: procedural irregularity or abuse of discretion; misconduct by the jury, prosecutor, or state witnesses; accident or unavoidable surprise; verdicts unsupported by sufficient evidence or contrary to law; newly discovered evidence; newly discovered exculpatory DNA or similar forensic testing evidence obtained under the DNA Testing Act; and errors of law. The bill was referred to the Judiciary Committee and repeals the original section. No executive agencies or departments are created or altered, and the bill contains no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations.The added text contains only the words "Misconduct Accident The Newly Newly Error." It does not mention any government agencies or departments, nor does it create or change any funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. No substantive policymaking or administrative directives are contained in the addition.
109-1-LB602_IntroLB602_Intro_Copy.docxLB602 (the "Delete Act") assigns primary administrative duties to the Nebraska Secretary of State and enforcement to the Attorney General. The Secretary of State must: maintain a public registry of data brokers (annual registration by Jan. 31; fee set by the Secretary, not to exceed $300); publish registration and deletion-mechanism information on its website; establish an accessible statewide deletion mechanism by Jan. 1, 2028 (features, security, free consumer access); select independent third-party auditors for triennial audits of data brokers and receive audit reports; adopt rules to implement the Act; and may charge data brokers an access fee limited to the Secretary's reasonable costs. The Attorney General may seek civil penalties, injunctive relief, and recover attorney fees and costs for violations. Civil penalties include $200 per day to the Secretary of State for each deletion request a data broker fails to complete; other registration-related penalties are referenced. No direct appropriations are specified.Adds duties for the Secretary of State and enforcement powers for the Attorney General. Key changes affecting agencies: - Secretary of State must publish data-broker registration info and create an accessible deletion mechanism by Jan 1, 2028 (security, accessibility, authorized‑agent support, consumer interfaces, auditing support). - Data brokers must annually register with the Secretary of State (by Jan 31), pay a fee up to $300, provide breach/audit/metric disclosures, and use the deletion mechanism beginning Aug 1, 2028. - The Secretary of State may charge data brokers an access fee limited to the agency's reasonable costs, select independent auditors, adopt rules, and receive civil‑penalty payments ($200/day per uncompleted deletion request). - The Attorney General may collect civil penalties, seek injunctive relief, and recover attorney fees. No general appropriations or budget line‑item allocations are added; provisions authorize user fees and penalties only.
109-1-LB603_IntroLB603_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB603 assigns several explicit responsibilities to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). DHHS will determine the poverty level used (including any federal poverty index or similar guideline) for client contribution determinations and must adopt and promulgate the client family income schedule as departmental rules and regulations. DHHS may reimburse care management units; reimbursement is to be based on actual casework time units and may include personnel, administration and planning, client eligibility review, contractual services, support services, and other direct and indirect costs. DHHS must adopt standardized reimbursement rates and adjust them at least every three years. Appropriations for DHHS reimbursement of services under sections 81-2229 to 81-2235 and for DHHS program administration must be made separately from funds under the Nebraska Community Aging Services Act.Department of Health and Human Services: Adds authority for care management clients to make voluntary contributions toward the cost of care management services (per section 81-2230). DHHS must use a client family income schedule based on federal poverty guidelines to determine each client's contribution. No specific appropriations, funding allocations, or dollar amounts are included; the provision establishes a cost-sharing mechanism but does not itself authorize or change state budget appropriations.
109-1-LB604_IntroLB604_Intro_Copy.docxLB604 amends initiative and referendum procedures in Nebraska statutes, reallocating duties among state officers and clarifying judicial review. Key agency provisions: - Secretary of State: receives sponsor filings and sworn statements; transmits proposed text to the Revisor of Statutes; keeps filings confidential for five days after revisor review; prepares petition form within five business days of final language; posts measure text and circulation notice on the Secretary of State website until the filing deadline; must announce and state reasons when refusing placement on the ballot for non-signature legal insufficiencies. - Revisor of Statutes: reviews proposed measures and suggests form/draftsmanship changes within ten business days. - Courts: Lancaster County district court has primary jurisdiction for related litigation; suits challenging placement (non-signature issues) have tightened timing and party-join rules; the Supreme Court may exercise original jurisdiction when practicable. Administrative Procedure Act appeal procedures do not apply. No funding, appropriation, or budget changes are included.Adds procedural requirements for the Secretary of State and court review: - Secretary of State must post the measure text and a notice that it is in circulation on the Secretary of State's website until the petition-filing deadline. If the Secretary of State refuses to place a measure on the ballot for any legal insufficiency other than lack of signatures, the refusal and its reason must be announced the same day as the circulation posting; failure to state the reason waives those defenses. - Suits alleging legal insufficiency (other than signature insufficiency) must be filed within 60 days of the circulation posting (or by the petition filing deadline if the 60th day falls after that deadline). The Nebraska Supreme Court shall, if practicable and upon petition, hear non‑signature insufficiency cases under its original jurisdiction (see section 24‑204). - Parties and officials may raise substantive facial insufficiency claims without dismissal for lack of ripeness. The section does not limit other post‑enactment suits. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB605_IntroLB605_Intro_Copy.docxLB605 requires each school board to adopt a policy governing student participation as a transgender student in school-sponsored extracurricular activities and in activities governed by any athletics or activities association of which the school is a member. Under the policy school administrators or athletic directors must submit a written application from the student (and parent/guardian) and supporting documentation to the school board; the board must determine eligibility—generally based on biological sex on the student's birth certificate unless approved as a transgender participant—and, where applicable, submit required documentation to and cooperate with the athletics/activities association for its eligibility determination. The bill disclaims encouraging medical treatment and does not alter existing cross-gender participation exceptions. No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds requirements that local school boards (based on information provided by the school administrator or athletic director) determine and document transgender students' eligibility for extracurriculars and, when necessary, submit and cooperate with any athletics or activities association to which the school belongs. Permitted shared documentation includes current school registration, a written statement from the student and parent/guardian, and corroborating statements from others (parents, teachers, friends). Establishes that eligibility for male/female-separated teams defaults to the biological sex on the student's birth certificate unless the student is approved under the board's transgender or cross‑gender policy. Clarifies the policy does not encourage medical transition and does not alter cross‑gender exceptions when no female team exists. No agencies beyond school boards, school administrators/athletic directors, and athletics/activities associations are added, and no funding or appropriations are included.
109-1-LB606_IntroLB606_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of RevenueLB606 centralizes parole and community supervision authority in the Department of Correctional Services (DCS), abolishing the Division of Parole Supervision and its director and expanding DCS duties (custody, parole administration, recordkeeping, risk‑and‑needs assessment, training, reentry planning, sanctions, officer responsibilities). DCS must set standards and monitor community correctional facilities and reporting centers, may contract with private providers for work‑release/reentry centers, and collect/share parole data. Parole programming fees are credited to a Parole Program Cash Fund controlled by DCS. The Legislature intends a $1,000,000 General Fund appropriation for the Community Work Release and Reentry Centers Act. The Department of Health and Human Services may release health/social‑services records for overdose fatality reviews or licensing subpoenas subject to HIPAA and other federal limits, with requests due within 30 days (extensions allowed); subpoenas may be issued by a county attorney or the Attorney General. The Department of Revenue’s employees are excluded from the statute’s definition of “law enforcement officer.”Department of Correctional Services: New language requires the department to maintain all records and files for the Board of Parole, including records for individuals under lifetime community supervision (sec. 83-174.03), while clarifying it may still keep daily records/files for the Board of Pardons. Provisions also authorize DOC to assess and implement operational, treatment, medical, or vocational programming in facilities when such services will substantially improve an offender’s capacity for law‑abiding reentry. Department of Health and Human Services & Department of Revenue: No substantive additions or funding, appropriation, or budget allocations affecting these agencies appear in the added text.
109-1-LB607_IntroLB607_Intro_Copy.docxLB607 makes the Department of Environment and Energy (DENE) the primary implementing, oversight, and enforcement agency for battery stewardship, disposal‑fee changes, and the Minimum Recycled Content/Extended Producer Responsibility Data Collection Acts. DENE may adopt rules, approve stewardship plans, maintain a public producer list, set program fees to cover implementation, assess and collect penalties (battery: up to $1,000/day, $10,000/day for repeat violations; recycled‑content: initial $0.20/lb with a price‑based formula after 1/1/2029), and oversee manufacturer registration/reporting (reports due 1/1/2027; third‑party recycled‑content certification by 2028). Appeals go to the Environmental Quality Council; DENE may recover cleanup costs via civil action in Lancaster County District Court. Disposal fees rise (2026–2028) with revenues split 50/50 to the Integrated Solid Waste Management Cash Fund and the Waste Reduction and Recycling Incentive Fund; political subdivision reimbursements capped at 5% of prior‑year disposal‑fee revenue. DENE may deduct admin costs, award grants (including up to $1.5M/year for scrap tire projects through 6/30/2029), accept gifts, and remit penalties to the State Treasurer. Act operative Jan 1, 2026.Adds repeated central roles for the Department of Environment and Energy (and its Director): rulemaking, plan approval, enforcement, fee-setting, reporting, assessments, and posting data online. The department must establish annual fees charged to battery stewardship organizations to fully cover its implementation/enforcement costs and may set/modify a $1,000 annual manufacturer registration fee (waivers for de minimis manufacturers). Battery stewardship organizations must reimburse local governments for demonstrable collection costs and provide free collection materials/training. A disposal-fee schedule is added ($2.25 in 2026; $3.25 in 2027; $4.25 in 2028). Civil penalties (various caps) are assessed by the department and remitted to the State Treasurer; appeals go to the Environmental Quality Council. EPA nonwaste determinations are referenced.
109-1-LB608A_IntroLB608A_Intro_Copy.docxLB608A appropriates General Fund dollars to the Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education (CCPE), Program 692, to implement Legislative Bill 608. It provides $781,647 GF for FY2025‑26 and $1,351,495 GF for FY2026‑27, with both fiscal-year amounts designated solely for state aid. The appropriation explicitly prohibits using these funds for permanent or temporary salaries and per diems for state employees.Appropriates General Fund dollars to the Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education (Program 692) to implement Legislative Bill 608: $781,647 for FY2025-26 and $1,351,495 for FY2026-27. Each fiscal-year appropriation is explicitly designated for state aid only. The funds may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB608_FinalLB608_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Revenue- The bill defines a correctional officer as someone employed full-time by a jail or by the Department of Correctional Services. - The Department of Revenue is assigned administration and enforcement of the First Responder Recruitment and Retention Act, including rulemaking authority. Applicants and tuition-waiver recipients must file documentation with the Department of Revenue proving employment, eligible-disabled status, or Nebraska residency (via annual tax returns). Institutions must provide lists of tuition-waiver recipients to the Department of Revenue, which will maintain records and, by August 1 each year, report recipients who failed to file residency tax returns. - Funding: Beginning July 1, 2028, subject to available appropriations, the Coordinating Commission for Postsecondary Education shall reimburse state universities for 50% of tuition waivers granted the prior year for correctional officers, youth detention officers, formerly employed eligible-disabled persons, and their qualifying children. Reimbursements require commission-approved documentation and will be prorated if appropriations are insufficient.- Department of Correctional Services: The bill adds/defines "correctional officer" as a full‑time employee of a jail or the Department of Correctional Services and explicitly includes correctional officers (and youth detention officers) among eligible first responders for tuition waivers. Tuition waivers for current or formerly employed correctional/youth detention officers and their qualifying children are limited to state university attendance beginning July 1, 2027. - Department of Revenue: Applicants (first responders, eligible disabled persons, and qualifying children) must annually file documentation with the Department of Revenue proving employment/status and Nebraska residency to receive/renew waivers. - Funding: Beginning July 1, 2028, subject to appropriations, the Coordinating Commission will reimburse state universities 50% of those waivers (prior year), with claims prorated if appropriations are insufficient.
109-1-LB609A_FinalLB609A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Banking and FinanceAppropriates to the Department of Banking and Finance (Program 65) funds to implement Legislative Bill 609: $232,777 from the Financial Institution Assessment Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 and $185,061 from the same fund for FY2026‑27. Expenditure caps on permanent and temporary salaries and per diems charged to these appropriated funds are $85,000 for FY2025‑26 and $87,125 for FY2026‑27.Appropriates funds to the Department of Banking and Finance, Program 65, from the Financial Institution Assessment Cash Fund: $232,777 for FY2025‑26 and $185,061 for FY2026‑27 to implement Legislative Bill 609 (2025). Sets limits on permanent/temporary salaries and per diems charged to these appropriations: not to exceed $85,000 in FY2025‑26 and $87,125 in FY2026‑27.
109-1-LB609_FinalLB609_Final_Copy.docxLB609 creates the Controllable Electronic Record Fraud Prevention Act and assigns enforcement and oversight roles to state entities. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General must publish model notice language for gift‑card fraud warnings and may issue written citations; repeat violators face civil penalties up to $250 (first citation is a warning). The bill requires controllable electronic record kiosks and receipts to display contact information for relevant state or local law enforcement agencies and government agencies for reporting fraud. An unspecified “department” is given authority to require additional disclosures, request evidence of blockchain‑analytics use, and set other information requirements. The bill also amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §29‑817 to include “controllable electronic records” as property for search‑warrant purposes. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds requirements that controllable electronic record kiosk operators must display and provide contact information for the operator and "relevant state or local law enforcement agency or government agency" for reporting fraud, and that the (unnamed) department may require additional disclosures and request evidence of operators' use of blockchain analytics. Operators must maintain toll-free live customer service hours and a daily-monitored law‑enforcement contact method. Also requires a full‑time compliance officer and written antifraud policies; sets transaction limits and fee caps. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General must release model notice language for gift‑card fraud warnings, and the Attorney General may issue citations and civil penalties (up to $250 after multiple citations). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB60_IntroLB60_Intro_Copy.docxLB60 (2025) amends section 9-829 of the State Lottery Act to permit sale of lottery tickets via vending or dispensing devices by authorized lottery game retailers. The bill retains prohibitions on ticket sales by telephone or mail and on extending credit for ticket purchases. The original version of section 9-829 is repealed. Agencies/departments: changes apply to the State Lottery framework and to licensed lottery game retailers. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB610_IntroLB610_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB610 assigns several duties and authorities to the Department of Health and Human Services (the department) related to supplemental reimbursement for ground emergency medical transport. Key provisions: - The department must specify required evidence, data submissions, and recordkeeping that governmental entities must provide when seeking supplemental reimbursement on behalf of eligible providers. - By January 1, 2026, the department must seek any necessary federal approvals to implement the program and may limit reimbursement to Title XIX–allowable costs. - The department shall submit claims and annual assurances to obtain federal financial participation and may implement an intergovernmental transfer program only if federal participation/approval is available. - The department’s chief executive officer may return or refuse intergovernmental transfers or adjust payments to maintain Medicaid compliance and must declare the program inoperative if federal determinations require it. - No specific state appropriations or dollar amounts are included; payments are contingent on federal approval and federal financial participation.Requires the Department of Health and Human Services, in 2026, to seek any necessary federal approvals to implement subsection (2) of the Ground Emergency Medical Transport Act as of January 1, 2025. Implementation must be based on the actual and allowable costs defined by regulations that existed on January 1, 2025, and must comply with any other applicable federal requirements. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB611_IntroLB611_Intro_Copy.docxLB611 updates Nebraska's state building and energy code references to the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code (IECC) and incorporates specified 2021 chapters of the International Building and Residential Codes. Key agencies and duties: - Department of Environment and Energy (DENE): will review plans/specs for state‑funded buildings for IECC compliance, provide reviews to the funding agency, and receive verification that constructed buildings meet or exceed the code; the Director may adopt rules. - Department of Administrative Services (DAS) — State Building Administrator: in consultation with DENE, may specify a newer IECC edition, add energy/renewable requirements, or approve waivers based on life‑cycle cost analyses; agencies seeking waivers must supply the analyses. - Counties/cities/villages: must adopt the state code or an equivalent within two years of updates and must notify DENE if they delete certain code chapters. The bill repeals the prior listed statutory sections. No appropriations or budgetary allocations are included.The added text references specific parts of the 2021 model codes—namely Chapter 13 of the 2021 International Building Code and Chapter 11 of the 2021 International Residential Code—and indicates those chapters (and related provisions) take effect after this act’s effective date. No state or federal agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the inserted language.
109-1-LB612_IntroLB612_Intro_Copy.docxLB612 (2025) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §24-514 to require the State of Nebraska, using funds appropriated to the Nebraska Supreme Court, to pay fifty percent of county courts' operational costs. The statute already directs the state (via Supreme Court appropriations) to cover all salaries, benefits, and judge/employee education and travel expenses for county courts. The bill preserves that county-owned property purchased as a county court expense remains county property and repeals the original section. Agencies affected: Nebraska Supreme Court (appropriation authority), county courts, and county governments.The underlined additions consist only of the phrase "fifty percent of ." and a new subsection label "(2)". No government agencies or departments are referenced, and no appropriations, funding changes, or budget allocations are specified. The inserted text appears incomplete and does not establish any financial or agency-related directives.
109-1-LB613A_FinalLB613A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueAppropriates General Fund amounts to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to implement Legislative Bill 613: $90,200 for FY2025‑26 and $88,000 for FY2026‑27. Of these amounts, expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $64,100 for FY2025‑26 and $66,200 for FY2026‑27. Funds are designated to aid in carrying out the provisions of LB613.Appropriates General Fund to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to implement LB613: $90,200 for FY2025‑26 and $88,000 for FY2026‑27. Sets caps on use for personnel costs — permanent/temporary salaries and per diems may not exceed $64,100 in FY2025‑26 and $66,200 in FY2026‑27 — implying remaining funds are for other implementation expenses.
109-1-LB613_FinalLB613_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Labor, Department of Revenue- Department of Administrative Services: Officials and employees of the Department of Administrative Services are explicitly included among persons prohibited from disclosing confidential tax information; unauthorized disclosure is a Class I misdemeanor. - Department of Labor: The Tax Commissioner may disclose tax information to the Department of Labor as necessary to administer the Employment Security Law, the Contractor Registration Act, or the Employee Classification Act. - Department of Revenue: The bill clarifies Department of Revenue (Tax Commissioner) duties: collect and remit municipal local-option sales taxes; notify municipalities annually (by March 1) of estimated refunds and, beginning with the 2025 notification, include adjustments for prior-year differences; provide municipalities lists of retailers on request and, upon written request and proper municipal certification, supply confidential sales/use tax returns and return information (10 business days to prepare; secure electronic transmission allowed); accept annual municipality requests for lists of qualifying businesses (due June 30). The Department is protected from liability for municipal impermissible disclosures. No appropriations or budgetary allocations are changed.- Department of Revenue: Added duties to provide municipalities with information on qualifying businesses and tax returns. The Tax Commissioner must comply with municipal requests and may disclose returns/return information to a certified municipal employee solely to verify collection/analysis/forecasting, allocation among municipalities, or that taxes are used as voted. Municipalities may annually (by June 30) request from the Department of Revenue a list of businesses that filed for incentives under the Employment and Investment Growth Act, Nebraska Advantage, ImagiNE Nebraska, or Urban Redevelopment Act. Qualifying businesses must provide information to municipalities by June 30 each year. If tax-levy proceeds are received but the originating incorporated municipality is not identified within six months, the amount is credited to the Municipal Equalization Fund. - Department of Administrative Services & Department of Labor: No changes, funding shifts, or appropriations affecting these agencies are included in the added text.
109-1-LB614_FinalLB614_Final_Copy.docxLB614 amends extraterritorial zoning statutes for Nebraska municipalities. Key agency/department actions: - Cities of the first class: general ETZJ remains two miles, but for purposes of sections 70-1001–70-1020 the ETZJ is set to one mile. - Cities of the second class and villages: general ETZJ remains one mile, but for purposes of sections 70-1001–70-1020 the ETZJ is set to one-half mile. - Board of adjustment may exempt specified farm buildings (defined by reference to section 77-1359, on farmsteads ≥20 acres producing ≥$1,000/yr) from municipal ordinances within ETZJ when consistent with the comprehensive plan. - Cities/villages must notify the county board at least 30 days before final action on zoning changes affecting ETZJ; county boards may comment within 30 days. Notification requirements do not apply if the county’s population (per the U.S. Bureau of the Census) exceeds 100,000 or there is a joint planning commission/department. - Original sections 16-901 and 17-1001 are repealed. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds authority for cities of the first class, and for cities of the second class or villages, to exempt certain farm buildings located in their extraterritorial zoning jurisdiction from zoning, property‑use, building, electrical, plumbing and related ordinances. Exemptions are made by the municipal board of adjustment pursuant to statutory procedures (sections 19‑907 to 19‑915) and must be consistent with the jurisdiction’s comprehensive development plan, including documented population and economic projections. "Farm building" is defined by reference to section 77‑1359 as agricultural buildings on farmsteads of 20+ acres producing $1,000+ in annual farm products. References also include ordinances authorized by section 16‑240. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB615_IntroLB615_Intro_Copy.docxLB615 (amending Neb. Rev. Stat. §49-1401) prohibits distribution of deceptive or fraudulent deepfakes and synthetic media that depict or misattribute speech or actions to political candidates, requires clear, persistent disclosures for visual and audio synthetic media, and authorizes candidates to seek injunctive or other equitable relief to stop such publications. Exceptions cover radio and television broadcasters (including cable and satellite operators) when material is part of bona fide news coverage or when federal law requires airing candidate ads, online/news publishers that routinely carry news if they disclose inauthenticity, and satire/parody. The bill includes harmonization and severability provisions and repeals the original section. No specific Nebraska state agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.Adds disclosure rules and remedies for materially deceptive "deepfake" media: required labels (Image, Video, or Audio); readable on-screen text; video disclosures shown for the full video; audio disclosures spoken at start, end, and every two minutes for audio over two minutes. Gives candidates injunctive/equitable relief to block publication of prohibited deepfakes. Exempts radio/TV broadcasters (including cable/satellite), paid broadcasters who acted in good faith, internet sites and periodicals that clearly disclaim inaccuracy, and satire/parody. References "federal law" obligations for airing candidate ads but names no federal agency and includes no funding, appropriations, or budget changes.
109-1-LB616_IntroLB616_Intro_Copy.docxLB616 authorizes local authorities and law enforcement to enforce red‑light violations using automatic license plate reader (ALPR) systems, and expands permitted ALPR uses (outstanding parking/traffic violations, unregistered/uninsured vehicles, equipment or registration violations, vehicles linked to warrants/missing/stolen persons, ongoing criminal investigations). The Department of Motor Vehicles (department/director) retains approval authority over driver's safety training curricula and fees and over registration renewal procedures. For ALPR red‑light enforcement, jurisdictions must offer violators a choice to pay a fee or enter a department‑approved driver's safety training program (the program fee is waived if the violator participates), no points are assessed, and no warrants may issue for nonpayment/nonparticipation. Unpaid fees become a county‑treasurer collection requirement prior to registration renewal; proceeds are allocated to the county, local school system/school district, city, and village in the vehicle’s tax district. Evidence from ALPR use is limited to enforcement proceedings under the bill. [NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.]Adds authority for local authorities to use automatic license plate reader (ALPR) systems to enforce red‑light violations, subject to specified safeguards: the motorist may pay a fee or enter a driver's safety training program under the pretrial diversion provisions (secs. 29‑3605 to 29‑3609); fees are waived if the motorist completes the program; no points assessed (sec. 60‑4,182); no warrant for nonpayment/nonparticipation. The county treasurer collects unpaid fees as a condition of vehicle registration renewal (sec. 60‑392) and must allocate proceeds to the county, local school system/school district, city, and village in the vehicle's tax district. Evidence from ALPRs is limited to proceedings enforcing this section. Agencies/departments: local authorities, county treasurer, and local government entities/school districts.
109-1-LB617_IntroLB617_Intro_Copy.docxLB617 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §48-102 (Workers' Compensation Act) to expressly abolish certain employer defenses. Under the amended language, it shall not be a defense that (1) the employee was negligent (except when negligence was willful or the employee was intoxicated), (2) the injury was caused by a fellow employee's negligence, or (3) the employee assumed risks due to unsafe premises or appliances. The bill also repeals the original §48-102. No state agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary provisions.The underlined additions consist only of the fragments "(1) That (2) That (3) That . Such." They do not reference any government agencies, departments, or programs, nor do they include any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The language appears incomplete and contains no substantive fiscal or agency content.
109-1-LB618_IntroLB618_Intro_Copy.docxLB618 disapproves a specific claim against the State that had been filed with and recommended for disallowance by the State Claims Board and subsequently appealed by the claimant. The bill denies payment of $XX.00 for Claim Number XXXX-XXXX asserted against the Department of XX. No appropriation or budget allocation is provided for the claim; the Legislature’s action affirms nonpayment and removes state liability for that specific claim.Adds a provision disallowing a claim recommended for disallowance by the State Claims Board and appealed by the claimant. The bill expressly disapproves payment of $XX.00 for Claim No. XXXX-XXXX against the Department of XX. No appropriation or funding is authorized; the state will not pay the claimed amount.
109-1-LB619_IntroLB619_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB619 directs the Department of Transportation to award joint grants to cities of the primary class and their counties to construct motor-vehicle infrastructure connecting a highway (per §39‑101) to the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways. Recipients must report to the Department annually until grant funds are expended. Unused grant funds must be repaid to the Department of Transportation; repaid amounts are remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The Legislature states intent to appropriate $15 million from the General Fund to the Department of Transportation for FY2025‑26 for these grants.The Department of Transportation is directed to administer joint grants to cities of the primary class and their counties to construct motor vehicle infrastructure that connects a defined state highway (per §39‑101) to the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways. Grantees must report to DOT annually until grant funds are expended; any funds not used for the intended purpose must be repaid to DOT and remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the General Fund. The Legislature intends a $15 million General Fund appropriation to DOT in FY 2025–26 for this program.
109-1-LB61_IntroLB61_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to take multiple actions and pursue federal approvals, including deadlines: submit a HCBS waiver amendment to add memory‑care rates for the aged and disabled (application due by Sept. 30, 2025); submit a Medicaid waiver/state plan by Oct. 1, 2025, to designate two medical‑respite facilities and report annually to the Legislature; seek federal approval to extend postpartum coverage; provide coverage for continuous glucose monitors (per prior statutory deadlines); provide electric personal‑use breast pumps and up to ten lactation consultation visits; and cover translation/interpretation services and maximize federal matching funds. Funding: intent language proposes General Fund and federal appropriations (placeholders) for memory‑care daily rates for FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27; lactation consultations funded at a 145% increase over current departmental rates; and multiple services funded from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund.Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to apply to CMS by September 30, 2025 to amend the aged-and-disabled home-and-community‑based services (HCBS) waiver to add a memory‑care rate for assisted‑living facilities. The Legislature expresses intent to appropriate unspecified amounts (placeholders) from the General Fund and matching federal funds for FY 2025‑26 and FY 2026‑27 to pay those memory‑care rates. The appropriated funds are to be used by the department to pay a specified daily memory‑care rate for assisted‑living facilities under the HCBS waiver (rate and dollar amounts are not provided in the text).
109-1-LB620_IntroLB620_Intro_Copy.docxLB620 creates the Neighborhood Revitalization Act, authorizing district courts to bring in-rem actions declaring blighted real property a public nuisance and to appoint certified receivers. Key government actors and duties: - District courts: receive petitions, determine nuisance status, appoint receivers, approve plans, establish and enforce receiver's liens, and conduct auctions per court rules. - Municipal corporations (cities, villages, counties): notified of filings, must inspect when needed, provide periodic updates to the court, may enter and secure subject parcels and charge owners for costs, and have discretionary enforcement authority. - County offices (clerk; register's office/register of deeds): receive filings (notice of lien/lis pendens, court orders) and record receiver deeds and liens. - Receivers: required to satisfy delinquent property tax liens within 30 days and may pay outstanding municipal fines and taxes from receivership funds. No explicit changes to state funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds procedures giving courts (district courts) authority to deem real property a public nuisance, appoint certified receivers, and supervise abatement. Municipal corporations (cities/towns) must be notified, may inspect subject parcels, may enter and secure property, provide periodic updates to the court, and may recover costs from owners. County registrars/ registers of deeds must receive and record notices (lien lis pendens) and receiver's deeds. Receiver liens are prioritized over other encumbrances (except general property tax liens), accrue interest at the statutory property tax rate, secure receiver expenses and a fee (10% or at least $2,500), and are satisfied from auction proceeds; receivers must pay delinquent property tax liens within 30 days. No new appropriations or state budget/agency funding changes are created.
109-1-LB621_IntroLB621_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesLB621 amends section 71-7611 to (1) direct an increase of $7,500,000 in FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to the Department of Health and Human Services (Program 502) for aid to specified community health centers to expand services (behavioral health, dental, new lines/locations, equipment, capital). Each listed center receives $700,000; remaining funds are distributed proportionately based on the prior fiscal year's uninsured patient counts per the Uniform Data System. (2) Maintain that up to $15,000,000 in transfers from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to the Board of Regents for UNMC pancreatic cancer research are contingent on matching funds certified by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services; upon such certification the State Treasurer shall transfer an equal amount.Department of Health and Human Services: The bill directs a transfer of $7,500,000 in FY2025‑26 and $7,500,000 in FY2026‑27 from the Nebraska Health Care Cash Fund to DHHS (Program 502) to provide aid to specified community health centers (Charles Drew, OneWorld, East Central/Good Neighbor, Community Action Partnership of Western NE, Nebraska Medicine Midtown, Bluestem Health, Heartland Health Center). Each center is to receive $700,000; remaining funds are allocated proportionally based on the prior fiscal year’s uninsured patient counts from the HRSA Uniform Data System. Funds may be used to expand access (e.g., behavioral health, dental), add services/locations, buy equipment, or complete capital projects. Department of Administrative Services: No additions or funding/appropriation actions affecting DAS are included in the underlined text.
109-1-LB622_IntroLB622_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of RevenueDepartment of Economic Development (DED): DED may use the Affordable Housing Trust Fund to finance community affordable housing projects, the new Statewide Housing Assistance Program (SHAP), and departmental expenses as appropriated. DED must attempt to allocate at least 30% of available funds to each congressional district, announce ≥90‑day application periods for projects and homebuyers, adopt a qualified allocation plan prioritizing lowest‑income projects and homebuyers, and may contract a nonprofit to administer SHAP. SHAP provides liened, repayable downpayment loans up to $30,000 per buyer. DED must report recipients, funding amounts, and its administration budget in its annual status report.
