Department of Revenue: The documentary stamp tax is $2.55 per $1,000; registers retain $0.50 and remit the remainder, which the State Treasurer credits $1.25 to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, $0.25 to the Site and Building Development Fund, $0.25 to the Homeless Shelter Assistance Trust Fund, and $0.30 to the Behavioral Health Services Fund. The department shall not overturn county assessor sale‑qualification determinations without review.Creates a Statewide Housing Assistance Program to be administered by a nonprofit contracted by the Department of Economic Development (DED). DED will adopt rules governing applicant eligibility. The program provides downpayment assistance as a loan (secured by a lien, repayable on title transfer), limited to $30,000 per homebuyer, for primary residences only. Priority for assistance is given to lowest‑income buyers and those in designated enterprise zones, federal opportunity zones, or areas declared extremely blighted. No changes to or actions by the Department of Revenue are specified, and the text contains no new appropriations, funding sources, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB623_IntroLB623_Intro_Copy.docxLB623 appropriates unspecified General Fund amounts (placeholders) for FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 to a program identified only as "XXX, Program XXX." Each year's appropriation includes a designated portion reserved exclusively for state aid. No specific state agency or department is named in the bill. The measure contains an emergency clause, making it effective upon passage and approval.Appropriates two General Fund amounts to "XXX, Program XXX": one for FY2025‑26 and one for FY2026‑27. Each year’s appropriation includes a specified sub‑amount that is explicitly earmarked for state aid and may be used only for that purpose.
109-1-LB624_IntroLB624_Intro_Copy.docxLB624 appropriates General Fund dollars to the Office of the State Treasurer: $10,000,000 for FY2025-26 and $10,000,000 for FY2026-27, designated as state aid and restricted for that purpose. The Treasurer is to contract to provide education scholarships for low‑income and at‑risk elementary and secondary students to expand access to approved or accredited private, denominational, or parochial schools. The bill states legislative intent to appropriate $10,000,000 annually thereafter to the State Treasurer for the same scholarship purpose.Appropriates $10,000,000 General Fund to the State Treasurer for FY2025-26 and $10,000,000 General Fund to the State Treasurer for FY2026-27 as state aid. Funds are restricted for the Treasurer to contract for education scholarships for low‑income and at‑risk elementary and secondary students to expand access to approved/accredited private, denominational, or parochial schools. The text expresses legislative intent for a $10,000,000 annual General Fund appropriation to the State Treasurer for this scholarship contracting; the appropriation may be used only for that purpose.
109-1-LB625_IntroLB625_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB625 directs creation of a statewide database of financial information from all school districts and expressly assigns duties to the Tax Commissioner and the Department of Revenue in connection with that database. The provided text does not detail the Department of Revenue’s specific responsibilities or any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB626_IntroLB626_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of LaborLB626 amends the Community Development Law definitions for workforce housing and directs the Department of Economic Development to annually update statutory housing-unit cost caps (owner-occupied $275,000; rental $200,000) using the most recent change in the Producer Price Index published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics. The bill cites the federal Department of Labor only as the source of the index. No explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Economic Development or the Department of Labor are included.Adds a definition of “affordable housing” as: (a) workforce housing; (b) housing targeted to households earning <60% of the county median income; or (c) housing under IRC §42 (LIHTC). Also inserts a criterion that an area may be characterized by having “less than twenty percent of the housing in the area” be affordable. The additions do not reference the Department of Economic Development or the Department of Labor and include no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for either agency.
109-1-LB627_IntroLB627_Intro_Copy.docxProvides the Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska authority to design and construct student residential facilities for nursing and allied health in Norfolk. State-supported project cost: $23,000,000. The Legislature intends annual appropriations of $1,150,000 for 20 years to support the project. The Board may enter long‑term financing contracts (payments not to extend beyond June 30, 2045), may convey/lease or lease back facilities to facilitate financing, and may schedule payments monthly, quarterly, or semiannually. The Board may not pledge the State's credit except for legislative appropriations. Any unneeded funds appropriated from the Nebraska Capital Construction Fund and the General Fund held in the treasury or by trustees shall be transferred to the General Fund by August 31, 2045. Appropriations for the project should not be reduced until related contracts and securities are completed or paid, but not beyond FY ending June 30, 2045. Also intends a $250,000 appropriation to the Board for educational technology in Norfolk.- Agency: Board of Regents of the University of Nebraska authorized to design and construct student residential facilities for nursing and allied health in Norfolk. - Funding/appropriations: total state-supported project cost $23,000,000; Legislature intends annual appropriations of $1,150,000 for 20 years. Legislature also intends a one-time $250,000 appropriation to the Board for educational technology for Norfolk facilities. - Financing/terms: Board may enter long-term financing (including conveyance/lease/leaseback) with private parties, schedule payments monthly/quarterly/semiannually, and must approve contracts by Board resolution. Contracts may extend no later than June 30, 2045; appropriations cannot be reduced until related contracts/securities are paid but shall not extend past FY ending June 30, 2045. - Budget cleanup: any project funds from the Nebraska Capital Construction Fund or General Fund held in treasury or by trustees and not needed for financing must be transferred to the General Fund by August 31, 2045.
109-1-LB628_IntroLB628_Intro_Copy.docxLB628 adopts the Recreational Trail Easement Property Tax Exemption Act and amends filing and exemption procedures in §§76-214 and 77-202. It requires the Tax Commissioner to prescribe recording statements and the Property Tax Administrator to provide processing instructions; registers of deeds must forward statements to county assessors, who in turn forward them to the Tax Commissioner. The bill excludes most easements from the recording-statement requirement except conservation, preservation, and easements used to qualify for the new recreational-trail exemption. Section 77-202 adds a property-tax exemption for a portion of property pursuant to the new Act. The State Records Administrator retains records-disposition oversight. Operative date: January 1, 2026. No appropriations or budget allocations are included.Adds standards and procedures for qualifying recreational-trail easements: alignment with public access and conservation goals; procedures to certify an easement’s public benefit (including required connectivity to existing or planned trail systems); and methods to ensure ongoing compliance with the statute’s public-purpose requirements. Also cross‑references easements and portions of property that qualify for the property tax exemption under the Recreational Trail Easement Property Tax Exemption Act. No specific government agencies or departments are named and no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB629_IntroLB629_Intro_Copy.docxLB629 creates the "County Initiative and Referendum Act," reserving initiative and referendum powers to the qualified electors of each county. It establishes that the Act governs use of initiative to enact and referendum to amend or repeal measures affecting county governance. Key government entities affected: county governments and county boards (measures include ordinances, charter provisions, and resolutions within a county board's legislative authority). The bill defines "circulator" (a person soliciting petition signatures) and excludes actions authorized under the Nebraska Advantage Transformational Tourism and Redevelopment Act. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Creates the "County Initiative and Referendum Act," reserving initiative and referendum powers to qualified electors of each county and making the Act the governing law for using initiative to enact, and referendum to amend or repeal, measures affecting county governance. Defines "circulator" (person who solicits petition signatures) and "measure" (ordinance, charter provision, or resolution within a county board's legislative authority). Explicitly excludes actions authorized under the Nebraska Advantage Transformational Tourism and Redevelopment Act. Agencies/departments referenced: county boards/counties. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB62_IntroLB62_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB62 appropriates $19,000,000 from the General Fund for FY2025-26 to the Department of Administrative Services, Program 245. DAS is directed to provide these funds to the Office of the Chief Information Officer to support interoperable communications (portable and mobile radios, programming, installation) and related training via a grant program to connect volunteer departments to the Statewide Radio System. The CIO shall not charge subscription, programming, or training fees to volunteer departments receiving a grant. The Legislature intends all grant funds to be distributed by June 30, 2028.The bill appropriates $19,000,000 General Fund for FY2025-26 to the Department of Administrative Services (Program 245). DAS must provide these funds to the Office of the Chief Information Officer to create interoperable communications for volunteer departments and state agencies by funding portable/mobile radios, programming, installation, and interoperability training via a grant program. Grant eligibility is based on each volunteer department's size and radio needs. After a grant, the OCIO may not charge the volunteer department subscription, programming, or training fees. The Legislature intends all grant funds to be distributed by June 30, 2028. "Volunteer department" is defined per section 35-901.
109-1-LB630_IntroLB630_Intro_Copy.docxLB630 amends the Occupational Therapy Practice Act. Key government entities and actions: - "Board" (the occupational therapy regulatory board) retains authority to approve training courses and examinations and to identify subjects for the national licensure examination. - "Department" is directed to issue certificates for physical‑agent and instrument‑assisted modalities to occupational therapists who meet board‑approved criteria and to authorize occupational therapy assistants to set up/implement superficial thermal agent modalities after board‑approved training/exam, only under onsite supervision of a certified occupational therapist. - The Hand Therapy Certification Commission (or equivalent entity recognized by the board) is referenced as an approved credentialing body. - Examination results from the national licensure entity are sent to the board for verification. - Temporary license provisions and a revised definition of supervision are included. - Original statutory sections listed are repealed. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds licensure and practice provisions for occupational therapy. Key agency references: the state licensing board (the "board") and the entity that administers the national licensure examination. New provisions: temporary licenses expire on issuance of a permanent license, denial, 180 days, or notification of exam failure; applicants must take the national exam per the exam entity's rules and the exam results are sent to the board. Expands and clarifies practice scope (comprehensive evaluation domains, performance patterns/skills, client factors, intervention methods including prevention, health promotion, occupational justice, and group interventions). Defines supervision as a collaborative accountability process where the occupational therapist is accountable for assistants/aides. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB631_IntroLB631_Intro_Copy.docxLB631 creates (amends) the School Emergency Response Mapping Fund and assigns administration to the State Department of Education. The fund may include legislative transfers and gifts, grants, or bequests; the department will use it to award grants for implementation of mapping data under section 79-3110. Funds available for investment are to be managed by the state investment officer pursuant to the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and the Nebraska State Funds Investment Act. The Legislature states intent to transfer $4,000,000 from the General Fund to this Fund for FY2025-26. The bill repeals the original section 79-3111 and contains an emergency clause making it effective upon enactment.No agencies or departments are named. The added text provides funding of four million dollars ($4,000,000) for the 2025–26 fiscal year. No further appropriation details or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB632_IntroLB632_Intro_Copy.docxLB632 requires health care facilities that perform elective abortions to provide individual disposition of aborted fetal remains by cremation or interment (burial), and makes it unlawful to dispose of such remains in any other manner. If cremation or burial is not possible, disposition shall follow directions from the Nebraska Board of Health. The bill also specifies that facilities are not required to notify the woman undergoing the abortion of the method of disposition. No funding appropriations or budget allocations are included.The added text directs that the Legislature’s purpose is to protect public health and respect the dignity of unborn children by requiring health care facilities that perform elective abortions to ensure dignified, safe disposition of fetal remains. It defines “remains of an aborted unborn child,” makes unlawful any disposal method not authorized by the section, and requires individual disposition by cremation or burial—or, if those are not possible, as directed by the Board of Health. No notice to the patient is required. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB633_IntroLB633_Intro_Copy.docxLB633 amends section 79-239 and creates the Nebraska Option Enrollment Tuition Account Program. Key agency actions and requirements: - School districts must annually submit prescribed data on enrollment-option application rejections to the State Department of Education (number rejected, reasons, disability status, provision of capacity information). - The Commissioner of Education compiles those submissions and reports electronically to the Legislature annually (beginning Sept. 1, 2024). - Parents may appeal rejections to the State Board of Education (hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act; districts bear burden to prove capacity limits) or decline appeal and request a State Board‑issued option enrollment tuition account for the student. - The State Board may use up to 5% of scholarship account funds for program administration or contracting and may adopt rules. - The bill repeals the original section and takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.Creates the Nebraska Option Enrollment Tuition Account Program administration by the State Board of Education. Parents (or guardians) have 30 days after receiving a district rejection to send a request and the rejection notice to the State Board, which must then issue an option enrollment tuition account. Defines key terms (Board = State Board of Education; eligible student; parent; program). An eligible student remains subject to compulsory attendance rules if complying with program requirements. Clarifies the State cannot use program participation to expand control over public, private, or denominational schools or require their admission/continued enrollment. Budget: the State Board may use up to 5% of scholarship account funds for program administration or contract with a third party. The Board may adopt rules and regulations to implement the program.
109-1-LB634_IntroLB634_Intro_Copy.docxLB634 creates the Legislative Sunset Review Act and establishes a Legislative Sunset Review Committee (members: chair of the Appropriations Committee, Executive Board appointees including five legislators with geographic balance, plus others). It abolishes the Legislature’s Planning Committee. Reviewable entities (state agencies, reviewable entities and their advisory committees) must file detailed electronic reports to the Clerk of the Legislature; reviews begin in 2027 and recur every five years. The committee may access agency records, request assistance from state agencies and officers, and exercise standing‑committee powers. Reports must address Auditor of Public Accounts findings, public records/Open Meetings compliance, and program consolidation/privatization options. The act is operative Jan. 1, 2026, and repeals specified statutes. No appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are provided in the bill.Creates a Legislative Sunset Review Committee composed of the chair of the Appropriations Committee, five legislators appointed by the Executive Board of the Legislative Council (with geographic balance), and other elected committee officers. Initial appointments occur soon after Jan. 1, 2026; the committee gets staff support from legislative divisions. The committee must publish a sunset review schedule on the Legislature’s website, beginning reviews in 2027 and reviewing each “reviewable entity” every five years. Reviewable entities and state agencies must electronically submit validated reports to the Clerk of the Legislature before their review year, including performance measures, three years of data, compliance (e.g., Open Meetings, public records, small/minority purchasing), audit responses (Auditor of Public Accounts), duplication analyses, privatization alternatives, advisory committee inventories, and recommendations (including statutory or budgetary changes). The committee may use standing-committee powers, request assistance from agencies/officers, and inspect records. No direct funding or appropriation changes are specified.
109-1-LB635_FinalLB635_Final_Copy.docxThis bill expands the regulatory authority of the State Athletic Commissioner to include professional bare-knuckle mixed martial arts, professional mixed martial arts on ice, professional muay thai, amateur muay thai, and amateur kickboxing. It amends licensing, bonding, and enforcement provisions: promoter license fees set by the commissioner ($100–$300); referee fees $10–$40; matchmaker $10–$100; physicians/managers/judges/timekeepers/contestants $10–$20. Bond minimums are specified ($1,000 for amateur events; $5,000 for professional events). Licensees must report receipts and pay a tax of 5% of gross receipts (including 5% of television rights). The commissioner may adopt rules, limit event numbers, promulgate a banned-substances list, require testing, and impose suspensions/fines for violations (detailed graduated penalties up to lifetime suspension and fines up to $5,000 or 100% of purse). Administrative fines are remitted to the State Treasurer; contested fines follow the Administrative Procedure Act. [NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.]Adds and repeatedly enumerates covered combat activities and persons — e.g., professional bare‑knuckle mixed martial arts, professional mixed martial arts on ice, professional and amateur muay thai, amateur kickboxing, plus “matches” and “contestants.” No government agencies, departments, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned in the added text.
109-1-LB636_IntroLB636_Intro_Copy.docxLB636 authorizes counties to seek state reimbursement for medical services provided to county jail inmates. The Jail Standards Board is designated to administer the program: it will set eligibility, accept county board‑certified quarterly claims (within 45 days of quarter end), audit county records (at least biennially), request additional information, adopt rules, and deny reimbursement for costs resulting from county/jail employee negligence or misconduct. If approved, the board requests a warrant from the State Treasurer payable to the county treasurer and credited to the county general fund. The Legislature caps annual appropriations for the Jail Standards Board's eligible criminal court cost reimbursements at $21 million beginning FY2025‑26. The bill also revises sheriffs’ fee/mileage provisions (minimum $10 charges, prorated mileage, ability to charge for additional officers) and updates collection/reporting duties to county treasurers and county boards. An emergency clause makes the act effective on passage.Adds procedures and limits for county reimbursement claims administered by the Jail Standards Board. Key agencies: Jail Standards Board, State Treasurer, county boards/treasurers, county sheriffs, and the Legislature. New/changed provisions: - Claims must be certified by county boards and filed with the Jail Standards Board within 45 days after each quarterly period (Mar 31, Jun 30, Sep 30, Dec 31); late claims are ineligible. - If approved, the Board requests a warrant from the State Treasurer to pay the county treasurer, credited to the county general fund. - The Board has sole authority to determine reimbursable medical costs, may audit county records (at least once every two years), may request additional information, and may adopt rules; it will not reimburse costs caused by jail or staff negligence. - Funding cap: beginning FY2025–26 and thereafter, legislative appropriations to the Jail Standards Board for eligible criminal court cost reimbursement shall not exceed $21,000,000 annually. - Allows county sheriffs to charge fees for additional officers when safety requires (subject to existing rate limits).
109-1-LB637_IntroLB637_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Transportation- Department of Transportation: authorizes the Department of Transportation to enter into agreements with approved destination district applicants to construct roads, bridges, and other infrastructure within a destination district, subject to applicable federal and state laws and codes. - Department of Economic Development: requires annual updating of workforce-housing construction cost thresholds by the Department of Economic Development based on the Producer Price Index for all commodities. - Department of Labor: the bill cites the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source of the Producer Price Index used for those updates. No direct appropriations, agency budget increases, or other funding allocations to these departments are specified.Department of Economic Development - Will accept destination district applications through Dec 31, 2025, review/confidentiality rules, and approve up to two statewide districts (40‑year term, ≤5,000 acres) if projects exceed $3 billion and expect ≥10 million annual visitors. - May set a new state occupation tax (in addition to sales/use tax) for transactions on property owned by the applicant; rate set after notice and hearing. - May designate a trustee bank to hold occupation tax proceeds and use those funds in agreements with the district applicant. - May form and staff a Community Redevelopment Authority for the district (appoint/remove members; one must be a county board member). Department of Transportation - May enter into agreements with approved district applicants to construct roads, bridges, and other infrastructure within the district (must meet applicable laws/codes). Department of Labor - No changes, mentions, or funding/appropriation actions affecting the department are included.
109-1-LB638_IntroLB638_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Natural Resources (DNR) administration: LB638 designates the DNR as administrator of the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive program and allows collaboration with local natural resources districts. Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund: The bill continues DNR administration of the Cash Fund, authorizes legislative transfers and gifts/grants as fund sources, and requires the DNR to apply (prior to the FY2025-26 application deadline) for a $25 million Nebraska Environmental Trust Fund grant payable in five $5 million annual installments. If awarded, proceeds are to be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Cash Fund. DNR must establish a subaccount for those grant proceeds, calculate monthly interest earnings, and notify the State Treasurer to transfer a like amount from the Cash Fund to the Nebraska Environmental Trust Fund. DNR may pursue other applicable grants; awarded grants are credited to the Cash Fund. Fund investments are handled by the state investment officer under existing statutes. Other provisions: The Act’s termination date is set to December 31, 2030, and it takes effect immediately under an emergency clause.The Department of Natural Resources must apply (by the FY2025-26 deadline) for a $25 million grant from the Nebraska Environmental Trust Fund, payable in five annual $5 million installments, with grant purposes aligned to the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund. If awarded, the State Treasurer will credit the grant proceeds to the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund to support the grant projects. DNR must create a subaccount within that cash fund to track the Trust grant dollars. At month-end DNR will compute interest earned on the subaccount and notify the State Treasurer, who will transfer an equal amount from the Nitrogen Reduction Incentive Cash Fund back to the Nebraska Environmental Trust Fund.
109-1-LB639_IntroLB639_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of InsuranceLB639 defines "Department" as the Department of Insurance and "Director" as the Director of Insurance. It requires dental plan carriers to annually submit to the Department, beginning January 1, 2027, a dental loss-ratio report (form and content to be prescribed by the Department) demonstrating compliance with the minimum 85% dental loss ratio. The Department is authorized to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to carry out these provisions. The bill grants reporting and rulemaking duties to the Department of Insurance. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department are specified in the bill.Creates an 85% minimum dental loss ratio effective Jan 1, 2026, and requires dental plan carriers to annually file with the Department of Insurance (beginning Jan 1, 2027) a Department-prescribed report showing incurred claims, earned premiums (net of taxes and regulatory fees), rates, rating schedules and supporting documentation (including historical ratios). If the minimum ratio is not met, carriers must return excess premiums to insureds. The Department of Insurance and the Director are defined parties and are authorized to adopt rules and regulations to implement the section. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB63_IntroLB63_Intro_Copy.docxLB63 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §9-1103, redefining terms tied to racetrack gaming and sports wagering and repeals the original section. It designates the State Racing and Gaming Commission as the regulatory authority with specific powers to: - approve designated sports wagering areas and the boundaries of licensed racetrack enclosures in accordance with the Nebraska Constitution and law; - issue racing and authorized gaming operator licenses; - define and determine prohibited participants and exclude sporting events from wagering; and - authorize the systems of sports wagering. The bill also references keno conducted under the Nebraska County and City Lottery Act. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.I don’t have the underlined/added text — you only sent “(c)”. 109-1-LB640_FinalLB640_Final_Copy.docxLB640 (Judiciary Committee) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §47-502 concerning persons confined in city or county jails, including those serving custodial sanctions for parole or probation violations. After the first 15 days of confinement, the bill directs that the aggregate remaining term—including the sum of any consecutive sentences imposed at the same time or imposed during confinement—be reduced one day for each day the person does not commit a breach of discipline or other violation of jail regulations. The bill repeals the original section. No state agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are created or altered.Adds language clarifying that “the aggregate of” includes the sum of all consecutive sentences a person receives, whether imposed at the same time or at any later time during that sentence or confinement. No government agencies or departments are referenced, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB641_FinalLB641_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB641 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §68-919 governing Medicaid estate recovery by the Department of Health and Human Services. Key provisions: expands the definition of “medical institution” to include assisted living facilities; restricts foreclosure on a recipient’s home where a sibling (with equity) or an adult child resided and provided care (physician attestation is sufficient); creates an additional exemption for life‑estate interests after 12 months where a relative resides solely and continuously and provided care (physician attestation suffices); requires the department to certify to estate representatives whether reimbursement is due and permits the department to release property, waive or compromise claims, enforce recovery, and adopt rules. Recovery actions may be brought within five years of specified triggering events. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds that care by a sibling, adult child, or other relative — reimbursed or unreimbursed — that delayed a recipient’s admission to a medical institution may be documented by a physician’s written attestation. The Department of Health and Human Services must accept such an attestation as sufficient to (1) avoid foreclosure on a medical‑assistance lien where a sibling or adult child provided the care, and (2) exclude a retained life‑estate interest in real estate (after 12 months from deed recording) from the recipient’s estate when a relative resided solely and continuously with the recipient and established to the department’s satisfaction that the relative provided the delaying care. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB642_IntroLB642_Intro_Copy.docxLB642 establishes the Artificial Intelligence Consumer Protection Act and assigns enforcement and oversight roles principally to the Nebraska Attorney General. The Attorney General may, in connection with an ongoing investigation, require deployers or contracted third parties to produce risk‑management policies, impact assessments, and related records within 90 days, evaluate them for compliance, and treat disclosures as nonpublic (with proprietary/trade‑secret protections). Banks, credit unions, their affiliates/subsidiaries, and service providers are exempt if subject to state or federal prudential regulator guidance that the Attorney General finds substantially equivalent; such guidance must, at minimum, require regular audits for antidiscrimination compliance and mitigation. Insurers and certain fraternal benefit societies governed by the Unfair Insurance Trade Practices Act are exempt. The bill cites federal research and safety rules (45 C.F.R. part 46; FDA) for exemptions. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds roles for the state Attorney General and federal regulators but contains no funding or appropriation language. Key agency points: - Attorney General may demand, within 90 days during an investigation, deployer or contracted third parties’ risk‑management policies, impact assessments, and related records; those disclosures are not public records and may be designated proprietary/trade secret. - Exemptions reference federal agencies and rules: FDA and HHS human‑subjects regulations (45 C.F.R. part 46) for research activities. - Banks, credit unions, their affiliates/subsidiaries and service providers are exempt if subject to examination by a state or federal prudential regulator whose guidance is deemed by the Attorney General to be substantially equivalent (and requires auditing for antidiscrimination compliance and mitigation). - General cooperation with law enforcement and compliance with federal/state/municipal legal processes are explicitly preserved.
109-1-LB643_IntroLB643_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill authorizes a person to appeal to the Department of Revenue claiming their single‑family residential property was offered for sale at fair market rate for at least 90 days with no good‑faith offers. If the Department of Revenue sustains the appeal, the person may claim Nebraska income tax deductions for interest, taxes, or maintenance related to that property. The bill contains no provisions altering funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue.Adds an appeal process to the Department of Revenue: a property owner may appeal to DOR asserting their single‑family residential property was offered for sale at fair market value for at least 90 days with no good‑faith offers. If DOR sustains the appeal, the owner may claim Nebraska income tax deductions for interest, property taxes, and maintenance expenses related to that property. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are specified.
109-1-LB644A_FinalLB644A_Final_Copy.docxLB644A appropriates funds to implement Legislative Bill 644. It provides the Attorney General (Program 507) $30,000 from the State Settlement Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 (and $0 for FY2026‑27). It provides the Nebraska Accountability and Disclosure Commission (Program 94) $50,000 from the General Fund for FY2025‑26 and $50,000 from the General Fund for FY2026‑27. Both appropriations include a prohibition on using the funds for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates funding to implement LB 644: - Attorney General (Program 507): $30,000 from the State Settlement Cash Fund for FY2025-26 and $0 for FY2026-27 to assist in carrying out LB 644. Funds may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems. - Nebraska Accountability and Disclosure Commission (Program 94): $50,000 from the General Fund for FY2025-26 and $50,000 from the General Fund for FY2026-27 to assist in carrying out LB 644. Funds may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB644_FinalLB644_Final_Copy.docxThis bill creates the Foreign Adversary and Terrorist Agent Registration Act and the Crush Transnational Repression in Nebraska Act and assigns primary administration and enforcement to the Nebraska Attorney General. The Attorney General must collect registrations, maintain public records and a web portal, transmit filings to the U.S. Secretary of State, report semiannually to the Legislature, and may issue civil investigative demands and regulations. The Nebraska Accountability and Disclosure Commission (NADC) gains authority to sanction violations of lobbying/consultant disclosure (including enhanced penalties for failures to disclose Chinese military company principals), to pay informants $50,000 contingent on recovery of assessed penalties, and to deposit penalties into the State Treasurer for constitutionally prescribed distribution. Businesses must attest compliance in filings with the Secretary of State, Director of Insurance, or Director of Banking and Finance. Public entities are barred from contracts with scrutinized/foreign adversarial companies; such companies are ineligible for specified state incentive programs (e.g., ImagiNE Nebraska, Nebraska Advantage acts).Adds extensive enforcement and reporting duties primarily for the Nebraska Attorney General: registration, retention, public posting (monthly portal), six‑monthly legislative reports, authority to issue civil investigative demands, share information with state and federal agencies, and to transmit registration copies to the U.S. Secretary of State. The U.S. Department of State is referenced for diplomatic/consular exemptions. The Secretary of State (Nebraska) and the Directors of Insurance and of Banking and Finance must receive or include statutory attestation language on business reports; the Secretary of State may adopt rules. Civil penalties (including those for Chinese military company disclosure violations) are remitted to the State Treasurer for constitutionally prescribed distribution. A commission (unnamed) may award $50,000 to whistleblowers contingent on penalty recovery. No new appropriations or specific budget line items are provided.
109-1-LB645A_FinalLB645A_Final_Copy.docxLB645A appropriates funds to the Public Employees Retirement Board (Program 41) to implement Legislative Bill 645. For FY2025‑26 the bill directs $40,000 from the School Expense Fund and $26,000 from the State Patrol Expense Fund. No funds are appropriated for FY2026‑27. Of the FY2025‑26 appropriation, total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $20,000 (and $0 for FY2026‑27). The act contains an emergency clause and takes effect upon passage and approval.Appropriates $66,000 total for FY2025-26 ($40,000 from the School Expense Fund and $26,000 from the State Patrol Expense Fund) to the Public Employees Retirement Board, Program 41, to implement Legislative Bill 645 (109th Leg., 2025). No funds are appropriated from those funds for FY2026-27. Expenditures from these appropriations for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $20,000 for FY2025-26 and $0 for FY2026-27.
109-1-LB645_FinalLB645_Final_Copy.docxProvides amendments affecting the Nebraska School Retirement Fund, the Service Annuity Fund, Class V school district retirement systems, and the Nebraska State Patrol Retirement System. Key agency/finance changes: - State Retirement Board/Director of Administrative Services/State Treasurer: continue to certify and effectuate annual state deposits and transfers; transfers to the Service Annuity Fund remain payable and invested by the State Investment Officer under state investment law. - Class V school districts: beginning July 1, 2025 the state must transfer to Class V districts an amount equal to 2.0% of members' compensation plus the actuarially determined service-annuity payment; districts may petition the Legislature’s Appropriations Committee for additional transfers. - School Retirement Fund: beginning July 1, 2025 employee contribution rates become tiered by funded ratio (9.75%, 8.75%, 8.00%, or 7.25%); state contribution similarly becomes tiered (2.0%, 0.7%, or 0%), calculated July 1 each year. - Nebraska State Patrol/State Patrol Retirement Fund: survivor benefits increase from 75% to 100% of an officer’s annuity for surviving spouses beginning July 1, 2027 (affects post- and pre-retirement deaths). - Emergency clause: act effective on passage.Adds required transfers and contribution schedules affecting the State, Class V school districts, the district retirement systems, the School Retirement Fund, and the retirement board (which must produce the annual actuarial valuation under section 84-1503). Key funding changes: - Beginning July 1, 2025 the State must annually transfer to Class V districts’ retirement funds an amount equal to 2% of members’ compensation (in addition to other statutory transfers) payable on or before July 1. Legislature clarifies this does not shift district funding liability to the State. - Employee contribution rates (effective July 1, 2025) are set on funded-ratio tiers: 9.75%, 8.75%, 8.00%, or 7.25% of compensation. - State deposits into the School Retirement Fund (also beginning 2025) vary by funded ratio: 2.0%, 0.7%, or none. Deposits transmit with employer contributions. - Survivor annuity benefits for officers increase to 100% for spouses/eligible children beginning July 1, 2027.
109-1-LB646_FinalLB646_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB646 amends section 54-1,108 to authorize the Nebraska Brand Committee to charge an actual-expense fee for physical brand inspections performed outside the brand inspection area. That fee may include mileage calculated at the rate established by the Department of Administrative Services and an hourly rate (not to exceed $30/hour) for travel and inspection time. The brand committee shall charge and collect the fee; when tied to investigations of alleged brand-law violations, the fee may be charged against the person committing the violation. [NOTE: Budget-related content may be missing from this summary. Please review manually.]Adds brand committee authority to impose a surcharge (up to $20) per inspection location to cover brand inspector travel; the surcharge is collected by the inspector and paid by the person requesting or legally required to have the inspection. Also adds/clarifies a registration and annual renewal fee equal to $0.50 multiplied by the registered feedlot’s maximum livestock capacity. No references to the Department of Administrative Services and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DAS are included.
109-1-LB647A_FinalLB647A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueThe bill appropriates to the Department of Revenue, Program 102: $65,087 from the General Fund for FY2025-26 and $0 for FY2026-27 to aid in carrying out Legislative Bill 647. It specifies that none of the funds appropriated may be used for permanent or temporary state employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates $65,087 General Fund to the Department of Revenue (Program 102) for FY2025-26 and $0 for FY2026-27 to assist with implementation of Legislative Bill 647 (2025). Funds are one‑time for FY2025-26 only and may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems. No other funding or ongoing budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB647_FinalLB647_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of RevenueLB647 directs agency rulemaking, reporting, and fund changes. Department of Revenue must adopt rules for the Recreational Trail Easement property‑tax exemption (nonprofit eligibility, public‑benefit/trail‑connectivity certification, perpetual‑easement compliance) and may implement a refundable Adoption Tax Credit equal to 10% of the federal adoption expenses credit beginning in 2026. The Tax Commissioner will prescribe exemption/reaffirmation forms and require publicly traded partnerships to file unit‑holder data. The bill creates a Department of Revenue Miscellaneous Receipts Fund (specified receipts) to defray administrative costs; legislative transfers to the General Fund and investment by the state investment officer are authorized. DAS and the State Treasurer must set fund types for the 529 trust and report pro rata expense transfers to the Investment Council budget. DHHS must annually (by March 1) transmit newborn data to the State Treasurer; transfer costs are paid from the Education Savings Plan Expense Fund. Meadowlark caps: up to $250,000/year each for employer incentives and low‑income matching; endowment may accept private and legislative transfers but no General Funds.Department of Revenue - Must promulgate rules for the new Recreational Trail Easement Property Tax Exemption: define nonprofit holder eligibility, certify public‑benefit/connectivity of easements, and set compliance procedures. Exemptions persist without reapplication while a perpetual recorded trail easement remains in place. - May adopt rules to implement the Adoption Tax Credit Act: beginning for tax years on/after Jan 1, 2026, Nebraska allows a refundable income tax credit equal to 10% of the federal adoption expenses credit (26 U.S.C. §23). Department of Administrative Services & Department of Health and Human Services - No provisions, responsibilities, or funding/appropriation changes for DAS or DHHS appear in the added text. Funding/Appropriations - The added text contains no explicit appropriations or budget allocations.
109-1-LB648_IntroLB648_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationLB648 amends revenue distribution to direct certain sales/use tax proceeds to the Department of Transportation. Specifically, for transactions occurring on or after July 1, 2023, all proceeds of the sales and use taxes imposed under section 77-2703 on the sale or lease of aircraft (per section 3-101) are credited to the Department of Transportation Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund. The act’s operative date is July 1, 2026.The added language sets the statewide sales tax rate beginning July 1, 2026 at a placeholder "XX percent," with a special lower rate of 2.75% for transactions inside portions of Good Life Transformational Projects Act districts that lie within a city or village. There are no provisions in this text that change Department of Transportation authority, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB649_FinalLB649_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Labor, Department of Revenue- Department of Labor: The bill directs the Office of Labor Market Information of the Department of Labor to calculate the Nebraska statewide average hourly wage (using Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages data) by October 1 of the year prior to application; hourly wages are computed by dividing the reported average annual weekly wage by 40. - Department of Revenue: The Department of Revenue must submit an electronic annual report (fiscal-year, accrual basis meeting GASB) by October 31 and appear before the Appropriations and Revenue Committees by December 15; supplemental information requested by three or more committee members must be provided within 30 days. The report must list signed and active agreements, identify taxpayer parties, and disclose agreement-specific aggregated credit use biennially (with confidentiality protections). - Fiscal provisions: a $5,000 nonrefundable application fee is credited to the Nebraska Incentives Fund; wage-credit caps are $4 million per year and $40 million total.Department of Labor - Office of Labor Market Information must calculate the "Nebraska statewide average hourly wage" using Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages data and provide it by October 1 preceding an application. Department of Revenue - The Tax Commissioner (DOR) administers the program: accepts $5,000 nonrefundable applications (remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Nebraska Incentives Fund), approves applicants, executes agreements, monitors compliance, and enforces recapture of credits for noncompliance. - Wage-credit limits: 5% of qualified employees' compensation, capped at $4 million per year and $40 million total statewide. - DOR must file an annual GASB‑basis electronic report to the Legislature by Oct 31, appear at a joint Appropriations/Revenue hearing by Dec 15, provide certain agreement and credit disclosures (with confidentiality protections), and supply requested supplemental information within 30 days. - No new appropriations to either agency are specified.
109-1-LB64_IntroLB64_Intro_Copy.docxLB64 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §44-3614 to revise eligibility and premium rules for Medicare supplement policies for individuals under 65 who qualify by reason of disability. Premium differentials by age are permitted if actuarially sound, not excessive, inadequate, or unfairly discriminatory; premiums for a disabled individual under 65 may not exceed 150% of the premium for a similarly situated 65-year-old. The bill also provides that such disabled, under-65 individuals become subject to the same open enrollment rules applicable to newly eligible 65-year-olds beginning the first day of the month they turn 65. No state agencies, departments, or budgetary appropriations are named or changed. The original section is repealed.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB650_FinalLB650_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Agriculture, Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of RevenueThe bill assigns roles and limits across agencies: - Department of Economic Development (DED): administers the Community Development Assistance Act (certifying programs, adopting rules, approving proposals) and reviews Urban Redevelopment Act applications (fee $500; approvals capped at $8 million expected incentives), transmitting approved materials to the Department of Revenue (DOR). - Department of Revenue / Tax Commissioner: prescribes forms/rules, certifies and approves multiple tax credits (including food-donation credits—up to $500,000 in FY2025‑26—and reverse‑osmosis/other credits), caps Community Development Assistance Act credits at $350,000/year, publishes county lists of property subject to tax sale, and gains expanded enforcement, audit, confidentiality, and disclosure authorities (including permitted disclosures to municipalities, certified municipal representatives, and the Auditor). The Tax Commissioner may disclose taxpayer data to the Department of Labor when necessary. - Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): collects vehicle sales tax at registration, may retain a collection fee (deposited to the Motor Carrier Division Cash Fund), must remit collections to the Tax Commissioner by the 15th of the following month (fee forfeited if collection rules are violated), and remits specified penalties set at $5. - County/large-county provisions: county treasurers (in counties ≥150,000 pop.) must remit $1 of their collection fee for each of the first 5,000 registrations to the State Treasurer for credit to the DOR Enforcement Fund. - Department of Administrative Services (DAS): budget division directs timing/amounts for a $750 million General Fund transfer to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund (FY2024‑25); DAS employees are covered by the misdemeanor prohibition on disclosing taxpayer information.Department of Economic Development - Adds/clarifies administration of the Community Development Assistance Act: defines terms, authorizes the Director to promulgate rules, certify community betterment programs for tax-credit status, approve/disapprove proposals within 45 days, and transmit decisions to the Tax Commissioner. - Temporarily bars new program certifications for eligible businesses for calendar years 2026–2029; allows approvals beginning 2030 up to $6 million in tax credits per calendar year. Department of Revenue (Tax Commissioner) - Must adopt forms/rules to allow and apply the new tax credit against specified state taxes and accept department certifications; receives copies of approvals. - Provisions for certification/transfers affecting the Cash Reserve Fund and the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund; Legislature intends General Fund transfers beginning FY2025‑26 to fund property tax relief. - Multiple tax-credit caps appear: a $350,000 annual cap in one provision and separate calendar-year caps (e.g., $7.5M for 2025, $1M for 2026+), plus carryforward rules. Department of Administrative Services, Department of Agriculture, Department of Labor, Department of Motor Vehicles - No added provisions, funding changes, or responsibilities for these agencies in the underlined text.
109-1-LB651_IntroLB651_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Military DepartmentThe bill assigns the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to operate the medical cannabis registry (30‑day application decisions; issuance/renewal of registry cards; disposal/transport authorizations; rulemaking). The Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission must collaborate with DHHS, the Department of Agriculture and the Department of Revenue on regulation of cultivation, processing, manufacture, distribution, transportation, testing and sale. Department of Correctional Services (DCS) employees (and jail employees and peace officers) are barred from holding medical cannabis licenses; persons convicted under amended controlled‑substances provisions and sentenced to DCS must attend treatment and counseling. Fiscal changes: creation of a Medical Cannabis Control Fund; application fees split 50/50 between that Fund and local treasurers (credited to local school funds); bonding premiums for commissioners/executive staff paid from the State General Fund. Separately, sales/use tax proceeds on aircraft sales/leases (from July 1, 2023) are credited to the DOT Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund. DHHS, DCS, Military Department, and Department of Agriculture vehicles receive limited exemptions from state lettering for specified operational uses.Summary (focus on named agencies): - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): Defined as "the Department." DHHS will run the patient/caregiver registry, issue/renew registry cards, process applications (30-day target), coordinate authorized transport/disposal of patient-held cannabis, adopt rules to implement the Patient Protection Act, and collaborate with the Medical Cannabis Commission. - Department of Agriculture: Explicitly required to work collaboratively with the Commission on cultivation, processing, manufacture, distribution, transportation, testing, and sale; cultivation standards (pesticides, testing, waste) set by the Commission. - Department of Revenue: Required collaborator; statute directs tax/fee flows. A Medical Cannabis Control Fund is created for commission use. License/application fees: 50% to that fund and 50% to local treasurers (credited to school funds). Proceeds of sales/use taxes on dispensary cannabis sales are credited to the Medical Cannabis Control Fund. - Department of Correctional Services: Employees of jails or the Department are disqualified from licensure; possession/use is prohibited in jails/correctional facilities/youth centers. - Department of Transportation & Military Department: no substantive new duties or funding changes directed to them in the added text (transport rules referenced generally, but no agency-specific allocations). - Funding note: bond/premium costs for commissioners and certain commission employees paid from the General Fund; Medical Cannabis Control Fund authorized to fund commission operations.
109-1-LB652_IntroLB652_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB652 terminates the Board of Educational Lands and Funds on July 1, 2027, and directs the Department of Administrative Services to assume control of all school lands formerly managed by the board. The department must sell those lands as existing leases expire, give the current lessee a right of first refusal, and otherwise sell at public auction. Proceeds from sales are to be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the permanent school fund. Any funds remaining in the temporary school fund on July 1, 2027, are to be distributed to the state's school districts.The amendment terminates the Board of Educational Lands and Funds on July 1, 2027 and transfers control of all school lands it managed to the Department of Administrative Services (DAS) on that date. DAS must sell those lands as existing leases expire; the current lessee has a right of first refusal to buy, otherwise DAS will sell at public auction. Sale proceeds are to be remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the state's permanent school fund. Any monies remaining in the board's temporary school fund on July 1, 2027 will be distributed to school districts. No separate appropriations or direct DAS budget increases are specified.
109-1-LB653_IntroLB653_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB653 references the Department of Administrative Services in two operational funding provisions. It requires the State Treasurer to transfer $1.0 billion (FY2023‑24) and $250 million (FY2024‑25) from the General Fund to the Education Future Fund on dates and in amounts directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services, with legislative intent for $250 million annually beginning FY2025‑26. For monthly special education reimbursements, the State Treasurer must notify the Director of Administrative Services of available General Fund and Education Future Fund balances, and the Director shall draw warrants against those appropriated funds to effect payments.Summary (Department of Administrative Services focus): - The added provisions do not reference or change any roles, appropriations, or budget authority for the Department of Administrative Services (DAS). No DAS funding or allocations are affected. - The bill does create a funding mechanism administered by the State Department of Education: districts may apply (by Oct. 15) to the Education Future Fund for students with IEPs whose expected costs are at least five times the prior year's adjusted average per‑pupil cost. The State Dept. of Education must pay qualifying districts by Nov. 15 an amount equal to the expected cost minus the prior-year adjusted average per pupil; payments are prorated if requests exceed the fund balance. The stated purpose is to fund education/support services so districts can accept more option students. Other non‑fiscal changes address application notices, sibling automatic acceptance, and denial limits for students with IEPs.
109-1-LB654_IntroLB654_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureLB654 appropriates General Fund transfers to the Department of Agriculture (Program 78): $300,000 for FY2025-26 and $300,000 for FY2026-27, designated as state aid. The funds are earmarked to purchase assistive technology and equipment for farmers and ranchers through the Nebraska AgrAbility program where such items are not eligible for U.S. Department of Agriculture funding. The act contains an emergency clause and takes effect upon passage.Appropriates $300,000 General Fund for FY2025-26 and $300,000 General Fund for FY2026-27 to the Department of Agriculture, Program 78 (state aid). The funds are designated for the Nebraska AgrAbility program to purchase assistive technology and equipment for farmers and ranchers when those items are not otherwise eligible for U.S. Department of Agriculture funding.
109-1-LB655_IntroLB655_Intro_Copy.docxLB655 creates statutory protections for conscience-based objections by health care providers and payors and identifies enforcement channels involving government agencies. Key agencies referenced: the Nebraska Attorney General (authorized to receive complaints, investigate, determine violations, commence civil actions seeking damages, injunctive relief and attorney fees, issue subpoenas, compel testimony and evidence, conduct inspections, and promulgate rules), “the department” (statutory recipient of disclosures), any other state agency charged with protecting medical conscience, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and the HHS Office for Civil Rights (and other federal agencies with similar jurisdiction). The bill protects disclosures to those agencies and cites EMTALA (42 U.S.C. 1395dd) for emergency treatment obligations. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds enforcement and reporting provisions naming the state Attorney General, "the department" (unspecified state department), any state agency charged with protecting medical conscience, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, the Office for Civil Rights, and other federal agencies with similar authority as recipients of reports or complaints. Health care providers/payors may report suspected violations to these entities; complaints may be filed with the Attorney General, who may investigate, subpoena, take depositions, inspect (when authorized), commence civil actions (damages, injunctions, fees), and promulgate implementing rules. References federal EMTALA (42 U.S.C. 1395dd). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB656_IntroLB656_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Labor, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill assigns primary responsibility to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to maximize federal SNAP options and federal funding, minimize use of state General Funds, employ necessary personnel, and submit annual and evaluation reports (including administrative costs and federal funding availability) to the Legislature. DHHS must develop a USDA Food and Nutrition Service–approved state outreach plan, may accept gifts/grants/donations and seek federal matching funds, and may decline implementation if private or federal funds are insufficient. DHHS shall create a TANF‑funded policy temporarily increasing gross income eligibility to 165% of OMB poverty guidelines (returning Oct 1, 2025) and must assign most 16–59-year-olds to employment and training programs. The Department of Labor is referenced as administrator of a SNAP Next Step partnership with DHHS; the Legislature intends no General Funds be used by Labor for that program. The bill also bars DHHS from seeking certain federal SNAP work‑requirement waivers.Department of Agriculture - Prohibits the department from seeking, applying for, accepting, or renewing SNAP work‑requirement waivers (7 U.S.C. 2015(o)) unless federally required, and bars use of the state's discretionary exemption under 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(6)(E). - Requires the department to assign all people ages 16–59 to SNAP employment & training programs under 7 U.S.C. 2015(d), subject to enumerated exemptions (e.g., parents/caregivers of children under 6, incapacitated persons, half‑time students, certain employed individuals, inpatient rehab participants, those already under Title IV/unemployment work registration, and some 16–17 year‑olds). Department of Labor - Likely operational impact from increased referrals to employment and training programs, but no statutory changes to Labor’s authority or appropriations. Department of Health and Human Services - Affected by exemption categories (incapacitated persons; inpatient substance‑use treatment), but no new funding or budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB657_IntroLB657_Intro_Copy.docxLB657 amends section 28-101 of the Nebraska Criminal Code to add a new offense, "assault on a sports official." It defines "athletic contest" and "sports official" (including referees, umpires, etc., who are registered with or members of local, state, regional, or national organizations that provide education/training to officials). The offense occurs when a person intentionally or knowingly causes bodily injury to a sports official immediately before, during, or immediately after an athletic contest, and the offender knows or reasonably should know the victim is a sports official. Violation is a Class IV felony. No specific state agencies or departments are named, and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a new offense defining "athletic contest" and "sports official" (including those registered with local, state, regional, or national organizations) and makes intentionally or knowingly causing bodily injury to a sports official immediately before, during, or after such a contest a Class IV felony. No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes included.
109-1-LB658_IntroLB658_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureThe bill explicitly grants the Department of Agriculture authority to investigate all credible complaints that food products are misbranded or falsely advertised as meat products, regardless of whether a political subdivision or another state agency serves as the regulatory authority for food-establishment inspections. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Agriculture are included in the bill.Adds definitions for "agricultural food animal," "cultivated‑protein," "insect‑protein," "plant‑protein," "manufactured‑protein," "identifying meat term," and "qualifying term." Imposes labeling and advertising rules for manufactured‑protein products: any identifying meat term must be accompanied nearby by a conspicuous qualifying term; products sold at food establishments must be stored separately from animal‑derived meat and clearly distinguished (e.g., distinctive shelf tags). Sets criteria for false advertising based on absence of qualifying terms or inadequate separation/identification at retail. Grants the Department of Agriculture authority to investigate credible complaints of misbranding or false advertising of meat products regardless of whether another state or local agency is the food‑inspection authority. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB659_IntroLB659_Intro_Copy.docxLB659 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§32-101 and 32-1049 to impose new testing, reporting, and procedural duties on election commissioners and county clerks and reporting obligations for the Secretary of State. Key agency provisions: - Election commissioners/county clerks must run at least three independent pre-count tests of vote-counting devices (by the commissioner/clerk; the chief deputy or a registered voter of a different party; and the program installer/operator). They must secure ballot transport, retain precinct containers after counting, safeguard device media, handle overvotes/damaged ballots without judging intent, count write-ins, and adopt procedures for ballot pickup, drop-box transport, and same-day counting (no tabulation before one hour prior to poll closing). - Each political party’s county central committee may appoint one watcher; watchers/observers must meet §32-1525 rules and cannot be excluded unless an unobstructed CCTV view is provided. - Commissioners/clerks must certify and submit testing dates and an anticipated completion date to the Secretary of State; the Secretary of State must post certifications on its website and receive a written election‑day plan 25 days before each election. No appropriations or funding changes are included.Requires election commissioners or county clerks who use vote‑counting devices to run at least three independent pre‑count tests (by the commissioner/clerk, a chief deputy or registered voter of a different party, and the device installer/operator). Allows one party watcher per political party appointed and credentialed by each county central committee; watchers/observers must follow section 32‑1525 and may only be excluded if an unobstructed CCTV (or similar) view is provided. Prior to any statewide primary or general election, the election commissioner or county clerk must certify the testing completion date to the Secretary of State, who must post that certification (and be notified of the anticipated completion date). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB65_IntroLB65_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human ServicesThe bill directs the Nebraska Crime Victim Fund to transfer amounts (as determined by the Department of Correctional Services and certified to the Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice) to the Department of Correctional Services Facility Cash Fund and the Supreme Court Automation Cash Fund to pay initial implementation costs of Laws 2010, LB510. After those costs are fully reimbursed, the Crime Victim Fund terminates and remaining receipts are distributed 75% to the Victim’s Compensation Fund and 25% to the Reentry Cash Fund. The Department of Health and Human Services may accept juveniles into temporary care/custody when secure detention is unnecessary, and when a juvenile is committed to DHHS the department must pay costs for the juvenile’s support, study, or treatment not otherwise paid by the parent. No specific appropriations are specified.Adds blanket fee exemptions for any person defined in section 1: no court, probation, testing, program, juvenile diversion, filing, or local participation fees or costs may be charged or imposed; counties must pay waived fees “in the same manner as other claims.” For juveniles, diversion programs cannot condition participation on fines/fees, nonpayment cannot block sealing, and courts may inquire about health insurance and order parents to continue paying deductibles. Impact: Department of Correctional Services — fee prohibitions remove the ability to require or collect probation/program-related fees from covered individuals, potentially reducing agency/local revenue. Department of Health and Human Services — limited operational effect other than courts’ ability to seek/continue private insurance payments (deductibles); no direct programmatic or operational funding changes. No explicit appropriations or new budget allocations are included; potential cost shift to counties.
109-1-LB660_FinalLB660_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Correctional Services, Department of TransportationKey agency provisions in LB660: - Department of Administrative Services (DAS): The State Building Construction Alternatives Act places design‑build and construction manager–general contractor procurement under the state building division of DAS. Authorized agencies must obtain Director of Administrative Services approval before using such contracts. DAS/state building division shall adopt guidelines and will adjust dollar thresholds for contract/letting every four years beginning Jan 1, 2026. The division remits rental proceeds to the State Building Revolving Fund and the State Building Renewal Assessment Fund and must provide periodic project cost and appropriation reports. - Department of Correctional Services: Buildings and grounds owned, leased, or operated by the Department of Correctional Services are exempted from certain DAS facilities administration duties. - Department of Transportation (DOT): The Division of Aeronautics (DOT) will maintain a List of Secure Drones in consultation with DAS. Effective Jan 1, 2027, state agencies may purchase only DOT‑cleared drones; state funds are prohibited for purchases barred by the Act.- Department of Administrative Services (DAS): New approval requirement — agencies must get the DAS director's sign‑off before executing design‑build or construction manager–general contractor contracts, submitting written justifications (cost, schedule, complexity, emergency, competition safeguards). DAS’s State Building Division must adopt RFQ/RFP guidelines and publication rules. Agencies must hire licensed architects/engineers under the Consultants' Competitive Negotiation Act (those hires cannot later bid). DAS will adjust specified dollar amounts every four years starting Jan 1, 2026 using a construction cost/construction‑cost index to account for inflation. DAS is also a consultant on the Secure Drone list. - Department of Transportation (DOT): The Division of Aeronautics must create a List of Secure Drones by Jan 1, 2026; effective Jan 1, 2027 state agencies may only purchase drones on that list. State funds may not be used to buy prohibited drones; violating contracts are void. Security criteria (DoD Blue UAS, NDAA FY2024 compliance, US‑hosted data, AES‑256/TLS, segmented networks, MFA/role‑based access) are specified. - Department of Correctional Services: No additions or funding/appropriation changes affecting DCS in the underlined text. No new appropriations specified.
109-1-LB661_IntroLB661_Intro_Copy.docxBill LB661 assigns and clarifies duties for state investment bodies and officials: - Nebraska Investment Council: appointed members are fiduciaries for investments of Public Employees Retirement Board systems, the Nebraska College Savings Plan, the ABLE program, and state funds; prohibited from investing retirement-system assets in defined "restricted entities" (largely specified China-related lists) and must divest holdings tied to such entities once the State Treasurer publishes the list. - State investment officer: subject to the same prohibition and divestment duty; must file monthly pooled-account operation reports to the Governor, State Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Department of Administrative Services, and the council. - State Treasurer: must create and publish the restricted-entity list by Oct. 1, 2025, and update it at least semiannually. - Legislature: semiannual electronic reports to the Nebraska Retirement Systems Committee and Clerk identifying each restricted entity holding, asset class, and amount; first due Jan. 15, 2026. No funding or appropriations are changed; original statutory sections are repealed. An emergency clause makes the act effective on passage.Adds investment prohibitions, reporting, and list‑creation duties affecting state retirement investments. Key agencies/departments: - State Treasurer (or designee): must create and publish a “restricted entities” list by Oct 1, 2025, and update it at least semiannually. - Public Employees Retirement Board / state investment officer: prohibited from investing in restricted entities; must identify and divest retirement holdings in such entities as soon as practicable. - Nebraska Retirement Systems Committee of the Legislature and Clerk of the Legislature: receive semiannual electronic reports from the state investment officer (first due Jan 15, 2026, then semiannually). - Federal agencies and lists referenced as bases for restriction: Office of Foreign Assets Control (U.S. Dept. of the Treasury), U.S. Dept. of Defense, Federal Communications Commission, U.S. Dept. of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (plus referenced Presidential orders). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are added.
109-1-LB662_IntroLB662_Intro_Copy.docxLB662 requires each state agency to prepare and maintain a federal funding inventory. For each federal receipt the inventory must identify positions obligated by the agreement; other resources or obligations incurred by the agency; the applicable federal law, regulation, or grant citation; an operating plan if federal receipts decline by 10% or more from the prior fiscal year; the actions or results promised to obtain the funds; the state statutory objective served; and a list of receipts with foreseeable end dates and schedules. The bill does not make appropriations or change funding allocations.Adds reporting requirements for any state agency that accepts federal receipts. Agencies must report positions obligated by the agreement; other resources or obligations incurred; the federal law/regulation/grant citation; an operating plan if federal receipts fall by 10%+ from the prior fiscal year; the actions/results promised to receive the funds; the state statutory objective met by accepting the funds; and a list of federal receipts with foreseeable end dates and the expected receipt schedule. No specific agencies are named and no direct appropriation or budget allocation changes are included.
109-1-LB663_IntroLB663_Intro_Copy.docxLB663 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §23-114.01 governing county planning commissions and county boards. Key agency provisions: - Requires each county planning commission member and each county board member to complete two hours of role-specific education per term, developed and presented by the respective county attorney. - Clarifies conditional-use/special-exception procedures for county planning commissions and county boards: mandatory written factual findings with decisions; timelines for completeness determinations and final action (commission: 30/10/30/90-day sequence; board: 30/10/30/90-day sequence); presumption that applicants will comply with local, state, and federal requirements (burden shifts to challenger); and prohibition on conditioning approvals on obtaining other agency permits. - Retains existing compensation/per diem provisions and appellate routes (county board or district court as applicable). No new appropriations or funding changes are included.- Requires each planning commission member and county board member to complete two hours of role-specific education per term; the respective county attorney must develop and present that training. - States that conditional use permits/special exceptions must be decided based solely on county zoning regulations; commissions/boards cannot condition approval on applicants obtaining other federal, state, or local agency permits, nor are applicants relieved of any separate agency permit requirements. - Establishes a presumption that applicants will comply with all local, state, and federal requirements; challengers bear the burden of proof, and absent contrary evidence the commission/board must approve. - Sets procedural deadlines: commission—30 days to deem an application complete (10-day notice of deficiencies, 30 days after supplemental info, 90 days to act or recommend); board—mirror 30/10/30/90 timelines to determine completeness and decide. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB664_IntroLB664_Intro_Copy.docxLB664 amends Nebraska’s Administrative Procedure Act. It requires state agencies considering rules to solicit public comment (including by newspaper notice), permit any person to submit supportive or opposing comments or materials by mail or electronically, and not force in‑person submissions. The bill revises judicial review of agency rules: declaratory‑judgment petitions may be filed in district court in the petitioner’s residence county, the petitioner’s principal business county, Lancaster County, or the county of the agency’s headquarters; the agency must be made a party. Courts may invalidate rules that violate the constitution, exceed statutory authority, or were adopted without required statutory procedures (excluding Negotiated Rulemaking Act procedures). Agencies are barred from restricting venue. Original sections repealed; emergency effective date. No funding or appropriation changes.Requires any Nebraska state agency, when proposing or adopting rules, to accept public comments or materials in support or opposition electronically or by mail and not to require in‑person travel to submit them. Establishes that petitions challenging agency action must be filed in district court in a county with proper venue: the petitioner’s county of residence, the county of the petitioner’s principal place of business, Lancaster County, or the county where the agency has its headquarters. Prohibits agencies from imposing restrictions that would contravene these venue rules.
