No specific departments are named beyond generic "agency" and Lancaster County; there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB665_IntroLB665_Intro_Copy.docxLB665 amends the Animal Health and Disease Control Act. It defines "foreign adversary" by reference to 15 C.F.R. 791.4 (as of Jan 1, 2025). The bill: adopts 9 C.F.R. part 86 (animal disease traceability, as of Jan 1, 2020) by reference but gives the state act, rules, or Department of Agriculture orders precedence if inconsistent; authorizes use of USDA/APHIS/VS program standards; and clarifies who may apply official identification devices (owner, owner's representative, accredited veterinarian, approved tagging site) and limited removal circumstances. Crucially, it prohibits application of electronic identification devices manufactured by entities with direct or indirect ties to a foreign adversary and prohibits the Nebraska Department of Agriculture from requiring use of foreign‑manufactured electronic ID devices. No funding or appropriation changes.Defines "foreign adversary" by reference to 15 C.F.R. 791.4 (as of Jan 1, 2025). Establishes state policy prioritizing protection/conservation of livestock and private property rights over government bureaucracy, and frames foreign adversaries using surveillance tech as a security threat. Prohibits within the state the use or application of electronic identification devices for livestock if manufactured by entities with direct or indirect ties to a foreign adversary. Further bars "the department" (unnamed in the excerpt) from requiring use of foreign‑manufactured electronic animal identification for identifying or tracking livestock. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB666_IntroLB666_Intro_Copy.docxLB666 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §86‑1505 (Rural Communications Sustainability Act) to require the Nebraska Public Service Commission to act expeditiously, upon request by either the incumbent carrier or the competitive provider after a granting agency makes final payment under a broadband deployment program, to: - relieve the incumbent carrier of eligible telecommunications carrier (ETC) and carrier‑of‑last‑resort obligations in the affected deployment project area if the granting agency finds the competitive provider compliant; - determine allocations and distributions of support from the Nebraska Telecommunications Universal Service Fund for the deployment project area (consistent with Commission procedure rules); and - in coordination with the Federal Communications Commission and after consulting both carriers, determine whether ETC and carrier‑of‑last‑resort obligations tied to Nebraska Universal Service Fund support should be transferred to the competitive provider. The original section is repealed. No specific appropriations or dollar changes are included.Adds the phrase "or competitive provider expeditiously," indicating a requirement to move to or select a competitive provider promptly. No government agencies, departments, funding changes, appropriations, or budget allocations are referenced in this added text.
109-1-LB667_FinalLB667_Final_Copy.docxLB667 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §60-1438 (Motor Vehicle Industry Regulation Act). Key agency/process changes: dealers may establish an average parts markup by submitting 100 sequential or 90 days of customer-paid repair orders; manufacturers have 30 days to audit and 45 days after approval for the markup to take effect. If a manufacturer denies the declared markup, the dealer may complain to the board, which can find the denial an Act violation. Franchisors who supply parts at no or reduced cost must compensate dealers based on dealer cost plus markup multiplied by the part’s fair wholesale value (defined by three benchmarks). Manufacturers/distributors may request up to 100 additional repair orders (with specified timeframes and limitations) to reassess dealer rates and may adjust payments accordingly. The bill also sets timelines for claim submission, payment, audits, recall parts availability notices, and dealer compensation for recalls. No appropriations or budget changes are included.No government agencies or departments are mentioned, and there are no funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text. Summary of substantive changes: - When calculating parts compensation, retail sales tied to warranty repairs cannot be used; markups for recommended maintenance parts (oil, filters, fluids, brake components, spark plugs, wiper blades, tire repair/replacement, etc.) cannot be used. - If a franchisor supplies a part free or at reduced cost for warranty work, the franchisor must pay the dealer the dealer's cost plus the dealer’s markup, multiplied by the part’s “fair wholesale value.” - “Fair wholesale value” = greatest of: dealer’s paid amount; franchisor’s price-schedule cost at time furnished; cost of a substantially identical part in franchisor’s price schedule. - Manufacturers/distributors may request up to 100 additional dealer repair orders (from a dealer-selected 90‑day period within the past 12 months) to verify markup/labor rates, may adjust warranty payments if nonwarranty rates are lower, and dealers have 30 days to rebut. Requests cannot be made more than once in a 12‑month period. - Parties may mutually agree on retail labor or markup rates.
109-1-LB668_IntroLB668_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB668 assigns or clarifies multiple duties and authorities for the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): - DHHS must notify subjects before entering names on the Adult Protective Services central registry or the central registry of child protection cases, and a timely appeal request prevents entry until DHHS issues a final order. DHHS may amend/expunge identifying information or remove substantiated reports per statutory procedures. - DHHS shall maintain the child protection central registry, process name‑change cross‑references, and annually report registry data to the Governor and the Health and Human Services and Judiciary committee chairs. - DHHS may charge up to $5 per central‑registry records check, remit fees to the State Treasurer for credit to the Health and Human Services Cash Fund, waive fees for hardship, and use fees to defray costs. - Case managers for juveniles in DHHS care must be DHHS employees, except contracted providers may serve for defined prevention cases; DHHS case manager duties are specified.Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) must notify individuals at least 14 days before entering their name on the central registries (vulnerable adult or child protection) and inform them of the right to contest. Subjects have 14 days to appeal; appeals are handled under the Administrative Procedure Act, and if a timely appeal is filed DHHS may not enter the name until it issues a final order. DHHS may also use contracted providers as case managers for "prevention cases," defined by the department’s Families First prevention plan as: a household with at least one juvenile who meets the department’s candidate-for-foster-care criteria, no need for ongoing child-welfare services to maintain safety, and voluntary family engagement in community services. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB669_IntroLB669_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services- Defines "hospital" as institutions licensed by the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) under the Health Care Facility Licensure Act. - Requires physicians or their agents to inform patients that DHHS's website provides information on finding immediate medical assistance if they change their mind after taking mifepristone. - Requires physicians to notify patients that printed materials provided by DHHS describe the unborn child, list agencies offering alternatives to abortion, and include the mifepristone assistance information; DHHS must publish and make those materials available for physicians to be subject to civil liability for failing to offer them. - Mandates that, if requested, physicians provide a comprehensive, geographically arranged list compiled by DHHS of providers, facilities, and clinics that offer ultrasounds (including those offering free ultrasounds), with contact details. - The bill contains no explicit changes to DHHS funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds requirements that licensed providers must, in a private manner, ask and evaluate pregnant women whether they are being coerced into abortion, have experienced interpersonal/domestic violence, or have been victims of human trafficking. If a woman discloses coercion, domestic violence, or trafficking, the provider must give the national domestic violence and national human trafficking hotline numbers and offer the woman an opportunity to make a confidential telephone call. The provision also requires asking these screening questions and providing the phone numbers and call opportunity when applicable. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included; the Department of Health and Human Services would likely have oversight/implementation and potential training or administrative duties, but no new budget authority is provided.
109-1-LB66_IntroLB66_Intro_Copy.docxBill LB66 adopts the Uniform Health‑Care Decisions Act, establishing roles and procedures for courts, guardians, health‑care professionals, health‑care institutions, nursing homes and assisted‑living facilities (see §71‑5903), emergency medical responders, and medical‑records administrators. Key agency-related provisions: courts must hold hearings and determine incapacity within seven days by clear-and-convincing evidence; responsible health‑care professionals and record administrators must document and communicate advance health‑care directives and instructions; health‑care institutions may refuse care on conscience or capacity grounds but must notify and attempt transfer and provide limited continuing care; guardianship and default surrogate authorities and disqualifications are defined; emergency medical responders receive limited liability protections. The bill creates civil remedies with statutory damages and attorney fees. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds a comprehensive advance health‑care directive scheme referencing courts for capacity determinations and enforcement and citing the federal Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1396r(a)(1)) for the nursing‑home definition. It regulates health‑care institutions, health‑care professionals (including emergency medical responders), guardians, agents, and default surrogates (with disqualification rules for nursing‑home staff). Includes electronic witnessing, an optional mental‑health‑only directive with limited irrevocability, required documentation in medical records, limits on agent consent for long nursing‑home placements and forced admissions, transfer/continuity obligations for providers, civil remedies and statutory damages, and interstate recognition. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB670_IntroLB670_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to adopt and promulgate rules for mandatory training for child care and school-age-care providers. Requirements include a preservice orientation and annual inservice training limited to no more than four hours. Licensed child care programs must complete a DHHS‑approved or -delivered preservice orientation before receiving a provisional license. For programs reporting to the Nebraska Early Childhood Professional Record System, DHHS shall use that system to document staff training levels and verify minimum training requirements. DHHS must provide or arrange statewide training opportunities and information at registration/licensure/renewal, require attendees to submit their Social Security number, and review and recommend rule updates to the Governor at least every five years. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.Added provisions require each public and nonpublic school board to adopt and annually update a safety plan (fire, tornado/ weather, vehicle evacuation, and other drills as appropriate). Districts must submit their safety plan to the state school security director every three years; the director may offer suggestions, training, and resources and provide a model plan. The State Board of Education is barred from requiring more than four hours of annual inservice training for teachers, paraeducators, and pre-K home visitors (local boards may impose more). Initial evidence-based training is capped at 12 hours; recommendations and minimum safety standards may be issued to nonpublic schools. Department of Health and Human Services is not mentioned and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget changes.
109-1-LB671_IntroLB671_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB671 permits the State Department of Education to work with the Department of Labor (and other entities) to develop and implement the Nebraska Teacher Apprenticeship Program. The program uses an apprenticeship model leading to a Commissioner‑issued teaching certificate for completers. The bill expresses legislative intent to appropriate $1,000,000 annually from the Education Future Fund beginning FY2023‑24 to the State Department of Education for the program.The additions require Boards and the Commissioner of Education to expand reports under §79-528, §79-237, and §79-11,157.01 to include detailed information on K–3 students who display reading deficiencies (including dyslexia characteristics), with counts by grade and by school, and to adopt accreditation rule provisions pursuant to §§79-318 and 79-703. Reports may withhold information as allowed under §84-712.05. There is no mention of the Department of Labor or any directed changes to its statutes. The draft contains an unclear reference to “funding”/“October 15 Act contract,” but no specific appropriations, budget allocations, or funding transfers to the Department of Labor are identified.
109-1-LB672_IntroLB672_Intro_Copy.docxLB672 (Raybould) amends the Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act (sec. 49-1401) to cap contributions to a candidate committee at $1,000 per donor during an election period (defined as the calendar year of the election). Candidate committees must refund within ten days any contribution that causes a donor to exceed $1,000 and must disclose on subsequent campaign statements the contributor's name and address, amount received, date received, and date returned. A candidate's personal funds are exempt. The bill was referred to the Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee and repeals the original section 49-1401. No state agency funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed or referenced.Adds a $1,000 per-person contribution limit to a candidate committee for an election period (defined as the calendar year of the election). Candidate committees must refund any contribution that causes a person’s total to exceed $1,000 within 10 days and disclose the refund on subsequent campaign statements, including contributor name and address, amount received, date received, and date returned. Candidate's personal funds are exempt. No government agencies, departments, appropriations, or budget changes are referenced.
109-1-LB673_IntroLB673_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesRequires the State Treasurer to transfer $500,000,000 from the Perkins County Canal Project Fund to the Water Sustainability Fund on or before June 30, 2025. The timing and amounts of transfers are to be set by the budget administrator of the Budget Division of the Department of Administrative Services.Requires the State Treasurer to transfer $500 million from the Perkins County Canal Project Fund to the Water Sustainability Fund by June 30, 2025. The timing and installment amounts of that transfer are to be set by the budget administrator of the Budget Division within the Department of Administrative Services. No other appropriations or new funding lines are specified.
109-1-LB674_IntroLB674_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesThe bill directs the State Treasurer to transfer a total of $500 million from the Perkins County Canal Project Fund by June 30, 2025: $250 million to the General Fund and $250 million to the Water Sustainability Fund. Both transfers are to occur on such dates and in such amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services.Requires the State Treasurer to make two transfers from the Perkins County Canal Project Fund by June 30, 2025: $250 million to the General Fund and $250 million to the Water Sustainability Fund. The timing and specific amounts of each transfer are to be set by the budget administrator in the Budget Division of the Department of Administrative Services, giving that DAS official directional control over the transfers' schedule and allocation. Total redirected funds: $500 million.
109-1-LB675_IntroLB675_Intro_Copy.docxLB675 amends school-land statutes to change how the Board of Educational Lands and Funds and the Governor handle transactions involving lands within Indian reservation boundaries. Key agency actions: - Board of Educational Lands and Funds: must give the Indian tribe with jurisdiction a first right of refusal to purchase or lease school lands located within reservation boundaries; may adopt leasing rules, enforce a soil conservation program, and enter into land-exchange agreements with the U.S. Government. - Governor: must provide written approval for exchanges of state educational lands with individuals or tribes; the Board must find sales/exchanges to tribes are not detrimental to state interests. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds tribal rights and Board authority regarding state school/educational lands. Key points: - The Board of Educational Lands and Funds must give an Indian tribe with jurisdiction over reservation lands the first right of refusal to purchase or to lease any school lands located within reservation boundaries (references definitions in §§81‑2509 and 43‑1503). - The Board, with the Governor’s written approval, may enter agreements with an Indian tribe to sell or exchange state educational lands for other lands of equal area or value. If the lands are within a reservation, the Board must first determine the sale/exchange is not detrimental to state interests. - No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB676_IntroLB676_Intro_Copy.docxLB676 amends the Certified Nurse Midwifery Practice Act and related credentialing statutes. It directs the state credentialing board to monitor CNM scope of practice, recommend disciplinary action, and adopt rules (for promulgation by the department) including approved certification organizations and professional liability insurance. The board may require midwifery programs be accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Midwifery Education. The bill removes practice-agreement requirements, revises definitions (including collaboration and consultation), clarifies CNM scope (prenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, gynecologic, newborn care to 28 days, prescribing within scope, death pronouncement), and adds certified nurse midwives to the Nebraska Hospital‑Medical Liability Act definition of health care provider. No appropriations or funding changes are included.Adds the Accreditation Commission for Midwifery Education and defines “health care provider” as a professional licensed under the Uniform Credentialing Act. Establishes that certified nurse midwives may consult with physicians or other licensed health care providers, must refer care beyond their scope, and specifies midwifery scope (prenatal/intrapartum/postpartum care, gynecologic and female primary care, newborn care to 28 days, ordering tests/treatments, prescribing within scope, dispensing manufacturer-provided samples, pronouncing death/signing death certificates). No government funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB677A_IntroLB677A_Intro_Copy.docxAppropriates $1 from the Medical Cannabis Control Fund to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission (Program 96) for FY2025-26 and $1 for FY2026-27 to aid implementation of Legislative Bill 677. Expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from these appropriated funds are capped at $1 for each fiscal year. The act includes an emergency clause, making it effective upon passage.Appropriates $1 in FY2025‑26 and $1 in FY2026‑27 from the Medical Cannabis Control Fund to the Nebraska Liquor Control Commission (Program 96) to support implementation of Legislative Bill 677 (109th Leg., 1st Sess., 2025). Specifies that total expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems from these appropriated amounts shall not exceed $1 in each fiscal year.
109-1-LB677_IntroLB677_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Military DepartmentLB677 requires the Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission to coordinate with the Department of Agriculture, Department of Revenue, and Department of Health and Human Services on cultivation, processing, testing, distribution, transportation and sale compliance. It creates a Medical Cannabis Control Fund (fees, gifts, grants; application fees remitted to the State Treasurer credited to the fund) to finance commission operations; bonding premiums for commission employees are paid from the General Fund. Department of Correctional Services employees (and jail employees/peace officers) are barred from holding medical cannabis licenses; persons sentenced to DOC under amended Section 28-416 must receive drug‑abuse treatment while incarcerated. Vehicle‑lettering exemptions are extended to DOC and DHHS (for offender transport, communicable disease control, drug investigations), to the Military Department, and to Agriculture for special investigations. Sales/use tax proceeds from aircraft sales/leases are credited to the DOT Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund; medical cannabis sales to qualified patients/caregivers are taxed at 4%, with dispensary proceeds credited to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund.Summary of additions affecting specified agencies: - Department of Agriculture: Required to collaborate with the Medical Cannabis Commission on regulation. Commission rules for cultivators include pesticide, residue testing, destruction, record‑keeping and waste disposal standards—areas overlapping agricultural expertise. - Department of Correctional Services: Possession or use of medical cannabis is prohibited in jails, correctional facilities, and youth centers; employees of a jail or the Department of Correctional Services are disqualified from holding licenses. - Department of Health and Human Services: Required collaborator with the commission; health‑care practitioner recommendations and health‑care facility accommodations/restrictions addressed (patient access, consumption limits). - Department of Revenue: Collaborative role; application and license fees are credited to a new Medical Cannabis Control Fund. Sales/use tax proceeds on dispensary sales to qualified patients are directed to the School District Property Tax Relief Credit Fund (via State Treasurer/Revenue administration). - Department of Transportation: Commission may set transporter standards (insurance, timeframes, vehicle requirements); no direct DOT funding changes. - Military Department: No references or fiscal changes.
109-1-LB678_IntroLB678_Intro_Copy.docxLB678 directs General Fund appropriations to the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges (Program 48): unspecified sums ($XXX) for FY2025‑26 and FY2026‑27. Funds are earmarked for salary increases required by negotiated agreements with the Nebraska Association of Public Employees, the State College Education Association, and the Nebraska State College System Professional Association; to cover minimum wage increases required by the Wage and Hour Act; and to cover increased health insurance premiums. The bill includes an emergency clause making it effective on enactment.Appropriates two General Fund amounts (one for FY2025-26 and one for FY2026-27) to the Board of Trustees of the Nebraska State Colleges, Program 48. Funds are for salary increases required by negotiated agreements with the Nebraska Association of Public Employees, the State College Education Association, and the Nebraska State College System Professional Association, to cover minimum-wage increases mandated by the Wage and Hour Act, and to pay higher health insurance premiums.
109-1-LB679_IntroLB679_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborThe bill ties annual adjustments of the statutory attorney’s fee awarded in tax-foreclosure decrees to the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, Midwest Region, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the United States Department of Labor (or its successor agency). Specifically, the fee will be increased beginning January 1, 2027, and each January 1 thereafter by the percentage change in the CPI as measured in August year-over-year. No Department of Labor funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are changed or provided.The amendment requires that attorney's fees awarded under the section be increased beginning January 1, 2027, and annually thereafter by the percent change (as of August) in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, Midwest Region, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the U.S. Department of Labor (or its successor). The Department of Labor is cited only as the CPI publisher; no new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor are created.
109-1-LB67_IntroLB67_Intro_Copy.docxLB67 creates the Sexual Assault Emergency Care Act and assigns enforcement and oversight functions to "the department" (and its director), with appeal rights under the Administrative Procedure Act. Hospitals providing emergency care must offer and, unless declined, dispense emergency contraception, provide written/oral information, train personnel, and adopt policies to address staff moral or religious objections. Complaints may be filed with the department, which may investigate, conduct informal conferences (department or contracted peer review representative), hold hearings, and issue written decisions. Sanctions: a first substantiated complaint results in a written warning and corrective requirements; second and subsequent substantiated complaints carry fines of $1,000 per affected survivor or $1,000 per month until required training is provided. No appropriations or other budget allocations are specified.Adds a complaints/enforcement process centered on "the department" (the agency charged with enforcing the Sexual Assault Emergency Care Act) and its director, and permits use of contracted peer review organizations. Key points: - Any complaint about compliance may be filed with the department; the department decides whether to investigate using listed factors. - Procedural timelines: hospitals have 15 days to respond to notices; informal conferences must be held within 30 days; reports, decisions, and appeal-request windows are specified (20 working days, 10 working days, 5 working days, 30 days, respectively). - The director assigns an investigator or peer-review representative (not the original investigator) for informal conferences; hearings follow department rules and Administrative Procedure Act appeal rights apply. Witnesses may be subpoenaed and paid per rule. - Sanctions: first substantiated complaint = written warning and required corrective action. Second and subsequent = $1,000 fines either per survivor denied emergency contraception information/offering or per month until required training is provided.
109-1-LB680_IntroLB680_Intro_Copy.docxLB680 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §79‑1204 to clarify the role and mission of educational service units (ESUs). ESUs are designated as providers of core and requested services to member school districts and must act cooperatively with the State Department of Education in planning and implementing statewide long‑range educational goals. The State Board of Education retains authority to set minimum accreditation standards for ESUs to ensure taxpayer accountability, equitable statewide services, and program quality. ESUs may administer federal, state, and private funds for participating districts "when appropriate and as funds become available," may contract with nonmember districts, nonpublic schools, other ESUs, and other public agencies (via the Interlocal Cooperation Act and Joint Public Agency Act), and may use ESU funds to pay board membership dues. No specific appropriations or funding allocations are made.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB681_IntroLB681_Intro_Copy.docxLB681, introduced by the Legislature’s Education Committee, amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §85-931 to revise the statutory definition of "graduate degree programs." The bill lists covered first professional degrees, expands and itemizes master's degree professional and general academic/occupational program examples, and confirms doctoral degrees (e.g., Ph.D., Ed.D., D.A.). No state agencies or departments beyond the Legislature and its Education Committee are referenced, and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations. The original §85-931 is repealed.The addition simply inserts a definitional/reference line enumerating subsection identifiers — (2)(a), (b); (i)–(xvii); and (c)(i)–(xii). It contains no mention of any government agencies, departments, or programs and makes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB682_IntroLB682_Intro_Copy.docxLB682 (amending Neb. Rev. Stat. §79-770) requires school districts, at a parent/guardian's request, to issue a certificate of attendance to students receiving services under the Special Education Act who are 17 and have not completed their individualized education program (IEP). It permits such students to participate in a high school graduation ceremony (one certificate and one ceremony), preserves the district’s obligation to continue special education services, and allows participation in a later ceremony if the student subsequently earns a diploma. The bill cites Neb. sections 79-729 and 79-730 and repeals the original §79-770. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.I don’t see the underlined text to summarize — you’ve only provided “program program.” Please paste the actual added (underlined) bill text or upload a screenshot/PDF of it.
