109-1-LB683_IntroLB683_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB683 requires county assessors to transmit the statutorily required real‑property valuation notices to the Department of Administrative Services for state printing. The bill also alters treatment of excess tax collections: political subdivisions must return excess countywide levy proceeds net of collection fee; county treasurers must certify return amounts by July 31 of the following fiscal year; and for fiscal years beginning prior to July 1, 2025, such excess collections are designated as restricted funds in the receiving county's budget under section 13‑518.The added text requires each county assessor to transmit property valuation/notice mailings to the Department of Administrative Services for state printing. Notices must include prior and current year valuations and levies, budget hearing times/places (reported by political subdivisions), and a prominent "KNOW YOUR RIGHTS" protest/blurb. Political subdivisions must report budget hearing time/place to county assessors by May 15. No explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Administrative Services are specified in the text. (Potential printing costs or administrative impacts are not addressed in the provision.)
109-1-LB684_IntroLB684_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative Services, Department of Economic Development, Department of Labor, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor VehiclesThe bill creates a statewide Juvenile Probation Agency and imposes reporting and budget actions involving state agencies. The Juvenile Probation Administrator must submit semiannual reports to the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services; valid encumbrances certified to DAS’s accounting division as of June 30, 2026, will be paid by the Juvenile Probation Agency from existing unexpended appropriations. Certain FY2025–26 appropriations and salary limits enacted for the Supreme Court are nullified and reappropriated to the Office of Probation Administration/Juvenile Probation Agency. DHHS remains the Title IV‑E single state agency, must seek IV‑E reimbursements (remitted to the Juvenile Probation Program Cash Fund), may receive sealed juvenile records for case purposes, provide foster‑care oversight and transition supports, and will transfer some community‑services/parole funds to the new agency. Courts must send adjudication abstracts to the DMV; the DMV, DOL, DCS, and DED are named in related records, employment‑access, and interagency integration provisions.Key points affecting agencies and funding: - Reporting: The Juvenile Probation Administrator must electronically report to the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services (DAS), the Legislative Fiscal Analyst, and the Supreme Court on Jan. 15 and July 15 each fiscal year (case and intake/detention counts). - Appropriations/Transfers: On and after July 1, 2026, probation positions transfer to the new Juvenile Probation Agency; transferred employees retain state personnel/bargaining rights. Any FY2025‑26 appropriations and salary limits previously enacted to the Supreme Court for specified program classifications are voided and reappropriated to the Office of Probation Administration (new agency). - Encumbrances/accounting: Valid unpaid obligations certified to the accounting division of DAS will be paid by the Juvenile Probation Agency from unexpended balances in those program classifications. - Funds/costs: A Juvenile Probation Contractual Services Cash Fund is created; the state pays salaries, travel, drug testing, electronic surveillance equipment, and interpreter costs (via Supreme Court appropriations or other funds). - Departments of Economic Development, Labor, Correctional Services, Health & Human Services, and Motor Vehicles are not addressed or changed in the added text.
109-1-LB685_IntroLB685_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesLB685 amends section 84-612 to clarify that transfers to and from the Cash Reserve Fund are executed by the State Treasurer on dates and in amounts as directed by the budget administrator of the budget division of the Department of Administrative Services. It preserves the requirement that the Director of Administrative Services certify when the General Fund cash balance is inadequate (and may notify to reverse transfers). The bill lists numerous specified transfers that are to be carried out under that direction and adds a new transfer: $1,000,000 from the Cash Reserve Fund to the School Safety and Security Fund to be made as soon as administratively possible after the act’s effective date.The addition directs a $1,000,000 transfer from the Cash Reserve Fund into the School Safety and Security Fund to be used for grants (per section 79-3108) for exterior secure master key boxes. A subaccount must be established to hold those funds. The State Treasurer is ordered to make the transfer "as soon as administratively possible" after the bill's effective date, with the timing and amounts to be set by the budget administrator of the Budget Division of the Department of Administrative Services.
109-1-LB686_IntroLB686_Intro_Copy.docxLB686 prohibits government entities and officials from knowingly keeping lists, records, or registries of privately owned firearms or firearm owners, except records kept in the regular course of a criminal investigation, prosecution, or as otherwise required by law. It bars payment card networks from requiring or incentivizing merchant category codes (MCCs) that distinguish firearm retailers, and prohibits covered entities from assigning such distinguishing MCCs. Enforcement is vested exclusively in the Nebraska Attorney General, who may investigate, issue a written notice to cease, file for injunctions, and, for noncompliance after injunction, seek civil fines up to $1,000 per violation (with the court weighing violator resources and harm to constitutional rights). A lawful requirement to assign an MCC is an available defense. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are provided.- Agency: Nebraska Attorney General — given exclusive authority to investigate alleged violations of the new prohibitions on keeping firearm ownership registries and on assigning or requiring merchant category codes that distinguish firearm retailers. - Enforcement process/timeline: AG must issue written notice; alleged violator has 30 business days to cease. If not, AG may seek a court injunction; noncompliance with an injunction after 30 business days exposes the violator to civil fines. - Penalties: Civil fines up to $1,000 per violation; courts must consider violator’s financial resources and harm to the state constitutional right to keep and bear arms. Fines are stayed pending appeal. - Other: Defense exists if a merchant category code was required by law. - Budget/funding: No changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB687_IntroLB687_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Administrative ServicesSection 5 assigns the Department of Administrative Services the authority and responsibility to review state agency contracts to confirm compliance with the Firearm Industry Nondiscrimination Act. The bill includes no language authorizing additional funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department.The added language creates a "Firearm Industry Nondiscrimination Act" requiring covered government contracts (companies with ≥10 FTEs, contract value ≥$100,000, entered on/after the act's effective date) to include company verification they will not discriminate against firearm entities/trade associations; exemptions include sole‑source contracts or lack of compliant bidders. The Department of Administrative Services is given authority and responsibility to review state agency contracts for compliance. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for DAS oversight are specified.
109-1-LB688_IntroLB688_Intro_Copy.docxLB688 makes it unlawful for any person to advertise an "electronic nicotine delivery system" in Nebraska, using the definition already established in Neb. Rev. Stat. §28-1418.01. The bill contains no references to any specific state agencies or departments, and it includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.Adds a definition reference and a statewide ban on advertising electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS): ENDS is defined by referral to section 28‑1418.01, and it becomes unlawful to advertise any ENDS in Nebraska. No government agencies or departments are named and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes included.
109-1-LB689_IntroLB689_Intro_Copy.docxLB689 amends §§79‑930 and 79‑992 (School Employees Retirement Act and Class V Act). Key agency actions and changes: - Nebraska Public Employees Retirement Systems (NPERS) director: may determine whether a returning member has satisfied a 180‑day separation requirement based on clear-and-convincing evidence received within 45 days; member may appeal to the retirement board. The board’s appeal decision is final and not judicially reviewable. - Retirement board/administrator (Class V): analogous authority to issue 180‑day determinations and receive appeals; administrator decisions appealable to the board; board decisions final. - Substantive benefit rules clarified: work as temporary, substitute, or volunteer generally does not count for contributions or service credit unless the member becomes a regular employee (then contributions and credit begin immediately, including prior temp/substitute work). - Direct rollover designation for refunds transitions to designation by the retirement board beginning September 1, 2024. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB68_IntroLB68_Intro_Copy.docxLB68 amends the Medical Assistance Act to require coverage and reimbursement rules for FDA‑approved self‑administered hormonal contraceptives. Insurers (individual/group sickness and accident, hospital/medical/surgical, and self‑funded employer plans to the extent not federally preempted) must reimburse in‑network health care providers or dispensing entities per unit: up to a three‑month supply on the first prescription and up to a twelve‑month supply for subsequent refills. Under the Medical Assistance Program, "the department" is directed to ensure a prescription for a one‑time twelve‑month dispensation. The bill references the federal Food and Drug Administration as the approval authority. No changes to appropriations, funding, or budget allocations are included.Adds coverage and dispensing requirements for FDA‑approved self‑administered hormonal contraceptives: insurers, hospital/medical policies, and non‑preempted self‑funded employer plans must reimburse in‑network providers per unit — first prescription up to a three‑month supply, subsequent refills up to a twelve‑month supply. It clarifies providers are not required to prescribe 12‑month supplies and plans may not impose cost‑sharing for an alternative method if a patient switches before using the previously dispensed supply. The federal Food and Drug Administration is referenced for product approval. The bill also directs "the department" administering the medical assistance (Medicaid) family planning program to ensure a one‑time dispensation of a 12‑month supply. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB690_IntroLB690_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor Vehicles, Department of TransportationThe bill designates the "Department" in the Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act as the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) and assigns DMV duties to prescribe the LPE‑learner's permit written exam, collect school and LPE‑learner permit fees/surcharges (by department staff or county treasurers), approve motorcycle safety‑course proof forms, and update DMV systems to record course‑completion dates on driving records. Fiscal provisions: a $50 special‑interest license plate fee is split $25 to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund and $25 to the Highway Trust Fund; DMV may charge a postage/handling fee for mailing plates, remitted to the DMV Cash Fund; if plate manufacturing costs exceed the statutory charge, the excess is credited first to the Highway Trust Fund (to cover the difference) and any remainder to the DMV Cash Fund. Proceeds of sales/use tax on aircraft sales/leases (on/after July 1, 2023) are credited to the Department of Transportation Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund. The act becomes operative January 1, 2026.Summary for agencies: - Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): Adds ATVs and utility‑type vehicles (UTVs) into the Motor Vehicle Registration Act when registered. Requires certificates of title, issues license plates, and sets registration fees at $10 for both ATVs and UTVs. Incorporates the phrase "manufactured for off‑road use" into title/registration language. - Department of Transportation (DOT): Clarifies where registered ATVs/UTVs may be operated—permits operation on county and township roads outside municipal limits (per §60‑6,356) but prohibits use on the Interstate System, state highways, expressways, and freeways; adopts vehicle definitions that affect applicability to DOT‑managed roadways. - Funding: No changes to appropriations, budget allocations, or new funding streams are included in the added text.
109-1-LB691_IntroLB691_Intro_Copy.docxLB691 requires each public school board and the governing board of any approved or accredited private, denominational, or parochial school that receives state funds to display the Ten Commandments: in every elementary classroom and in each middle‑ or high‑school building. Boards determine the display’s appearance subject to minimum specifications (text, at least 11"×14", specified wording). The State Board of Education is authorized to adopt rules and regulations to implement the law. The bill does not appropriate funds or require schools to expend budgeted dollars for displays; schools may accept contributions or donated displays to cover costs.Requires each public school district school board—and governing boards of approved/accredited private, denominational, or parochial schools that receive state funds—to display the Ten Commandments: in every elementary classroom and in each middle/high school building. Boards set display style but must include the full text and a poster/framed size of at least 11" x 14". Schools are not required to use their funds to purchase displays; boards may accept donations or contributions to cover costs. The State Board of Education may adopt rules to implement the requirement. No new appropriations or budget allocations are provided.
109-1-LB692_IntroLB692_Intro_Copy.docxThis bill amends provisions for calculating and accounting school district property tax request authority. The state "department" (responsible for calculating and certifying authority to school boards) must annually: compute each district's property tax request authority using a specified formula that adjusts prior-year requests, non‑property‑tax revenue, investment income from special building funds, and the district's base growth percentage; reduce that amount by current-year non‑property‑tax revenue; and certify the resulting authority to the school board. The department also must calculate and report each district's unused property tax request authority for carryforward, but excludes carryforward of increases attributable to base growth percentage increases under section 79-3405. Original sections 79-3403 and 79-3406 are repealed. No explicit appropriations or budget allocations are included.Adds a deduction to a calculation equal to any amount by which a school district’s prior-year property tax request exceeded its property tax request authority under section 79-3405. It explicitly excludes from that comparison any increases in request authority that resulted from increases to the district’s base growth percentage under section 79-3405. No specific state agencies, new appropriations, or funding allocations are created.
109-1-LB693_IntroLB693_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Veterans' AffairsLB693 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §87-302 (Uniform Deceptive Trade Practices Act) to make it a deceptive trade practice to receive compensation, directly or indirectly, for preparing, presenting, prosecuting, advising, consulting, assisting, or referring any individual in connection with veterans benefits matters before the United States Department of Veterans Affairs, the United States Department of Defense, or the Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs. The bill defines "veterans benefits matter" (claims under laws/regulations administered by those agencies affecting veterans, dependents, survivors, or other eligible individuals) and defines "compensation" as money, things of value, or financial benefit. Exceptions: fee-splitting between attorneys allowed under Nebraska law/rules and county veterans service officers are exempt. No funding or appropriations are included.Adds prohibitions on receiving compensation for preparing, presenting, prosecuting, advising, consulting, assisting, or contracting such services on veterans benefits matters before the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, U.S. Department of Defense, or the Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs, and likewise prohibits paid referrals for such services, except as allowed by state or federal law. Defines "veterans benefits matter" and "compensation." Preserves lawful attorney fee‑splitting and explicitly exempts county veterans service officers. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Veterans' Affairs are included.
109-1-LB694_IntroLB694_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of TransportationThe bill amends eligibility for tourist‑oriented directional sign panels by requiring applicants to provide the Department of Transportation an assurance they comply with applicable anti‑discrimination laws, explicitly adding military or veteran status to the listed protected characteristics. Entities found to violate those laws become ineligible for sign panels and must remove any unlawfully erected advertising devices. Other examined excerpts contain no additional references to the Department of Transportation and the bill includes no DOT appropriations, funding changes, or budget reallocations.Adds "military or veteran status" as a protected class across referenced statutes (including the Nebraska Fair Employment Practice Act), defines that term, and clarifies exceptions: entities may on a nondiscriminatory basis limit admission, offer discounts, provide housing or favorable loan/contract conditions to veterans/servicemembers or their families; veterans' preference programs remain intact; the change is not meant to duplicate USERRA or require different treatment for absent servicemembers. For the Department of Transportation: this likely requires treating military/veteran status as a protected class in DOT employment, services, facilities, and contracting practices, and updating related policies, but the bill contains no new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB695_IntroLB695_Intro_Copy.docxLB695 requires the Lower Elkhorn Natural Resources District (LENRD) to construct a dam and implement associated flood control measures, following stated legislative findings related to natural resources and flood management. The bill mandates that the LENRD secure necessary funding for the project; it does not specify state appropriations or alter any department budgets. No other state agencies or funding allocations are referenced.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB696_FinalLB696_Final_Copy.docxLB696 amends Nebraska’s Professional Landscape Architects Act, reallocating responsibilities and authorities of the State Board of Landscape Architects. Key actions for the Board: maintain and provide a public roster (for a fee under sections 84-712 to 84-712.09); accept Council of Landscape Architectural Registration Boards records and examinations; treat exam materials as nonpublic; issue, replace (fee up to $50), and set renewal/late‑renewal rules (late renewals increase 10% per month to a 2x cap; no renewals after one year); and impose professional development requirements. The Board’s disciplinary powers and sanctions are clarified. Financial provisions: civil penalties are remitted to the State Treasurer for distribution pursuant to Article VII, §5 of the Nebraska Constitution, and costs collected are credited to the State Board of Landscape Architects Cash Fund. Original statutory sections listed are repealed.Adds definitions and procedural provisions for the licensing board (the Board under the Professional Landscape Architects Act). Key points: - Defines "direct supervision" as having full professional knowledge and control over landscape-architecture work. - Authorizes the board to provide copies of the complete roster of professional landscape architects on request and to charge a fee for such copies consistent with sections 84-712 to 84-712.09. - Requires the board to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations governing these processes. - Clarifies that examination materials are records subject to disclosure under sections 84-712 to 84-712.09. No new appropriations or budget allocations are made; the only financial provision permits fee collection for roster copies.
109-1-LB697_IntroLB697_Intro_Copy.docxLB697 amends the Pharmacy Practice Act. Key agency-related changes: - Board of Pharmacy: composition set at eight members — five actively practicing pharmacists (at least one hospital pharmacist), one pharmacy technician, and two public members. - Compounding: persons authorized to compound must follow USP–NF chapters 795 and 797 as of Jan 1, 2023, and may compound only for a practitioner’s medical order, research/teaching (not for sale), or office use by an outsourcing facility operating under 21 U.S.C. §353b or Neb. §71-470. Hospital compounding permitted across health system affiliates. Reconstitution and beyond-use dating must follow manufacturer labeling or USP–NF. Compounding prohibited for FDA-withdrawn drugs, essentially copied drugs absent shortage/allergy, or products designated by FDA/Board as noncompoundable. - Delegated dispensing permits for public health clinics: allow non-pharmacist dispensing without onsite pharmacist under detailed conditions (initial dispensing rules, formulary limits, labeling and documentation requirements, director-approved patient info, and mandatory availability of a delegating/on-call pharmacist). No funding or appropriation changes. Original sections repealed.Adds that two members must be either from an "outsourcing facility" operating under federal law (21 U.S.C. §353b) or under state §71‑470, or be Nebraska‑licensed practitioners affiliated with a public health clinic holding a delegated dispensing permit. Agencies implicated: federal oversight of outsourcing facilities under 21 U.S.C. §353b, state regulatory authority tied to §71‑470, and public health clinics subject to state permitting for delegated dispensing. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB698_IntroLB698_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborDefines "Department" as the Department of Labor and assigns enforcement authority to the Commissioner of Labor. The commissioner must issue citations when investigations indicate violations of the Nebraska Healthy Families and Workplaces Act, notify employers of proposed administrative penalties (max $500 for a first violation; $5,000 for subsequent violations), and accept contests within 15 working days. The commissioner must provide hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act. Employers with unpaid citations are barred from contracting with the state or political subdivisions until paid (contested citations are not treated as unpaid until resolution). Citations and cited employer names are releasable to the public, except while contested. No funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are included.The added language appears to create or enumerate covered/exempt categories of persons in subsection (3), explicitly including: (b) individuals employed in seasonal or other temporary agricultural work, and (d) individuals under sixteen years of age (with an unclear clause referencing “at least eleven”). Parts (a) and (c) are blank or incomplete in the excerpt. There is no mention of the Department of Labor, nor any changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the provided text. The fragmentary wording prevents a definitive reading; provide the full underlined text for a complete summary.
109-1-LB699_IntroLB699_Intro_Copy.docxLB699 amends the ImagiNE Nebraska Act (section 77-6831). Key agency actions and fiscal changes: - Tax Commissioner: authorized to issue rules, regulations, certificates, and forms; to issue direct payment permits at agreement execution; and to determine and certify eligibility for personal property tax exemptions to taxpayers and county assessors. - Director (collection agent): collects a 0.5% administrative fee on incentives (except personal property exemptions) when incentives are received or used; fee may be paid directly or via withholding of refunds; a credit is allowed for fees paid with the application. - State Treasurer: receives fee receipts for credit to the newly created ImagiNE Nebraska Cash Fund. - Department of Economic Development: administers the ImagiNE Nebraska Cash Fund, which consists of collected fees and any legislative appropriations and is used to administer the Act. - State investment officer: may invest available fund balances under the Nebraska Capital Expansion Act and Nebraska State Funds Investment Act.Adds that when a contractor (purchasing under subdivisions (2)(a)(iii)–(v)) has elected to be taxed as the consumer of building materials under §77-2701.10(2) or (3): if the contractor already paid sales or use tax, the contractor must certify the amount to the taxpayer and the taxpayer may claim a refund as if they had paid the tax; if the contractor has not paid sales or use tax, the contractor’s purchases are treated as tax‑exempt as if purchased directly by the taxpayer. No state agency or department is named, and no changes to funding, appropriations, or budgets are included.
109-1-LB69_FinalLB69_Final_Copy.docxLB69 revises statutes governing the Commission on African American Affairs. The commission is set at 14 governor-appointed members (all of African ancestry), with one initial appointee identifying as an immigrant/new American and one as a young professional (18–24). Members may serve no more than two full four-year terms; commissioners’ names must appear on the commission website. The commission may receive and administer state, federal, and other funds, employ personnel of its choosing, and shall be provided an office for executive management. Duties emphasize coordination with state and federal agencies and elected officials and reporting to the Governor’s office. Reporting requirements must include financial information (budget, funding sources, expenditures, grants, public funds allocated). An executive board (chair + four members) may contract up to $2,000 per contract. Original sections are repealed.Adds composition and transparency requirements for the commission: one initial appointee must be an immigrant/new American and one a young professional (18–24); all commissioners' names must be posted on the commission website. Expands required public-facing content to include program areas and partnerships (scholarships, mentoring, school partnerships, career advancement), health and wellness programs, criminal justice/public safety initiatives (including police-community relations and services for formerly incarcerated persons), and housing/community development (affordable housing, eviction prevention, partnerships with housing agencies). Requires metrics/KPIs (employment, graduation, health, recidivism), public feedback/community needs assessments, and publication of the commission’s financial information (budget, funding sources, expenditures, grants, public funds). No new appropriations or dollar allocations specified.
109-1-LB6_IntroLB6_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB6 amends section 28-416 of the Uniform Controlled Substances Act to require that any person convicted of a violation of that section who is sentenced to the Department of Correctional Services shall attend appropriate drug abuse treatment and counseling. The bill contains no provisions changing funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Correctional Services.Adds a new penalty-enhancement (subsection 16) for convictions under subsection (1): the offender is punished at the next higher penalty classification than those in subsections (2), (7), (8), (9), or (10) where either (i) [text fragment in bill] or (ii) the violation involved use of the controlled substance that directly and proximately caused another person's death or serious bodily injury. The provision begins to limit how far an enhancement may go (text incomplete). No language allocates funding, appropriations, or budget changes for the Department of Correctional Services. (Operationally, longer sentences could increase prison population and future DOCS costs, but no explicit funding or budget directive is included.)
109-1-LB700_IntroLB700_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services- Department of Correctional Services (DOCS) - Courts may commit an offender to DOCS for a complete institutional study to inform sentencing (sec. 29-2204.05/29-2204 discussion). - The bill clarifies that a "staff secure juvenile facility" expressly excludes any institution operated by DOCS (sec. 43-245 definition). - Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) - Peace officers may deliver juveniles taken into temporary custody to DHHS, which must place the juvenile in the least restrictive temporary setting, supervise placement, and may consent to emergency medical, psychological, or psychiatric treatment; DHHS's temporary custody ends if no court order is entered within 48 hours (sec. 43-250 subsections). - For juveniles needing mental-health evaluation, officers may deliver them to DHHS (with required certification and notification to county attorney and family) (sec. 43-250). - DHHS, jointly with the Office of Probation Administration, shall use, oversee, and may reimburse day-reporting and evening-reporting centers for juveniles and may adopt related rules (sec. 12). No specific appropriations or budget allocations are included.Department of Correctional Services: Adds a sentencing cap for young adults—any person convicted of a Class IB felony when under 22 now faces a maximum of 60 years and a minimum of 20 years imprisonment—potentially reducing exposure to longer incarceration terms. No agency-specific funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included. Department of Health and Human Services: Requires DHHS (with the Office of Probation Administration) to use day‑reporting and evening‑reporting centers for juveniles as appropriate, to adopt rules for selecting/overseeing those centers, and to reimburse them (rulemaking and reimbursement authority granted). Prohibits transferring adjudicated juveniles out of state except for emergency medical or mental‑health treatment and reinforces confidentiality obligations for juvenile information. No explicit funding amounts or new appropriations are specified.
109-1-LB701_IntroLB701_Intro_Copy.docxLB701 amends section 68-901 (public assistance) to express legislative intent to reimburse doula services, establishes a work group (see subdivision (3)(a)) to develop an implementation plan, and defines "doula" as a trained support person who may attend prenatal visits, labor, and postpartum care. The bill requires appropriate training, certification, or experience as set by the work group’s implementation plan and prohibits doulas from performing clinical/medical tasks or diagnosing/treating. It repeals the original section 68-901. The text contains no specific agency names, nor does it specify new appropriations, funding amounts, or budget allocations.Defines "doula" as a trained professional providing emotional, physical, and informational support before, during, and after labor — including attending prenatal visits, supporting delivery, and offering postpartum resources. Requires doulas to have training, certification, or experience as specified by an implementation plan developed by the work group referenced in subdivision (3)(a). Explicitly prohibits doulas from performing clinical or medical tasks or diagnosing/treating. No specific state agencies, funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are mentioned.
109-1-LB702_IntroLB702_Intro_Copy.docxLB702 (McKinney) adopts the "Neighborhood Empowerment Act" within the economic development context and establishes a state‑administered grant program. The bill directs annual General Fund appropriations—specified in the excerpt only as "million dollars from the General Fund each fiscal year"—to "the department" for grants under the Act. The excerpt does not identify the department by name or the exact dollar amount.Adds an annual General Fund appropriation of "million dollars" (amount unspecified in the excerpt) to "the department" to provide grants under the Neighborhood Empowerment Act. No other agencies are named.
109-1-LB703_IntroLB703_Intro_Copy.docxLB703 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81‑2604 governing the Commission on African American Affairs. It adds a new duty requiring the commission to develop an exchange program with the Republic of Ghana and states the Legislature’s intent to appropriate $1,000,000 annually for that program beginning in FY2026‑27. The commission’s existing roles remain—coordinating programs and working with other state and federal government agencies, elected officials, and the Governor’s office. The bill repeals the original §81‑2604.Adds a mandate to develop an exchange program with the Republic of Ghana and states the Legislature’s intent to appropriate $1,000,000 annually for that program beginning in FY 2026–27. No specific state agency or department is named.
109-1-LB704_FinalLB704_Final_Copy.docxLB704 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 43-512.12 and 43-512.13 governing Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) review of Title IV-D child support orders. Key agency-related changes: - DHHS must initiate review within 15 business days after learning a noncustodial parent will be incarcerated >180 days, notify both parents and the incarceration facility administrator (per §47-1003), and require financial submissions within 30 days. - DHHS must complete review and notify parties within 120 calendar days and refer orders to the county attorney or other authorized attorney for district-court modification when criteria are met. - If DHHS finds a decrease in support unwarranted after an incarceration-initiated review, it must offer the incarcerated parent a conference (in-person or virtual) within 30 days and issue a final determination within 30 days after the conference. - References include Supreme Court child support guidelines and the Medical Assistance Act. No appropriations or budget changes are included.Adds procedural duties for "the department" to review a noncustodial parent's child‑support order when the parent is to be incarcerated. Key agency/actor points: - The department must require parties and the facility administrator (per §47‑1003) to submit financial information within 30 days of notice and complete the review within 120 calendar days, notifying parties under §43‑512.13. - If no decrease is warranted, the department must offer the incarcerated parent a conference (in‑person or virtual) within 30 days of review; notices to both parents by first‑class mail must include findings, format, date/time/location, evidence deadlines (10 business days), waiver option (5 business days), etc. - Within 30 days after the conference the department makes a final determination and may refer the matter to the county attorney or authorized attorney; waiver triggers a direct final determination. - Notices to incarcerated parents must be sent to the facility address and facility administrator. Final determinations are not treated as contested cases under the Administrative Procedure Act. - No funding or appropriation changes included.
109-1-LB705_IntroLB705_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Agriculture, Department of Economic Development, Department of Correctional Services, Department of Health and Human Services, Department of Motor Vehicles, Department of Revenue, Department of Transportation, Military DepartmentThe bill assigns DHHS to operate the qualified patient/registered caregiver registry and enrollments, and creates a Medical Cannabis Control Fund (fees, gifts, grants) to finance commission administration (including salaries/benefits) and allow legislative transfers to the General Fund. Application fees are split 50/50 between that Fund and local treasurers (credited to local school funds); bonding premiums for commissioners and staff are paid from the General Fund. The Nebraska Medical Cannabis Commission must coordinate with DHHS, the Department of Agriculture, and the Department of Revenue. Department of Economic Development (DED) will administer a new Medical Cannabis Business Equity Fund (gifts, contributions, legislative appropriations), provide technical assistance, grants, mentorships, and invest available funds per state investment law. Department of Correctional Services employees are barred from licenses; sentenced persons must attend drug treatment. Courts must notify the DMV of certain clean‑slate orders and juvenile drug penalties trigger abstracts to the DMV. State vehicle‑lettering exemptions are expanded for Correctional Services, DHHS, Agriculture, and the Military Department. Sales/use tax from aircraft transactions is credited to the Department of Transportation Aeronautics Capital Improvement Fund.Summary of added provisions affecting agencies and funding: - Department of Health and Human Services: defined as “Department”; must run the patient/caregiver registry, issue registry cards, adopt caregiver/health‑facility rules, maintain confidentiality, and collaborate with the Medical Cannabis Commission. - Department of Agriculture: required to coordinate with the Commission on regulation, cultivation, processing, testing, transport, and sale. - Department of Revenue: included as a collaborator; sales/use tax on dispensary sales is allocated: 50% to the Medical Cannabis Control Fund, 25% to the Medical Cannabis Business Equity Fund, and 25% to the Cannabis Community Reinvestment Fund. - Department of Economic Development: will administer the Medical Cannabis Business Equity Fund (gifts/legislative appropriations allowed), provide technical assistance/mentorship, and run grant programs for social equity/disproportionately impacted areas. - Department of Correctional Services: employees barred from holding licenses; bill funds re‑entry programs via the Reinvestment Fund and creates resentencing/clean‑slate processes affecting incarcerated persons. - Department of Motor Vehicles: to receive notice of clean‑slate orders; clean‑slate does not affect commercial driver’s license obligations. - Department of Transportation and Military Department: no direct budget or program changes specified.
109-1-LB706_IntroLB706_Intro_Copy.docxLB706 requires law enforcement agencies to screen dispatch calls for mental health indicators, flag them as "Mental Health Priority," notify and, unless unsafe or impracticable, dispatch an APS social worker (Department of Health and Human Services) to accompany officers and lead de-escalation and trauma-informed interactions. The Nebraska Commission on Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice must set minimum policy standards, may provide a model policy, and will annually review agency compliance within its existing appropriations (including grant funds) and report to the Governor and Legislature. Noncompliant agencies become ineligible for loans, grants, funds, or donations administered by the commission until corrected. The Law Enforcement Training Council (under the commission) may suspend or revoke officer certificates for willful failure to comply; administrative fines remain authorized and are collectible by the Attorney General. No new appropriations are specified.Requires all law enforcement agencies to screen dispatch calls with a checklist for signs of mental illness, flag qualifying incidents as a "Mental Health Priority," notify the nearest unit and an APS social worker, share mental‑health information with responders, and—unless unsafe—have officers accompanied by an APS social worker who takes the lead using de‑escalation/trauma‑informed care. Agencies must adopt written dispatch policies and file them with the commission, which will set minimum standards and may offer a model policy. The commission will annually review compliance within existing appropriations (including grants), report to the Governor and Legislature, and may bar noncompliant agencies from receiving loans, grants, funds, or donations it administers until corrected.
109-1-LB707A_FinalLB707A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueAppropriates General Fund amounts to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to implement LB707: $164,210 for FY2025‑26 and $50,800 for FY2026‑27. Of those appropriated funds, expenditures for permanent and temporary salaries and per diems are capped at $37,000 for FY2025‑26 and $38,200 for FY2026‑27.Department of Revenue (Program 102) receives General Fund appropriations: $164,210 for FY2025‑26 and $50,800 for FY2026‑27 to support implementation of Legislative Bill 707. Salary-related spending from these appropriated funds is capped: no more than $37,000 for FY2025‑26 and $38,200 for FY2026‑27 may be used for permanent/temporary salaries and per diems.
109-1-LB707_FinalLB707_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of RevenueThe bill designates the "Department" as the Department of Economic Development (DED) and gives DED authority to review, approve and monitor Good Life district and project applications, receive applicant reports, approve boundary adjustments, terminate districts that fail thresholds, and adopt rules to implement the Act. DED must transmit district maps, retailer lists, and ownership updates to the Department of Revenue (DOR). The DED and DOR may share confidential information as needed to administer the Act. Beginning October 1, 2025, the Tax Commissioner (DOR) will allocate and remit specified "allocated sales taxes"—generally 50% of certain state sales taxes from qualifying retailers—monthly to cities for Good Life district programs, provide detailed remittance reports to cities and DED, deduct refunds and offset uncovered refunds from local remittances. Unencumbered city Good Life funds may be recaptured to the General Fund on district termination.Key additions affecting the agencies: - Department of Economic Development (DED): may adopt rules and guidance for both the Good Life Transformational Projects Act and Good Life District Economic Development Act; must receive annual reports and ownership updates; may approve project areas and require memoranda of understanding tying local revenue use to eligible project-area costs. DED and Revenue may share confidential information to administer the programs. - Department of Revenue / Tax Commissioner: beginning Oct. 1, 2025, state sales tax rate set at 5.5%. The Tax Commissioner will allocate ("allocated sales taxes") and remit monthly to cities 50% of certain state sales taxes from qualifying good life district transactions, administer 50% refunds for new development costs (subject to available allocation), enforce a $5M annual cap for relocated retailers with excess rules, offset refunds from local remittances, provide detailed confidential remittance reports (parcel, taxpayer, taxable sales) to cities and DED, deposit project-area funds with trustee banks, and enforce recapture of unencumbered funds to the General Fund on termination.
109-1-LB708_IntroLB708_Intro_Copy.docxLB708 (Ibach) amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §85-1504, which defines the six community college areas for the Nebraska community college system. The bill revises county boundary assignments among those areas — notably adding Dawson County to the Mid‑Plains Community College Area (while retaining Red Willow) — and retains existing provisions allocating specific Cherry and Boone County precincts to Western, Northeast, and Central areas. The bill repeals the original section and replaces it with the amended boundaries. No state agency other than the community college system is referenced, and the bill contains no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.The only addition is the text ", and Dawson," which appears to add the name “Dawson” to an existing list. No government agencies or departments are mentioned and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations.
109-1-LB709_IntroLB709_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB709 authorizes the Department of Revenue to adopt and promulgate rules and regulations to implement the new Adoption Tax Credit Act. The bill amends section 77-2715.07 to add the Adoption Tax Credit Act to the list of refundable income tax credits. Separately, the statute continues to vest the Department of Revenue with recapture authority for the residence purchase credit (requiring recapture if residence is sold or ceases to be the primary residence within five years). No direct appropriations, funding increases, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included in the bill.Creates the "Adoption Tax Credit Act," effective for tax years beginning or deemed to begin on or after Jan. 1, 2026. It allows a Nebraska income tax credit for taxpayers eligible for the federal adoption expenses credit (26 U.S.C. §23). The Nebraska credit is refundable and equals 10% of the federal credit in the same taxable year. The Department of Revenue is authorized to adopt rules and regulations to implement the Act. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB70_IntroLB70_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill assigns multiple explicit duties to the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS). DHHS (or a licensed child‑placement agency) must complete required preplacement or postplacement adoptive home studies, perform central‑registry checks under section 28‑718, and may set or waive the adoptive‑home‑study fee or rate. DHHS must provide the medical‑history form used with adoption reports, be notified if medical histories are not filed, and receive originals of medical histories after decree entry. For children committed to DHHS, prospective adoptive parents must be given the opportunity to read the department's case file; DHHS may redact legally protected material and must file a verification with the court. The bill contains no explicit appropriations or budgetary allocations for DHHS.Adds rules allowing a "second adult" to adopt a minor or adult when a sole legal parent consents, requires parent-child relationship and an adoptive home study per section 43-107, and defines "sole legal parent." Creates a six‑month exception: if the sole parent adopted the child less than six months earlier and the second adult was included in that home study, a new study is not required unless the court orders one; otherwise a separate home study is required. Requires spouses to join petitions, bars creating more than two legal parents, and confirms parental support liability. No provisions change Department of Health and Human Services’ funding, appropriations, or budget allocations; adoptive home‑study processes are referenced but no DHHS budget actions are specified.
109-1-LB710_IntroLB710_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueLB710 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77‑2715.07. It explicitly authorizes the Department of Revenue to recapture the $5,000 nonrefundable residence‑purchase credit (subsection (7)) if the claimant sells or transfers the residence or ceases to use it as their primary residence within five years after the taxable year the credit was claimed. No other provisions explicitly reference the Department of Revenue, and the bill contains no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.Adds subsection setting the state credit rate: 10 for taxable years beginning or deemed to begin before Jan. 1, 2025, and 20% of the federal credit under IRC §32 for taxable years beginning or deemed to begin on or after Jan. 1, 2025. The Department of Revenue would apply these rates when administering the credit (see cross‑reference to subdivision (2)(e)(i)). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB711_IntroLB711_Intro_Copy.docxLB711 amends multiple sections of the Tax Equity and Educational Opportunities Support Act, changing certification and reporting dates and related procedures. Key agencies: the Department of Education (department), State Board of Education, Director of Administrative Services, Auditor of Public Accounts, Governor, and the Legislature’s Appropriations and Education Committees. Major changes: deadlines for the department to determine and certify state aid, school district budget authority, and applicable allowable reserve percentages are set “on or before June 15, 2025, and on or before March 1 each year thereafter.” Certified state aid must be shown as budgeted non‑property‑tax receipts and deducted before calculating local property tax requests; distributions remain ten monthly payments (Sept.–June). Applications and approvals for a two‑year new‑schools adjustment have October 15 and December 1 processing dates. Prior certifications completed before the bill’s effective date for FY2025‑26 are void. The Appropriations Committee must include the necessary funding in its annual recommendation. Emergency clause makes the act effective on passage.The added text repeatedly references "schools" and an "application" used as the basis for an adjustment, and establishes the act’s effective timing as 2025–26 (references to 2025). No specific government agencies or departments are named, and there are no explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the provided excerpt.
109-1-LB712A_IntroLB712A_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueAppropriates $12,600 from the General Fund for FY2025‑26 (and $0 for FY2026‑27) to the Department of Revenue, Program 102, to aid in carrying out Legislative Bill 712. The appropriation may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates General Fund to the Department of Revenue, Program 102: $12,600 for FY2025-26 and $0 for FY2026-27 to support implementation of Legislative Bill 712 (2025). 109-1-LB712_IntroLB712_Intro_Copy.docxLB712 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §77-4008 (Tobacco Products Tax Act). It sets the tax on electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) at 40% of (i) the purchase price paid by the first owner or (ii) the price at which the first owner who made/manufactured/fabricated the ENDS sells it to others. It retains snuff at $0.44 per ounce and other tobacco products at 20% of purchase/wholesale price. For retailers, the ENDS tax is triggered when products are brought into the state, manufactured in-state for sale, or sold to consumers. Collections are to be distributed pursuant to §77-4025. No specific state agencies or appropriations are named. 109-1-LB713_IntroLB713_Intro_Copy.docxLB713 amends the School Employees Retirement Act (sections 79‑902 and 79‑930) to eliminate the definition of "prior service" and harmonize related statutory definitions and return‑to‑work provisions. The bill clarifies when a member is deemed to have terminated employment, when contributions and service credit resume, and limits interim work (volunteer/substitute) following separation. It identifies the Public Employees Retirement Board as the retirement board and assigns the Nebraska Public Employees Retirement Systems (NPERS) director authority to make 180‑day separation determinations, with appeals to the Public Employees Retirement Board. 109-1-LB714_IntroLB714_Intro_Copy.docxLB714 amends motor vehicle tax and fee administration. The department (statutory motor vehicle agency) will continue to determine and notify registrants of annual taxes and fees. County treasurers retain 2% of motor vehicle tax proceeds and 2% of motor vehicle fees for costs. The State Treasurer receives 1.3% of motor vehicle tax proceeds for credit to the Vehicle Title and Registration System Replacement and Maintenance Cash Fund. Remaining motor vehicle tax proceeds are allocated by tax district: generally 40% county, 37% local school system/district, 23% city/village (special allocations for non‑city districts and counties with a metropolitan class city). A Motor Vehicle Fee Fund is created: counties receive 70% and municipalities 30% of the fund quarterly in proportions matching recent Highway Allocation Fund distributions. Funds are for road, bridge, and street purposes. Operative January 1, 2026.No government agency or department is referenced. No explicit funding, appropriations, budget allocations, or named agencies/departments are included.

109-1-LB71_IntroLB71_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services- The Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) shall assess market rates and costs and adjust child care reimbursement every odd-numbered year to at least the 75th percentile; nationally accredited providers and programs rated step two or higher under Step Up to Quality may receive higher rates based on quality ratings (section 43-536). - DHHS shall administer the state's social services program, may contract for services, and must participate in the federal Child Care Subsidy program (section 68-1206). DHHS will promulgate rules implementing accommodations and enrollment provisions effective July 1, 2025. - Funding: for July 1, 2021–Sept 30, 2026, Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) funds must pay costs from prior income-eligibility changes; if insufficient, Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) funds may be used. No General Funds (except administration) shall be used for those costs. DHHS shall collaborate on a privately funded independent evaluation.The provided text ("two two two") contains no underlined or legislative content referencing the Department of Health and Human Services. 109-1-LB72_FinalLB72_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesLB72 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §§28-405 and 28-416; the provision affecting the Department of Correctional Services requires that any person convicted under §28-416 who is sentenced to the Department must attend appropriate drug‑abuse treatment and counseling. The bill contains no other references to the Department of Correctional Services and includes no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for that department.Adds and clarifies controlled-substance definitions: excludes FDA‑approved crystalline polymorph psilocybin pharmaceutical products; expressly adds xylazine and a long list of its isomers/metabolites to the controlled-substance list while carving out uses tied to FDA‑approved or investigational animal drug authorizations and permissible veterinary/pharmaceutical compounding; and adds zuranolone by chemical name.
