109-1-LB73_IntroLB73_Intro_Copy.docxBill LB73 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-1414.07 to set annual continuing-education requirements for law enforcement officers (excluding noncertified conditional officers): the greater of 32 hours for officers serving in counties with 40,000+ residents or 20 hours for counties under 40,000 (population determined by the U.S. Bureau of the Census). It retains exemptions for the year of initial full certification and for retirement in good standing, and treats non-employed officers as serving in their county of residence. Required topics include de-escalation, mental health, substance abuse, at least two hours of anti-/implicit-bias training, firearms, officer wellness, legal updates (including First and Fourth Amendment issues), and vehicular pursuit policy review. Training formats may include seminars, college courses, agency instruction, or online delivery. Operative date: January 1, 2026. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds a population-based distinction for a law enforcement officer’s required hours: counties are classified using the most recent federal decennial census or revised certified count by the United States Bureau of the Census; officers in counties under 40,000 require twenty hours (larger-county requirement referenced but not restated). Also adds that an unemployed officer seeking to maintain professional status is treated as serving in the county of their residence for purposes of subdivision (1)(b). No state agencies beyond county governments and the U.S. Bureau of the Census are newly created or referenced, and there are no funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes.
109-1-LB74_IntroLB74_Intro_Copy.docxLB74 amends section 49-1446.03 of the Nebraska Political Accountability and Disclosure Act to clarify and expand allowable campaign-committee expenditures. Permitted uses include continued operation of campaign offices; social events for campaign workers/constituents; public-opinion activities; repayment of pre‑election campaign loans; newsletters and communications; gifts of acknowledgment (limited to $50 per individual annually); meals, lodging, travel, and conference fees for officeholders, their staff, minor children, and immediate family when related to duties or candidacy; and child care for officeholders. It explicitly applies similar conference/travel provisions to the candidate committee for the Governor. The bill repeals the original section. No appropriations or budgetary changes are included. The bill was assigned to the Government, Military and Veterans Affairs Committee.Adds repeated possessive references to "the officeholder's" and "the Governor's" and expressly includes "Child care services incurred by an officeholder when the officeholder is involved in activities related to the duties of the officeholder." No specific state agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the added text.
109-1-LB75_IntroLB75_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB75 repeatedly references the Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Labor. Key provisions: - Defines “Department” as the Department of Labor and “Commissioner” as the Commissioner of Labor. - Requires the Nebraska Department of Labor to calculate and publish the CPI‑based annual minimum wage by October 15 each year, beginning October 15, 2026. - Grants the commissioner authority to approve certain training‑wage programs, subpoena records and witnesses, inspect records, and gather testimony. - Requires employers to make records available to the commissioner (including by demand if kept outside the state) and authorizes the department to receive confidential records (disclosable only by court order). - Permits employees to file complaints with the department; the department shall forward credible complaints to county attorneys or pursue enforcement and must develop forms and rules. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds definitions identifying "Commissioner" as the Commissioner of Labor and "Department" as the Department of Labor. Requires employers of tipped employees to retain for 3 years records listing employee name, address, occupation, rate of pay, pay per period, and daily/weekly hours; records must be kept on-site or at a suitable location and made available to the Commissioner (out‑of‑state records must be produced on demand). Employers must provide sworn statements on forms the Commissioner prescribes and any nonprivileged information needed for enforcement. All records obtained by the Department are confidential, are not public records, and are disclosable only by court order. The Department may accept complaints from employees (in a manner it prescribes), must develop forms and rules, forward credible complaints to county attorneys or take enforcement itself, and may inspect workplaces. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB76_IntroLB76_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of LaborLB76 references the United States Department of Labor twice. It requires the retirement board to use the U.S. Department of Labor’s Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI‑W) — using June 30 factors — to calculate purchasing‑power and cost‑of‑living adjustments for Nebraska State Patrol retirees. If that CPI is discontinued or replaced, the board must select a reasonable substitute index published by the U.S. Department of Labor. The bill contains no explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Labor.For the Department of Labor: the added language sets a change effective July 1, 2025 — a rate of 4% applies beginning that date (the provision also references a different treatment “prior to July 1, 2025” but does not specify a rate in the inserted text). No portions of the underlined additions allocate funding, create appropriations, or change budget authorizations for the Department of Labor.
109-1-LB77A_FinalLB77A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of InsuranceAppropriates $500,000 from the Department of Insurance Cash Fund for FY2025‑26 and $500,000 from the same fund for FY2026‑27 (total $1,000,000) to the Department of Insurance, Program 69, to aid in carrying out Legislative Bill 77 (109th Leg., 1st Sess., 2025). The appropriation expressly prohibits using these funds for permanent or temporary employee salaries and per diems.Appropriates $500,000 from the Department of Insurance Cash Fund for FY2025-26 and $500,000 from that fund for FY2026-27 (total $1,000,000) to the Department of Insurance, Program 69, to implement provisions of Legislative Bill 77 (109th Leg., 2025). Funds must not be used for permanent or temporary state employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB77_FinalLB77_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Insurance, Department of Health and Human ServicesThis bill defines "Department" as the Department of Insurance and assigns it authority to approve uniform prior‑authorization request forms and to receive exemption requests from utilization review agents that implement standardized electronic prior‑authorization methods (including APIs meeting 45 C.F.R. 156.223(b)). It also requires the medical assistance program (administered by the Department of Health and Human Services) to cover biomarker testing no later than January 1, 2028, with specified clinical criteria, requires contractors to provide testing at equivalent scope/duration/frequency, and mandates that DHHS post a clear exception‑request process on its website. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Department of Insurance - Sets Department = Department of Insurance and strengthens prior-authorization oversight: utilization review agents must post new/amended requirements online and give contracted providers 60 days' notice. - Adverse determinations and appeals must be made/reviewed by physicians or appropriate clinical peers; medical directors must be physicians licensed in the U.S. - Notices of denials must cite written clinical review criteria and allow provider discussions (requestable within 3 business days) with expedited re-notice (1 business day urgent, 2 nonurgent). - Establishes timeframes for prior-authorization decisions (shorter deadlines before and after Jan 1, 2028), honors prior authorizations for 60 days after plan changes, and permits API-based exemptions with 90 days' provider notice. Department of Health and Human Services - Requires the medical assistance program to cover biomarker testing by Jan 1, 2028 under specified clinical criteria, minimize care disruption, and obligates contractors to match scope/duration/frequency. - DHHS must publish a clear exception-request process on its website. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.
109-1-LB78A_FinalLB78A_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill appropriates funds to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program 514, to implement Legislative Bill 78. It directs (1) $830,000 from the Domestic Violence and Sex Trafficking Survivor Housing Assistance Fund for FY2025‑26 and (2) $1,135,000 from the same fund for FY2026‑27 to DHHS. Both appropriations are Cash Funds designated for state aid only. The bill prohibits using these appropriated funds for permanent or temporary employee salaries and per diems.The amendment appropriates funds to the Department of Health and Human Services, Program 514, to implement Legislative Bill 78 (109th Leg., 1st Sess., 2025): $830,000 (FY2025‑26) and $1,135,000 (FY2026‑27), both from the Domestic Violence and Sex Trafficking Survivor Housing Assistance Fund. Each fiscal year’s amount is designated as Cash Funds for state aid only. The appropriation may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB78_FinalLB78_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human Services, Department of RevenueCreates the Domestic Violence and Sex Trafficking Survivor Assistance Act, designating the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to administer housing stability programs for domestic violence and sex‑trafficking survivors, including grants, loans, reimbursements, housing‑related assistance, formulaic distribution (developed in consultation with service providers), contracting with qualified third parties, and authority to direct up to 20% of excess assistance funds to certified organizations for housing acquisition/rehabilitation. Establishes the Domestic Violence and Sex Trafficking Survivor Housing Assistance Fund, administered by DHHS, funded by legislative transfers and public/private sources, and investable by the state investment officer. Amends documentary stamp tax allocation: from each $2.32 collected the register retains $0.50 (county general fund); remitted amounts credit: $0.95 Affordable Housing Trust Fund, $0.25 Site and Building Development Fund, $0.25 Homeless Shelter Assistance Trust Fund, $0.30 Behavioral Health Services Fund, and $0.07 to the new Survivor Housing Assistance Fund. The Tax Commissioner/Department of Revenue issues rules; taxpayers may seek declaratory rulings, and the Department of Revenue may not overturn county assessor sale‑qualification determinations without its own review finding them incorrect.Added provisions designate DHHS as lead, define terms, and require DHHS to promote housing stability for domestic violence and sex‑trafficking survivors by providing grants, loans, rental/utility/security deposit assistance and provider reimbursements. DHHS may contract with qualified 501(c)(3)s or tribal entities, must use a formula (developed with provider input) to allocate assistance, and may redirect up to 20% of any fully satisfied housing‑assistance obligations to certified organizations for housing acquisition/rehabilitation. The Domestic Violence and Sex Trafficking Survivor Housing Assistance Fund is created, to receive legislative transfers and public/private contributions, be administered by DHHS, and be invested by the state investment officer. The added text does not clearly assign any new duties or specific appropriations to the Department of Revenue.
109-1-LB79_IntroLB79_Intro_Copy.docxLB79 requires Nebraska trial courts to dismiss a defendant’s direct‑negligence claim in civil cases involving a commercial motor vehicle that requires a commercial driver’s license if the defendant stipulates that the alleged negligent person was the defendant’s employee or independent contractor and was acting within the course and scope of employment or as an independent contractor. If such a stipulation is made and the employee/contractor’s negligence is found to have caused or contributed to damages, the defendant’s liability is then adjudicated solely under respondeat superior. The bill relies on the definition of “commercial motor vehicle” in section 60‑316. No funding or appropriation changes are included.Added text allows a defendant in a civil action involving a commercial motor vehicle that requires a commercial driver’s license to move to dismiss any claim of the defendant’s direct negligence by stipulating that the negligent person was the defendant’s employee or independent contractor and was acting within the scope of employment or as the defendant’s contractor. If those stipulations are made and the employee/contractor’s negligence caused the damages, the defendant’s liability is limited to respondeat superior. “Commercial motor vehicle” is as defined in section 60-316. No government agencies, departments, or budget/appropriation changes are mentioned.
109-1-LB7_FinalLB7_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of AgricultureThis bill assigns the Department of Agriculture specific enforcement and reporting roles under the Foreign‑owned Real Estate National Security Act: - Any restricted entity (or agent/trustee/fiduciary) that meets certain CFIUS conditions must annually certify compliance to the Department of Agriculture by January 15, 2026, and each January 15 thereafter. - Any person may notify the Department of Agriculture of a violation or potential violation. - The Department of Agriculture is charged with investigating alleged violations; the Director of Agriculture must refer suspected violations to the Attorney General or retained outside counsel for enforcement. - The Director of Agriculture, together with the Attorney General and retained counsel, is responsible for determining whether a person is subject to or in violation of the act. No provisions in the bill change funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Agriculture.Adds an annual certification duty to the Department of Agriculture: any "restricted entity" (or its agent, trustee, or fiduciary) that has either (1) a CFIUS determination of no unresolved national‑security concerns or (2) an active national security agreement with CFIUS must certify that status to the Department of Agriculture on or before January 15, 2026 and each January 15 thereafter. The change also clarifies exemption language for certain foreign owners under the Foreign‑owned Real Estate National Security Act but preserves exceptions for restricted entities. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Agriculture are specified.
109-1-LB80A_FinalLB80A_Final_Copy.docxAppropriates $20,000 from the Supreme Court Automation Cash Fund to the Nebraska Supreme Court (Program 570) for FY2025-26, and $0 for FY2026-27, to aid implementation of Legislative Bill 80 (109th Legislature, 2025). Funds are restricted: they may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.Appropriates $20,000 from the Supreme Court Automation Cash Fund for FY2025-26 (and $0 for FY2026-27) to the Nebraska Supreme Court, Program 570, to support implementation of Legislative Bill 80 (109th Leg., 1st Sess., 2025). Funds may not be used for permanent or temporary employee salaries or per diems.
109-1-LB80_FinalLB80_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill designates the "Department" as the Department of Health and Human Services (Sec. 31; Sec. 40 amending 42‑903) and assigns DHHS explicit child‑protection duties: conduct investigations and implement traditional and alternative responses; manage non‑court‑involved cases; operate and maintain the central child‑abuse/neglect registry and provide notice to subjects regarding entry, amendment, expungement, and mandatory expungement hearings (Secs. 31, 33). DHHS must contact and notify appropriate military installations (per negotiated MOUs) when a report involves military families, may adopt rules to implement MOUs and information‑sharing/confidentiality, and must establish internal Review, Evaluate, and Decide Teams for report review (Sec. 32). No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds duties for the Department of Health and Human Services (the department) regarding child abuse/neglect reports involving military families: after contacting the family and determining the subject is a military family member, DHHS must notify the appropriate military installation and negotiate memoranda of understanding with each Nebraska installation that has a Military Family Advocacy Program. MOUs must set procedures for identifying military-family subjects, information sharing required by the section, and confidentiality consistent with state/federal law. The department may adopt rules and regulations to implement these requirements. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB81_IntroLB81_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of RevenueDefines "department" as the Department of Revenue and assigns it these roles: determine the "allowable growth percentage"; set the annual credit percentage so total refundable credits for school district taxes equal specified statewide amounts—$548,000,000 for taxable years beginning in calendar year 2022, $560,700,000 for 2023, and for 2024 the prior-year maximum increased by the allowable growth percentage; and provide forms and schedules to verify eligibility and allocate school district taxes. The credits are refundable and are taken against Nebraska income tax or the franchise tax.The added language gives the Department of Revenue authority to determine the "allowable growth percentage" — the year‑over‑year percent change in total assessed real property value statewide — and requires the department to set the credit percentage for taxable years beginning (or deemed to begin) in calendar year 2024 so that total credits equal the prior year's maximum credits increased by that allowable growth percentage. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included.
109-1-LB82_IntroLB82_Intro_Copy.docxLB82 adopts the Cosmetology Licensure Compact and amends Nebraska's Cosmetology, Electrology, Esthetics, Nail Technology, and Body Art Practice Act to implement it. Key state actors: each Member State's State Licensing Authority (responsible for issuing, investigating, disciplining, and delegating an administrator to the Compact Commission) and the state's executive and judicial branches (charged with enforcement). The Compact establishes a Compact Commission and Executive Committee to administer multistate licenses, operate a centralized Data System for licensure/investigative information, promulgate binding rules, and initiate enforcement or dispute actions (including in federal court). Financing: the Commission may adopt a budget, hire staff, accept grants/donations, levy annual assessments on Member States, and charge fees to licensees to cover operations; it must conduct annual financial reviews. The bill does not appropriate state funds directly.Adds a Cosmetology Licensure Compact creating a interstate "Commission" and related Executive Committee to oversee a multistate licensing program. Key government actors: each Member State's State Licensing Authority (and its delegate), state executive and judicial branches, governors and state legislative leaders (for default/termination notices), law enforcement agencies (for cooperation), and federal courts (United States District Court for D.C. or district where the Commission's principal office is located) as venue for litigation. The Commission must develop/operate a centralized Data System; Member States must submit uniform licensure and disciplinary data. Financial provisions authorize the Commission to establish a budget, levy annual assessments on Member States (allocated by formula), charge licensee fees (initial and renewal), accept grants/donations, borrow money, and keep audited financial records subject to annual review. The Commission may not pledge Member State credit and must include the financial review in its annual report.
109-1-LB83_IntroLB83_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesLB83 amends licensure statutes to require criminal background checks for initial health professional licenses (including dentists and dental hygienists). Key provisions referencing the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS): - Applicants must authorize release of FBI national criminal history record information to the "department." - The Nebraska State Patrol will forward fingerprints to the FBI and issue a criminal history report to the department. - The department and Nebraska State Patrol may adopt rules concerning fingerprinting and criminal background check costs; applicants pay the actual costs. - For FBI interpretation, "department" is defined as the Division of Public Health of the Department of Health and Human Services. No direct funding, appropriations, or budget allocations to DHHS are included.Adds the Dentist and Dental Hygienist Compact, creating a multi‑state licensure pathway and a Commission to administer compact privileges, data sharing, rulemaking, investigations, adverse actions, and an online Data System. For Nebraska’s Department of Health and Human Services (as the State Licensing Authority), the bill: requires DHHS to regulate licensees/compact privilege holders, report licensure and disciplinary data to the Commission/Data System, enforce adverse actions and alternative‑program conditions, participate in rulemaking and Commission processes, and comply with monitoring/default procedures. The Commission may charge fees, levy assessments, accept grants/donations, establish a budget, and require State cooperation. No specific appropriations, funding increases, or direct budget allocations to DHHS are included in the added text.
109-1-LB84_FinalLB84_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends section 38-3113 to incorporate the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact and revises exemptions under the Psychology Practice Act. Explicit references to the Department of Health and Human Services: persons who performed duties described in the subdivision while employed in institutions accredited by the Department of Health and Human Services (among other agencies) for at least two years prior to September 1, 1994, may use the title "psychologist associate" in that employment context, subject to limits described. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Health and Human Services are included.Adds a School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact establishing definitions, Member State participation rules, a multi‑state Commission (powers, meetings, rulemaking, dispute resolution), information‑sharing requirements, and financing via member assessments, licensee fees, grants, and donations. No line items, appropriations, or direct funding are provided to the Department of Health and Human Services. Potential DHHS implications (if DHHS is the State Licensing Authority): enact compact‑consistent statute; participate in licensee data sharing and investigations; notify the Commission of adverse actions; and be liable for its share of Commission assessments or fees to fund operations. The bill contains no explicit DHHS budget allocations or new appropriations.
109-1-LB85_FinalLB85_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor VehiclesLB85 amends procedures for transferring certificates of title involving decedents’ estates. It requires persons seeking transfer of a title for a motor vehicle, motorboat, all‑terrain vehicle, utility‑type vehicle, or minibike to furnish the Department of Motor Vehicles an affidavit demonstrating applicability of the estate‑affidavit process and compliance with its requirements to obtain a new certificate of title. After ten years from estate closing, the DMV must waive the requirement to show that no personal‑representative application is pending (subdivision (a)(5)) if the applicant provides evidence the estate closed and a certified authenticated death certificate. No funding, appropriation, or budgetary changes are included.Adds language allowing an "abstract of death" (as defined in §71-601.01) to be used when a certified death certificate is delayed. For the Department of Motor Vehicles, this means the DMV may accept an abstract of death as alternative proof of death for title, registration, ownership transfers, or other death‑related transactions. No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB86_IntroLB86_Intro_Copy.docxLB86 appropriates $500,000 from the General Fund for FY2025‑26 to the Nebraska Department of Natural Resources (Program 334). The funds are designated as state aid to be used solely to issue a grant to a natural resources district that has more than 250 watershed structures. Grants may fund operation, maintenance, or repair projects for those structures; a project is eligible only if its total cost exceeds $30,000 per structure. The bill includes an emergency clause, making the appropriation effective upon enactment.Appropriates $500,000 General Fund for FY2025–26 to the Department of Natural Resources (Program 334) to issue a grant to any natural resources district that owns more than 250 watershed structures. Funds are for projects involving operation, maintenance, or repair of those structures; a project is eligible only if its total cost exceeds $30,000 per structure. The appropriation is designated as $500,000 General Funds for state aid and may be used solely for this purpose.
109-1-LB87_IntroLB87_Intro_Copy.docxLB87 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §71‑8616 to direct the Nebraska Commission for the Blind and Visually Impaired to develop a statewide support service provider program for persons who are deaf‑blind. The bill includes a legislative intent regarding appropriations to implement the program (no dollar amounts specified in the bill text provided), removes obsolete provisions, repeals the original section, and contains an emergency clause for immediate effect. Referred to the Health and Human Services Committee.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB88_IntroLB88_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic DevelopmentLB88 is an appropriations bill that directs the Legislature to appropriate funds to the Department of Economic Development and states legislative intent regarding future appropriations to that department. The provided excerpt contains no specific dollar amounts, line-item allocations, or budgetary details for the Department of Economic Development.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB89_FinalLB89_Final_Copy.docxLB89 (Stand With Women Act) requires public schools, public postsecondary educational institutions, private schools, private postsecondary institutions subject to the Act, and athletic associations that sponsor interscholastic athletics to maintain and implement policies providing separate athletic teams based on sex. The bill defines "female," "male," and related terms and directs the governing body of each covered school/institution to adopt an implementing policy (including provisions on visitor/public conduct). Postsecondary institutions are defined by membership in accrediting bodies recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. Individuals born with differences in sex development retain protections under the federal Americans with Disabilities Act. The bill contains a severability clause. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are specified.Adds findings supporting sex-separated athletics and defines key terms (athletic association; boy, girl, man, male, female defined by reproductive biology; postsecondary educational institution as Nebraska colleges/universities/community colleges that are members of an accreditor recognized by the U.S. Department of Education; private and public schools). Requires governing bodies of affected public and private K‑12 and Nebraska postsecondary institutions to adopt policies implementing the Stand With Women Act, including visitor/public conduct provisions. Specifies individuals born with a disorder or difference in sex development receive protections/accommodations under the federal Americans with Disabilities Act. No new funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB8_IntroLB8_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Revenue- Registration, certification, and administration: Producers of sustainable aviation fuel must register with the Department of Revenue and provide third‑party certification of compliance with applicable CORSIA or similar methodology requirements; the Department may require additional information. - Application and approval: Producers apply on a Department‑prescribed form. The Department of Revenue will consider applications in receipt order, determine qualification, approve applications, and certify the amount of tax credits to the producer. - Claiming credits: Producers must attach the tax credit certification issued by the Department of Revenue to their tax return to claim credits. - Recapture authority: The Department of Revenue may recapture the residence purchase tax credit if the taxpayer disposes of or ceases primary use of the residence within five years. - Fiscal note: The bill contains no explicit appropriations, funding authorizations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue.Adds the Sustainable Aviation Fuel Tax Credit Act language (repeated) and makes the credit refundable beginning in 2028. It requires the Department of Revenue to process credit applications in the order received (first-come, first-served). No explicit changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations for the Department of Revenue are included in the added text.
109-1-LB90_FinalLB90_Final_Copy.docxLB90 revises municipal improvement-district procedures for cities of the first class, assigning responsibilities to the city clerk and the mayor and city council. Key agency actions: - City clerk must publish district-creation notice weekly for at least 20 days. Property owners representing >50% of front footage who file written objections within 20 days require the mayor and city council to repeal the ordinance. - Mayor and city council must solicit bids (and allow material requests via a petition by owners representing 25% of abutting property), postpone bid award at least 10 days, and allow a majority of abutting owners to select a received bid material. - Costs are assessed by the mayor and city council as special assessments payable in up to 20 annual installments (interest limited by section 45-104.01). Three or more delinquent installments permit the council to declare all future installments due (with one-time 20‑day publication). - City may issue street‑improvement bonds (≤20‑year maturities); special assessments serve as the sinking fund. The council may deny district formation if basic infrastructure (water, sewer, grading) is lacking and must notify interested parties in writing. Original sections are repealed.Adds authority and procedural detail for the mayor and city council (specifically of a city of the first class) in creating and administering improvement districts (see secs. 16-619, 16-624, 16-617, 16-622). The council is directed to publish required notice, advertise bids for district improvements, and may fund improvements by levying special assessments on specially benefited property. Property owners may pay the entire cost chargeable to their lots within 50 days after the assessment to avoid liens. The bill also contemplates issuance of street improvement bonds per the authorizing ordinance.
109-1-LB91_FinalLB91_Final_Copy.docxBill LB91 amends Neb. Rev. Stat. §70-650.01 governing transfers of electric distribution systems from public power districts and public power and irrigation districts to cities or villages. It requires districts that have paid or reserved sufficient funds to redeem bonds/obligations tied to their systems to convey distribution systems (excluding generation and transmission) upon a municipal resolution request, subject to published notice and a potential referendum if a petition (signed by electors equal to ≥20% of the last municipal election turnout) is filed. Cities/villages may seek declaratory judgment to define "distribution system." The bill preserves limits on refinancing existing indebtedness, permits issuance of bonds for new facilities with pledged revenue, and authorizes district boards to allocate revenue attributable to additional facilities. Original section repealed. No appropriations or budget changes.The added text inserts the phrase "public power and irrigation district" (and surrounding filler words) into the bill. No specific state or federal agencies or departments are named, and there are no changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations in the provided excerpt.
109-1-LB92_IntroLB92_Intro_Copy.docxLB92 enacts the Residential Tenant Clean Slate Act. It directs Nebraska trial courts to immediately issue orders sealing (clean slate relief) eviction records when an eviction proceeding is dismissed. Tenants may petition the trial court for sealing when records remain public after dismissal, a writ of restitution or judgment is reversed/vacated or never executed, the eviction was for COVID-19-era nonpayment (3/13/2020–6/30/2021), a named defendant was a minor, or a judgment violated statute; otherwise petitions are allowed three years after writ issuance or final judgment. Petitions require service on former parties, a 30-day objection window, and a hearing if objected to (objector bears burden). Orders are final and appealable. The bill references the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act and Mobile Home Landlord and Tenant Act. No state agencies beyond the trial courts are designated, and no funding or appropriation changes are included.Adds the "Residential Tenant Clean Slate Act," defining terms (clean slate relief = sealing under §5; eviction proceeding; landlord; tenant; residential tenancy; trial court) and tying applicable definitions to the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act or Mobile Home Landlord and Tenant Act as appropriate. It requires the trial court that dismissed an eviction to immediately issue a §5 clean slate order. It creates a tenant petition process in trial court (immediate eligibility in listed circumstances — e.g., record still public, judgment reversed/vacated, writ never executed, COVID-19 eviction window, minor defendant, statutory-violation — otherwise eligible after 3 years), mandates notice to parties, 30-day objection period, automatic grant if unopposed, hearing if opposed (objector bears burden), and makes orders final and appealable. No executive agencies or departments are newly created or mentioned, and no funding, appropriations, or budget changes are included.
109-1-LB93_IntroLB93_Intro_Copy.docxLB93 amends Nebraska discovery law (sections 29-1912, 29-1913, 29-1918), affecting courts, prosecuting attorneys, and law enforcement agencies. Key agency-related changes: - Prosecuting attorneys and law enforcement agencies: must permit defendants to inspect/copy investigation materials, including reports developed or received by law enforcement that directly relate to the investigation. Discovery explicitly includes information on computers, electronic communication devices, and digital information. - Courts: may order access and must specify time/place/manner for defense testing of electronic evidence; may review sealed prosecutorial statements alleging risk of harm to witnesses and make those available to the appellate court. - Expert witnesses: prosecutors must disclose names, qualifications, and complete opinions with basis/reasons. - Remedy: prosecutorial neglect or intentional alteration of evidence can render prosecution tests inadmissible. - Jailhouse informants remain governed by sections 29-4701 to 29-4706. No funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.Adds disclosure requirements: prosecutors must provide names, qualifications, and complete expert opinions (including bases/reasons) for any expert witness. Reinforces the continuing duty of disclosure (sec. 29-1918). In felony, misdemeanor, or ordinance cases carrying possible imprisonment, courts may order the prosecuting attorney to produce electronic/digital evidence (devices, computers, or analyses) or permit defendants to run comparable tests with their own experts. Defines “computer,” “digital information,” and “electronic communication device” (cross-referencing secs. 28-1343 and 28-833). Requires parties to promptly disclose newly discovered material that is subject to discovery under secs. 29-1912–29-1921 if it was previously requested or court-ordered. Government entities referenced: prosecuting authority/prosecuting attorney and the court. No funding, appropriations, or budget changes included.
109-1-LB94_IntroLB94_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Economic Development, Department of LaborThe bill directs the Department of Labor, in collaboration with the Department of Economic Development, to establish: (1) a grant program (max $20 million/year) for local educational institutions and nonprofits to develop and operate digital skills training centers in qualified census tracts; and (2) a grant program (max $20 million/year) to cover tuition, materials, transportation, equipment, and child care for low-income individuals attending such centers. The Department of Labor, with Economic Development and industry input, must develop standardized, industry-aligned curricula and run employer/industry partnership and apprenticeship supports. The Legislature intends to appropriate $50 million annually from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund to the Department of Labor beginning FY2025-26 for these grants, and the fund statute is amended to expressly authorize such grants.- Defines "qualified census tract" by reference to 26 U.S.C. 42(d)(5)(B)(ii)(I) as of Jan 1, 2025. - Department of Labor, with the Department of Economic Development and tech‑industry input, must: create two grant programs—(a) grants to local educational institutions/nonprofits to develop and operate digital skills training centers located in qualified census tracts (cap: $20 million per fiscal year); (b) grants to cover tuition, materials, transportation, equipment, and child care for low‑income individuals to attend such centers (cap: $20 million per fiscal year). - DOL/DED to develop standardized, industry‑aligned curricula (core skills, specialty tracks, bootcamps). DOL will partner with employers and grantees to support apprenticeships, job placement, and career advancement. - Legislative intent to appropriate $50 million annually from the Workforce Development Program Cash Fund to DOL beginning FY2025‑26 for these grants.
109-1-LB95_IntroLB95_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends section 68-1206 and assigns the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) responsibility to administer the state's social services program, to contract for services, and to participate in the federal child care assistance/subsidy program. DHHS must create a child care workforce pilot (Oct. 1, 2025–Sept. 30, 2028), promulgate implementing rules (operative July 1, 2025), and electronically submit annual pilot reports to the Legislature (Dec. 1, 2026–Dec. 1, 2028) including monthly enrollment by county and employment type, employment-duration breakdowns, program expenditures, and average monthly household cost. DHHS shall collaborate with a private nonprofit for an independent evaluation if privately funded. Funding language directs Child Care and Development Block Grant (CCDBG) funds (July 1, 2021–Sept. 30, 2026) to cover related costs, allows TANF funds if CCDBG is insufficient, and prohibits use of General Funds for those costs except administration.The Department of Health and Human Services must create a pilot child care assistance program for the child care workforce under the federal Child Care Subsidy program, effective October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2028. Eligibility: household income ≤85% of state median; an applicant/household member listed in the Nebraska Early Childhood Professional Record System working ≥20 hours/week in a licensed child care program, Head Start, or Early Head Start (including self‑employed); and meeting federal non‑income requirements. Enrollees retain eligibility for 12 continuous months without cost‑share while employed as required. DHHS must file annual electronic reports to the Legislature (Dec 1, 2026–2028) with participation and expenditure metrics. No direct funding, appropriation, or budget allocation changes are specified.
109-1-LB96_IntroLB96_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe bill amends section 68-911 to place specific responsibilities on the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS), including submitting state plan amendments or waivers for: community-based behavioral health coverage (per earlier deadline), school-district–provided direct reimbursable services, and extension of postpartum coverage (seek federal approval by Oct. 1, 2023). DHHS must provide continuous glucose monitor coverage (effective Jan. 1, 2023; expanded Aug. 1, 2024) with intent that no more than $600,000 be appropriated annually from the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund for implementation. By Oct. 1, 2025 DHHS must submit a waiver/state plan amendment to designate two medical respite facilities, select one in a metropolitan-class city and one in a primary-class city, and—upon approval—report annually to the Legislature. Medical respite services shall be funded by the Medicaid Managed Care Excess Profit Fund.No underlined (added) text found in this bill.
109-1-LB97_FinalLB97_Final_Copy.docxDepartment of Motor VehiclesThe bill expands Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) authority over titles, identification inspections, electronic reporting by wrecker/salvage dealers, and issuance/renewal/replacement of operator licenses, state IDs, commercial credentials, permits and ignition‑interlock permits (including preserved digital image/signature methods and device/program rules). It authorizes DMV staff or county treasurers to collect statutory fees and creates a Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund (Director‑administered) to receive receipts, county reimbursements, a $10 identification‑inspection fee, capped wrecker/salvage reporting fees, and postage/handling fees for mailed plates/registration. Beginning with the 2029 plate cycle, certain license‑plate fees shift from the Highway Trust Fund to the License Plate Cash Fund. The bill specifies allocation splits for operator/permit and ignition‑interlock fees, allows legislative transfers from the DMV Cash Fund to the General Fund or the Vehicle Title & Registration System Replacement and Maintenance Cash Fund, credits fund investment earnings to the General Fund (from 10/1/2024), and creates an Ignition Interlock Fund for indigent assistance (transferable to the General Fund); prior transfers to the Violence Prevention Cash Fund are preserved.Key additions affecting the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV): - Identification inspections: a $10 fee per inspection is added, remitted to the State Treasurer for credit to the Department of Motor Vehicles Cash Fund; no fee when a U.S. Government Certificate to Obtain Title is presented. - Registration/plates: persons may opt for 2- or 3-year registrations (must prepay fees/taxes each year, including fees in §§60-3,141 and 60-3,156). The director may begin secure mail delivery of plates/registration by an implementation date on or before Jan 1, 2029; the DMV may charge a postage/handling fee (remitted to the DMV Cash Fund). Proof of registration allows 30 days operation without a mailed plate. - Fee flow change: beginning with the 2029 plate cycle, all fees under the section are remitted to the License Plate Cash Fund. - Titles/permits: bonded-title notice procedures added (certified mail, 30‑day lien extinguishment); DMV must screen applicants before issuing ignition‑interlock permits (eligibility, prior convictions, no‑drive periods).
109-1-LB98_FinalLB98_Final_Copy.docxLB98 amends definitions for "all-terrain vehicle" and "utility-type vehicle" in Nebraska statutory law—specifically sections 60-103, 60-135.01, 60-305, 60-358.01, and 60-6,355 (Motor Vehicle Certificate of Title Act, Motor Vehicle Registration Act, and Nebraska Rules of the Road). Key changes: ATVs are defined as motorized off-highway vehicles ≤50 inches wide, on three or more nonhighway tires, and designed for operator use only or for operator plus one passenger; utility-type vehicles are defined as motorized off-highway vehicles ≤74 inches wide, ≤180 inches long (including bumper), and on four or more nonhighway tires. Modified/retrofitted ATVs/UTVs with after-market equipment not required by specified statutes are ineligible for registration. Original sections are repealed and the bill takes effect immediately as an emergency measure. 109-1-LB99_IntroLB99_Intro_Copy.docxDepartment of Correctional ServicesDefines "Department" as the Department of Correctional Services and "Director" as the Director of Correctional Services. Expands statutory definitions to specify restrictive housing as confinement with out‑of‑cell time under ten hours per day. Requires that no inmate be held in restrictive housing except pursuant to rules and regulations adopted and promulgated by the department under the Administrative Procedure Act, and limits restrictive housing to no more than fifteen consecutive days. Directs the department to promulgate rules establishing levels of restrictive housing, behavioral/mental‑health criteria, individualized transition plans developed with the committed offender, and regulations addressing risks for vulnerable populations. Authorizes the department to develop secure mental‑health housing that provides meaningful social interaction, exercise, environmental stimulation, and therapeutic programming. No funding or appropriation changes are included.For the Department of Correctional Services: the added provisions limit restrictive housing to a maximum of 15 consecutive days and prohibit placing more than one inmate in a single-occupancy restrictive housing cell unless all occupants voluntarily agree in writing. The bill also adds definitions relevant to custody and placement decisions: "developmental disability" (by reference to §71-1107), and a broad definition of "serious mental illness" (biological brain disorder substantially limiting life activities, listing examples such as schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, delusional disorder, bipolar disorder, major depression, and OCD). No changes to funding, appropriations, or budget allocations are included.
109-1-LB9_FinalLB9_Final_Copy.docxLB9 expands regulation and taxation authority primarily under the Tax Commissioner. Key agencies and fiscal provisions: - Tax Commissioner/cigarette tax division: broadened enforcement powers (license suspension/revocation, administrative penalties), authority to employ inspectors/clerks with Governor's advice/consent, call Attorney General, county attorneys, sheriffs, or other peace officers for aid, and to seize contraband tobacco products without warrant. Notices of deficiency may be mailed or personally served; extended timeframes for certain violations apply. Operative Jan 1, 2026. - Attorney General: authorized to act on behalf of the Tax Commissioner (directory enforcement, injunctions, recovery of investigation and litigation costs). - State Treasurer: receives court-ordered remittances. - Federal agencies: manufacturers/importers must submit federal excise reports or consent to federal disclosure to the Tax Commissioner (Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau, U.S. Treasury). - Fiscal/appropriation changes: new taxes—electronic nicotine delivery systems ≤3 ml at $0.05/ml; >3 ml at 10% of purchase price; alternative nicotine products at 20% of purchase price; other tobacco products at 20%. Stamping-agent license fee $500 credited to the General Fund. Administrative/administration expenses payable by warrants against the General Fund, capped at 4% of collections.Adds definitions linking "nicotine analogue" and "alternative nicotine product" to section 28-1418.01 and imposes a tax on alternative nicotine products equal to 20% of the purchase price paid by the first owner or the first owner's sale price. Expands enforcement authority for the Tax Commissioner: examine returns, issue deficiency notices (generally within 3 years, 6 years for fraud/omission), and extend mailing periods by agreement. Authorizes suspension/revocation of licenses under sections 28-1420 to 28-1429 and administrative penalties up to $5,000 after notice/hearing; appeals follow the Administrative Procedure Act. Declares untaxed tobacco products contraband, allowing seizure without warrant by the Tax Commissioner, agents, or peace officers; forfeited goods are to be destroyed or used for law enforcement and costs borne by the owner. No new appropriations or budget allocations specified.
